incident_description:
I contacted Apple Support because the battery in my MacBook Pro exploded, causing serious damage to my laptop by blowing out the touchpad and the back of the hard case. The battery is from 2015 and installed by a licensed Apple Provider. 

The battery was installed into a 2010 MacBook Pro and I purchased that laptop in 2016. When I contacted Apple, they said only the serial number of the laptop denotes if they will repair the item. I explained that the BATTERY was replaced in the 2015-2017 recall event, not the laptop.

I was told that since they cannot search "battery serial numbers" that they will only service the laptops with the appropriate serial number. Apple then told me to bring my laptop to a service center 90 minutes away. In this pandemic, I do not want to drive 3 hours roundtrip across state lines. They refused to send me a shipping label, stating my laptop was "obsolete."

I reminded them that the recall is on batteries put into MacBooks in 2015-2017. That battery also went into my older model and did explode, creating huge damage to my computer. 

Because they do not have a "system" for checking the battery, they refused to commit to the Recall.
justification: While no injuries were reported, the incident caused significant damage to the laptop, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description: We purchased a the Eufy Spaceview baby monitor and mounted it as described in their product manual, perpendicular to the wall. On the second night we used the monitor, while our baby was sleeping, the bottom of the camera broke, causing the heavy camera to fall off the wall, while the base of the camera remained on the wall mount. Luckily we mounted the camera just outside of the crib, so it did not hit our child. After looking over reviews of this product on amazon and other sites, this seems to be a common problem. Given that many consumers may mount this camera above their baby's crib, this seems like a serious safety risk. Even if not mounted above the crib, the risk of the unit falling from the wall and hitting a child seems high. They should provide a better mounting solution, fix this faulty base, or not recommend this perpendicular mounting option. I can't believe they are allowing this known issue to continue.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the common design flaw poses a high likelihood of injury if the camera falls.

incident_description: Purchased White ONN Bluetooth in-ear headphones from Walmart [REDACTED] on 3/16/20. I plugged them in on 3/15/20 to charge as usual. I left them charging for approx 2 -3 hours. When I unplugged them I noticed they were unusually hot. At that time I didn't inspect them, I just left them to lay on my nightstand. That evening when I got in bed, I tried to connect them to my phone by pressing the power button. I was having a difficult time doing so, so I turned on my lamp for more light and saw how melted they were.
justification: The headphones overheating and melting, though not causing injury, indicates a potential safety issue (severity level 2). The likelihood of this occurring is possible, given the user's description of leaving them to charge for an extended period.

incident_description: We got this baby monitor as a gift. We have been using it for 8 months and it worked well. Tonight after we put my daughter in her crib we turned on the monitor and it started acting funny. The screen was really hard to see and the lights at the top were flashing. We turned it off and back on thinking that maybe the signal was bad. When we turned the screen on again it was completely blacked out. My husband went up to check the camera, as soon as he opened the bedroom door he said it smelt like something was burning. The camera was HOT and had MELTED at the connection plug. This all happened within 5 minutes. I am so thankful this didn't happen in the middle of the night. I am sick to my stomach thinking about what could've happened.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the melted camera posed a potential fire hazard, making it an incident with possible future recurrence.

incident_description: I purchased a MoKo Xbox One Battery Packs Rechargeable 2 x 1200mAh Controller Charge Power Kit for Xbox One/One S/One X/One Elite Controllers with USB Charging Cable - White on 12/282017 through Amazon.  On Monday night 3/30/2020 about 10:30 pm there was a strong electronic smell and some smoke in our house and we called the fire department. There was concern it was an electrical issue in the walls but there was nothing found. An examination of the furnace and motor also revealed no problems. On Tuesday afternoon 3/31/2020 I found that the battery which was connected to the charger and the xBox device had melted down, destroying the battery and damaging the charger. This was the cause of the electric burning smell and smoke we discovered the night before. The charger had always been a problem as only one of the charging ports was really usable for charging the battery.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and while it's possible for such issues to occur, it's not a common event.

incident_description:
My wife uses an Apple charging cable to charge her Apple iPhone.   When the charging cable is not in use, she leaves it plugged in to the Apple power block with the unterminated lightning connector under her pillow.

On the morning of April 7, she reported to me that her phone wasn't charging well and that it connected and disconnected repeatedly during the night.

I examined the charging port of the phone, cleaning out any dust that was present and asked her to try it again in the evening.

When we retired to our bed at about 9:30pm, she reached under her pillow and reported that the bedding was hot.  When she removed the pillow, we discovered the charging cable had a burned end, and had burned through the pillowcase, into the pillow, through the bed sheet and mattress topper, and had started burning and discoloring the mattress.  There was no smoke, but fabrics had burned through.

It is my belief that had we not returned when we did, that the mattress would have been penetrated and an open flame and accelerated fire would have occurred, causing extensive damage to my house and threatened the lives of my family and myself.

I have photographs and can supply them as needed.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident could have escalated to a severe fire, causing significant property damage and threatening lives.

incident_description:
I have a Pen+Gear 10 sheet paper shredder.   When left on automatic the shredder will run without any paper in it. It will run until it is manually shut off.  The printer gets hot and this is not safe.  Unless I unplug it will continue to run.  I have reached out to the company with no replacement.  I am afraid a fire may happen.
Model # C206C
Serial Number # 201908000222
Purchased from Walmart
justification: The shredder's continuous operation without paper can cause overheating, posing a fire risk.

incident_description: Fire hazard. Battery bulged in Microsoft Surface book. This is the second one in 4 years. Microsoft exchanged the first one under warranty, after sending me a special fire-retardant box to ship it back to them by ground, 2 years ago. The replacement recently experienced the same condition. Microsoft mentioned a recall and was going to send me an exchange unit, but reneged and would only offer a similar vintage computer for a $600 fee, with 90 days warranty. Microsoft Surface Book serial number 012019161257.
justification: Although no injury has occurred, the repeated fire hazard poses a significant risk.

incident_description: On March 21, 2020 a battery pack manufactured by Shen Zhen DNS Industries Co. LTD. overheated during charging inside of a vehicle and caught fire.  The battery pack sells at Walmart as a Battery Pack, Dual USB, SLim Design with no branding.  It is rated as 5000mAh battery capacity for charging [REDACTED], and USB Devices.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage (vehicle fire) but no injuries, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' level 2 severity. The likelihood is 'possible' as battery overheating during charging can occur but is not common.

incident_description:
The Microsoft Surface Pro 3 that I purchased had a manufacturing design flaw that caused the battery to overheat and swell in size.  So much so that it pushed the screen off of the devices frame.  This has happened to many consumers purchasing this product.  Examples can be found on Microsoft forums here:  [REDACTED]

My complaint written on the forum:  My Surface Pro 3 bought in 2015 was OK for around 12 months - then the fan started to make a loud noise like there was a hornet trapped in the machine.  This noise comes and goes and will always be triggered if I change the orientation of the device.  For a device that is supposed to be mobile this is terrible design.  Now the screen is actually separating from the device and I have discoloration (yellow streaks) at the bottom of the screen.  The screen is being held in place with scotch tape. This device has spent 99% of its life just sitting on the top of my desk and has never been bent or experienced any rough treatment.  I called MSFT and the best offer is to charge me $600 for a [REDACTED].  In addition I called the local store and they admitted that my configuration with processor & chip had overheating issued in 40-50% of the devices.  I am very unhappy with the durability of the device.  I feel like MSFT sold me a lemon and that they admit/know they sold me a lemon but are unwilling to replace it.  Called the Microsoft Baybrook store and spoke with [REDACTED] - he said there is a well known issue with overheating and the i7 chip in the Surface Pro 3 "definitley had a heating issue" he estimates that 40-50% of the units had the issue.  He said I could call the 800 642 7676 number and ask them to escalate the issue to Level 2 or ask to talk to a manager to see if they could give me a better offer than the store.  He said they could offer me a[REDACTED] for $600, it would be refurbished and only have a 90 day warranty.  Refurbished might just be a return or cracked screen but it would be refurbished by a MSFT approved service.  

Another Example in the Microsoft forum: I took mine into the Microsoft Store where I bought it two years ago.  The tech looked at it, said, "You've got burn-in, huh?" and immediately went in back for a replacement.  When she detached the screen from the keyboard and put it down, I noticed it didn't lie flat, and the screen was bulging.  She said the battery was expanding, and it was imperative to replace it - it could be dangerous. She transferred everything she could to the new computer, took the old one and didn't charge me anything.  (I still have to deal with reinstalling all my programs, but at least the machine isn't about to explode!)
justification: Battery overheating and swelling, pushing the screen off, with multiple reported cases and admission of issues by Microsoft.

incident_description: On 3-2-20, our insured [REDACTED] plugged his HP Pavillion Laptop Charger into a receptacle prior to going to bed.  Approximately 15-20 minutes later he heard a loud noise downstairs and through someone was trying to break into his house.  As he descended down the stairwell, he observed what appeared to be smoke coming from the den area which is the room they'd just left for bed and where the laptop was located.  As he got to the bottom of the steps, the smoke detector started going off.  When he entered the den area, he noticed a strong "electrical" type smell/odor and fire coming from the bottom bookcase where the laptop was left charging.  The fire was small and confined to the bookcase.  He grabbed a fire extinguisher and was able to extinguish the fire.  He reported the fire to the [REDACTED] Fire Dept. and they came out to ensure everything was extinguished.  A report was prepared.  He contacted his Home Owner's Insurance Carrier, [REDACTED] to report a claim.  After the First Notice of Loss was prepared and it was assigned to an Adjuster, the Adjuster contacted Sr. Special Investigator [REDACTED] who works that County.  Origin and Cause (O&C) Inspections were conducted on March 5th and the 10th.  We determined the Cause of the Fire to be a sudden explosion of the lithium batteries.  The battery was a replacement purchased on [REDACTED] and not an HP battery.  The battery was purchased on November 28, 2018, Brand: Bull-Tech K104 replacement.  It appears Bull-Tech is located in Henan, China and sells products via 3rd party platforms [REDACTED] and [REDACTED].  We currently have reserves set at $80k for repairs, cleaning and restoration activities.
justification: The fire was small, contained, and extinguished without injuries, but the likelihood of a similar event occurring with non-OEM batteries is possible.

incident_description: Purchased Aukey 30,000 mAH power bank from Amazon. Upon receiving it today I noticed it had no charge at all. Most li-ion batteryÃÂs are shipped with 80% charge. Upon plugging it into wall adaptor with supplied Aukey usb cable it immediately started smelling of a solvent / peach smelling- smell. The unit got very hot so I moved it outside. I have contacted Aukey and since this unit was already a replacement for another non working unit ( same model) I thought I better let someone know.
justification: Potential fire hazard due to overheating, but no injuries reported.

incident_description: I bought a personal gps tracker with chargeable lithium battery for my autistic son in case he got lost. It was plugged in to charge and burned up hje battery caught fire and destroyed the charger and tracker. It burned my finger and hardwood floor. I wrapped it in my shirt and threw it outside. It burned my shirt, too. If i was not home my house and son would have been in worse trouble.
justification: Injury occurred (burned finger) and property damage (floor, charger, tracker, shirt) due to a battery fire, which could have been worse if not at home.

incident_description: Easy Home Fabric extension cord,  9ft.  I tried to use this extension cord on a night light. When I plugged the night light in, it did not light, I touched the cord and the light lighted. I touched it again and the light went out. It went off and on buy itself. I could hear an arcing. This cord could start a fire..I unplugged the night light and will not use the cord again.
justification: The extension cord exhibited electrical arcing, posing a high risk of fire, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: Purchased a set of Galaxy Buds manufactured by Samsung to listen to my TV using a bluetooth connection. Upon 1st use, the volume of the ear buds was way too high. Upon contacting Samsung to determine how to lower the volume, I was told that volume control was an option in the settings which cannot be accessed/changed by installing an app on an Android cell phone. I do not have an Andriod cell phone, so my only option is to use the buds at the factory setting which is way too loud and I fear damaging my hearing. Samsung will not resolve what I consider a design problem and safety concern. After contacting Samsung the 1st time, they indicated it would be forwarded. Upon the second contact , I discovered they closed the incident report without informing me. Also the Chat discussion was supposed to be emailed to me each time, but it never arrives. Upon that complaint, I was told they could not send me a copy as it was part of the system. I feel they stopped the email so I did not have evidence of their response.
justification: While no injury has occurred yet, the high volume setting poses a potential hearing damage risk, making it an incident with possible future injury.

incident_description:
Loud noise was emitting from the laptop charger.  I reached down and the charger was very hot. At the same time my keyboard connected to the same power strip was blinking and would not function.  I removed the charger and replaced with the original Mac one and the keyboard worked fine.  I suspect that this charger has damaged a light and mouse connected through the same power strip.  

Other consumers indicated that this charger was hot and may cause a fire: [REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in no injuries but caused equipment malfunction, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence and potential for more severe consequences.

incident_description: Apple TV Remote Control - the top piece is made of unprotected glass and it shatters when dropped. My friends kid dropped the remote and put it in his mouth, making his lips bleed, he could have swallowed glass, I took it out and the shattered glass surface has cut my fingers and small glass shards fell off and stuck in my fingers.
justification: The remote's glass top shattered upon impact, causing injury to the child's mouth and fingers, and posing a risk of ingestion.

incident_description:
Caller stated that she fell asleep while the phone was charging, she was awakened by a burning sensation on her breast.  She stated that the cell phone overheated and seems as if it opened up.  She stated that the back part seems as it was starting to melt.  Caller stated that she was seen by her dermatologist who advised her how to treat the burn. 

Caller return the phone to the provider  but has photos of the incident.

Caller feels that this cell phone is a fire hazard and should be reported.
justification: Injury occurred due to phone overheating, likelihood is possible given the reported incident and lack of widespread reports.

incident_description:
I Purchase an Amazon Echo Dot with Clock (SKU: 810014301563, S/N: G0914704007503GH) recently. 
 have had this item for a few weeks plugged into a stereo receiver to provide better audio via the 1/8" Audio jack.  Today I touched the front panel of the receiver and it felt like I received an AC shock.  I used a [REDACTED] multi-meter to measure the AC voltage between the receiver chassis and ground and found that I had 63 VAC at the receiver chassis.  I then worked through all of my devices and eliminated them one by one until I finally unplugged the power supply for the Echo Dot with Clock.  The hazardous voltage went away.  I unplugged the power supply from the Echo Dot and measured from the outside of the coaxial power plug to safety ground with my meter.  I measured 11 VAC in one direction and when I flipped the power supply around (It does not have a polarized plug) it measured 96 VAC.  Either of these is enough to stop a human heart.  The issue has been reported to Amazon but they did not seem to understand the gravity of the situation - may have been lost in translation.  I work in the electronics industry so I am very aware of proper electrical safety and testing protocols.  The power supply did not have any DC continuity between the prongs and the barrel of the coaxial jack so there must be DC blocking caps - but line voltage is definitely being passed from one of the prongs to the barrel of the DC plug.  Touching this barrel while plugged in is an extreme hazard.  When plugged into the echo this can only be accessed by plugging in an audio accessory to the 1/8" jack but this is still an extreme hazard.
justification: The incident resulted in an electrical shock with hazardous voltage levels, posing a high likelihood of injury.

incident_description: I just learned about the recall to fix the Visio model T4 20 I IÃÂve had a tip over many times unfortunately this last time it fell over and it shattered the screen I would like to get a replacement if possible
justification: The incident resulted in property damage (shattered screen) but no injuries, and while it's possible for this to happen again, it's not likely to occur frequently.

incident_description: Laptop, continuously plugged into AC home electrical supply.  Never used as a portable device.  Now approaching five years of use when I noticed the battery bulging enough to dislodge the products back cover.  My concern is for fire potential.
justification: Potential fire risk due to battery bulging, though no immediate danger or injury reported.

incident_description: I was home with my girlfriend, when she smelled smoke. I went upstairs to find my bluetooth speaker was very hot and smoking profusedly. At the time it had been plugged in for approximately an hour to the charger supplied by the manufacturer. I unplugged the speaker and ran with it downstairs, and put it outside. The speaker got hot enough to melt the polyurathane coating on my wood floor. I reported the issue to the manufacturer the following morning. I brought the speaker and charger to my work the next day so that I could document the issue and sent that info to the manufacturer. I requested that they inspect the unit with me, so far they have declined to do so. In the pictures I am submitting you can observe the swelling of the unit near the battery, the polyurathane melted to the unit's base, and the damage done to the floor. Thermal damage to the unit is also visible. It is my belief that in unplugging and removing the unit I was able to avoid a much more damaging and dangerous situation.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident could have escalated into a more severe situation due to the speaker overheating and causing thermal damage.

incident_description:
Our business has been replacing expanded batteries at our own cost in our HP EliteBook laptops that have become rather dangerous after a year (after their warranty expired). When we contact HP, usually they say these batteries are not covered in the 2018 Recall, but the batteries exhibit the same symptoms: expanding over time, causing damage to the computer case, and most importantly in the AMD laptops, causing the computer to become so hot it can be dangerous to touch (especially the bottom). In one laptop the bottom case had completely been separated, breaking the bottom plastics. All of these batteries are the same base model, CS03XL.

I'd also like to note that HP has relatively recently released BIOS updates to these laptops which try to address these expanding batteries, so they do acknowledge it can happen in many more models than what's listed in the 2018 recall.
justification: Batteries expanding and causing damage, with potential for burns due to overheating, but no reported injuries.

incident_description:
HP recently recalled 80,000 laptops for possible battery explosions. 

HP laptop model Stream  was included in the recall but when I contacted HP, they said my serial number was not included.  I have HP model Stream HP-y010wm.  My laptop serial number is 5CD631519OT.  My HP case number is [REDACTED].

My laptop is all distorted from the battery slowly exploding. HP is impossible to contact support or anyone willing to help any further, they take my telephone number but do not call back.  My last call with them, after 30 minutes of insisting I talk with someone, I asked to be connected directly to a case manager..after 40 minutes on hold, I hung up.

If 80,000 laptop batteries were recalled, including my exact model...and my particular serial number was not included, and my laptop front keyboard is blowing up like a bubble, cracking the case...than the RECALL WAS NOT EXTENSIVE ENOUGH.
justification: Although the user's specific serial number was not included in the recall, the incident of the laptop battery exploding indicates a potential safety hazard, warranting a higher likelihood rating.

incident_description: I purchased an HP Spectre x360 laptop approximately 4 years ago.  Last year, I noticed my laptop was bulging out from the top and bottom where the internal battery is located.  When researching online, I found numerous similar complaints about swollen batteries on their HP support community website.  I called HP about the issue, however, because the laptop is past the warranty date, they wouldn't offer any support.  I also checked whether my battery is on the HP battery recall list, but found it wasn't.  The battery swelling has become progressively worse and I'm concerned that the battery might explode or catch fire.
justification: While no immediate danger is reported, the progressive battery swelling increases the likelihood of an explosion or fire, posing a potential incident risk.

incident_description:
I put 4 rechargeable batteries in the charger, the red light came on per usual. After about 20 minutes I noticed a strong odor like hot wring can make, I picked up the charger , it was almost too hot to hold.

I tried to contact the manufacturer however they never bothered to return my phone call

If I hadn't been home this would have caused a serious fire
justification: The incident involved a potential fire hazard, which could have caused property damage but no injuries, given the likelihood of the charger overheating was high.

incident_description: We have had several Lenovo T460S laptops where the battery has gotten extremely hot and has swollen almost to the point of exploding. We have replaced the batteries an a few of them under warranty with Lenovo and continue to experience the issue. This is certainly a fire hazard.
justification: The incident has occurred multiple times despite battery replacements, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence and posing a significant fire hazard.

incident_description:
The consumer indicates that her daughter was charging her cell phone for approximately thirty minutes when the micro USB charging wire it was connected to caught on fire. The consumerÃÂs daughter heard popping sounds and saw sparks flying. As soon as the surge protector the unit was plugged into popped, the fire ceased.

The consumer notes that the micro USB charging wire has a three centimeter burn area, and the surge protector and charging base the unit was connected to were partially blackened from the fire. 

The consumer contacted the retailer and explained the situation; the representative she spoke to informed her that the Manager would call her back however she has yet to hear back from them.

The consumer states that the unit was used daily for approximately two hours.

The consumer plans on keeping her unit for at least the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.
justification: No injuries were reported, but the incident involved a fire, making it an incident with no injury.

incident_description:
Plugged a usb charger cable into phone and 4-port usb quick charge. sku: 13400

Looked up after about 5 min. to see a thin trail of smoke coming from the cable on the cell phone side.  Only 3-4 ft. away, I grabbed cable and small yellow flame appeared.  Put it back down to smother flame.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the incident involved a fire, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' case. The likelihood is 'possible' as it's not a common occurrence but could happen under certain conditions.

incident_description: Purchased Silverstone Fan Hub LSB02-E, I was going to use this for some Lighting components on my pc and I plugged the stuff in like manual shows and the wiring on the ARGB 5V component started to  smoke so I turned off my computer unplugged everything and removed the smoking component connector. No injury occured.
justification: While no injury occurred, the incident involved a component smoking, indicating a potential fire hazard, thus severity level 2.

incident_description: On October 27th 2019. My galaxy note 4 exploded.  In my living room. Causing burning do my carpet and smoke damage to my electronics. I took samsung to court to get compensation for my belongings and it results that the battery was a recalled boot legged battery supplies by  fed ex.  I am looking to have fed ex supply chain contact me as their info listed on here is no longer valid
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no physical injuries, and the likelihood of a similar incident occurring with a recalled bootlegged battery is possible.

incident_description: I have the Microsoft Surface Book and there are yellow tints surrounding the left top and right sides of the screen.  The screen has a bulge and was taken to the Microsoft Store.  The battery is expanding which is causing the bulge and can explode at any moment.  They told me that the computer is hazardous and will not replace or refund the product.  The laptop can cause injuries and that I am not to use it.  Others that had the same product was issued a free replacement and they have refused to do so with me
justification: The battery expansion and potential explosion pose a high risk of injury.

incident_description: Good Morning, Last year my ex-girlfriend purchased me a Spansive Source wireless multi-phone charger for my birthday. About two weeks ago I had 3 devices on the charger, one of which was charging via usb port and the other two ([REDACTED]) via wireless. I kept this unit bedside of me when I heard my smoke detectors going off, I woke up in a panic thinking i left my oven on because I made dinner just hours early. After running around the house trying to find the source I ran back in the bedroom to realize that I ran right past the source. It was the wireless charger that had black smoke coming from the bottom of the unit. I immediately unplugged the unit and the usb that was connecting my [REDACTED] watch. As I went to take the two [REDACTED] off the unit I immediately had to retract my hand back off of the phones due to the screen singeing my thumb. I then quickly grabbed a shirt off the floor in order to be able to take the phones off the charger and tossed the smoking charging unit out the window due to the excessive smoke coming from it. It was insane and scary as heck! I put the phones in the freezer and after 15 minutes was able to take them out and luckily they were still function. As far as my thumb, not so much. Its finally just healing. After doing quite a bit of research online about why this would happen or how, I stumbled across a link from the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. Stating that there was a recall on certain units, in which mine of course either my luck, or my ex was just trying to kill me just so happen to be one of those units. The unit has/had exactly what is pictured in the CPSC website with a green peel sticker on the bottom of the unit. What mine says I am not quiet sure because it had so much soot on it from the smoke pouring out of it.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor burn injury to the user's thumb, and the charger posed a significant fire risk.

incident_description: I woke up this morning to the sound of popping as the power bank exploded across the bedroom. It was already engulfed in flames.
justification: The incident involved a power bank explosion and fire, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: I plugged the power strip into a wall outlet and turned it on with no appliances plugged into it. This tripped the breaker, which I reset. When I tried it in a different outlet, the device made a loud popping noise, sparked, and the case was opened by the force of the damage. There was a burning odor and brown smoke/residue on the device and on the counter where it sat. There are reports dating at least back to 2017 that similar incidents occured according to reviews left on the Amazon website.
justification: The incident caused property damage and could have led to fire, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
Had a Huawei Honor 7x for under 3 years, less time than my original mobile phone, before it combusted due to the battery.

A few (barely 2 at most) days ago, noticed the lid wasn't snapping in place and don't remember dropping it.

Today, suspected the battery may be bloated and that it was a danger.
Opened the thing just enough to see the battery and to feel it. the wrapping over the battery had trapped "air". not a good sign. The battery itself was relatively flat still.

Closed it up again with the same gap still there as before.. and smoke came out a little, which followed a display of.. fireworks.. as it charred the chair it was set on too. Apparently the trapped air was maybe gas buildup and the battery could've detonated anytime. Another family member barely got a metallic can, but not in time to toss the phone into. It was used to cover up the phone to deprive it of oxygen to burn.

The phone could have well went off while it was under my pillow or in my hand...
justification: Battery explosion caused minor injury and property damage, and could have resulted in severe harm if phone was in use or near person.

incident_description:
Investigated a fire in a detached garage adjacent to a single family dwelling.  Fire originates near a 2007 [REDACTED] that was last run in November of 2019.  The motorcycle's battery was attached to a 12 volt float charger plugged into an extension cord (appears to be an appropriate gauge) and into an outlet.  The motorcycle has been plugged in since November when it was parked. Interviews with the owner indicate that the battery was still attached to the vehicle.  The battery tender was purchased at rural king and identified by the owner as Model # BMFC12V (SKU: 210400522).  
After investigating and ruling out other potential sources of ignition, the battery charger is my ignition source for this fire.  

Link to Rural King Item:
https://www.ruralking.com/battery-maintn-float-charger-12v
justification: The fire was contained to the garage, causing property damage but no injuries.

incident_description: tried to turn laptop on it started smoking took it outside and it smoldered for 15 mins
justification: The laptop starting to smoke and smoldering for 15 minutes indicates a significant incident, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: Faulty item is a green extension cord that is designed for Christmas tree lights.  It has multiple sockets along its length and a single-pole switch.  The product deficiency is its plug.  The plug is encased in a plastic housing.  I pulled the plug from the wall socket and the slight friction of the plug blades in that socket caused one of the 2 plug blades to separate from the plug and remain in the wall socket; sticking out about one-half inch and posing a danger to anyone reflexively pulling on that blade to remove it from the wall socket. The cord has the words "Ting Shen TS-10A" stamped on the cord plug housing.
justification: Potential for injury due to exposed electrical contact in the wall socket, but no immediate harm reported.

incident_description:
We purchased an LG "XCharge" SP320 cell phone in April 2018. In November 2019 we discovered that the cell phone had swollen due to expansion of the (non-removable) Li-ion battery. 
The device case is swollen to 13.3 mm thick at max, asymmetric; the screen is convexed out slightly, also. Thickness specification is 8.4 mm. We are very concerned about potential fire/explosion. 

Device has been used in airplane mode on wifi as continuous monitor screen for front-door camera. We have, in our home, multiple other devices with Li batteries that are kept constantly plugged in to chargers. This includes 2 [REDACTED], 3 laptop, 4 [REDACTED], 2[REDACTED], & 1 [REDACTED] from [REDACTED]. The oldest are from 2006. All obviously have well-designed supervisory circuits that avoid overcharging, and have never swollen. This LG cell phone apparently has an unsafe charge supervisory circuit.

LG, the manufacturer denies responsibility as they have only one-year warranty. Yet other phone makers, including [REDACTED and [REDACTED, have several times extended specific warranties due to the inherent danger of explosion and fire. LG suggests sending it to them for repair, but I can not trust this dangerous condition to not recur. Also, please note that a second LG device (a "Stylo4", LGQ710) is also showing signs of swelling, causing us to disconnect all LGs from charging at all from now on.
justification: Potential fire/explosion hazard due to battery swelling, despite no immediate injuries.

incident_description: I investigated a fire at an occupied apartment of a multi-apartment building.  The Cause of the fire was discovered as a failure of a surge protector outlet strip. None of them have resulted in dell taking any report of the defect nor any resolution. incident_description: On 04/18/2019, I purchased a pair of 1More triple driver in-ear earphones through Amazon.com. The earphones worked properly until August 2019, when the right side began sending shocks into my ear canal. It was extremely painful, and I immediately stopped using the earphones. incident_description: The following complaint against Golf Cart King & their Modz Maxx brand battery charger is on the grounds that this charger is unsafe for the end user, in addition to the fact that there are false claims on performance/efficiency, and insufficient information regarding what battery types can be charged. I also can find no record of it being in compliance with Department of Energy Battery Charger Efficiency Guidelines. The charger lists on itÃÂs main label an efficiency of >93%. This charger is sold on Amazon.com and the Golf Cart King website alongside other ÃÂintelligentÃÂ chargers that actually do contain charge algorithms custom tailored to the battery application that end user will encounter with their golf carts. These other chargers can be found on the DOE public database listings for their energy consumption and efficiency with regard to specific battery applications. The Golf Cart King / Modz Maxx charger cannot be found on the DOE public database, it is not safe and can cause physical harm to the consumer, in addition to potentially damaging their equipment.
justification: Exposed fan blades pose a high likelihood of injury to users.

incident_description:

incident_description:

incident_description: I purchased a 30,000 mAh lithium-ion portable battery bank called the Zerolemon Tough in Dec. 2018 off Amazon that is advertised as drop/shock-resistant. On 11-24-2019, after charging the power bank to 100% the device spontaneously combusted into flames in my bedroom after being dropped from a height of less than 3 ft on to a carpeted floor. The device intitially spewed electrical smoke for 10-15 seconds and then burst into flames quickly thereafter. Luckily I was able to throw the burning battery pack onto my concrete porch and let it burn itself out safely. There are numerous other reports on Amazon of similar incidents occurring to other customers, sometimes causing burns to skin or property. I believe these devices are extremely dangerous and likely faulty in nature. The device in question can be found for sale here: https://www.amazon.com/ZeroLemon-30000mAh-External-Capacity-Portable/dp/B071DV6WS8/ref=cm_cr_arp_d_product_top?ie=UTF8.

incident_description: I purchased 2 of the PBS playtime tablet November 2018 as a gift for my children. I called again on November 21st again and received the same response. We have removed the tablet from our home but feel like this product in the hands of young children is unsafe .

incident_description:

incident_description:
I purchased Aero Sport "True Wireless Earbuds"  from Five and Below in Willow Grove,PA  on Friday, October 4th. 

We got home and plugged the new air buds in to charge (connecting the ear buds and wire and then hooking into the power source). Approx 10 mins after we plugged these in -- I started to smell smoke.  I looked around and I immediately saw the bright orange  embers on the wire and quickly tried to disengage the wire from the power source ÃÂ-  burning my fingers in the process :(. incident_description:
On August 15, 2019 I had a lithium-ion battery pack explode while in the charger which subsequently caught my house on fire. The battery exploded into a number of individual cells which continued to explode one-by-one starting several separate fires in my garage. It took two full fire extinguishers to put out the multiple fires over the course of 10 to 15 minutes . The battery pack had just been purchased from Amazon.com and installed into the charger about 6:30 pm on 09/14/2019. The battery pack exploded at 10:30 am the next morning 09/15/2019. The battery pack was an after-market direct replacement for a [REDACTED] cordless drill and sold as such. The battery pack was manufactured in China.  I had fire damage and some property damage to my garage. If my wife and I had not been home at the time, or had the battery exploded during the middle of the night while we were sleeping the entire house would have gone up in flames. It was very fortunate that we heard the explosion and that I had two fire extinguishers ready nearby to quickly put out the multiple fires. IÃÂm also lucky that I was not seriously injured while doing that since I only had shorts and sandals on at the time. I only sustained small burns on one toe and the top of my left foot where I came into contact with some of the hot metal or plastic while extinguishing the fires.  There were lithium-ion cells still exploding while I was trying to extinguish the flames.  I reported the incident to AmazonÃÂs customer service department shortly after the fire that same morning and they immediately removed the product for sale from their online store and refunded my purchase, but thatÃÂs all they would do. IÃÂve spent almost three hours on the phone during 3 separate calls and have been given different instructions and responses each time. In the end I received an email from AmazonÃÂs Executive Customer Relations department stating that Amazon takes no responsibility for any damages or losses caused by merchants selling through the Amazon marketplace...and that I could contact the merchant in China (through their merchant link) if I wanted to pursue the issue further with them.

One more thing - there have been a number of incidents of lithium-ion battery fires aboard commercial and package carrier aircraft, IÃÂd like to see some regulation against Amazon (and other online only retailers) to force them to take liability for selling counterfeit and poor-quality after-market products through their online store. If I had purchased an OEM battery from a brick-and-mortar store or directly from the OEM (even if the OEM product was manufactured in China) both companies would be liable for the damage and losses caused by their product. Why does Amazon get a free pass on incurring any liability for the products that they sell? That regulation needs to be changed.
justification: Injury occurred due to direct contact with hot debris while extinguishing fires, and multiple explosions indicate high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
The wireless keyboard goes to hp g142, 24 in all in one computer
When I was using the wireless keyboard on Friday August 30, 2019 there was a burning on my arm. My arm was in back of the keyboard. When I looked at my arm , there was a blaster. The wireless keyboard transmitter burned my arm.
Serveral days later the skin bubbled up.

incident_description: I used the heyday usb cord to charge my [REDACTED]. It gave me a 2nd degree burn on my leg.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (2nd degree burn), but it's unlikely to occur again due to the unusual use of a USB cord for charging.

incident_description:
I bought 2 ea. 5V 2.5A Rhino wall power adapters to supply a micro-computer ([REDACTED]) . On both adapters the
5V outputs are not floating, They have 40V to 60V AC superimposed. Connecting the (-) terminal of the power
supply to real ground with 1kOhm made the resistor smoke, so there is not just static or a high impedance path.
When I first hooked up the power supply I got severely shocked and holding the connector (Mini-USB) to a known
grounded USB port it sparked heavily. It also damaged my entertainment system. By profession I am a physicist and
have a lot of experience with electronics. If someone uses these power supplies with toys it may be very dangerous.
I am willing to send the objects in for evaluation.
justification: The incident caused injury to the user and potential danger to others, given the widespread use of similar adapters with toys.

incident_description: Had speaker with them while on vacation in a cabin in PA.  Speaker was charged night before and placed on a shelf.  The charging cord was not plugged into speaker at time of incident.  Female consumer left cabin for lunch.  Returned and smoke detector was activated and saw flames coming from speaker.  Grabbed a towel and carried it outside. Cabin suffered approximately $1,200.00 damage. No injuries.
justification: The speaker caught fire due to improper charging, leading to property damage but no injuries.

incident_description: This computer is home use only and is damaged beyond repair since the body of the computer is warped and it will no longer close due to the heat from the battery.  Upon inspection, battery is puffed out.  Monitor part of the lap seems to be ok.
justification: The incident resulted in damage to the computer but no injuries, and it's possible that similar incidents could occur due to battery issues.

incident_description: My wife and I were leaving the gym after a workout / swim late in the afternoon, I had a newly purchased Duracell 6ft USB Type C charging / data cable was connected to my cars 12V power port, or for the older generations, cigarette lighter socket.  As soon as we started the car, the small end of the cable started smoking and burst into flames. We ripped the charger, and chable out of the car and threw it out the door to the parking lot where we were.   We had purchased this particular cable just prior to going to the gym / pool.

incident_description: Earbuds are stored in a small unit that also serves as a battery charger.  Yesterday while recharging ear buds I picked up case and literally burnt my hand as the case had overheated.  I know if I didn't check it when I did it would of probably caught fire.

incident_description:
The consumer indicates that she had been using her home shredder the day of the incident on and off in the morning. The consumer went to use the unit again and so she plugged it in. When the consumer went to feed the shredder, it blew up on her. The consumer sustained injuries to her right arm, her face, and her head; her lashes, nasal hairs, and eyebrows were singed.

The consumer went to the Emergency Room and was treated for all her burn injuries; she was also prescribed ointment and pain pills.

The consumer states that she used the unit once or twice per year.

The consumer plans on keeping her home shredder for at least the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries to the consumer, making it a '3' on the severity scale. The likelihood is '4' as the consumer uses the shredder regularly and the incident occurred during normal usage.

incident_description:
On Jun 2nd, 2019 the battery in my son's LG K20 ( Model Number LGM255) cell phone came close to exploding / burning. He was sleeping with it about a foot from his head (he does because the alarm volume was not
sufficient to wake him from the nightstand), when he woke up to a phone that had burst open and was glowing bright red, emitting smoke. As he called out to me, the fire alarm began sounding and woke me. I rushed to his room to find it full of smoke and was able to scoop the phone onto a plate and rush it outdoors before it fully exploded. I then submerged it in water to cool it down. By the appearance, it looks like we caught it just before it burst. We were lucky it did not explode in his face. The phone briefly ignited his bedding and mattress. I do have photos of the phone and damage.  I have reported this to LG, but they are stonewalling me.

The phone was purchased in Nov/Dec of 2017 as a Christmas present. The phone was not plugged in to charge at the time it burst. It has always been in a case and he had not dropped it at any point. This is the original battery. There is no way his actions could have caused a puncture of the battery which would lead to this reaction.

This phone was only about a 1 & 1/2 years old. I cannot find any information about this happening in other K20s, but needed to let you know in case there are other occurrences. This phone is just out of warranty, but I feel that this damage is due to an obvious defect in the battery.
justification: The incident resulted in potential injury (smoke inhalation, fire) and property damage (bedding, mattress), but no physical harm was confirmed.

incident_description: My Samsung s6 phone over heats while in use or connected to the charger,this over heating has caused the screen to discolor I notified the company and was told nothing can be done however I read an article of several individuals with the same problem.
justification: Multiple users have reported the same issue, indicating a high likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description: Toshiba laptop was on back of couch turned off after use. Made a load popping sound and caught on fire. I knocked it off the couch and ran it to sink. Put fire out on couch. Thought fire was out on laptop in sink when exploded again catching it on fire. Threw wet towel over it and took it out side. Couch has a big burn hole on it and my laptop is ruined.

incident_description: 8 Batteries were installed in multiple burglar alarm sensors, an additional box was opened and 2 were installed in glass break sensors with only battery power. After being installed in the glass break sensor, the installer went to place additional batteries into from the same box into other sensors.  He then heard a loud crack and found flames shooting from one of the devices, the device fell to the floor and the battery shot around the room spitting fire.  It was quickly covered with a wet towel to extinguish the burning battery. As this was taking place a smoke detector in another room began sounding. When it was investigated a device with just installed battery had fire coming from the device as well.
justification: Injury occurred due to fire from faulty batteries, and likelihood is high as multiple devices were affected.

incident_description:
The product is a plug-in electrical power strip. 

While using this product, I received a shock from the equipment I plugged in to it. 

When I checked the plug polarity with a digital multimeter, I confirmed that the plug polarity is reversed. 

(According to US standards, only one certain prong of a plug is supposed to be used for the "grounded" conductor. This product's wiring and plug polarity is reversed, so that the "grounded" prong is crossed to the "non-grounded" wire, and vice-versa.)
justification: The reversed plug polarity poses a high likelihood of electrical shock, as evidenced by the user's experience.

incident_description: The laptop battery exploded while charging and put the laptop on fire. Fire restarted a couple of times after attempting to put it off. Fire caught the bed cover and the carpet and burned part of the wooden floor. The laptop battery melted and came off, the laptop got burnt and is completely damaged. This put my self and my family in great danger and jeapordized all our home possessions.

When he went into the shop, he found the battery charging area on fire and an exploded battery. He quickly grabbed an extinguisher on the wall and put out the fire.

incident_description:
While we were away, the surge protector, Supco SCM 150, connected to an air conditioner unit caught a fire. A section of the siding was burnt and the surge protector was badly damaged. At first, I thought my house was hit by lightning. After a short search through internet, I learned that  the surge protector was prone to overheat and catch a fire.  In fact, it was recalled by the manufacturer, Supco, this year. My air conditioners were installed in 2011 and 2014 by a local HVAC company in Powhatan, VA. Both of them have Supco SCM 150 attached.  I never received any recall notice although there was a recall letter sent by Supco to the local HVAC company.  I think it is the HVAC company's responsibility to inform me of the recall as we, the consumers, do not normally know what kind of surge protectors installed. In addition, Supco would not know we have the recalled product and they would not have a way to communicate with us.  

When I called the HVAC company, I was told that they would only replace the recalled products for those customers who have the maintenance contract with them.  What about the rest of the consumers who DO NOT have the maintenance contract with them?  The HVAC company personnel said that they would not know who they installed the Supco surge protector to. He admitted that the company received the recall letter.  However, they did nothing to inform the customers. I even told him that they could've sent us an e-mail notification to check the model of the surge protector. He didn't seem to take any responsibilities. In the end, I was told to contact Supco directly about the faulty product.  I am lucky that my house wasn't totally burnt down and I will be replacing the faulty surge protectors. I am very concerned that there may be many innocent consumers who are not aware of this dangerous surge protector attached on their air conditioners.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and the likelihood of similar incidents occurring is high given the widespread use of the recalled surge protectors.

incident_description: We purchased a Xtreme Cables 3' flowfx micro USB phone charger from Menards today. We plugged it in this evening to a USB port in the couch. Within 10 minutes it was giving off an odor. We unplugged immediately once we saw it smoking. Upon looking at the device itself, it was in-fact melted. There was no property damage or injury since we caught it quickly.
justification: Although no injury or property damage occurred, the incident involved a product malfunction that could have led to more severe consequences.

incident_description:
We were using a Microsoft Surface Book (model number 1703, serial Number 009526654457 purchased Dec 16, 2015 for 1699.99) when we noticed a bulging on both sides of the screen.  Online research indicated that the problem was a bulging battery inside the tablet portion of the computer.  We contacted Microsoft.  We spoke to Microsoft reps [REDACTED].  Microsoft acknowledged the problem, stating that it was a battery issue and that they were working with the battery manufacturer to fix the problem.

The advised us to stop using the device immediately because a potential fire and explosion danger.
They also offered to exchange our unit for a remanufactured one with a 90 day warranty for their standard $599. fee.

Microsoft has apparently known about this serious issue for quite a while but has chosen to not do the responsible thing and notify affected owners of the danger and offer to repair or replace the device without charging an unreasonable fee.  The computer was shipped with a defective battery.  It has posed a serious safety hazard for its users from the beginning.   Microsoft needs to take full responsibility for the problem.  It should recall the devices with the defective batteries and repair or replace them without additional charges to the purchasers.
justification: Potential fire and explosion hazard, as acknowledged by Microsoft.

incident_description:
I recieved a Monoprice Monoprice MP Select Mini 3D Printer V2, Black Product # 21711 found at https://www.monoprice.com/product?p_id=21711 as a gift for Christmas 2018. After approximately a month of use the device began to emit a rubber/plastic burning smell and a small amount of smoke. I powered the device down and found that wires from the hot bed, the heated metal plate that the printer prints onto, had worn through and shorted out due to being zip tied in place too tightly by the manufacturer with no strain relief. As a result of this the onboard computer died and the heat bed no longer heats. 
I am concerned that if I had not powered down the device when I did the insulation on the wire could have caught fire.
Monoprice customer service did not seem interested in my problem as they do not honor warranties on gifted items.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage (burnt wires, non-functional printer) and posed a potential fire hazard, but no injuries occurred.

incident_description: Computer got so hot during use it cracked the screen. There are a few different color lines across it and the entire edge all the way around is black. When you turn it on, cracks are visible through the center and off to the top RH corner where the glass is spidered
justification: The incident resulted in property damage (cracked screen) but no injuries, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' case. The likelihood is 'possible' as overheating can occur due to various factors, but it's not a common everyday occurrence.

incident_description:
Dell XPS15 model 9560 trackpad pushing up.  Found that the internal battery pack is swelling after only 2 years of use.  

Web search indicates that this is a common issue in this model, and Dell has been offering free replacements for the 9550 model for the same issue but has yet to do anything about the 9560.

Support forum discussions on this topic:
https://www.dell.com/community/XPS/Battery-swelling-in-XPS-15-9560/td-p/6226881
https://www.dell.com/community/XPS/XPS-15-9560-dead-battery/td-p/7301831
justification: The trackpad pushing up due to battery swelling is an incident, but no injuries are reported. The high likelihood is due to the commonality of this issue in the model, as evidenced by web searches and support forum discussions.

incident_description:
My phone was sitting on a wireless charger when I noticed the phone was hot, I removed it from the charger and let it cool. The following day the screen started to bulge and you can see the battery is expanding. I called Apple support and they said there was nothing they could do since the phone was one and a half years old, out of warranty. They did tell me that I could take it to Best Buy since they're a authorized repair facility and for a fee they'd replace the battery. I then made an appointment with Best Buy and at the appointment yesterday they said they wouldn't replace the battery because it's swollen.  

I'm not sure how dangerous these situations are but Apple support didn't seem to think the battery was a problem and Best Buy does? 

The iPhone battery monitor shows the battery as being good with 95% life left.
justification: While no immediate injury occurred, the swollen battery poses a potential fire hazard, hence severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 3 as such incidents, though not common, can happen due to improper charging or battery degradation.

I ran back to my room and my television had caught fire from the back where its mounted to the wall. no damage to my wall so I know its from inside the product somewhere it had malfunction internally.

A hospital visit was not needed, but it felt like I had sunburn on the tops of my legs for a few days, as they became very sensitive to wearing jeans, or anything that would rub the tops of my thighs.
justification: While the incident resulted in discomfort and sensitivity, no serious injury or medical intervention was required.

incident_description: I was plugging in a Samsung Galaxy S10 plus to charge it and dropped the charger cable. It was only a drop of about 4-5 inches, but when it hit the screen of the phone it made a loud pop and the screen chipped underneath the screen protector. I looked into this fenamena and found Samsung used a type of porcelain screen on its earlier S10plus phone's. After learning several customers had weird experiences with screens chipping and exploding from minor impacts Samsung went back to a plastic screen they previously used. They refuse to honor the phones first sold with the bad screens when the S10plus first came out in January 2019.
justification: While the incident resulted in property damage (chipped screen), there were no injuries reported.

incident_description: Belkin power strip that was being used for tv/dvd/cable box started on fire this morning.  It wasn't overloaded at all, only had 3 things plugged into it.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and the cause was a single power strip with only three devices plugged in, making it unlikely but possible.

incident_description:
A Microsoft Surface Pro 4, purchased in July/16, recently started to overheat when charging. The over heating was so server that the user obtained injury. As a result of the over heating, the device's battery swelled to the point where it pushed the screen out. A quick Google search shows this to be a common issue with the Surface Pro, and in some reported cases, the battery reportedly exploded.

In speaking to Microsoft, they acknowledge that this product does have a defective battery and will only recall those devices sold within 3 years of the initial warranty. 

Considering the potential injury factor, let a lone the explosion factor, MS should be required to recall all devices that show this issue to be current.
justification: Injury occurred due to overheating, and potential for more severe consequences like explosion exists.

incident_description: My computer (a [REDACTED]) and monitor were plugged into the APC 500 back-UPS unit. I waited a half an hour for it to cool and then remove the battery. There was no damage to the battery which was relatively new. 3 hours later you can still smell the burnt electrical smell from the APC unit.

incident_description: Kids tablet was stored in our kitchen cabinet for a few months with the power off.  When we took it out to use, the tablet was splitting apart.  Upon closer inspection, I realized the internal battery had swollen up and expanded which created a risk of combustion.

incident_description: Dell XPS 13 9370. Lithium ion battery spontaneously swelled making the trackpad buttons unusable. Battery swelling posed a serious fire hazard. incident_description:

On 7/23 at roughly 4:30am, our family was awoken by our smoke alarms going off.  When we exited our bedrooms, we found a house full of smoke.  As we searched for the source, we found that the power strip mentioned above had gotten so hot, that half of it was melted and turned to black ash on the cement floor.  We immediately unplugged it, and removed all remaining cords that were plugged into it.  Luckily the strip was not on carpet, as that may have started our home on fire.  Our house smelled like burning plastic for the rest of the day, and we were all blowing black soot from our noses with burning eyes.  I encourage you to recall this product so that no other incidents occur like the one we experienced. 
Thank you for your time.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident caused significant smoke and potential fire hazard, thus severity level 2.

incident_description: I purchased an AmazonBasics 6-Sheet Cross-Cut Paper and Credit Card Shredder in 2015. While we were away on vacation, the shredder began running by itself. incident_description:
On June 10, 2019, while my wife was just about to leave the house, she noticed a hissing sound coming from the direction of a small wooden file cabinet in our bedroom. She went over to the area and noticed that the sound was coming from the LifePod Power Bank, which was not connected to an outlet or device, and which I had purchased from Amazon on April 15, 2019. This is the cut-and-paste from the Amazon entry:

LifePod 10000mAh Power Bank External Battery Portable Charger Pack with Built-in Type C and Micro USB Cable for [REDACTED] Cell Pho
Sold by: INSTAdealZ

As soon as my wife picked up the battery, it spontaneously ignited. She threw it to the floor, which scorched our carpet. She then scooped it up with a paper plate (the only thing she had nearby at the time), and flipped it into the [whirlpool tub] in the bathroom, which burned and slightly melted the tub. She was able to extinguish the battery and then brought it outside away from the structure of the house.

I filed a product review on [REDACTED], who has contacted me and removed the device from its inventory. Our insurance company has authorized payment of about $18K for the damages. Thankfully, nobody was physically injured.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident caused significant property damage, making it a level 2 severity.

incident_description:
On Saturday, June 1, 2019, I had a lithium battery charger/flashlight, handed out to me when opening a new checking account in February 2017 at Bethpage Federal Credit Union, explode while charging in my kitchen for about ten minutes, shooting extremely hot debris and black soot up to ten feet away. It was not used more than twice before without incident. And it was not overcharged , showing a 25-50% charge level when I plugged it in about ten minutes earlier.

It literally burned and melted the Formica counter top where it sat, set fire to some papers on the counter top and a newspaper several feet away, burned the wood floor in several places with the flying, hot debris and melted an area rug in a spot eight feet away. The smoke alarm going off was the only alert we had. No one was in the room at the time and that saved it shooting directly at me had I been sitting in my normal chair, which had a piece of the debris starting to melt the vinyl seat.

It took about two hours to clean up the mess plus the laundry time needed to clean all the furniture covers covered in this burned lithium soot.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident caused significant property damage, making it a level 2 severity.

incident_description:
I had a Surface Book laptop (1st generation) which was purchased direct from Microsoft in December 2016. About 14 months later, the screen started bulging out, and after doing some research I determined that the problem was that the battery (which is located behind the screen) was swollen, pushing on the back of the screen and causing it to bulge out. I contacted Microsoft and they replaced the computer in July 2017 with a refurbished unit. Then, on the refurbished unit, the SAME EXACT ISSUE occurred, once again, after about 14 months of use. I once again contacted Microsoft and elevated the claim to a manager. The manager contacted Microsoft HQ requesting permission to replace my computer again, and was denied. However, they said they could give me another refurbished unit at a cost of $599. I am less concerned about the cost issue. However, I am very concerned with the potential explosion and fire hazard, which this issue is causing me, as well the dangers which defective Surface Books are posing to other consumers who are suffering from the same problem. 

I have done a great deal of research on this topic. There are MANY, MANY stories on various message boards and web sites of people suffering with the same bulging battery issue. Consumers have had mixed results as to whether Microsoft would replace their defective bulging battery laptops free of cost.

Microsoft's 1st generation Surface Books obviously have a defective battery and/or charge controller issue. Now I am left with a computer which is an unsafe fire/explosion hazard. Shame on you Microsoft!
justification: While no injuries were reported, the incident involved a significant safety hazard (battery explosion/fire) and affected multiple consumers.

incident_description: We purchased a PBS playtime pad, model #PBKRWM5410 NS FCC, IN December 2017. In June 2019 we noticed that the battery is expanding and causing the casing to separate exposing the internal components. We have secured the device so that our children and dogs do not have access to it. The battery continues to expand and the casing is almost completely disconnected. It is currently wrapped in a bag and placed in a plastic lock box in case it does explode. My sister purchased the same item for her son in December 2017 as well. Her device was purchased at a different store and in a different city. Her device did the same thing a couple months ago. At that time we figured she got a defective device. Now that it has happened to our device as well I believe it is more likely a defective product (not just an individual device). I would like to strongly urge a recall of this item. If a child were to find it before the parent and get curious the results could be toxic. It could also be possible for the battery to completely explode before an adult is aware of it. Again the results could be toxic. I am currently involved in email communications with ematic, the company that makes the product. I have requested that my device be replaced with a safer device or that they return my money as this is not the result of normal wear and tear. I also told them about my sister's device and I am urging them to do a recall of this item. I have pictures that I hope that I can include with this report. In the event that I cannot please know that they are available and I would be happy to send them. Thank you.
justification: While no injuries have occurred yet, the expanding battery poses a high likelihood of toxic exposure or explosion, making it an incident with potential injury.

incident_description: Our client purchased a Walmart Blackweb 10400mAh Portable Battery with LED Readout on Saturday, November 10, 2018. The battery had a 70% charge when he purchased it. He charged his phone with it on Saturday without having charged the battery. He charged the battery on Sunday, November 11, 2018, though connection to a USB port on a wall plug. He took it to work with him on Monday but did not use it. At approximately 6:58 am. on Tuesday, November 13, 2018, the client put the battery in his right back pocket as he prepared to leave for work. As he was putting his lunch box in the car, he felt a warm pressure in his right back pocket and heard what sounded like a coke bottle spewing and he noticed smoke around him and realized the charger had burst into flame. He tried to get the battery out of his pocket with his right hand but was unable to, so he dropped his pants and stamped the fire out with his boots while his pants were around his ankles. He went to the emergency room and was treated for second degree burns to his right buttocks and right hand. He reports that he never dropped the battery, banged it on anything, didn't sit on it, and did nothing out of the ordinary that would have caused the battery to explode and catch fire like it did.
justification: The battery's spontaneous combustion caused second-degree burns, indicating a severe incident.

incident_description: My wife and I purchased two  Just Wireless - Apple MFi Certified 6' Lightning USB Charging Cable - Slate gray charging cables for use in our minivan. These cables stay in the car and are not removed so they see only minimal wear and tear. We purchased these from Best Buy in Eau Claire, WI on February 26, 2019. However, there were no physical signs of damage to the charger visible on inspection. Later in the day, when she tried to plug her phone in again, the cable, about a centimeter below the actual charging plug started getting really hot and smoking. Before she could let go, the nylon sheath of the cable melted, burning her thumb. I managed to unplug the based of the cable from the cigarette lighter plug. We're not sure what happened exactly, but somehow there is not a melted hole in the sheath where you can see the electrical wires underneath. I have heard of several complaints about the safety of frayed phone chargers, but this model of the charger with the flexible nylon sheath hides any signs of apparent damage or defect underneath and poses a serious risk of electrical shock or burns.

incident_description:

But the painful symptoms in my hands + arms lasted for about 6 weeks. During that time a doctor advised me to "use my hands as little as possible until the symptoms subside."

A customer service tech at Apple + a manager at Verizon both told me that "other people have also reported sensitivity to this voltage." I've since found out that the newer phones emit an even stronger signal.

I feel that these devices could have a warning label, + that there should be alternatives to this technology for people who could be injured by it.

incident_description:
Products: Apple MacBook Pro 13", Apple MacBook Pro 15"
Model Year: 2016, 2017, 2018+

Issue: 
The MacBook Pro's are advertised to be able to handle professional applications, which apple makes and some 3rd party professional applications as well as games. Yet, when using these types of applications for more than 1-2 straight on Apple's Laptops, their MacBook Pro's specifically, the metal chassis that surrounds all the keyboards keys get so hot that it literally burns your finger if touching it for more than 2 seconds.

I have told Apple's Corporate Executive Relations about this, but they didn't take the issue very seriously and just talked me in circles around the whole issue among the other issue I was mainly having with the product; since it over-heats by design.

Apple's Laptops have always been known for being hot computers and having the bottom of the unit burn you if you left it on your lap to long, but todays models are much thinner in design so the heat gets trapped inside the unit and well the chassis becomes a heatsink which makes it get very hot. I used a thermostat on the top panel on mine and it reached 130ÃÂ°! Yes that is the part right above the Touch Bar on a 2017 MacBook Pro after 1-2 hours of straight use with a Game or Professional App like Final Cut Pro, Logic Pro X, or Adobe Premiere Pro CC. Apple has refused to take responsibility for this issue after years of consumers posting YouTube videos and posts about there computers overheating issues.

The reason behind why the Chassis get so hot in the first place that causes it to burn your finger when resting your finger on the keys, which most do when working with professional apps, since keyboard shortcuts are more efficient way of doing things. But the reason is since apple's thermal cooling system is so poorly designed in there laptops, it can't cool the CPU nearly at all during heavy use or when GPU intensive apps are loaded and used, so since the heat needs to escape what doesn't make it out though the fans makes its way thought the chassis making it a giant heatsink. Other Computer companies have already realized this issue and have gone to liquid cooling since its 90% effective at prevent this hazard with laptops with a metal chassis.
justification: Users may experience burns on their fingers due to excessive heat from the metal chassis, which is a common point of contact while using professional applications.
