justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident caused significant damage to the phone, making it a level 2 severity.

incident_description: I purchased a HP Hewlett Packard Pavilion x360 laptop for use in travel to Alaska in 2016. Product worked as advertised, returned home, placed in air conditioned storage on a bookshelf in my home. In 2017 laptop taken to CA for use at which time it was discovered that the battery was swollen to the point that the physical enclosure / case of the laptop was noticeably externally swollen/ bulging. In the past 12 months i have contacted HP repeatedly by telephone and their online customer service to address the issue. The main source of my frustration with their corporate inflexibility is that this specific model is subject to a recall for a defective battery, but upon repeated contact with HP they refuse to repair or replace this swelling, bulging, damaged product. I have photographic documentation of the damage with a steel straightedge. HP claims that because my laptop serial number falls outside the boundaries of their recall that they are not liable for any repair replacement service or any other means to make amends for this soon-to-be unusable product. The battery has swollen the case visibly noticeably and has impinged upon the functionality of the trackpad so that the buttons no longer function or "click". All i ask, is that this laptop model, which is subject to a battery recall, and whose battery is swollen and damaged the trackpad, be replaced and repaired to as new condition and functionality. Again, the core issue is that HP refuses to expand the scope of the serial number range of this particular laptop model, Pavilion x360, which is subject to a current recall and was expanded previously.
justification: While no injuries have been reported, the incident involves a defective product that poses a potential safety risk due to battery swelling.

incident_description:
Turned computer on, got a message that some code was not found and to check with administrator.
Took computer to Best Buy Geek Squad, they turned it on, got same message. They gave me a number to call, which I did and was told to take computer beck to Geek Squad and they would call and report what they found.  I did that and the code message was still coming up.  GS said couldn't do anything since it was a hardware issue, but Best Buy Manager called HP, talked to [REDACTED] who gave the Best Buy manager this web address.  I was told to return home, look at the website and follow the instructions.
justification: The incident involved a software issue, resulting in no physical harm, but the likelihood of occurrence is possible given the frequency of software glitches.

incident_description: Surge suppressor was plugged into the wall outlet, no other items plugged in to that duplex outlet.  Small electric heater was plugged in and operating at a medium setting (1500W max heater).  It had been running for approximately three hours when all of the sudden there was a flash and a "pop" and the heater and TV (plugged into a different duplex wall outlet on the same circuit) stopped working.  A slight smoke odor was noticed coming from the wall outlet.  The surge suppressor and the wall outlet were warm and had black soot.
justification: The incident involved a minor electrical fire, causing damage to equipment but no injuries.

incident_description: iTek Qi Wireless charger was used to charge my iPhone. After 4 months of use, the charger's back melted and burned my desktop. Fortunately, the desk did not ignite and I did not have papers or other flammables near the charger. The possibility of a total loss home fire resulting in property damage and death was very high.
justification: While no injuries or deaths occurred, the incident resulted in property damage (melted charger and burned desktop), making it a level 2 severity. The likelihood is high as the charger was used daily for four months before the incident.

incident_description: On March 17, 2019 to report of a Structure Fire in Bowie residence hall on the campus of Appalachian State University.  Reported as a battery charger on fire on a bed.  On arrival, we discovered a HALO ACDC BOLT 58830 that had burned.  The fire had originated in the device and spread to the bed and bedding. The device had a charger attached to the device in one of the USB ports.  The charger was not the charger was supplied with the device.
justification: No injuries were reported, but the fire spread to the bed and bedding, causing property damage.

incident_description: I was charging my wireless Skullcandy Sport headphones with a standard micro USB charger, when I noticed a faint electrical burning smell. At first I didn't know where it was coming from. After about 30 minutes, I went to unplug it and felt that charging port of headphones and the charger tip itself was very hot, enough for the battery pack of the headphones to start melting. For the few seconds it was in my hands, I sustained a small burn to my middle finger. I was able to unplug it and let it cool down.
justification: Injury occurred due to direct contact with overheating device, likelihood is possible given the common use of such devices and chargers.

incident_description: Responded to an incident involving a LiPo 11.1 Valken. com battery pack for an air soft gun. The battery caught fire while charging, the associated charger was a Valken Energy digital display charger for2-3 cell 7.4-11.1 volt batteries.
justification: The battery caught fire, but no injuries were reported, making it an incident with no injuries.

incident_description: I found a small, sharp metal plate in my 10 month old sonÃÂs mouth.  The plate came from my older sons Elecder i37 kids headphones.  The plate was originally glued onto the inside of the headband of the headphones and the glue bond failed. It had ÃÂMade in ChinaÃÂ etched into it. The other side of the headband has a matching plate with a ÃÂCEÃÂ certification etched into it.  Fearing that the ÃÂCEÃÂ plate could fall out I removed it and it practically fell out.  My concern is that it could injure another child.
justification: The sharp metal plate could cause injury if it falls out and is ingested or inserted into the ear.

incident_description: The battery pack inside of the monitor exploded
justification: While the incident caused damage to the monitor, it did not result in any injuries, making it a level 2 severity. The likelihood is rated as 'possible' (3) as battery explosions, though rare, can occur due to manufacturing defects or improper handling.

incident_description:
On 1/7/19 a multi-charger, cord, and adapter tip I purchased on Amazon.com from LVSUN caught fire while plugged into my laptop.  The fire burned my laptop, burned my arm (I now have a scar as well) and had I not been home (it was plugged in and sitting on my couch) could have burned my house down.  I was lucky to be sitting right next to the product when it caught fire.

I reported it to the manufacturer as well as amazon.  I took photographs as well.

Then, a second charger, identical to the first,  melted within two days of the first.  This unit was in my bedroom and caught my mattress protector on fire. (The cable that was attached to it was sitting next to my bed and melted onto the plastic protector)

Again, I contacted amazon and the seller/manufacturer.  I was refunded but the products are still listed for sale.

The company claims in their listings to be UL certified amongst other certifications.  I believe this to be false.

The company, upon seeing that I left negative feedback for them, offered me $200 as compensation for my damages (my computer cost over $1000 and was destroyed) IF I would agree to remove the negative feedback.
I did not accept and they had my feedback removed.  I added more feedback and to this date, it is still up- as well as others that have claimed fires, shorts, and melting.  

The products are dangerous- that I'm convinced of.  What are the odds it would happen not once, but twice with two different items in the same household?
justification: The incident resulted in burns to the individual's arm and could have caused significant property damage, making it a severe event with a high likelihood of recurrence given the identical nature of the faulty products.

incident_description:
I own multiple Apple TV's. The 2 most current units i purchased have a very slim remote. This version was released in Oct of 2015 and continues to be sold today with their newest version the Apple TV 4k. 

My 3 year old son dropped the remote from maybe 3 feet above the tile floor and it shattered and glass went everywhere. My foot was cut cleaning up the glass.  I cannot believe that someone would first put glass in a remote that is constantly getting dropped and second not notify their customer that the product has glass in it so we can protect our children from using the device with such a safety hazard. If i would have known the remote had glass in it I would not have let my children use it. 

This product is marketed as a smart TV device as well as a machine to play video games to children.  I am amazed that this product has been available for over 3 years without a recall.
justification: Injury occurred due to glass in the remote, and the likelihood is high as the product has been widely available for over three years.

incident_description:
Cord from a Delta Electronics, Inc. AC Adapter Model EADP-32BB going into a Motorola cable box suddenly became overheated, sparked blue and melted.  We've had the unit for quite a few years and is the same for our whole house DVR system by Spectrum (formally Time Warner Cable).
I was able to pull the plug to stop power otherwise flames would have taken hold.
Smell of burnt wiring and rubber was the sign that alerted me to the problem.
The other 2 boxes are fine.
Spectrum came out the next day and replaced with a different unit.
I have pictures if needed.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident could have caused a fire, hence severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 3 as it's possible but not certain that other units could also overheat.

incident_description: Purchase HP Pavilion 15t laptop from Costco a little over two years ago.  About 8 months after the purchase the keyboard on the left side started rising.  Now the side cover and keyboard are elevated to the point the laptop won't close at all.  After online research, we found out that certain HP laptop batteries are recalled.  Contacted Costco and HP but they both claim that our model is not on recall list.  Costco even went further saying that because the warranty expired this past November they won't and can't do anything about it until our laptop catches fire and burns.  Costco Case No. 10325558.
justification: The laptop's keyboard is damaged and cannot be closed, posing a potential tripping hazard but no immediate physical harm.

incident_description: The wifi extender caught on fire. It was working for fine for one month. After that it constantly connected and disconnected from the router. It caught fire today while being plugged into the wall outlet by itself in the hallway. The product did not last 7 months. Luckily my ten year old son saw it and unplugged it before it spread. This should not happen for $59.99.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident could have caused property damage and posed a potential fire hazard.

incident_description:
I purchased the wireless charging pad by Bytech Intl right before Christmas for our children. A couple days ago my daughter had her phone charging on the pad and it caught fire. Thank goodness she was in her bedroom and noticed it, so she was able to put the small fire out quickly. I can not get this company to call me back and or respond to my email.
I am seeking a refund for the charger and repair to the dresser that was damaged. I would at least like to see these removed from the market so that no one else has to experience a larger loss from a phone charger.
justification: While no one was injured, the incident of a phone catching fire on the charging pad is significant and could have resulted in more severe consequences.

incident_description:
I bought a pixel 3xl phone two weeks ago. It came with a (pure.gear) tempered glass screen protector.
Yesterday, after pushing my phone into my shirt pocket, I felt a sharp prick on my left thumb.When I looked at it i was bleeding. I took my phone out and saw that the screen protector was slightly cracked. I proceeded to peel the screen protector off and the problem was gone.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury, and while it's not common, it's possible for screen protectors to crack and cause minor cuts.

incident_description: reported vehicle fire. Vehicle owner found the battery of a 2003 [REDACTED to be dead. Owner used a Halo Bolt 57720 to jump stat the vehicle. Vehicle started and owner into their home to retrieve something and came out to find their vehicle on fire. Fire was contained to the area of the battery of the vehicle, and the front grill/bumper.
justification: The fire was contained and did not cause injury, but the incident could have been more severe.

incident_description:
The USB-C connector of a USB3-to-USBC cable heated , melted, and caught on fire while connected to an ordinary USB charger for mobile devices, which was plugged into an ordinary 120v electrical wall outlet. At the time, the cable was NOT connected to any device.

The cable is manufactured by Anker and purchased on Amazon.com on November 14 2018.
Description is:
USB C Cable (2-Pack 6ft) Anker Powerline USB C to USB 3.0 Cable with 56k Ohm
Pull-up Resistor for Samsung Galaxy Note 8, S8, S8+, S9, iPad Pro 2018, MacBook, Sony
XZ, LG V20 G5 G6, Xiaomi 5 and More

At the time of the incident, there was no apparent wear or damage of any kind to the cable.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the cable catching fire poses a potential hazard, making it an incident.

incident_description: Student was using an HP Chromebook 11 G5 EE in class for ~10 minutes when the student reported to the teacher that a burnt smell was coming from the chromebook. Sure enough, the teacher saw smoke coming from the charging port on the chromebook. The teacher unplugged the chromebook and removed it from the classroom. The charging tip appears to have melted in places and has scorch marks along the tip. The charging port also appears to have melted in places
justification: No injuries were reported, but the incident involved a potential fire hazard.

incident_description: Sabrent wall charger model AX-U5PW started burning even when nothing was connected to it.
justification: The charger burning even without a device connected indicates a potential fire hazard, making it an incident with possible occurrence.

incident_description: My Razer Blade V6 - 4K UHD - 512GB laptop that is less than a year old caught fire. I was sitting down doing work and I noticed fumes rising from the keys and I was quick to unplug everything and set it aside. I learned my laptop had caught on fire and the circuit board had burnt. It was so hot that I nearly scalded myself. I am thoroughly disappointed with Razer's product line as this product posed a fire hazard to me. If I was asleep and my laptop was on downloading a file perhaps, it could've been a much different story.
justification: The laptop catching fire and emitting heat capable of causing burns indicates a high severity level, and the fact that it happened while in use and could have been worse if left unattended suggests a high likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description:
JBL Charge 3 - AGE 2.5 years old.
Put on charge. Speaker caught fire!
justification: Speaker catching fire is an incident with potential for injury, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: I want to report a potential fire hazard safety concern regarding the Belkin 27 Watt Power Adapter USB charger, model F7U011dq.  I plugged in the USB charger while in flight to an AC power outlet provided at the seat.  I connected the charger to an [REDACTED].  The USB charger was intermittent in charging.  I observed arcing and heard a sizzling sound coming from the charger.  This appeared to be happening at the pivot point on the charger at one AC input prong.  I immediately pulled the charger from the AC outlet.  There was no arcing at the AC outlet itself.  The same arcing and sizzling occurs when I plug the charger into a home power strip.  There is what appears to be carbon deposits from the arcing visible at the pivot point of one AC prong.  I am concerned that if I leave the charger plugged the charger will start on fire or start the outlet on fire. I can provide photos. I purchased the charger at Walmart on 2 Jan 2019.  It was brand new in a sealed box.   I tried contacting Belkin Technical Support at 1.800.223.5546 to report the issue and was not able to get to speak to a human.  After 13 minutes of going through menu choices and being place on hold I gave up.  Maybe you all can get Belkin's attention.  If this arcing is a common issue it could lead to a fire on an airplane or at home.
justification: Potential for fire, though no immediate injury reported.

incident_description: A local business Burns and Scalo located at [ REDACTED] received a video card from Zoresco Equipment Company located at 1241 Lower Rodi Road, Turtle Creek, Pa 15145. Upon opening the card it caught fire. Left a small burn mark on the floor and a "Sulphur" smell in the office.
justification: Although the incident caused no injuries, the fire and sulfur smell indicate a potential hazard, making it an incident with possible reoccurrence.

incident_description:
On Feb 12th while sitting in the passenger seat of my vehicle, the phone charger I had plugged into my husband's cell phone started smoking and burning. I immediately pulled the phone charger from the phone and unplugged it from the car, but it had already melted both the charger and the charge port on the phone.

After posting on FB about my experience, other people shared the same thing happened to them with the same brand.

The charger is a Target brand, so I contacted them. On Feb 13th, I was contacted by the guest relations person to whom my case was assigned. She could not tell me that others had the same issue, but she was able to tell me that she had the manufacturers information readily available, which is not typically the case, and inferred it was due to this incident happening multiple times. She also strongly encouraged me to stay vocal and try to get this item taken out of the stores.

Other people told me that it started a small fire on their couch when only plugged into the wall (not into another device), and one that started a fire in a car.

It is the Heyday USB to USB-C charger from Target.
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the incident caused property damage and posed a potential fire hazard, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description: My Samsung 65 inch TV broken off the original TV stand and fallen from TV table, crashed to ground, the Samsung's V-shaped TV stand for big screen TV is an unsafe product, it has defect. I bought the TV on 12/22/2017, barely over one year, the TV stand has broken, fortunately it happened closed to the middle night, no one near the TV. If it had happened during daytime and had people around the TV, the accident would have caused unimaginable injuries.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident could have resulted in serious harm if it had happened during the day with people nearby.

incident_description:
mine is a safety concern with my acer laptop I perchesed from Best Buy in the spokane Valley WA. 
I noticed it started to overheat when I would set it on my lap to use..it really got hot and it burned the surface skin of the top of my legs the first time, then didn't use again for a long while, the 2nd time was later in the fall and again set it on my legs not thinking, and again it burned the top of my legs , but this time through my jeans... so it kinda worried me so I used it sparingly after that and mostly went back to using my old [REDACTED] desk top that I very much dislike, and just used my lap top sparengly and kept in mind that it heats up quite a bit so always having to take that into consideration I usually sit it on a little steel sitting stool next to my bed.
never really wanted to part with it due to really loving my little laptop but wishing that it had a few better things on it like a back lit keyboard, and longer battery life and obviously not wanting to have to 
worry about the scarry overheating thing!!!
justification: The laptop's overheating caused burns to the user's legs, resulting in injury.

incident_description:
Three (3) electronic items were plugged into the surge protector.

Make: Belkin
Model #: BE106000-08R

The unit's plug became hot and burnt.  One prong remained stuck in the receptacle outlet.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and the likelihood of this occurring with a surge protector is possible.

incident_description:
I was awakened at 0430 this morning by a strange burning plastic smell. I was unable to figure it out after unplugging just about everything in my room but a lamp and the Samsung TV, and assumed the smell was coming from outside and went back to bed. I then woke up at 0645, turned on the TV and began to get ready for work. The smell became stronger, I unplugged the lamp, looked at the TV and the top half of the screen was turning black and the smell was becoming increasingly stronger. I immediately unplugged the TV. 

This TV sits on top of a tall dresser with nothing to block the flow of air surrounding the TV

02/25/2019 - Additional Information:

The risk associated with this fire and health/lung issues.

I was coughing, felt out of sorts and nauseous for the entire day after the incident. 

The TV had smoke from the back and sides and the screen was turning increasingly black. 

Please let me know if you need further information. This TV is a fire hazard.
justification: Potential for serious injury due to fire and smoke inhalation, as evidenced by symptoms of coughing, feeling out of sorts, and nausea.

incident_description: We had a patient in our medical practice whom had spontaneous ignition of a vape pen battery that was loose in her purse (not in the vape unit). It caught her purse on fire and sent sparks that glanced off her trunk. It burned a hole through our tile floor.
justification: No injuries were reported, but the incident caused property damage, making it a level 2 severity.

incident_description: Last night, 1/21/19, as I was falling asleep, I heard a loud pop. I turned around. I few seconds later 1 heard several more pops. Then more pops with sparks and fire coming from the back of the computer. The computer was turned off at the time, at the computer and the power control it was attached was also switched off, I had not used the computer for some days. MY computer is the Cyberpower brand. This is an unsafe situation as it could cause a fire;
justification: While no injury occurred, the incident involved a computer spontaneously sparking and catching fire, posing a significant risk.

incident_description: Cell phone (2017 Pixel 2) caught fire while not in use in pocket. Consumer heard pop/hissing noise, saw smoke emerging from his pocket, threw phone on the ground where it continued to smoke, bubble and melt. Burns visible in his pocket and toxic smell lingers.
justification: Consumer suffered burns due to phone catching fire, making it a '3 - Injury' severity level. Occurrence likelihood is '3 - Possible' as such incidents, though rare, can happen.

incident_description:
Surge protector from Prime made a sizzling sound and melted part of the unit and cause black scorching on unit as well as wall receptacle.

Had a space heater and [REDACTED] charging in the Surge Protector unit. Neither item was damaged. 

My concern is that the unit go hot enough to melt and cause black scorching.

I called the company and they quickly pointed out that in the very fine print it states not to plug a heater in the unit. 99.9% of consumers do not read, the over half way down the page, super fine print and would miss this.  Put this at the top of the page!!

In my opinion there should be a larger warning on the packaging and not buried in the fine print.
justification: Although no injuries or damages occurred, the incident could have led to property damage or fire, making it likely to happen again due to lack of clear warnings.

incident_description:
The Harrison Township Fire Department responded to an apartment fire in which I performed the investigation.  It was found that the unattended computer system's power supply was the cause and origin of the fire.  A complete investigation report is available upon request.  Referenced Fire Run Number:  [REDACTED].
Item:  HP Pavilion All-In-One
Product Number: N0A38AA#ABA
Model Number: 23-q128
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and the likelihood of a similar occurrence is possible given the prevalence of unattended computer systems.

incident_description:
Generic camera with external lithium battery

Battery constructed with no protective metal shell/case, encased in shrink wrap to mimic normal battery

Fire/explosion/hazardous gas hazards, no way this passed U.N. testing requirements.

Shipped sans required postal lithium notice on package.
justification: The lack of a protective metal shell and the absence of a required postal lithium notice on the package increases the likelihood of an incident, potentially causing a fire or explosion, but not necessarily leading to death.

incident_description: The product burst into flames while not in use.  No item was being charged and the unit was not being charged.
justification: The product spontaneously combusted, which could have led to property damage if not noticed.

incident_description:
On April 4, 2017, I purchased, from BestBuy Electronics,[REDACTED], one (1) Logitech-brand G602 Wireless Gaming Mouse, which is an expensive unit.   This not an ordinary wireless mouse but is designed for playing computer games. It has six (6) buttons on the left side, three (3) additional buttons on the upper portion in addition to the professional-style wheel and the left and right control buttons. (My grandson gave me directions as to how to use it when we play "[REDACTED]".).
This was my primary mouse for several months until the start of November 2018.  I went down to my basement office, turned on my computer and monitor then reached for my Logitech G602 it felt slightly warm to the touch (but not hot).  Coupled with that the arrow on the screen was not present and the mouse would not "wake-up".  I turned it over and saw that the power button was in the 'on' or green position.  I usually don't turn off my mouse(s) [mice?] because the modern units put themselves in a 'sleep' mode after several minutes of inactivity.
What surprised me that the bottom of the mouse had melted to a size of approximately 4cm x 3cm, and approximately 2mm inward into the mouse base. No interior electronics or wiring was visible.
Overnight the mouse had been sitting on the wood on my desk. It is cordless and is powered by two (2) AA batteries. It has not modified in a single way.  There are no incandescent or halogen lighting units on or around my desk.  Also, all illumination is produced by lower voltage, 12-volt DC LED small 'puck' lights none of which are close to the area where the mouse is used. The LED 'puck' produces no noticeable heat.  All lights are turned off when the desk is not being used.
We built our house in 1994 and no one has ever used any form of tobacco product on our property let alone inside of our house.
There is nothing on, around or in my desk that would produce any heat. I do not have a coffee cup heater/warmer anywhere close to my desk. There are no high or low power electric wiring any where in the vicinity where the mouse is used.  My telephone is corded and does not use any power supply.  There is no under-desk small space electric heater.
My wife and I are the only residents of this house.
I contacted Logitech Consumer Support repeatedly and they requested photographs, complete details, etc. I even offered to mail them the defective mouse at my expense.  They never responded except to ask me for more photographs and Logitech stated that they would send me a replacement mouse.
What worries me is that this melting of the base of the mouse occurred while it was touching a laminated wood (over particle board) material.  Also, this melting of the mouse plastic took place when no one was sitting a the computer.  I now have installed a smoke detector over my desk space.
I am graduate of the University of [REDACTED] Fire Training Institute Academy and this incident bothers me, especially if the mouse users leave the unit unattended on a couch, chair, plastic table, etc.
I will be happy to send the aforementioned mouse to any of your testing facilities.  I also have all of the photographs I have taken and forwarded to Logitech.  I will also send photographs of my desk area.  No one was injured.  I saw no reason for any kind of Fire Department report.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the incident involved a product malfunction that could potentially cause injury or fire if left unattended.

incident_description: I was shocked by Dell Recalls Hybrid Power Adapters Sold with Power Banks Due to Shock Hazard that has been recalled.
justification: The incident involves a product recall due to a shock hazard, but no injuries have been reported.

incident_description: Dell Latitude 5510 was being used started to get real hot around the touchpad and then the cover started bulging where the battery is located.
justification: Potential for injury due to heat and bulging cover, but no immediate threat of death or severe injury.

incident_description:
Three outlets were had plugs in them at the time of the incident.

This surge protector was on a computer table with computer cables attached.  It burned a wooden shelf on the computer table.  It appears to have burned for a while and self extinguished.


The consumer searched on-line and found a recall (Recall# 10-024),  and called the firm:   Tel:  800-223-5546.  He went through the options and the call was disconnected.  The called back and pressed the option for technical support, where he held on the phone for 27 minutes, prior to hanging up, because he was unable to speak with anyone.

The consumer is extremely concerned about the fire hazard, because part of the protector has melted.  The consumer estimates that 25% of the product is melted and the entire top is blackened and he believes that some of the internal parts are melted as well.

He estimates that an approximately 18ÃÂ area of the shelf is burned and there was a lot of soot on the shelf.  It seems that plastic materials may have shot out of the surge protector and caused this soot damage.

The consumer removed the power cord for a computer from one of the surge protector outlets and the metal prongs were burned.  He did not notice any burn damage to the prongs of the other two devices.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident involved a significant fire hazard with substantial property damage, indicating a high likelihood of future occurrences.

incident_description:
I was sitting in my bedroom and heard a buzzing static sound, looked over and saw my surge protector smoking. I rushed over to turn it off and it got worse. I moved my bed away from the wall and unplugged it.  An electrical fire had started in the surge protector and turning off the switch on it didn't stop it from buzzing and getting worse.  There were no injuries, but I was very alarmed because if I hadn't been sitting near it, it would have ignited the shag carpet it was sitting on and my house would have been burned down - or had it happened when I was asleep, it might have killed my wife and me.  I WAS UNABLE TO SEND VIDEO DEMONSTRATING THE PROBLEM IN THIS REPORT SO I AM SENDING IT AS AN ATTACHMENT AND WILL INCLUDE CONTROL NUMBER IN THE EMAIL OMB Control Number [REDACTED]  

I had sent this all to [REDACTED] at Belkin, and before sending him the surge protector I want to know if you want to see it first to inspect it.  I am aware that corporations don't always report dangerous defects to CPSC, so I'm initiating this report with you.  I have communicated with [REDACTED].
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident involved a significant risk of property damage and potential loss of life if left unnoticed.

incident_description:
The product is Owlet Smart Sock 2. It was being used to monitor my baby during the night. Followed instructions to the max. It malfunctioned as causing 2nd degree burns to his left foot. I took him to an urgent 
Care clinic for medical care.
justification: The Owlet Smart Sock 2 malfunctioned, causing a 2nd degree burn, indicating a possible occurrence given the product's intended use.

incident_description: Business suffered a fire. Origin was a Tekkeon External Laptop Battery, MP3450
justification: The fire caused property damage but no injuries, and while such incidents are possible, they are not common.

incident_description: I purchased a cellphone charger and was using it on my nightstand. I woke up to check the time and saw red glowing from the charger on my nightstand. When I reached over, my phone was hot. I got up and turned in the light to discover my charger melted onto my nightstand. When i disconnected it, I could smell the burning.
justification: The charger overheating and melting onto the nightstand could have caused a fire, posing a potential injury risk.

incident_description:
I am a fire investigator for Mecklenburg County NC, on Christmas night I responded to a house fire and the results of my investigation found a 'Portable Unicorn Phone Charger" was the cause of the fire.

The victim told me that this product was brand new that day and just opened the package. it was plugged in for the first time.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and the cause was a newly purchased, first-time used product, making it a possible occurrence.

incident_description:
This consumer is reporting that he purchased a camera with the adapter from a large communication company sometime during the first week in September 2018.
On October 4th, 2018 he plugged the adapter in to charge the camera and when he returned 45 min to one hour later to remove it from the outlet the adapter had become so hot that it melted and the area of the camera where it was plugged into the adapter also melted as a result to the adapters heated temperature.     
The caller does not have the model or serial number for the camera and he states that it is the adapter not the camera he is reporting.
He does still have this camera and adapter
There are no injuries
He has not contacted the manufacturer but he does intend to contact them.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident resulted in property damage (melted adapter and camera), making it a level 2 severity.

incident_description: I have a j1 cell phone which the battery exploded while charging causing property damage.
justification: Property damage occurred but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
I installed a Li-Ion battery purchased from ebay user "[REDACTED]", Shenzhen Uni-Sun Electronics Co., Ltd. in my [REDACTED] laptop.

The battery was initially at zero charge when bought and this increased to only 6% after about 12 hours. About 6 hours later, the battery exploded, starting 3 fires in my bedroom and melting parts of the carpet. If nobody had been home, I expect the whole house would have been burned down.

There is nothing wrong with the charger or the laptop. The laptop is still usable, even after being bent and blown 5 feet away by the explosion.

This company's products should not be allowed to be sold in the USA, or anywhere else.
justification: The battery explosion caused significant property damage and could have resulted in injuries or death if someone hadn't been home.

incident_description: I recently purchased and tested out the "Hearing Things" game manufactured by Hasbro. Immediately upon placing the headphones on my ears in accordance with the instructions it became obvious that the volume produced by the headphones exceeded safe levels, especially when considering this product is marketed for use by children as young as 12
justification: The incident involves a product intended for children, with a high likelihood of misuse due to excessive volume, potentially causing hearing damage.

incident_description:
The submitter is reporting his TV for posing a fire hazard. His wife had the TV on and when she returned to the room she noticed the screen was blank. The TV lost video but still had sound. She contacted the submitter and notified him. He suggested she check the back for a reset button but upon she noticed burn damages near the panel. The TV was then turned off and unplugged. From front - lower right corner. Obvious signs of heat or fire behind screen about 1 foot high.

He indicated that the TV is usually used everyday for about 20 hours. Due to remote feature TV always has power.

He obtained the TV from his daughter sometime in 2016 and he believes the TV was purchased Nov. 2013.

No prior incident. 

Samsung was notified twice. First, 11-26-18, with no results. 11-30-18 were supplied all details and information.
justification: Potential fire hazard with visible burn damages, though no injury reported.

incident_description:
I received a brand new Apple iPhone 7 as a gift in December 2017. It was activated a few months later, and not long after that I started to experience burning, itching, aching pains in my forearms whenever I would hold and use this phone. If I put this phone in my pants pocket, it would cause a localized burning, itching aching pain on my leg. If the phone was turned off or set to "Airplane" mode the pains would cease to occur. Other times if I had been holding the phone for too long, the pain would linger for days after. 

The least painful way I found to use this phone was to not hold it and lay it on a flat surface, but this only proved to slightly lessen the pain. Eventually the pain escalated to the point that I made an appointment with my Physician, and I was advised to stop using this phone. I even applied bags of ice to both my forearms to alleviate the pain, but that only helped slightly. I am now scheduled to see an orthopedic specialist.

There is quite a bit of anecdotal evidence on the internet that many Apple products (i.e. Apple watches, iPads, iPhones) are causing many people physical symptoms. This is a very real problem that may be posing a great risk to Apple users and should be investigated as soon as possible.
justification: User experienced persistent, severe pain and required medical intervention, with many others reporting similar issues online.

incident_description: Using a cell phone charger on my Huawei Nexus 6P phone as normal. I awoke in the morning and disconnected the phone from the charger which was sitting on the bedside table. The USB-C connector which interfaces with the phone fell to to the carpet which was normal. I went downstairs to get breakfast and feed the cats.  While cleaning the cat box I could smell something like hot electronics which  was stronger than the cat box odor. After about 10 minutes of being puzzled I went back upstairs to look around to find the charger connector had melted and burned the carpet and was smoking. This is the Huawei factory charger which came with my Nexus 6P Phone.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and while it could have been more severe, it's not likely to occur frequently.

incident_description: We received this call as a structure fire.  Upon our arrival, we found a HVAC surge protector that had burnt up on the right side of the house.  The homeowner had discharged a dry chemical extinguisher on the area prior to our arrival.  The HVAC #2 breaker had tripped and was switched to the off position by T52.  Command removed the main breaker in the panel at the HVAC unit itself.  We checked inside the house and in the crawl space for extension and found none.  There was light scorching on the hardy plank just above the surge protector.  There was no smoke inside the house.  Car 21 was requested to investigate. Surge protector type Supco SCM-150.
justification: No injuries reported, but the incident caused property damage and could have escalated if not extinguished.

incident_description:
Product: LG Wireless Head set and Power re charger

Model HBS-920 Silver

Approximately on 11 Nov 2018, I re-charged by headset with the LG provided power cord. Later on in the evening there was a distinct smell coming from a location near the head set. As I looked closer I detected a burnt end of the power cord that melted away the mini-USB end of the cord, and it was melting. I immediately unplugged the unit from the power source. 

I have contacted LG on four different occasions via their website (the only method of communication I can locate), provided them with a close up picture of the burnt device, asked them if there was a product recall, advise to get a resolution etc, and their customer service section has provided no valuable information. I also provided my telephone contact. Hopefully you can assist me.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage (burnt power cord) but no injuries, and the likelihood of occurrence is possible given the product's age and lack of recall.

incident_description:
I ordered a Samsung 860 EVO Solid State Drive to replace an exiting hard drive in my PC. The drive was installed, using the existing SATA power and Serial ATA connector. Shortly after the PC was turned on, the drive caught on fire damaging the entire PC. Had I not been around when the fire happened, it could have burned my entire house down. This is a serious safety issue that needs to be addressed by the manufacturer.

My other issue is who pays for the damage to the PC? How do I even begin to estimate the loss of data and what impact tat will have? I would estimate the hardware damage to be at least $1600 - which is not nearly as big of a deal as the damage to the drives in the PC. The resulting loss of data is catastrophic to me. Years of recordings of music including at least 35 entire songs that were recorded and stored on that PC are now lost forever. 

The drive was intended to be used as a backup to the other drives, in case of data loss. now I am looking at total data loss.

As a musician who has been recording for 30+ years the loss of my music is completely heart breaking. No amount of compensation could ever be determined that would be fair for this loss.
justification: The incident resulted in significant property damage and potential loss of life, with a high likelihood of recurrence given the product's defect.

incident_description: Plugged in Sound Mates earbuds to charge and within 4 hours they burst into a fireball about 6-8 inches around and burnt/singed our headboard, sheets, and some nearby paper.
justification: Fire caused by overheating earbuds during charge, leading to property damage but no injuries.

incident_description:
Coby portable DVD Player / TV had been plugged into a wall electrical outlet in a bedroom for 2 days and was being used to play music CDs.  Tonight, flames started violently spitting from the base setting off the fire alarms.  The wall paint was burned, and thew fire would not be put out by blowing.  I unplugged the Coby and brought it to the bathroom sink and doused it with water.  After about 30 seconds, the fire was out, but there was smoke and burning bits of plastic trailing the path from the bedroom to the bathroom.

We never received a recall notice and are the original purchasers of the Coby device.  Had someone been sleeping in the bedroom, serious injury or death could have occurred. Had no one been home, the spray of flame was so violent that the house could have burned down before the fire department would have arrived on site.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (burns from extinguishing the fire) and could have led to serious injury or death if someone had been sleeping in the bedroom.

incident_description: I have an Apple iPhone 7 Plus red.  The iPhone was overhead and started to burn.  The temperature was too hot and melted some parts of the phone to irritate my skin.
justification: The phone overheating and melting caused skin irritation, classifying it as an injury incident.

incident_description: The battery exploded in the Coby Kyros 7-inch android tablet model number MD7015B
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and while it's possible, it's not common for tablet batteries to explode.

incident_description:
Belkin Power strip BE106000-06R started to burn with outside plastic housing melting and nearly causing a fire.  Had I not smelled this item burning, my house could have burned down.


Please look at the 1 star rated reviews on Amazon as there are photos of this same power strip burning out or causing fires.

https://www.amazon.com/Belkin-6-Outlet-Commercial-Protector-BE106000-06R/product-reviews/B000JJI6XA/ref=cm_cr_dp_d_hist_1?ie=UTF8&filterByStar=one_star&reviewerType=all_reviews#reviews-filter-bar
justification: The power strip's burning and melting plastic housing posed a high risk of causing a house fire, although no injuries were reported.

incident_description: The power Cube burned my fingers when trying to disconnect from an extension cord or wall plug while trying to recharge my {REDACTED] and/or my {REDACTED]
justification: Injury occurred due to direct contact with a heated object.

incident_description: While using a whistler jump&go portable car starter, it caught ignited internally and caught fire as I threw it away. I only suffered an extremely small burn on my hand, before putting the fire away. I saw a whistler recall with the recall # 15-123 and wanted to know if I was eligible for a replacement starter.
justification: Although the incident resulted in a minor burn, the primary impact was property damage (destruction of the car starter).

incident_description:
Hello,

I have a PANASONIC  BQ-CC75 charger which I purchased as part of a battery/Charger package K-KJ75MC64CA from Costco late 2017.

While plugged into an outlet in order to charge the batteries that came with this device, THE CHARGER CAUGHT FIRE. This fire damaged my property. It burned the side of a kitchen cabinet. Smoke filled the Kitchen causing respiratory issues for my wife and me.

The item was sent to Panasonic. Panasonic determined that the device was faulty.

Yours,

[REDACTED]
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the fire caused property damage and respiratory issues, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
My product has not actually proven to be unsafe yet. But when researching it online I see many  reviews siting how their battery has swelled (like mine), and in some cases exploded.

The product is the Samsung Wireless Baby Monitor - Model# SEW-3043WN and the battery pack model is 455271PHV. 

A few days ago the backing to the baby monitor popped off and wouldn't fit back on. That's when I noticed the swelling. I tried to go online to order a new battery. That is when I noticed all of the reviews: [REDACTED]

I've got two of these monitors running in my house and it worries me that there is danger of fire because of the batteries. I tried to go back to the amazon page where I ordered them to inquire about returning them, but those pages have been taken down. I assume the seller has stopped selling these because of this issue.

It just seems like something that should be recalled.
justification: While no injuries have been reported yet, the likelihood of an incident due to battery swelling and potential explosion is high based on numerous customer reviews.

incident_description: I moved my electric fireplace heater away from the wall to clean behind it and found that the plug had melted to the outlet extender it was discolored and burned.  I consider myself lucky that it did not burn down my house.
justification: The incident resulted in damage to the outlet extender but no injuries, and it could have been more severe.

incident_description:
The printer was sitting on a desk in a dormitory room. It was plugged into a nearby power strip. The power strip was plugged into a duplex outlet adjacent to it. The printer was not in use at the time of the incident. Two girls live in the dorm room. Neither tenant was in the room at the time. No one had been in the room for approximately one and a half hours prior to the incident. According to one of the tenants, the printer is very rarely used.

The printer appears to have overheated internally. It generated sufficient heat to ignite the printer plastic housing. If facing the printer, the fire appears to have started within the left corner of the device. Fire extended to the adjacent walls and underside of a wooden bookshelf which is hung on a wall above the desk. An activated room fire sprinkler extinguished the fire. Fire damage was limited to the printer, some surrounding contents on the desk, and the adjacent walls and bookshelf above.
justification: Fire was contained and extinguished by the sprinkler system, preventing any injuries, but caused damage to the printer and surrounding items.

incident_description:
Approximately 2 years ago, I purchased a GE branded surge protector, what appears to be model E192912.  This item was made in China, and appears to bear a date code of March 2016.
	On the evening of 29 November, 2018, this surge protector seems to have catastrophically failed, having heated up to a high temperature, melted the case, caused several electronic devices to heat up dramatically and possibly fail.  When my daughter picked up the surge protector, it either burnt her finger, or delivered a shock to her finger.
justification: The surge protector overheated, melted, and caused injury, but no death.

incident_description:

Plugged in the charger with batteries properly placed. Red LED lit as expected. After about 8 hours, Red LED still lit and batteries very hot. Appears the auto-shutoff did not work (at least with the included rechargeable batteries).

incident_description: [REDACTED] was plugged into the surge protector. [REDACTED] was not on.  Surge protector was charging another item too.  There was a loud pop and the power went out to the outlet and all outlets on that circuit.  The surge protector was black where the [REDACTED] was plugged in and the [REDACTED] plug was damaged so it is unusable.  It also killed the [REDACTED].  Thankfully the circuit breaker to my house tripped and I was able to restore electricity to the house.
justification: No injuries reported, but significant property damage (unusable device and power outage).

incident_description: Galaxy S7 cell phone bought through Verizon almost caught on fire while charging overnight.  About 6 months into the contract we had to contact Verizon to get the phone replaced because it would not hold a charge.  The agent said this was a known issue with the phone and they sent us a new phone.  Again we continued to have issues with the phone and tried 4-5 times to get it replaced.  All we got was the run around and was told to go purchase a new charger which cost $40.00.  A month or two later my son was charging his phone on his bed while he was sleeping.  During the night he moved and his arm touched the phone.  It burnt him enough where he woke up and touched the phone.  It was so hot that the plastic on the end of the charger melted onto the phone and there are burn marks on both the phone and the charger piece.  Verizon refused to replace the unit because it has a crack on the back of the phone.  The crack did not cause the issue of the phone potentially catching on fire and killing my kid or burning down my house.  I still have the phone and the charger if you would like to test it to start a recall notice to the public.  I will be posting this on line and contacting local news to try to get coverage on the poor quality and customer service.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (burn) and could have led to more severe consequences such as a house fire if not noticed.

incident_description:
Samsung S7 edge was kept on charging by my son(17 years) this phone is regularly used by husband and now since he just bought a [REDACTED] on 24/10 while on his visit to Indonesia it is used by my 6 year old daughter to watch her [REDACTED] channel .

We live in a two storey house . The mobile was left behind for charging upstairs and smelling smoke we ran upstairs to find the phone burning . It was pulled out by the plug and thrown down on the floor ... once it cooled we took it outside and kept it far away in the compound fearing explosion ... since it was so scary and all were horrified as this incident could have happened while the phone was in my daughters hand !! 
Later after about two hours I pulled open the back cover and separated the battery out with the help of a stew diver .. to prevent any internal combustion.. itÃÂs in a totally dialipted state and not expected of Samsung ... my entire family uses Samsung and we have two new [REDACTED] purchased recently , [REDACTED] and this S7 edge . 
I am so horrified I Cannot believe in Samsung anymore ... I want to return all the Samsung phones . I feel cheated and this ripping off trust by the brand and itÃÂs cheap unsafe manufacturing . I need immediate action in this terrifying hazardous incident .

I had kept the phone in proper condition , charging at absolute proper points and no abuse of the gadget ! For a decade we have been loyal and this is like absolute failure .

Regards 
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and the likelihood of it happening again is high given the continued use of Samsung devices in the household.

incident_description: Purchased iPhone 5 pink glitter waterfall cellphone case at Walmart in Albany, NY, December 21, 2017. It was a gift from my son. Yesterday, I dropped my phone and the case leaked. I took my phone out of the leaky case, and the fluid dumped on my leg gradually causing a chemical burn. I washed my skin off, but it continued to burn until I went home to shower and put first aid cream on.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (chemical burn) and could have been avoided with a more secure phone case.

incident_description:
Batttery Charger - Lester - EZGO TXT
Ordered on Aug 2, 2017 From Amazon.
When charging it melted the post down into one of the batteries
justification: The incident resulted in damage to property (charger and battery) but no injuries, and while it's possible, it's not likely to happen frequently due to the charger's design.

incident_description: On two separate occasions the port on the side of my MacBook Pro caught fire/started smoking. Both times it happened at the Apple store after experiencing power-up issues at home. After the first time Apple replaced the logic board. The computer died repeatedly (multiple times/day) after that. Power issues started acting up again so I took it back to Apple. Within 15 minutes of plugging it into their adapter, the port caught fire again. (This was a new port, since it was a new logic board.)
justification: Port catching fire is an incident with no injury, and its recurrence with a new logic board makes it possible but not certain.

incident_description:
Ryobi lithium 18v battery evidence over heated with melted plastic around battery post with normal Ryobi tool use.  Had reported same issue to CPSC in 2016 and was contacted by Ryobi rep who deemed that Ryobi blower was possibly at fault rather than battery with blower replaced  by newer model along with battery replacement.  The battery identifying numbers are: P108, 130429075, E206252, CS15454D461827.  
The past battery replaced was the same numbers except for CS15283D510849. 
Do see that a P108 battery was recalled in past for overheating but was a different number (130429028) though appears same issue.
justification: Battery overheating is a recurring issue, as evidenced by the previous recall and replacement, indicating a high likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description: An occupant was charging a cell phone under the pillow and woke up to fire on the pillow. Another occupant came in the room and saw fire in the same area. The cell phone was charging for an unknown length of time.
justification: Fire started due to cell phone charging under pillow, a common cause of electrical fires.

incident_description: On Saturday, November 24 one of my hairstylist at My beauty salon was blow drying someoneÃÂs hair with her blow dryer plugged  into a Belkin  model number BE106001-06RBlk  surge protectors when suddenly a popcorn sound and sparks flying! She tried to unplug the cord and burned her finger. There is no damage to the wires inside of the wall however the  surge protector is completely fried! I have a large beauty salon with the leaven hair stations all of them at this product! My hairstylist is afraid to work at that station again even though I have tried to assure her that it was the search protector!
justification: Injury occurred when hairstylist tried to unplug the cord after a surge protector malfunctioned, indicating a possible recurrence.

incident_description: My daughter had a cell phone case that she fought from walmart. It was a ONN brand. It had glitter inside of it. The case leaked the liquid that contained the glitter out and burners her. I had to take her to the ER to be treated for 1st degree burns.
justification: The incident resulted in 1st degree burns, and while it's not common, it's possible for a cell phone case to leak harmful substances.

incident_description: Tonight our Digital Dynex TV that we had purchased from Best Buy made a loud bang like an explosion and caught fire. We quickly unplugged the TV
justification: The TV catching fire is an incident with potential for injury, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: The rubber edge at the bottom that holds a 14 pound speaker to a mount is not secured to the base of the mount.  This can and did fail.  The speaker then falls from an elevated mounted location, causing potential damage to the speaker and personal injury.
justification: The speaker's unsecured edge increases the likelihood of it falling, posing a high risk of injury.

incident_description:
On April 17, 2018, [REDACTED]'s little 19 month old swallowed a button battery that fell out of a 
Polk Audio SurroundBAR 300 remote. The remote was not manufactured with adequate safety features to prevent easy access to the battery. The child suffered permanent injuries to his esophagus and continues to treat.
justification: The incident resulted in permanent injuries to the child, hence severity level 3. The likelihood is high as the remote lacked adequate safety features, making it easy for a child to access the battery.

incident_description:
Summer Baby Monitor S/N DIA0C  (other tag on monitor shows ÃÂ15072453 EX15110 #29340ÃÂ). Battery overheated and almost exploded. Destroyed the battery and warped the plastic battery compartment on the monitor. 

Battery is 3.7v Li-ion 1480mAh 5.48 Wh #29360-10 S/N JNS180F42502281

IÃÂm concerned that if I hadnÃÂt been as close as I was to this and unplugged it from the wall charger that it could have started a fire, obviously not an ideal scenario when kids are around.
justification: The battery overheating and warping the compartment, along with the potential fire risk, indicates a high likelihood of future incidents.

incident_description: A power strip tripped circuit breaker due to faulty internal wiring.  The power strip was inside a wall unit and I believe it would have caused a fire had the breaker not trip.  Power strip is a cheap model manufactured in China and I would like to try to prevent other people from having a more disastrous outcome for people who live in older homes.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the incident involved a fire hazard due to faulty wiring in a power strip, making it likely to happen again.

incident_description:
Video monitor was used indoors to monitor kids room per instructions.

Over time, the monitor would not long fit in its cradle.  Upon investigation, I could see that the case was cracked.  The battery had expanded to the point that it had cracked the monitor's.  Now, the battery has expanded to the point that it looks like it will vent/explode.
justification: Battery expansion indicates a potential explosion, posing a risk of injury.

incident_description:
I was using a BLACKWEB USB cable purchased at WALMART to charge my [REDACTED]

for no apparent reason, the cable shorted out and burst into flame. The cable was plunged into a surge protector.
My wife burnt her hand trying to unplug the cable, and it also burnt/melted our nylon rug

Cable Model # BWA17W1072
justification: Injury occurred due to the cable shorting out and bursting into flames, causing burns to the wife's hand.

incident_description: I had left my NOAA radio, model WR-111 (Ambient Weather)  plugged in to charge it's battery. A few hours later I heard a bang and found that the battery had exploded out of the radio and on to my floor and was on fire. I blew out the flame on the battery. I am very lucky that I was home and that the battery did not land on something flammable.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident resulted in property damage (burn marks on the floor) and could have been catastrophic if the battery had landed on something flammable.

incident_description:
My Samsung  HDTV had an explosion when I turned it on yesterday

There was a loud bang like a gunshot, then a cracking sound and a smoke cloud.
I immediately turned off the power and later covered it with a towel.
justification: No injuries reported despite the explosion, but the TV was damaged.

incident_description:
I was reaching to turn off alarm and when I touched it a large spark and yellow flame came from the clock. I unplugged it and found the cord burnt at the point where it goes into the radio. see pictures. I contacted Emerson and sent them the radio for analysis. have not received a call back. 
 This is not only a electrical shock risk, it also a fire risk and should be recalled.
justification: While no injury was reported, the incident involved a significant electrical hazard (spark and flame) and a fire risk, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
The submitter noticed a strong burn odor and realized it was coming from the shredder. Upon inspection he noticed the slide switch had melted. He indicated that the shredder was plugged in but it was not being used when the incident occurred. 

He may contact the firm to report the issue.

The submitter said throughout the few months that he had the unit he shredded about 2 cups of coffee worth of paper.

The unit no longer turns on.
justification: The incident resulted in damage to equipment but no injuries, and the likelihood of occurrence is possible given the infrequent use of the shredder.

incident_description: Received information from Amazon.com that the speaker I purchased was in for recall due to potential fire hazard. The only incident is the speaker just stopped working a few weeks ago for  ot reason. Wont take a charge for long and wont connect to devices.
justification: While no injury or fire has occurred, the potential for a fire hazard exists, making it an incident with possible occurrence.

incident_description: The television was functioning normally for about an hour before I heard a loud pop. Immediately after, the screen went dark but for a flame inside the tv behind the screen and drops that were on fire dropping towards the bottom of the screen. The flame looked to be in the middle slightly to the right of the display while the flaming drops were falling to what seemed the very edge of the    Back panel.  The flame inside kept growing until I rushed to shut it off by disconnecting the power supply from the display input.  By then, the smoke began to fill the room and spread throughout the house.  My wife and I opened a window near the tv after making sure the fire was extinguished and stepped outside to allow ventilation of our home.  The smell was very much like burning plastic from electronics to me and my wife.  It was so overwhelming that we had to remain outside for about an hour.  The tv has not been connected to power after the incident.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a fire, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' (Level 2) with a 'Possible' (Level 3) likelihood of reoccurrence due to the commonality of electrical fires.

incident_description: My mother-in-law purchased the Suc It cell phone accessory for me and upon taking it out of the packaging I realized it was not going to suit my needs. She insisted that I try it out and that I may like it, however after 5 minutes of having my phone in this accessory and suction to the front of my smooth microwave door the device came loose and my phone Came Crashing Down onto my stove and then onto my floor. My phone screen shattered as well as the back case on my phone. I immediately contacted the company and they offered to give me $100 towards the repair. When I insisted that they pay for the Full Repair due to the device malfunctioning, I was told at best I will get a refund on the product which was $15. The company states that on the packaging and the disclaimer it says that the company is not responsible for damaged or cracked screens, I was told that this was due to operator error however in no way was I responsible for the suction cup losing suction and falling to the floor. I was upset at the fact that the company did not take any responsibility and instead directed me to the disclaimer. I also found in the disclaimer where it states that they do not recommend using your phone while driving in the second device however it is advertised to do such things. The person I spoke with on the phone also stated that they have three years of experience and that only a handful of phones have been reported to have broken. He continue to insist that it was not the company's fault, but rather my own. I think this is bad business and they should be held responsible when the device does not work as advertised.
justification: Phone screen shattered and back case cracked, no injuries reported.

incident_description: Product was plugged into a 15 amp household 115v outlet (dual). Computer, [REDACTED], light were plugged in. Device was intermittent. When diagnosing the problem noticed burn marks on the hot lead on back of device. Pictures are available. There was also a slight smell of burning plastic but not strong.
justification: Burn marks and smell of burning plastic indicate an electrical issue, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: I purchased a smartphone that, on first use, burned my eardrum and caused damage that led to an infection. the pain on using it was within 20 minutes of use and increased as I used it. As my father has recently died and other family issues have caused me to need to be on the phone for longer periods of time than per usual my ear is very painful. incident_description: My daughter [REDACTED] has an I phone 7 Plus rose colored 32 GB. She has had it for around a year. She has never had problems with it until recently. Over this past weekend she was talking on her phone, ended her call and put her phone in her purse, so she could enter her apartment. She placed the phone in her purse with only her wallet also in there. It is a light wallet and nothing protruding from it. After she entered her apartment she pulled out her phone and went to press the home button and there was a message that read: unable to use Touch ID thumbprint. She also looked closely and saw there was a tiny crack on the home button, but no cracks anywhere else. The only issue up to this point she had been having was that the home button had seemed warmer than normal. Anyway, she switched the phone so that she could use it without the use of the home button. She called and told me there was a tiny crack but nothing else. Yesterday she called me to say not only was the phone hot, it burned her inner arm in the shape of the home button. She had taken a nap and the phone was next to her. Her arm canÃÂt in co tact with the phone and burned her only where the home button was located. Immediately she called me and sent me pics. She called [REDACTED], our provider, and they told her she should not just use insurance or have the home button replaced but instead should contact Apple since there was an injury. She called Apple spoke to a lady who put her in contact with a man named [REDACTED]. He told her they would look into it, asked for pics and said he would confer with people in the engineering department. He contacted further and wanted to see every aspect of the phone. In the end they said even though there was no indention which may have caused the small crack, the point he made to her earlier, but that it was her fault and it can be replaced at her cost. At no time did they put her in contact with the safety department. Then I called. A nice lady looked up the account, saw the pics, and was appalled it was never sent to the safety department. They put me in touch with safety and I was told it needed to be replaced and to discontinue use, it was her fault she was burned because it should not have been next to her and once the engineering department made the decision there was nothing that could be done.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury, and the likelihood of occurrence is high given the phone's overheating and the user's proximity during sleep.

incident_description: Two phones, needed replacing. Cricket did not follow their own policy. Spent money I should not have had to spend. HE said "it has no insurance so you cant use warranty" so I asked him what do I do? He said you will have to buy another phone. I was like WOW ok. SO I paid out 30 bucks for the phone and 25 for the upgrade even tho it was a DOWNGRADE from the phone I had brought in. I had this phone for about a month and it was getting too hot to use, I was charging it up and I went to hold it in my hand and the screen shattered near the earpiece was were it was getting too hot to handle. I tried to call cricket and got no results. I then called the store I bought it at and the manager said "well you have a warranty on your phones the phones warranty is for a year" I said wait if thats the case WHY didnt your sales rep tell me to call warranty and get it exchanged? He said I dont know. I said WHY didnt your sales rep ask me if I wanted insurance when I bought it. HE said I dont know. He took NO responsibility for this. SO NOW I have a LG Harmony that just up and DIED on me for no reason and a LG Fortune that shattered in my hand. HOW does a company state a BATTERY is an accessory when YOU NEED the battery to have the PHONE function?? its not like headphones or a new back cover or anything that you dont really have to have to use the phone..its a BATTERY..something you NEED for the phone and comes WITH the phone..it dont make sense. incident_description:
I have an iphone 8 with a Casemate Rose Gold Glitter Waterfall case. On Friday night, 9/21, I had my iPhone in the waistband of my pants as my pockets were not big enough to fit it. About an hour or so later, I felt as if my skin were burning or as if I was burned by something. The area became really red and really inflamed. I assumed that my phone had heated up and burned me and assumed it were an Apple issue. 
The following day, 9/22, I was working and had my phone in my pocket, not thinking too much about the incident the night before. At one point throughout the day, when the phone was no longer in my pocket, I felt an intense burning sensation near my right pants pocket where my phone once was. After checking my skin, I found another burn that was, and still is, super painful. 
After researching what could have caused this, I saw a recall from last year stating  "The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission announced Monday that certain models of the popular liquid glitter iPhone cases from MixBin electronics are being recalled because the liquid and glitter in the cases can leak, causing skin irritation and burns". Immediately I checked my phone case and sure enough, there is no more liquid in the case, just glitter and beads. I also checked the item on the Casemate website, and the product description states "NOTE: Case-Mate Waterfall cases are certified safe and NOT part of a recent product recall issued by the Consumer Product Safety Commission." I beg to differ. I have two very painful burns that lead me to believe otherwise.
justification: The incident resulted in two painful burns, indicating an injury (severity level 3), and the likelihood of occurrence is high given the recall notice and personal experience (likelihood level 4).

He had the cord plugged into a charger block (with  two prong plug ([REDACTED])).  The [REDACTED] block was plugged into a surge protector.

We got home around 6 pm and I noticed a slight plastic smell in our apartment. I took a walk through the rooms but did not locate the smell. 
About an hour later, my son walked into his room, and immediately told me that he smelled "smoke or something hot" and it was very strong  in his room.  Again I walked into the room and I could also smell it very strongly. I walked over to where his surge protector was, and went to check the plugs, and I burnt my hand on the exposed USB connector that had melted the cord right off of it.  I immediately cut the power by turning the surge protector OFF.  I was able to unplug that [REDACTED] block with the end of the cord still in it. incident_description: My company ([REDACTED]) ordered a batch of 30 Dell Latitude 7390 notebook computers in the April 2018,  of that thirty 18 have burned up catastrophically. incident_description:
I have a Dell computer laptop, model type lnspiron 15 7000 2-in-1, with an external power supply converting 120volts to a lower voltage. The power supply has 2 power and 1 ground pins.

One day in August 2018, I received a nasty shock from the pc while using it in normal conditions.

I removed the plug from the laptop and measured the voltage on the external pin and found it to be about 50 volts ac.

I discovered that the Ground connection between the wall outlet and my extension cord was broken.

THIS MEANS THAT IF THE GROUND PIN OF A RECEPTACLE IS BROKEN, A SERIOUS HAZARD EXISTS.

This information was reported to Dell, but the best they offered me is another power supply unit, which seems to have
the same issue-based on my measurements.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (electric shock) and the likelihood of it happening again is high due to the widespread issue with the power supply.

incident_description:
I own a Fellowes PS60C-2 paper shredder.  I don't use it too much these days but I use to use it for light home office duties and have loved it.  I've owned this shredder for maybe 6 or 7 years (honestly, I forget exactly when I had bought it). That was annoying but not that big of a deal.  

The other night, I was woken up in the middle of the night by an odd sound.  It roused me out of bed and I found that the shredder had spontaneously turned itself on, the motor was running and it was beginning to overheat and smoke.  I worry that had I not heard the noise that it might have caught on fire!!  I'm now afraid to even have it plugged in for fear that it's going to burn my house down!

incident_description:
On August 3, 2018, my 2-year-old Samsung S7 cell phone was on my night stand, plugged in and charging overnight. At 1:00 AM, it began shaking. As I woke up and looked over, the phone began hissing, emitting smoke, and spontaneously caught fire. A 5-inch flame shot from the phone and it took off like a rocket from my nightstand. The power cord pulled it back, and fortunately it fell into a waste basket. Still on fire and billowing smoke, I grabbed the waste basket and dumped the contents into my bathroom sink, now filling with water to extinguish the fire. 

I did nothing out of the ordinary to this phone for it's entire lifetime, simply charging it and using it each day. The power cord in use at the time was the one that came with the phone. I am informing your agency about this product safety concern for obvious reasons, as you need to know that Samsung cell phones still have this issue occuring today, August 2018. It is a serious public safety concern.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and the likelihood of occurrence is high given the recent date of the incident and the widespread use of Samsung S7 phones.
