incident_description:
Close to a year ago I purchased a OnePlus 5T cellular smartphone from the company OnePlus. Since owning this phone I started to notice randomly the phone getting very hot during charging and sometimes even during normal usage. However, since it comes with its own fast charging adapter and cord, I just chalked it up as normal. However, 4 days ago as this issue has been worsening randomly, I went to go get my phone after I had charged it, as I had been turning it off while charging to try to mitigate the issue, likewise I had not reported anything because it did not seem to affect the functioning of the phone. This is where things get scary, I went to go get my phone, and I looked down at it and seeing there was a white bluish hue Circle in the middle of the screen, I thought maybe something had got on the screen, I went to grab the phone and it was so hot, it would burn your finger to touch it, so I very quickly grabbed a sock off the floor which is the first thing I could find and unplugged it and took it downstairs in our basement and left it for a little while.

Upon returning, after calling a friend and telling him about it on my wife's phone, he told me quote; "[REDACTED] be careful, I just read a story about those phones exploding!ÃÂ I about freaked out, so I told him that I had had it for close to a year, and it seems like it's gotten worse, and worse, when charging, and sometimes during normal use. He told me I should call customer service immediately.

I called customer support for OnePlus after sending them a tweet on [REDACTED], and the operator made me feel much better as she told me they have had no incidents of phones, getting hot and exploding, and said that she was going to send me an email and start a troubleshooting ticket on the issue, which needless to say made me feel much much better.

So today, I called my friend, who is [REDACTED] certified, and works in network Administration, who actually sent me the link of the story, where I saw the pictures of the exact model of my phone, clearly and separate pieces charred all in black, showing obviously where the phone had exploded similar to the pictures I had saw when [REDACTED] had their issues, needless to say I cannot begin to tell you how upset, and scared it made me, to find out they had clearly lied to me.

I do not know what to do at this point, as the company is headquartered in China, however someone told me that they also have a US headquarters, and then I should likewise contact the FCC and FTC, which I plan on doing, if there's anything, or anyway you can help me it would be much appreciated as I naturally I'm concerned, to say the least
justification: Phone overheating and potential explosion poses immediate risk of injury.

incident_description:
Good Morning,

I am writing to report a safety concern on behalf of clients, [REDACTED].  My clients recently had a ductless air conditioning unit installed at their home by a trusted contractor.  The contractor installed a surge protector manufactured by Sycom Surge, Inc, model number SYC-120/240-T2.  On Sunday, April 21, 2018, the surge protector started on fire during normal use of the A/C unit.   The fire department was called to my clients' home.  Thankfully, [REDACTED] rushed to the circuit box in the residence and turned off the particular circuit to the surge protector.   According to the fire department, had the [REDACTED] not been home and taken this immediate action, their home could have become fully engulfed and destroyed.

The contractor was contacted, who then began to conduct research on the particular surge protector that was used.  Apparently, UL had issued a warning in 2016 that this particular Sycom unit may constitute a fire hazard and was not UL approved.   Fraudulent UL approved stickers appear on these units.  (I have the warning)

In checking the Sycom web site, where you can purchase this unit, despite the UL warning, Sycom is still advertising these units as UL approved and lists the UL seal on its web site. (I have the printout of the item).

When my client contacted Sycom to inquire about the faulty surge protector, Sycom offered to pay my client (without specifying for what or an amount), in exchange for return of the unit.    My clients have declined the offer.  They are in the process of obtaining quotes for the damage to their home. 

There has been at least one litigation case in the US District Court for the District of Maryland ([REDACTED]) in which a faulty surge protector manufactured by Sycom was alleged to have been the cause of a home fire

Something is seriously wrong here.

[REDACTED], Esquire
 
[REDACTED]
         
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a significant risk of property damage and potential injury, given the fire's destructive potential.

I believe the oily substance slowly leaked into my jeans causing 2nd degree burns on my right thigh.  So even when I removed the phone, it continued to make the burn worse. incident_description:
At 2:15AM the battery in my Toshiba Portege R830 laptop exploded. The noise woke my fiancee up and she woke me up. There was a roughly 6 inch stream of fire shooting out the back of the laptop. The laptop was upside down, unplugged form the charger, and it was in sleep mode. I had been using it previously up until about 12:15AM that night. Thankfully my fiancee had a full water bottle and was able to put the fire out with that. After the fire was out initially, it restarted again right away and needed to be doused with water a second time. After that, my fiancee threw it in the sink and started running cold water on it. About 3 minutes later we took it outside and it was smoking and sizzling for about an hour after that.

Our apartment was filled with smoke and reeked of burned plastic. We had property damage in addition to the value of the laptop. Our upstairs neighbor woke up and heard all the commotion and the fire alarm. We called the fire department and they came out but there wasn't anything for them to do.

I had a cut on my finger from using the fire extinguisher (it was one of the Kiddie fire extinguishers that was recalled, and it did not work); my fiancee had minor singed hairs on her leg. Psychologically, we were extremely shaken: I had panic attacks that night for the first time in my life; we were nervous and easily scared for a few days after; even still today when I have a phone call about the case, I get stressed.

I contacted Toshiba about it promptly and they were initially receptive but eventually denied responsibility for the fire and stated that this is not one of the batteries affected (even though, based on the serial number and the recall notice 17-064, it is). I kept pushing them and now their insurance company is involved and the battery and my laptop are being inspected by Panasonic. I figure it has been about 6 weeks now since Panasonic received the battery and laptop and they have not provided an update yet.

Toshiba's handling of this case has been dismal given that people's safety is at risk.
justification: Injuries occurred (minor burns and panic attacks) despite the fire being extinguished promptly.

incident_description:
Dear Consumer Protection,

I recently bought an Avantek WN-1B white noise machine. Last night within seconds of plugging the machine in we found our 18 month old son with the USB cord in his hand, and the USB plug had come apart with a simple tug leaving exposed metal prongs extending from the wall outlet. This is clearly an extreme hazard for both electrocution and fire. I have recreated the condition using an unplugged extension cord for illustration.  (photos available but not able to be attached here).

Upon examination, the USB adapter can come apart by either pulling on the USB cord while plugged into the wall, or by pushing on the USB cord which pushes all the internal part out of the casing
The exposed prongs are live, extend from the casing, and are easily contacted.  Without rapid reaction on our part this could have lead to tragedy. This is such an extreme hazard I believe it needs to be acted on rapidly. I can make the USB adapter and sound machine available for examination.
justification: The exposed live prongs pose a high risk of electrocution, especially for young children, making an injury likely.

incident_description:
Laptop Battery exploded and started a house fire. Report below is available: 

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Fire Investigator [REDACTED] delivered the evidence for the above loss [REDACTED]
Berkeley office on September 6, 2017. The following items, identified per chain of
possession, were collected from the residence at the above loss location:
DP-#1) HP laptop CPU and charger
DP-#1a) Laptop battery
DP-#1b) Charger and debris from fire
DP-#1c) Sprinkler head
[REDACTED] of [REDACTED] inspected the evidence on September 13, 2017. The
evidence was non-destructively examined visually and through radiographic imaging. Scene
photographs were also reviewed. Based on the non-destructive examination and the review
of scene photographs, the most likely ignition source for this fire loss is the energy released
from the HP laptop battery pack. There are several possible causes of failure of these
batteries including: manufacturing defect, overheating, overcharging (of specific cells), or
mechanical damage to the battery cells.
This brief does not intend to fully outline my investigation. At your direction, a more
detailed report will be provided. Select photographs and radiographic images are embedded
in the body of the report. Additional photographs and radiographic images will remain in my
file and will be available upon request.
[Redacted] Page Claim 2 # [REDACTED]
LABORATORY SUMMARY
DP-#1) HP Laptop CPU and Charger:
Photo 1: Photo depicting the incident laptop and charger remains from DP-#1.
This evidence item consisted of an HP Pavilion g6 laptop and HP laptop charger. The
charger exhibited directional and external damage. The wall side cord was severed just after
exiting the A/C to D/C converter box. This severed wire had beads on th e stranded copper
conductors consistent with an electrical arc suggesting that the charger was plugged into an
electrical outlet. It is unknown at this time if the other end of the charger was connected to
the laptop. A radiographic image of the charger
Photo 2 (left) and 3 (right): Photos depicting the charger remains from DP-#1.
Photo 3 shows the beaded electrical conductors on the severed wall side cord of the charger.
[Redacted] Page Claim 3 # [REDACTED]
The laptop appears to have been closed during the fire. Most of the damage is concentrated
at the battery compartment at the bottom rear of the laptop and to the left side of the screen.
Additionally, there is a section on the bottom of the laptop, remote from the battery
compartment, which appears to have peeled open from heat. There are pieces of copper foil
stuck to the bottom of the laptop which appear to have been ejected from a lithium -ion
battery. These battery ejections could have caused the peeled open section on the bottom of
the laptop. A radiogr
the laptop. The laptop batteries were not included in this evidence item.
Photo 4: Photo depicting the bottom of the incident laptop from DP-#1.
DP-#1a) Laptop Battery:
Photo 5: Photo depicting the lithium-ion battery array from evidence item DP-#1a.
This evidence item contains six 18650 sized lithium-ion batteries connected in series which
were in turn connected to a small printed circuit board. The size of this ba ttery array appears
[Redacted] Page Claim 4 # [REDACTED]
consistent with the size of the battery compartment of the laptop from DP-#1. The positive
terminal end caps from two of these batteries were missing along with a portion of their
internal contents. A radiographic image of these batteries revealed that the density of the
two batteries with the missing end caps was far less than the density of the remaining four
batteries, which confirms that a portion of the internals of those two batteries were ejected.
Photo 6: Photo depicting the missing end caps from two of lithium-ion battery array from
evidence item DP-#1a.
Image 1: Radiographic image depicting the lithium-ion battery array from evidence item DP-#1a.
Note the two batteries on the left with significantly lower density and missing end caps.
[Redacted] Page Claim 5 # [REDACTED]
DP-#1b) Charger and Debris from Fire:
Photo 7 (left) and 8 (right): Photos depicting the debris from evidence item DP-#1b.
This evidence item contained the remains of a three-conductor power cord and a various fire
debris. Upon review of the scene photographs, the power cord serviced a soldering iron that
as reportedly not plugged in at the time of the fire. Melted plastic on the distal end of the
cord suggests indeed that it was not plugged in at the time of the fire. Among the debris of
this evidence item were pieces of the laptop monitor, bits of copper foil, and other pieces
from the laptop. The pieces of copper foil are most likely part of the internal components
ejected from the lithium-ion batteries from DP-#1a.
DP-#1c) Sprinkler Head:
Photo 9: Photo depicting the sprinkler head from evidence item DP-#1c.
[Redacted] Page Claim 6 # [REDACTED]
This evidence item contained a sprinkler head. This sprinkler head appears to have activated.
The sprinkler head also exhibited signs of mechanical damage most likely caused by fire
department overhaul and/or evidence collection. This sprinkler head was rated for 160ÃÂ° F.
CONCLUSION
Based on a non-destructive examination of the evidence collected from this loss and the
scene photographs, the mostly likely cause of the fire in this case is a fault or failure of the
HP lithium-ion battery pack leading to the ejection of the contents of two of the battery cells
and the combustion of the HP laptop.
A search of the Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) website revealed that there
are three separate recalls for HP Pavilion battery packs, two of which had been expanded in
their scope (one was expanded twice). Because of the damage to the battery pack identifying
information, it is unclear at this time if the battery pack was included in one of these recalls
or their expansions.
Recommendations:
[REDACTED] recommends performing destructive testing on the evidence collected in
this case to further refine the ignition scenario hypothesis. In addition, [REDACTED]
will be placing HP on notice of this loss and inviting them to have their own expert attend
the destructive testing.
Our assessment of this case is based on an analysis of the physical evidence and an
evaluation of all possible causes. Please do not hesitate to contact our office if you have any
questions or if we can be of further assistance.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and the cause was a battery failure, which is likely to occur again given the recall history of similar batteries.

incident_description:
A ten-foot extension cord purchased about a year ago started melting at its receiving end.

The cord was purchased from Harbor Freight in San Antonio, TX. It has black plastic connectors with an orange cord and carries a ground wire.

The cord was in regular use until last night. I noticed the smell of burning plastic after turning on an electric heater that was plugged in to it. I used the same heater and cord last winter.

Assuming the smell was from the heater and it was operating normally, I ignored the smell at first. After about an hour, I got a headache and turned the heater off in response. The odor dissipated. 

I turned it back on about 45 minutes later and noticed the smell again. I discovered the smell was the strongest near my bed's headboard, so I pulled the bed frame and mattresses away from the headboard. The extension cord was directly under where my head lays as I sleep under the box spring.

I saw the cord and its black plastic connector was melting on to the end of the other cord. It was very hot to the touch as I pulled them apart. One of the prongs of the cord plugged into the end of the cord had melted black plastic on it as a result of pulling the two cords apart.

I measured the temperature within five minutes with an IR thermometer which read 150 degrees F. I had to scrape the melted black plastic off the prong of the other cord as it was completely covered by melted plastic, preventing it from carrying electricity.

I photographed the cord and the thermometer reading.

I continue to use the same heater without a problem. The cord is noticeably melted at its connector and the orange sheath is permanently bent just below where it connects to the black connector.
justification: The cord's melting posed a fire risk, but no injury occurred.

My hand and my fingers immediately began to burn from extreme heat. I finally took it to my husband to make sure I wasn't imagining things and he confirmed that the battery was extremely hot.  I finally decided to put the battery outside where it was about 40 degrees.  Then I put it in a ceramic bowl outside since out deck railing is wood..  It is cool right now but I am afraid to bring it in the house or put it in the trash since I am sure it would heat up again and cause a fire.  This battery is really hot.
justification: The incident resulted in burns to the individual's hand and fingers, classifying it as an injury event, and the likelihood of occurrence is high given the common use of battery packs and decorations.

incident_description:
On Friday, December 8th  2017 at ~ 5:40 PM Eastern Standard Time my daughter, who was working on a college paper, screamed to me that her Microsoft Surface Book was smoking and sparking.  I ran into the room and immediately unplugged it.  Upon a closer look, I could see where the power supply wires were frayed and the Surface had a burn mark. 

This was extremely concerning as my daughter narrowly escaped being burned (the Surface was in her lap when the unit started smoking and burning) or when unattended the Surface Book could have caught my house on fire.  Note:  The Surface Book was purchased in 2017 and is only 7 months old.

This does not appear to be an isolated incident because if you go on Microsoft's website under Microsoft Store - [  https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/store/d/surface-book-power-supply-unit/920j5rj42kd6?activetab=pivot%3areviewstab#ratings-reviews  ] there are numerous reviews  about this specific power supply with frayed wires.  Further, there is even a history of faulty power supplies with a similar product as Microsoft issued a recall for the Surface Pro power supplies in 2016.

I truly believe my family dodged a bullet here in terms of my daughter not getting burned and/or my house being set on fire.  I think the pictures are pretty telling as to the danger these power supplies pose.

I am reporting this product because a) there is clearly a defect in the power supply as evidenced by the multiple reported occurrences b) I would hope you agree there is a safety issue and begin to take appropriate action so as to mitigate any additional fire hazards or tragedies for other families.

Of noteworthiness:  Microsoft refuses to replace this unit with a new one and wants to give me a unit that was already defective and refurbished.  I am currently disputing their position given the unit was only 7 months old (under a one year warranty) and how close we came to avoiding a real tragedy.
justification: The incident resulted in no injuries but had the potential for serious harm, and there is a high likelihood of recurrence given the history of similar issues.

incident_description:
Review for VideoSecu TV Wall Mount Tilt Low Profile Ultra Slim Television Mount Bracket for Most 26"- 47" LED LCD Plasma TV, Some up to 55" TV with VESA 200x100 to 400x400 1FE; Model
Really thought this mount was okay at first. SO WRONG! Almost lost our brand new 55 inch UHD TV with 400x400 VESA mounting. Probably would have worked fine with VESA 300x300 or smaller pattern.
Mounted the hanging rail on the wall. I found screws that met the VESA 400x400 standard for length, and attached the brackets to the back of my 55" [REDACTED] TV. With help, I hung the TV on the rail, sliding the right side bracket top hook all the way to the right stop before lowering the left bracket onto the rail. I started attaching the interface cables when the left end of the TV suddenly dropped! I held the right end of the TV while my wife jumped up to stabilize the left end.
Took it down and analyzed it; it seems that the mounting hooks on the brackets when attached to my TV were positioned about 1/8 inch too wide, wider than the distance between the horizontal rail stops that prevent the TV from sliding off an end; distance between the mounting hooks of the brackets is set by bracket design and distance between VESA compliant mountings on the TV; no consumer adjustments are available
No injuries or property damage, but the potential for both existed.

Manufacturer	VideoSecu
ASIN	B0019D6H2M
Item model number	MP409B

Sold by "Warehouseseller" (Amazon Storefront) and Fulfilled by Amazon
justification: The incident involved a near-miss where the TV could have fallen, potentially causing property damage or injury, but no actual damage or injuries occurred.

incident_description: Last night we had an incident with my 2012 HP pavilion. My husband and I were sleeping when our cat started banging on the door. This only happens in the morning when we're waking up, so we ignored it. The second time I heard a loud noise. I got up, opened the door and saw light coming from our living room. I hurried down there and my laptop was on fire. I ran to the laptop, grabbed a blanket that was thankfully on the couch right next to it, and started hitting the laptop with it to stop the fire, I then wrapped the laptop with the blanket, unplugged it and told my husband to open our back door, because it started to smoke really bad, and I placed it outside. My husband then told me to hurry back in our room because I am 19 weeks pregnant and didn't want the smoke to harm the baby, he then proceeded to the place where the laptop had been, and the battery had stuck to the carpet. When he removed it from the carpet it caught on fire in his hand, so he hurried and took it outside. Thankfully only the patch of carpet where the laptop had been is damaged. The burn went straight through the carpet and it is black. My husband placed baking soda on top of the burned patch, just for precaution. Apart from inhaling a lot of smoke, none of us got burned. We have never had problems with this computer in the past. When it overheats it turns itself off, which is exactly what it's supposed to do. It should have done that this time too.
justification: While no one was injured, the incident caused significant property damage and could have escalated if not quickly contained.

incident_description: We have a 65 inch Sony Bravia television that was mounted on the wall. The television began to have vertical lines and ghosting on the screen while we were watching it.  After a short while the ghosting went away but the vertical lines continued. I turned the TV off and turned in for the night. The next morning, December 10, 2017, I noticed that the left lower portion of the TV had melted from obvious heat source. At that time I contacted Sony regarding this issue. Sony sent a technician out on December 14, 2017 to evaluate our TV. After the technician's evaluation, he stated that we should not use the TV because it was dangerous and posed a fire hazard. We followed up with Sony a week or so after the technician's evaluation. Sony's representative stated that our case has been forwarded to the National Customer Relations office for response. Sony's representative continued to say due to the fact that our unit was diagnosed with Physical Damage, Sony will not be able to honor its warranty and that Sony was unable to assist us with the repair/exchange. We requested a copy of the technician's report but Sony declined our request. During weeks of corresponding with Sony's representatives, one requested photos from us of the damage TV because Sony had no photos on record from the technician. We emailed photos of our TV to Sony. On January 26, 2018 a Sony's representative called me, [REDACTED], and said our case was being closed and Sony would not be able to assist us any further because the TV is more than a year old. The purchase date of our TV is 2/24/2016.
justification: The TV posed a fire hazard, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: We have a 50" Samsung LED TV, Model UN50F6300AF, Serial: Z6WF3CCDA00946E. A couple days ago we noticed vertical lines that ran across the screen, fading the picture in and out. Then today the screen went black. Upon examination, we noticed a spot on the screen in the lower right hand corner that was white. The plastic frame in that same area was extremely hot and it appeared the plastic was melting there as well. We have called Samsung and reported the incident. A customer service rep told us they are turning our case over to product liability and we are awaiting a call from that department.
justification: The TV's physical damage and potential fire hazard pose a risk, but no injuries have been reported.

I have saved the TV in a storage closet in case anyone wants to examine it.  This seems to me to be an extremely dangerous situation, and I am lucky that the sparks coming out the bottom did not start a fire.

I have these speakers: Vizio SB3651-E6 36" 5.1 Channel SmartCast Soundbar System connected via HDMI cable to the HDMI ARC port of a TCL-branded TV (Model 55P605). When the speakers are left in the "on" position, with the input device turned off (i.e., that's the TV in the "off" position, which actually leaves it in a sort of "stand-by" mode), there have been at least three separate occasions now (the first being on 01/03/2018 and the last being today, 01/26/2018) that the speakers have given off an EXTREMELY loud, and very high-pitched sound that has lasted from between 10 to 20 seconds. The sound is so loud that it fills the whole house, and it is almost impossible to figure out where it is coming from. The last episode, which occurred today while I was sitting in a room upstairs from the unit, has left my ears ringing (they are still ringing and this happened a few hours ago). The noise is definitely damaging to hearing.
Aside and relevant: Through a very brief internet search, I found another person who reports a similar occurrence with this specific Vizio model. incident_description:
We bought three generic USB cords for Apple IPhones at a local discount store in Fairview Heights, IL called Five Below.  Initially they seemed okay but we soon realized that the phone end was getting dangerously hot on two of them.  I am an electrical engineer and intimately familiar with how this kind of stuff works.  It was not the phone and not the charger.  We very quickly isolated it to the phone ends of the two cords.  Please do not waste my time with a lot of dumb questions.  I'm saving you time and telling you what the problem was.

We were not injured but feel we were lucky to detect it before any harm was done to the phone, the charger, the house or the cars.  It was hot enough that I think prolonged contact with most combustibles could have led to a fire under the right circumstances.  The connector and boot on the phone end of at least one cord shows subtle but clear evidence of deformation by melting.

Unfortunately, we don't have the box or the receipts or anything.  The only markings on the cable are the usual USB icon.  I can send you the cables if you wish.  But if you want to know anything about them I think you will have to call Five Below and ask them about what they might have sold to us in August in Fairview Heights.  We don't recall how many colors were offered in the brand/model we chose but we got one white, one pink and one blue.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a potential fire hazard due to overheating USB cords, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' scenario.

incident_description:
Our golf cart needed new lead-acid batteries, so the company that sold the cart to us, and continues to provide maintenance support, suggested we install six 8-volt batteries instead of the four 12-volt batteries that needed replacing.

While charging, potentially dangerous hydrogen gas is produced that made our carbon monoxide detector a floor above the cart garage alarm. Readings of 300 ppm were obtained in our house. When the detector was placed upon the batteries, the detector max'd out at 999 ppm.

I called the fire department, and their more sophisticated measuring device measured, and alarmed.
They said that firefighters will evacuate a building if hydrogen is measured above 50 ppm!

My cart company never received a complaint before about this, and didn't necessarily understand the gravity of the situation, but hydrogen gas had been escaping into my house for weeks!
justification: Hydrogen gas leakage from batteries posed a significant risk, with readings up to 999 ppm, although no injuries were reported.

incident_description: I had my iPhone on my lap which had the glitter iPhone case on it. I started to feel a terrible burning sensation on my leg. I went to the bathroom and noticed a very large burn/welt on my leg. I couldn't figure out what had caused the burn because it was as if it was spontaneous until I looked at my phone case and it was cracked, leaking out the liquid which was what caused the burn. The burn and pain were so severe that I could not wear clothing on the area for a week. I had to constantly apply burn ointment as well.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe burn requiring ointment and preventing clothing wear for a week, hence severity level 3. The occurrence was likely due to a cracked phone case, which is possible but not common, hence occurrence likelihood 3.

I have since had to get a new device due to fluid damage, but since I am seeing this recall information on the Victoria's Secret site, I am reporting this incident now.

incident_description:
My grandson was charging his new 10.1" FLEX tablet for [REDACTED] (Insignia) with the cord included with the tablet.  When he went to unplug it it was very hot and smoking.  He screamed, "something is on fire".  I ran to him, smelled the pungent smell of burning plastic, and quickly unplugged the charger cord from the wall.  Once it cooled enough to touch, we could see that the plug into the computer was melted and its shape was distorted.  On the tablet itself, where it plugged in, the plastic was also melted.

We later attempted to charge the tablet with another plug, but it no longer will charge.  We even re-tried the melted charger, but it would not charge the tablet.

My grandson was terrified by this incident (he is 6) and is devastated by the loss of his best Christmas gift.  I have contacted the company, www.insigniaproducts.com and am waiting for the receipt from his aunt in order to replace the tablet.  However, I believe this is serious enough to report to you in order to prevent potential fires, burns and even deaths.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident involved a fire hazard and resulted in a damaged product, causing distress to the child.

incident_description: Nyko charge station for the WiiU was charging the wiiu controllers. Happened to walk by the unit in the morning and smelled burning plastic. Then saw smoke coming out of the Nyko charge station. Quickly unplugged it and took outdoors. If I were not there, it would have caught on fire and burned the house down. Only the Nyko charge station was affected.
justification: Smoke and burning plastic indicate a fire risk, which could have spread if not noticed.

incident_description: I was plugging my phone (Moto G4) in to charge.  I use the cord provided with my phone which includes a cord with a mini-USB end to go into the phone and a USB side that plugs into a converter box and the provided converter box has a USB inlet for the cord-side and the prongs which plug into the wall.  (I apologize that my technical vocabulary is lacking.) The converter box seems to have some sort of "turbo" effect as it makes the phone charge quickly. I already had my phone attached to the cord and the cord plugged into the converter box.  As I plugged the prongs into the wall outlet (barely the tips were in), a giant yellow-white spark occurred between the outlet and prongs. I instinctively pulled back and noticed the metal prongs were covered in black "soot" (probably oxidation caused by the high current), and the plastic immediately around the prongs was discolored and shinier than the rest of the box. The tongs were warm but I was able to touch them within a few seconds. Also, the outlet no longer had power as the spark had tripped the circuit breaker, but it reset fine. My phone didn't seem harmed. I have not tried using the converter box since; instead I am using a non-turbo converter which takes longer but doesn't pose a hazard.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a significant electrical hazard, with a spark and evidence of heat damage, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
Vizio Sound bar (Model SB3851-D0) was in use with [REDACTED] television. Television audio out was sent to the sound bar unit via an optical cable. When going to adjust the volume on the unit itself, an electric discharge between the user and the unit occurred. Arc was severe enough to cause pain in entire right arm and through the left side of jaw, through teeth and into tongue. Sensitivity in jaw and tongue persists 24 hours later (at time of this report).

Ran speakers diagnostic test and speakers continue to function, but the optical channel is completely unresponsive. Ran additional test with auxiliary input (7 mm audio cable), and unit functions, but with persistent audible whine.

Upon contacting manufacturer for investigation of safety hazard, Vizio requests return of the device and offers replacement with new unit. Will not honor a full refund (within 1 year warranty).
justification: User experienced pain and persistent sensitivity due to an electric discharge from the sound bar, indicating a severe incident with potential injury.

incident_description: A local fire Chief reported that his adult daughter purchased a replacement battery online for her Apple MacPro laptop. She later discovered that the battery had expanded and distorted the plastic casing of the laptop. No fire was caused in the incident and no one was injured.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the incident involved a potentially hazardous product (expanding battery) and thus merits a severity level of 2.

incident_description: I purchased 2 different phone cases from Victoria Secret for my iPhone. The first one started leaking and I purchased another as I loved them and they wear georgous. I am sad to hear this about them.
justification: The incident of the phone case leaking is an isolated event, but it's possible that other cases from the same batch could also leak.

incident_description:
The product is a Samsung Galaxy S7 Edge cell phone battery which grew extremely hot to the touch and swelled the case out on the phone while laying on a table.  It was not being charged at the time.  

We took the phone to Sprint and they referred us to another store an hour from here that repairs phones.  Their tech said the battery "exploded" and said that by law he could not return the defective battery to us.  He wrote out a statement and gave us a receipt for the repair ($80.62)  We were also told that Samsung would reimburse us for the cost of the battery replacement since the phone was only 5 months old.  Samsung said they would not reimburse us without seeing the old battery which is not possible.  

I am aware that other types of Samsung phones have had battery issues and were recalled, including versions of the Samsung 7.  I was told that the Edge was safe.  I now know it is not.  I am just grateful it did not burn down my house.
justification: The battery swelling and heat indicate an incident, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
This is the 2nd incident that we reported to me. I have previously reported this to you via this website. 

We have had several 9V Interstate batteries fail. None have started fires. One did slightly injure an employee when it failed in his pocket. This was the case I reported to you earlier. The electrodes on the top of several of the batteries in different locations around the country are blowing off in some sort of small explosion/reaction.
justification: Employee injury occurred in the past due to battery failure, and the likelihood of similar incidents is high given the repeated failures.

incident_description: I own a case-mate waterfall cel phone case. It is 8 months old. During a baseball game, I placed my phone (with case) under my leg for a few minutes. Later that night, I began feeling a burning on my skin in the same area. When I was able to investigate, I noticed a large hot and red mark on my leg. The case has lost most of the liquid inside of it. It has been two days since the incident and my leg is still hot and red however it has not gotten worse. I contacted case-mate and they maintain that the product is safe. They did offer to send me a new case (the same kind). When I refused that offer, they offered to send me a different case up to $50.
justification: Skin burn injury occurred due to heat retention in the phone case, though not severe enough to cause lasting damage.

incident_description: Sony Xperia Z Ultra mobile phone started experiencing bulging battery ~1 month ago.  Battery has expanded to the point that rear cover of phone pushed off.  Think this is a safety issue.
justification: Battery bulging poses a potential safety risk, but no injuries reported yet.

incident_description: I plugged in my Ambient Weather WR-334-U Emergency Solar Hand Crank Weather Alert Radio, Flashlight, Siren, Smart Phone Charger into my electrical outlet in my house with the provided AC adapter before going to bed to let it charge. When I awoke in the morning I found the rechargeable battery had exploded. When I checked online for a replacement battery I learned about the recall.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage (exploded battery) but no injuries, and the likelihood of occurrence is possible given the product recall.

incident_description:
(07/28/2017) The consumer stated that the charger was plugged into the wall. When the charger was pulled out of the outlet, the plastic housing came apart. exposing the prongs in the outlet.

The consumer did not know how long the charger had been in the outlet. The charger was not connected to the phone.

(07/28/2017) The consumer contacted the firm and was advised that there was a 14-day guarantee on accessories.
justification: The incident resulted in no injury but could have caused one if the exposed prongs had come into contact with a conductive object.

incident_description:
I purchased a retractable cord reel from Harbor Freight www.harborfreight.com at a retail store in Atlanta. I installed and used it, but discovered it didn't on several of my tools. I used an electrical circuit tester and discovered that the Hot and Neutral on the unit were reversed. I double check the incoming circuit and it was properly wired. Hot and neutral reversed can cause electrical shock on some devices. I informed the company of the problem with the equipment. They said there was no recall on it, and only offered to replace it if it was less than 90 days old. I was not, nor was anyone else hurt, this is just a dangerous product defect.

part number 61558 retractable cord reel

[REDACTED]
Product Support
Harbor Freight Tools
P.O. Box 6010
Camarillo, CA 93011
Phone: 1.888.866.5797
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the reversed hot and neutral wires pose a significant risk of electrical shock.

incident_description: My TV was bought in a Walmart 02 \ 05 \2017. Several days ago the TV was switched on, I was in the next room. Suddenly I heard a loud bang. When I ran into the living room, I saw a smoking TV and a broken screen. In this room in the children's arena my 8-month-old granddaughter, who was very frightened and only miraculously did not suffer from the scattered sharp fragments . Besides, my house could catch fire and we could die. I contact VIZIO. VIZIO refuses to repair or replace.
justification: Although no one was injured, the incident could have resulted in injury or fire, hence a severity level of 2.

incident_description: I purchased galaxy note 7 on November 2017 at a Verizon store ,,I asked the seller if it was safe to use because of the recalls ,,he assured me it was safe ,I used it for at least 3 mths ,,was unable to use it because I changed cartiers. On November 29 2017 I was unpacking my things from a box sitting on my couch ,I found my galaxy 7 & as I picked it up from out of the box I accidentally dropped it ,,I reached to pick it up I saw sparks coming from the phone & I dropped ,,it burned my finger a like bit ,,it immediately started smoking & was on fire ! The fumes were so strong & the sme was intense ,!I poured water ,which only made the smoke stronger ! I was having trouble breathing because of the smoke & fumes but didn't want apt to catch fire ! Luckly I have time floors ,I was able to Finney put the fire out using a broom ,I did call Samsung to report it .but haven't heard back I am still traumatized from the incident!
justification: Injury occurred due to phone catching fire, likelihood is possible given the history of Samsung Galaxy Note 7 recalls.

incident_description: A plug extender started making a sparking sound so my husband got up and saw the plug melting. He had his laptop plugged in to it.
justification: The incident involved a sparking plug extender, which could have caused a fire, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
I was not aware of the recall for Toshiba laptops due to faulty batteries. 
My laptop was 6 years old, still working OK except for the short battery life and for the occasional overheating while charging. I didn't use it very often, so this time that I did, it needed system updates. I left it in my office with the power cord plugged in so it could run the updates and went home for the night, thinking it would simply power down or sleep once it was finished. I came in the next morning to find it toasted/melted with a mess around it indicating the battery had exploded. Luckily no one was injured and the fire self-extinguished with just the table and few unimportant items around it left damaged. I don't want to think what would have happened if it had set furniture and other computers around it on fire!
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident resulted in property damage, highlighting the potential severity of such events.

incident_description:
We utilize a touchscreen kiosk for a visitor management system. We initially utilized the Pipo P1 tablet as our tablet. Once the P1 was discontinued, we used the Pipo P1+. Out of 278 tablets we purchased, 66 burst when the battery swelled and warped the enclosure - and our expectation is that many more would have had problems if we had not pulled them from the field and retired them. We pulled the tablets out of our customer locations and have them stored in our warehouse. We have contacted the company and they do not seem concerned about the danger or our financial hit due to their defective product. They only offer to take the tablets back and repair them. Most are well beyond repair but we couldn't use them anyway due to the danger. We have replaced all of them with a competitor's tablets and have had no issues at any customer locations. 
The information below regarding dates and locations should be as follows: 
Incident Date: 2016 and 2017
Incident location: In more than a dozen states
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the incident involved a significant number of defective tablets, posing a potential safety hazard.

incident_description: I received a replacement phone cover from casemate. The product was from their waterfall collection. The company advertises mineral oil as what suspends the glitter and gems in the case. On 10/23/17, the fluid leaked from the case leaving me with a large chemical burn to the lower abdomen that formed pustule blisters. After showering not knowing what the reaction was from, the burn spread to two other places leaving painful welts.
justification: The incident resulted in chemical burns and blisters, and the likelihood of occurrence is possible given the product's design and the user's lack of awareness about the fluid's contents.

incident_description: Recently, my wife's 4GB Apple Ipod Nano, while playing suddenly exploded and caught fire on my wife's desk at work, almost burning her hand as she had to toss on the floor, also damaging her office carpet before be able to extinguish the flames.
justification: While no injuries were reported, the incident caused property damage, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description: I had had difficulty with the lithium ion battery in my HP Pavilion 17 Notebook PC. The product number is G4X63UA#ABA. The serial number is 5CD41412MB. I have had this laptop for a couple years now. Off and on for years my battery has overheated, which has caused a burn hazard. If it is in contact with someone's skin, it is so hot it could cause a burn. I saw that HP recalled some batteries last year and checked to see if mine was on the list. I was surprised it was not. My computer has been overheating a lot lately due to the battery. I checked HP's website and saw that they updated the recall. Again, I thought my battery would be listed and it was not. It gave the option to report an unsafe product. I do not think that this product is safe. It has been a continuous issue. My battery number is 6DGAHN5GW6G8K3. Although they has not been a permanent injury, no one in my family holds the laptop or puts it on their lap due to the intense heat. The battery will overheat and shut the computer off. I do not think this is safe.
justification: While no permanent injury has occurred, the recurring overheating issue poses a significant burn hazard, making it likely to cause injury if not addressed.

incident_description:
My 9 year-old daughter was using our iPad (2nd generation). While using the Apple iPad, playing games, the iPad became extremely hot and violently burst open.  It scared my daughter and she brought me the iPad, crying because of the disturbing nature of the failure.

The device was not plugged into any power source at the time of the incident.

I observed the residual heat in the aluminum housing and also that the screen and some other components had "popped off"."  The inner LED display was cracked and small bits of the (glass?) LED display were loose inside of the device; some were ejected from the device when it burst open.  I observed that the two (I had later come to understand) batteries were swollen into the shape of pillows, obviously they had expanded outside of the volume meant to contain them.

I brought the device to the local Apple store where I was told that this type of failure could (paraphrasing) happen at any time, to any battery powered device.

I was unsatisfied by their seeming disregard for the safety issues and proceeded to contact Apple directly over their internet portal.  Frankly speaking, they seemed unconcerned about the failure.  I sent pictures, and told me that their safety engineer explained that since the unit was outside the warrantee there was nothing that they could do.  They did not request the device as to evaluate possible failure modes, nor did they explain what caused this.  They seemed to be aware that this failure mode was infrequent but common.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the iPad's violent burst open due to battery swelling posed a potential hazard, making it an incident with possible future occurrence.

incident_description: I purchased a Samsung Galaxy S6 when it first came out.  Have used it without incident until Saturday 11/25/17.  The phone was last charged at 3:30pm, using the Samsung fast charger that it came with.  I made a call and then put the phone in my purse.  At 9:30pm there was a loud pop and the purse caught fire.  After putting out the fire, the cause was clearly the phone battery.  The phone was partially melted with a clear rectangle shape on both the front and back of the phone.  The screen had slightly popped out as well.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and while it's possible, it's not likely to occur frequently due to the specific circumstances.

incident_description: I have a Gateway computer model NV55C, serial number LXWSG0205714212DC11601. I had it on the manufacturer charger, when the batteries exploded and caught fire. I got it outside of my house, sprayed it with water to get the fire out. then after about 10 minutes, another battery exploded, and another fire. My antique kitchen table is burnt, my floor is burnt, as well as smoke damage. This computer is about 6-7 years old, but other consumers should be aware of this issue. I have tried to contact Gateway, but no response yet. I believe I should be compensated for my loss.
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the incident caused significant property damage, including a burnt kitchen table, floor, and smoke damage, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description: There are sparks and smoke coming out of the a/c plug where it folds into the unit.  I bought four of these less then a year ago and all four are doing the same thing.
justification: All four units exhibiting the same issue within a year indicates a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: I have purchased a Samsung Galaxy S8+ cell phone. It has a glass screen. The phone is made so that you are unable to buy as case that protects it all the way around. I also purchased the screen protector for it. It slid off of the bed and the screen cracked. The glass has shattered near the edge and has sharp edges that protrude. there is no way to cover it or protect it the way the phone is made.  I have cut myself on it and had injuries. it presents further risk. I have contacted Samsung and it is not repairable under their warranty. They will not provide replacement or fix it at their cost, In making a product of this kind, a company needs to provide safety features to prevent risk of injuries. I feel the glass screen on this product is a danger.
justification: The phone's design, with a fragile glass screen and no full-coverage case option, increases the likelihood of injury upon impact.

incident_description: Turtle Beach Ear Force X04 headset was purchased a few years ago, brand new at Walmart in Yakima WA. They have been faulty for the last year or so given the microphone would cut and the cord was becoming faulty. The issues with chronic cough and sickness like allergen related nasal blockage has been prevalent.
justification: The incident involves a faulty product causing inconvenience, but no physical harm.

incident_description: Ambient Weather Radio WR-111B purchased March 2014 from Amazon. On 11/2/17 the rechargeable battery exploded and caught fire. Radio destroyed.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' case. The likelihood is 'possible' as battery explosions, while rare, can occur due to manufacturing defects or improper usage.

incident_description: Our children turned on our Samsung LED television set this morning and woke me up saying there was something wrong with the television.  I came downstairs and saw that the television had strange colored lines and the bottom and then in the bottom left corner there was a bright white dot on the screen with some red it in as well. Tried switching channels, turned off and on, and it remained.  Shortly thereafter, we smelled a burning smell coming from the television and open closer inspection, I observed that the left corner of the television had melted!  I touched it and it was extremely hot (no injury).  I contacted Samsung customer service and they provided no service once they determined there was no injury or damage to property, since the warranty expired 7 months ago.  I encouraged to them this wasn't a warranty issue but safety issue.  I searched on the internet and found numerous instances to this model line of Samsung LED televisions of the approximate same age doing the same thing, some of which consumers reported combusted. There were 24 pages of consumers reporting this same issue on the Community Forum support section of Samsung's customer support website.  I also posted our experience and pictures as well.   I feel strongly that this product should be recalled.  Many people sleep with their television on and had someone not been paying attention to the television, a fire certainly could have started.  Pictures are attached of the television.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the television malfunction posed a significant fire risk, making it an incident with high likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description: 7/11/2014, I purchased a refurbished Philips docking speaker from Wal-Mart online.  I have used this unit coupled with Apple IPods, as intended, without any event.  There was never any glitch or abnormal behavior from the unit prior the the incident.  On the morning of 7/31/2017, I woke up to a strange sound coming from my bathroom.  I went inside and the room was smoky.  I heard a strange chirping sound and quickly realized the smoke was coming from the Philips unit.  I unplugged it and took the IPod off.  My hand was slightly burned, as the IPod unit was very, very hot.  I thought to videotape the unit smoking and chirping, because it was so strange and scary.  I have photos and the unit in my possession.  Upon inspection, after everything cooled down, the connector of the Philips unit and the IPod connector had both melted.  It was alarming, because had I not gotten up and gone to the unit, there, no doubt, would have been a fire.  I contacted Philips on 8/11/17 about this.  I let them know that I wanted to impress my concern for other people using this docking speaker model too. The unit was not in play mode at the time.  I take good care of my things, so I can't imagine what went wrong.  Maybe the device was not flush-on, possibly causing the IPod and docking connection to try to communicate and heat up?  I'm just not sure, as I'm not an electrical engineer. I strongly feel that this incident took place because of a Philips design flaw.  I let them know that.  If this was the impetus, had they had a click and release coupling mechanism, this likely would not have occurred.  I am not an electrical engineer.  All I know is that I used this product properly and it was heading toward a fire.  I have retained the video footage of this.  I felt they should have at least shown concern enough to inspect the unit.  They did not.  They closed the case because I could not produce the receipt in their time frame.  I do not know how many units were sold, but I had purchased a second unit new and let them know that I will retire that one for safety sake.  I was very surprised and found it disturbing that they just dismissed this without inspection.  I think that is very irresponsible and reckless.  I am bringing it to your attention because it was alarming and I am concerned for the public's safety.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor burn injury, hence severity level 3. The likelihood is high as the unit overheated and could have caused a fire, given the circumstances.

incident_description: Concern has to do with Ryobi lithium + 18V rechargeable battery with model # P108, part #130429075 Purchased from The Home Depot. Samsung 50" LED Television.  Melts in lower right corner.  See link below for discussion.  Samsung's customer service people act like they've never heard of this.  We smelled something burning and noticed TV was melting.  Have unplugged due to fire hazard.

incident_description:
On Oct 23rd, 2017, my 10 year old daughter had a strange mark that looked like a burn or a rash on her abdomen. She couldn't recall anything that may have happened to cause an injury. 
Oct 24th - The next day, it blistered. 
Oct 24th - blister popped
Oct 26th - another blister formed on the same burn
Oct 26th - A new mark appeared on her arm
Oct 27th - A new mark appeared on her leg
Oct 28th - the wound on her leg blistered
Oct 28th - Two new marks on her abdomen appeared

I took her to the doctor on the 26th when the 2nd mark showed up on her arm. They diagnosed as a burn - possibly from friction. I continued to research on my own because the "friction" didn't make sense and came across a recall on cell phone cases that have liquid and glitter in them leaking and causing burns. My daughter has case similar but not from the manufacturer. I inspected her case and it has a small crack in it and the fluid leaks out slowly. She listens to music before falling asleep and sleeps in the top bunk so just falls asleep with the phone on her stomach which explains the 3 marks on her abdomen. The one on her arm and leg are in a perfect spot for her to roll over onto her side and have the phone under her. I contacted the seller through Amazon and they offered to refund the price of the case. Obviously, that is not my concern.
justification: Injury occurred due to a defective phone case leaking and causing burns, with a high likelihood of recurrence given the product's continued use.

incident_description: I bought this tv 3/17 and it's 7/17. Four months I've had this tv and it's been watched for about 20 hours. incident_description:
I bought a device charger at CVS in Galveston, TX and plugged my iPhone into it. Several hours later I found the device partially melted. 
I returned it to the store and talked to the store manager who said he would show it to his boss who happened to be there. 
They were out of the chargers but I got a pic of another product made by the same company (the manager showed me) so I could get the company info. I also have pics of the melted charger.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident resulted in property damage (melted charger), making it an 'Incident, No Injury' case. The likelihood is 'possible' as it's not a common occurrence but has happened.

incident_description: I had bought a couple of the glitter iPhone 6 cases from Victoria Secret. I don't use them often cause they're really expensive and I didn't want to break. Anyways I've noticed when I do, I will break out in like a rash almost looks like carpet burn. The most recent incident I had shorts on and had to drive for like an hour and had phone in case laying on my leg, well it started burning and itching and I'm left with this horrible Mark on my leg!
justification: Skin irritation and burns occurred, indicating an injury (severity level 3), and while not frequent, it's possible given the right conditions (occurrence likelihood 3).

incident_description:
This is regarding my Samsung flat screen t.v. Model No. UN50J6200AF, Model Code UN50J6200AFXZA. Version No. DH03. 
When I turned on my t.v. last Thursday night, there were vertical lines on the screen/display that went away after a few minutes, so I kind of ignored it. I did not use the t.v. again until last night (Tues). It had the vertical lines initially, but they faded again. I watched about ten minutes, and then paused it about 10 minutes to talk to my daughters. When we were done talking, my 16 year old walked by the t.v. and said what's wrong with the t.v.? To indicated the problem, she touched the lower left hand corner (where the glass and plastic frame meet). Apparently, the area was so hot the plastic was melting and she actually burned her finger (not badly) when she accidentally touched it while pointing at it. She said it was a fire hazard, I agreed, and turned the t.v. off. I Googled "samsung tv melting" and there is a thread on samsung.com customer support of over 200 posts regarding this issue. There should be a recall.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury, and the likelihood of occurrence is high given the numerous reported cases of the same issue.

incident_description: On September 29, 2017 I had plugged in my HP G61-511WM laptop to charge and went to bed.  A few minutes later I heard 2 pops and rolled over and saw my bedspread and mattress on fire.  Then watched as something shoot across the room and catch my curtains on fire.  After putting the fire out and calling 911 I realized that the battery had caught on fire and exploded.  Pieces to the battery were melted into the carpet in both the bedroom and my living room (about 20 feet away).  Half of a wall was burnt and has to be replaced, my mattress and box springs were burned up, and I have 2nd degree burns on my hand and foot.
justification: Injury occurred due to direct contact with fire caused by battery explosion, with likelihood rated as 'possible' given the rarity of such incidents.

incident_description: My Galaxy 6 Samsung phone melted while sitting on a wireless charger.  It was out of direct sunlight and there was no other source of heat on the desk where it was plugged in.  I had not used this phone for a few weeks and did not realize it had overheated and burst out of its case until cleaning up on October 7, 2017.  It is totally ruined and cannot be salvaged.
justification: The phone melting and being ruined is an incident, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: HTC One A9 almost caught on fire yesterday. Plugged it into the same charger used for over a year with this phone. Almost immediately, the phone began to smoke and melted part of the charging cord. It burned!
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and while it's possible with the given charger, it's not a common occurrence.

incident_description:
On 7-11-17 the Topeka, KS Fire Department responded to a structure fire located at [REDACTED].  The structure involved a detached garage and it was subsequently suppressed.  The Kansas Office of the State Fire Marshal was requested to conduct an origin and cause investigation.

The fire's origin was determined to have been upon a shelf within the interior of the garage.  Fire ignition was determined to have been from a fault within a Whistler Portable Jump Start & Power Supply.  The owner had plugged in the device for charging the evening before the fire.  

CPSC has reported certain models of this device have been recalled due to reported fires.  I was unable to obtain the model number from the product due to damage.  The owner claimed to have purchased the product from a Walmart about 6 months ago.  If correct, this appears to be after the recalled models.  The product manual was salvaged in good condition, but it did not contain the model number.

No injuries occurred as a result of this fire.

The origin and cause report may be forwarded to your office if requested, when completed.
justification: No injuries occurred, but the fire could have been more severe.

incident_description: Battery pack Lenovo 45N1126 overheated and caused my nano mouse receiver to melt into the laptop motherboard.d
justification: The incident resulted in damage to property (laptop) but no injuries, and the likelihood of such an event occurring is possible given the overheating of a battery pack.

incident_description: I would like to report a faulty and defective batter pack in the hisense C11 chrombook laptop. The battery has swelled up and heats up and could be a risk for a fire.
justification: While no immediate danger is present, the swollen battery poses a potential fire risk, hence a severity level of 2.

incident_description: I checked online recalls multiple times to see if my iPhone case was coming up as recalled and it is not. After months passing I figured mine is safe. Tonight I fell asleep with my phone in my bed and woke up to it being wet and intense arm pain. I quickly washed my arm and took the glitter case off. I have a huge chemical burn and my phone has the liquid on it now. I pulled up the etsy seller and the exact make and model of mine is still being sold. I am just upset this was not recalled and others could get hurt. I emailed the company as well.
justification: The incident resulted in a chemical burn, indicating severity level 3, and the continued sale of the product suggests a high likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description: While a clerk/technician at a cell phone retailer was replacing the battery of an Apple I-Phone 6-Plus smart phone with a new battery, the old one ignited.
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the incident of a battery igniting poses a potential risk for future occurrences.

incident_description:
My AT&T Universal box (U-verse) which is the box for the cable is secured on an entertainment center in its own cubby with no other devices with it in the cubby. I was home alone with no tv on. While sitting on the couch a large flaming spark ignited from the box with a bopping sound. I quickly sprain into action and as nervous as I was, I released the back wires from the box. The room filled with an awful electronical burning smell from the box. I called the company (Frontier) right away. Not to pleased with their response. Frontier bought out AT & T and they choice to continue to use their product. I have 2 other boxes in the home and when I asked to have them replaced, I was left to have a technician come out with a cost associated with it. Very very poor customer service. I am concerned other boxes will do the same.

serial# M91322EAL128
Motorola
VIP2250
justification: The incident involved a spark and electrical burning smell, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
[REDACTED] was on scene of a structure fire at [REDACTED] branch. The fire was confined to a monitor in a break room. The fire caused damage to west wall in break room where tv originally was mounted and smoke damage in rear of structure. The monitor was investigated by the security service technician and also the fire department fire investigator. The fire origin was confirmed the monitor via pictures, video and information. I spoke to the consumer but received a careless acknowledgement. 
[REDACTED]: Chase Bank Facility Manager - [REDACTED]
[REDACTED]: NAVCO Security Technician - [REDACTED]
[REDACTED]: Scottsburg Fire Department Investigator - [REDACTED]
justification: The fire was contained to a single monitor, causing property damage but no injuries.

incident_description: We purchased a Samsung 50 inch TV in Jan of 2016. We have used the TV less than 20 hours. Its in our family room. We only watched it when we were entertaining or waiting for company. On July 2nd we were waiting for someone to come over. We had the TV on and noticed something melting from the inside of the screen on the bottom left hand corner. When my husband went to investigate it area was scorching hot. We immediately unplugged the device and have only re-plugged it to do the Samsung diagnostic tests the company required.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a potentially hazardous malfunction of an electrical appliance, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' scenario.

incident_description: TV sparked and popped, will not turn back on. Smells like something caught fire. My 4 year old daughter was about 10 feet away from it. She did not get hurt, but it scared her and I pretty badly.
justification: While no one was injured, the incident involved a fire hazard and could have resulted in injury.

incident_description: A surge protector with a shredder plugged into it and plugged directly into a wall outlet (not daisy chained) caught fire.  This was a black unit with six outlets and marking that the model number was 100467, but with no brand name visible.  It does look like the Power Sentry online with the same model number.  The fuse melted and the strip caught fire.  I only caught this because of the popping noise of the electrical short and was able to get a fire extinguisher to it in time.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and while similar incidents could occur, it's not likely due to the specific circumstances.

incident_description: I was using a kintron kb-1 e186244 extension cord. Had it plugged into a wall socket & as soon as I plugged my iPhone in, the extension cord outlet where I plugged my phone shot out sparks, then a small fire started. My iPhone is now fried & won't turn on along with my tablet that was plugged into the socket as well. I was shocked in the process of trying to unplug it from the wal & have injuries.
justification: Injury occurred due to electrical shock while attempting to unplug the faulty extension cord.

incident_description: I watched as a car driver dropped a burning cell phone to the ground. The driver was passing through an intersection and I was waiting for the traffic light to change. The driver continued to drive away and I got out of my car and extinguished the fire with my boot.
justification: No injury occurred, but the incident could have caused property damage or a chain reaction if not extinguished.

incident_description: The tv (LG LED) was turned on and being watched when a popping sound occurred, followed by several more popping sounds (actually mistaken initially as broadcast audio).  Then smoke began flowing from the top vents as well as other areas of the tv casing.  The picture never failed; the tv was remotely turned off, unplugged and removed to outdoors.  The smoke was adequate enough to set off a nearby fire detector, but there were never any visible flames.  No one was injured, and no property was damaged.
justification: While no injuries or property damage occurred, the incident involved a significant safety hazard with smoke and a potential fire, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
Philips Plasma TV model 50PF9630A/37 serial YA1A0543007653
arcing by capacitors inside the left and right side of the back cabinets of these TVs can pose a safety risk.
I followed the instructions: For more information, contact Philips at (888) PHILIPS [888-744-5477] anytime. When you call this number, an automated voice attendant will ask you to say or enter a "Priority PIN number." Please enter the numbers "4445" and you will be put in contact with a Philips representative who will assist you. Consumers also can go to the firm's Web site at www.philips.com, or write to Philips' at V.P. Service, Philips Consumer Electronics North America, 64 Perimeter Center East, Atlanta, GA 30346
I called Phillips, representatives kept transferring me from department to department for hours. I was not able to get repair service. They even claimed that this model does not exist, nor they aware of the problem.
justification: Though no injuries were reported, the incident (arcing capacitors) poses a potential safety risk, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' scenario.

incident_description: As directed I plugged my cordless speakers in to charge. I had done this twice before with no problems. When I went to check on the speakers, one unit was completely melted at the charging input and the surrounding controls.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and while it's possible, it's not likely to happen every time.

incident_description: galaxy tab A, 8 inch tablet overheated, got a bubble in the screen and continued to get hotter. stopped working. too hot to even touch. only 3 months old, but of course 4 days past being returnable.
justification: The tablet overheating and becoming unusable is an incident, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: My RCA 10 inch Tablet that quit charging. Had put it in a bottom drawer until I could have battery replaced.  Several months later I opened drawer to find it had exploded!
justification: The tablet's explosion caused potential injury, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
The consumer's adult son had the phone in his front pocket, when he felt something warm.  He removed the phone with his hand and found that it was extremely hot to the touch.  He threw the phone on the grass and he heard a cracking noise.  The son then touched the phone again and found that it was still hot, so he threw water on it.  

After the phone cooled down, a bubble was discovered on the back of the phone, which is also glass.  This contributed to the cracking of the glass.

The following day, the consumer and her son took the phone back to the dealer in Downey, CA, but were told that this was a manufacturer's issue and that they could not correct it.  They advised the consumers to contact the mfr. directly.

While at the retailer, the consumers called the mfr.  Their rep. said that they needed to see the phone and provided a return shipping label, by email.  The consumers sent the phone back to the mfr.  The consumer's son received an email from the mfr., which stated that since the front of the phone was broken prior to this incident, they consumers needed to pay $200+ for that repair, prior to them fixing the latest issue.

NOTE:  The consumer admitted that the screen was broken as the mfr. indicated, but she also noted that the phone worked fine prior to the latest issue.

There were no injuries.
justification: No injuries occurred despite the phone overheating and cracking, but the incident could have resulted in burns.

incident_description:
Lamp door cover has melted as well as the area around the lamp.
I was never notified of this safety issue by Sony.  I did just discover there was a class action filed and has since expired in 2012.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage (melted lamp cover) but no reported injuries, and the likelihood of occurrence is low given the class action's expiration in 2012.

incident_description:
The Apple MagSafe 85w power adapter for my MacBook Pro has frayed and shorted out at the base of the power supply. After this happened, the cable started heating up, and I wasn't using my computer at the time I believe it would have caught on fire. This is the second power adapter I have had this exact issue with and after doing my own research, have found many others with the exact same issue.

According to Apple, this is considered accidental damage and normal wear and tear. I believe this is a defect I the design and needs to be recalled and corrected.
justification: While no injury occurred, the potential for fire poses a significant risk, making the likelihood of an incident high.

incident_description:
Caller stated that she awaken to a loud noise and saw a small fire ball dispersing towards her bed  and fell to the floor.  She stated that she used the fire extinguisher to contain the fire , the fire burnt the are of the flooring that it landed on.

Caller feels that this could have caused serious damages had it landed on her bed.  The provider was contacted and she filled out a form to receive a replacement.  

Caller is concerned about this cell phone battery and feels that it should be investigated.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident involved a fire which could have caused serious damage and potential injury if not contained.

incident_description:
I purchased an AT&T GoPhone LGB470 (SKU:6444A) flip phone from BEST BUY on Sept 8, 2017. Tonight Sept 18th my phone started beeping an alert saying the battery was hot and that I needed to power OFF the phone immediately. However the phone was so HOT it burned my fingers and dropped it on the floor. I grabbed a hot pad and picked it up and put it in my freezer. I waited for 30 minutes to power it off. I contacted AT&T but they were not aware of any fires or over heating problems with the phones. These phones have the SAME Lithium Ion batteries that have caused FIRES in other phones. My concern is if people with these phones take them on an airplane, a fire could cause major problems, especially if it is put in the luggage. I was told by AT&T to take it back to BEST BUY and get another phone (I guess the same model) she didn't clarify.
I think you guys need to RECALL this phone IMMEDIATELY to save lives and notify the Airline Companies to IMMEDIATELY BAN these phones or ALL phones that use a LITHIUM ION BATTERY!!!
justification: The phone's battery overheating caused burns, indicating potential for severe injury or property damage.

incident_description: Apple iPhone charger overheated.  The unit was VERY hot, emitted a burning electronics smell, and the outside surface was partially melted and discolored brown.
justification: The charger overheated and melted, posing a potential fire hazard but no immediate injury was reported.

incident_description: I bought replacement color ink cartridges (model   952) for my Hewlett Packard 8715 printer.  The packaging requires a sharp knife to remove a cartridge and I cut myself in the process.  The packaging is an invitation to serious injury, many of which are undoubtedly not reported.
justification: The packaging design requiring a sharp knife to remove the cartridge increases the likelihood of injury.

incident_description:
My daughter has a Toshiba laptop (I was unaware of the recall, but it seems to be in the group of recalled items) and when she turned it on this afternoon it sparked and started smoking. No one was injured. She unplugged it 

When I came home this evening I tried to take a look at it, but when I opened it it started to flame out the back.  The flame stopped when I closed the laptop.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the laptop sparked, smoked, and later caught fire, indicating a significant safety hazard.

incident_description: My daughter, 4-year-old granddaughter, and 12 week old grandson were displaced due to a fire in her apartment .  It appeals that the vTech baby monitor that she received as a shower gift, exploded and caused her bedroom to go up in flames.  My family is now displaced and lost everything due to this incident.
justification: No injuries were reported, but the incident caused significant property damage and displacement.

incident_description: User plugged in the power connector of a Zebra GK420t label printer and walked away to get coffee. Upon return user saw smoke and small flames at the rear of the printer. The fire was extinguished without additional damage. The printer was removed, photographed and retained by the IT department.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a fire, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' (Level 2). The likelihood is 'Possible' (3) as it's not common but could happen due to human error.

incident_description: I had bought a Victoria's Secret glitter case at 12/28/16. It worked good for protection but after a month of having it a liquid starting leaking from near the camera part. There was a crack and I tried to seal it but that only lasted a week or so. It would leak through the day, and oil base liquid I'm assuming. Sometimes it would leak in my pocket. It has also gave me a rash that took a week to get rid of.
