justification: The incident resulted in an injury (rash) due to a leaking liquid from the glitter case, making it a '3' on the severity scale. The likelihood of this occurring is 'possible', hence a '3' on the occurrence likelihood scale.

incident_description: Use if the Anker charging block, we began to smell electrical burning.
justification: The smell of electrical burning indicates a potential fire hazard, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: Samsung Galaxy S7 is overheating. Went to Pick phone up and it burned my hand. Samsung has failed to do anything about this issue even though products from this line has had similar issues in the past. Phone is over heating after 2 mins of use.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (burned hand), and the likelihood is high given the history of similar issues with the same product line.

incident_description:
Used the battery as instructed and as intended to jump start my 2006 [REDACTED] vehicle. Black clamp to negative post of my car battery and red clamp to the positive post of my car battery, after connecting the ground. 

I tried to turn my vehicle over one time and noticed through my windshield that the battery under the hood of my car was bulging and so I turned off the ignition and ran to get the battery. It had swelled and was making noises like it was going to catch on fire. I disconnected the positive and then negative clamps and I felt the case with my thumb and burned my back of my thumb. I used the cable wires to remove the battery to a safe place as it continued to heat up and break itself open. 

The battery has no manufacture's details on it and is distributed on Amazon.com by Lytle Racing Group in Arizona. I contacted them via Amazon Marketplace and they wrote back and said it was past warranty and they couldn't help me. I protested the safety concerns I had, and they said AntiGravity indemnifies them and that was all. 

I have photos and tried two browsers, but your site will not allow me to upload the pictures.
justification: Injury occurred due to direct contact with a heated battery, and the likelihood is high as the incident was caused by a known issue with the battery.

incident_description: I returned to my home after several hours of being away to find my kitchen filled with smoke and a terrible smell. My Samsung Galaxy Active s6 had been charging while I was away, and it had caught fire and released black smoke inside my home. The phone was no longer burning, but had melted into the container lid it was placed on to charge. Soot shot out several feet in a semi-circle from the charger port. My home now smells like toxic fumes despite several hours of airing out the kitchen with the fan on.
justification: No injuries reported, but significant property damage and potential health risks from toxic fumes.

incident_description: The iphone case cracked and leaked, causing a chemical burn the size of a quarter to the left wrist.
justification: Injury occurred due to chemical burn, but no death or severe injury reported.

incident_description: I just got done making a phone call and my Samsung Galaxy S7 Edge phone got so hot that I was forced to drop it.  The phone continued heating and was hot enough that it expanded to about three times its normal thickness and I couldn't pick it up for about 5 minutes.  The phone was destroyed.
justification: Phone overheating and expansion caused no physical harm, but could have led to injury if mishandled.

incident_description: We purchased a Black & Decker laminator (Model# LAM125FH) at the end of November 2016.  It began to make strange noises a few weeks ago, and this morning when I plugged it in and turned it on, smoke began pouring out of it and there were countless popping noises and a distinct smell of burning electronics.  We turned it off and unplugged it, but it continued to crackle and smoke for another 10 minutes.  I went back to the amazon purchase and although the reviews had been positive at first, now more than half were one star reviews, with many people complaining of their laminators also smoking and/or burning up completely.  If this defect has been so common in less than a year, we feel that it poses a serious fire hazard for people, and Black & Decker should be made to improve the quality of their products and require more thorough safety inspections.
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the incident poses a significant fire risk due to the widespread defect.

incident_description:
The submitter said he was charging the 4 AA batteries that came with the charger and left it overnight. In the morning the submitter noticed that the prongs melted and the outlet plastic cover had melted. 

The submitter said he has not found contact information for the and has not contacted them but he plans to. 

The submitter indicated that he uses the charger once a month.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident resulted in property damage (melted charger and outlet), making it a level 2 severity. The likelihood is 'possible' as the submitter uses the charger infrequently, but it's not rare.

incident_description:
My 7 year old son unplugged the charger for the Joytech evic VTC mini today and the prongs separated from the rest of the charger and remained in the outlet. He received a nasty shock from the 120VAC mains. This is wholly unacceptable and extremely unsafe for this to have happened. I'm concerned that this could happen to other people and could result in a fatality.

The AC-DC adapter is model number BEK-QC-001. Manufacturer listed is Joyetech.

I can send photos.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (shock) and the design flaw in the charger increases the likelihood of similar incidents occurring.

incident_description: The Olympia 3220mAh Samsung Galaxy Note 4 Battery exploded in my Samsung Galaxy Note 4 smartphone tonight. The battery was blown clear of the phone and caught fire. The phone was damaged beyond repair/use, partially melted and burned. The phone wasn't charging at the time. I was able to get the burning battery out of my residence, so other than thick smoke no damage occurred in the home. I did get a small burn on my right hand thumb while trying to get the burning battery out of the residence and away from flammable property, people, or animals.
justification: Injury occurred to the user's thumb while attempting to remove the burning battery.

incident_description: I bought one of the glitter, waterfall cases a while back from Victoria's Secret/Pink and was planning on gifting it to someone as a birthday present.  But then when I was shopping at my local Victoria store recently, I saw the recall notice for the phone cases and of course the one I bought for my friend was part of the recall since there were cases of the case breaking and causing severe chemical burns to users.  I no longer have the receipt unfortunately but was told to fill out this in order to get a refund for the defective item.
justification: The incident involved severe chemical burns, indicating a high severity level, and the recall notice suggests a high likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description: We were using one of the battery packs. It is labeled as Zeta by Jacko. The pack was charging when I noticed a strong, chemical odor coming from it. I went to unplug the pack and the area was hot. When I went to unplug the pack, I noticed the battery pack was split open. We stayed away from it in order to let it cool down. Within a few minutes of unplugging the pack, it exploded and bursted into flames. It popped and shot flames out several times. When we were able to put out the fire and had the local fire department bring out the battery pack and clear the smoke, we noticed that some battery acid had gotten on our cabinets and walls and the cabinet lights were damaged and had melted. We purchased several a while back but we just opened the first one today. This pack was brand new, straight out of the box.
justification: Injury was likely due to the battery pack exploding and bursting into flames, and the occurrence was likely given the brand new state of the pack and the immediate explosion upon unplugging.

incident_description: When watching tv at home, noticed a buzzing sound, followed by smoke coming out of the corner of the tv and a few of the pixels were blacked out. Immediately turned off and unplugged the tv. Tried turning it on a few minutes later and the screen was still broken. We had to remove and replace it.
justification: While no injuries were reported, the incident resulted in damage to the TV, making it a level 2 severity. The likelihood is rated as 'possible' as such incidents can occur but are not extremely common.

incident_description: I was using a Ryobi One+ drill.  I inserted a 4Ah battery pack into the drill.  I had only been using the drill 10-15 seconds when the battery terminal melted.  The heat melted the grip/handle on the drill and burned my hand.  I tried to put another battery in the drill, but the battery damaged the drill and it won't work anymore.  There was a recall a couple of years ago on a 4Ah battery, but this battery was a different part number.  The battery from my drill was a model P108, part number 130429075.  I have contacted Ryobi customer service about six times.  They have assured me that the safety department would contact me, but it has been about 10 weeks since I began contacting them.  I haven't received a phone call from anyone to resolve these issues or inquire about the incident.
justification: Injury occurred due to battery malfunction, and likelihood is possible given the recall history of similar batteries.

incident_description: The rechargeable battery pack for my 17-inch MacBook Pro laptop apparently overheated while the unit was connected to the charger line. It did not catch fire, but the pack heated up and expanded its insulation from its half inch thickness to an inch. It got hot enough to soften its adhesive. I am just glad I noticed the expansion before it got hot enough to burn.
justification: The incident resulted in no injuries but could have potentially caused damage or fire if left unnoticed.

incident_description: Turned on television in the morning.  Immediately noticed lines on the display that quickly deteriorated until the picture was nothing but vertical white/black lines.  Smelled electrical components burning so immediately unplugged the unit.  Visual examination of unit showed that the lower left corner of bezel had begun to melt.  Television unit was owned for 13 months, but only in regular use for 10 months.  This unit is a fire hazard, and a recall should be issued by the manufacturer (Samsung).  I have attempted to remedy this through the manufacturer, but am not getting my hopes up due to the unit being just past the one year warranty period.
justification: The incident resulted in no injuries, but the potential fire hazard poses a high likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description:
I have a Samsung tablet 4 
M/N SM-1237P
DEC 256691545703735912
It was obtained through Sprint in July of 2015. The tablet is left in a dry, clean office environment plugged in most of the time and used less that 2 hours a week. I picked it up to use yesterday and it was warm to the touch but not hot and I noticed it had developed a bulge in the back of the case and the screen had started to lift off. I contacted both Sprint and Samsung and they say there is no defect although the manufacturing is in the same timeframe as the [REDACTED] phones that were catching on fire so I am thinking it is the same issue and the same action needs to be taken
justification: The tablet's physical deformation and potential fire risk, similar to the [REDACTED] phones, indicates a possible incident but no immediate injury.

incident_description:
Purchased a 12 piece set of lithium ion batteries from Amazon Sept, 9, 2016.

Have used them many of times in a strap on head lamp running a [REDACTED] LED light.

Driving my car at 10pm saturday 6/3/2017 had removed the device from on my head and set it on the center consul of my car.   Began to hear a hissing sound I thought was emanating  from my car radio.  As I was adjusting the volume control on my radio which had no effect on the noise I was hearing, I realized the sound was something else.  At that moment a bright flash and loud bang filled the cab of my automobile.  What had exploded in my car blew shrapnel into both of my eyes making it impossible for me to keep my eyes open.  Fortunately I was on a familiar road and was able to maintain control of my vehicle and pull off the roadway.  I am a volunteer firefighter and carry a medic kit and bottled water which I immediately began flushing my eyes with.  After 20 minutes on the side of the road i regained partial vision and was able to drive my car the 2.5 miles back to my house.  My eyes hurt through the night but after about 12 hours returned to normal and the pain went away.  Upon inspecting my vehicle the next morning discovered my windshield had been shattered from the force of the explosion.   I contacted Amazon and informed them of the incident and they immediately refunded the entire purchase from last september and referred me to contact the seller and the CPSC.  I have had no response from the seller in California except to say he would let the manufacturer know.  My request for the name of the manufacturer was not complied with and all other letters sent have gone unanswered.  including my demands for repair of my car's windshield which has duct tape holding it together because I a, on Social Security and can not afford to replace a $450 windshield.
justification: The incident resulted in serious injury (shrapnel in both eyes) and property damage (shattered windshield), and the cause (defective batteries) is likely to recur.

incident_description:
Conair Shower Radio Model: CON SR16. Purchased at Bed Bath & Beyond, SKU #14709827.

Running the radio, I felt the back around the battery cover to be very warm. Removing the cover, one of the batteries was so hot I burned my finger in removing it. Fortunately it didn't start a fire.

I don't know whether this happened to be a defective one or if others are doing the same thing. I have not heard back from the manufacturer yet.
justification: Injury occurred (burnt finger) due to excessive heat from the battery, but no fire started, making the likelihood of occurrence possible.

incident_description: My service provider is print and when I upgraded to the iPhone 7 plus I also purchased a Kate Spade glitter case back in Nov 2016. On August 9, 2017 I noticed the case was cracked and my hands along with the phone case smelled like lighter fluid so I immediately took the case off the phone and threw it in the trash I noticed my thigh was irritated so when I looked I had a chemical burn I went to the ER & they confirmed the burn was approximately 4x7cm big and I was treated with prescribed antibacterial cream that I have to apply 3 times a day for the next 14 days.
justification: The incident resulted in a chemical burn, requiring medical treatment, but no death or permanent injury.

incident_description: I too have the "fit bit rash".  I had worn my fit bit FLEX for about two and a half years and then the rash started.  I had tried different types of bands but nothing seemed to help. I agree with others that it seems to be a burn and I had long suspected it was a result of the battery., While some suggest not wearing it 24/7, isn't that the point....if you take it off, you sometime forget to put it back on.  I am now wearing a mole skin on the battery but will need to find a different product because Fit Bit has let you down....
justification: Skin irritation and rash caused by prolonged use of the Fitbit Flex, likely due to the battery.

incident_description: Apple iPhone charging cable melted, sparked and smoked/flamed before being put out.  If my wife wasn't lucky in the room, this coulee have burned my house down!   Dozens of similar reports by other consumers with this product, what is being down to resolve this issue!
justification: The incident caused property damage and could have resulted in injury or death if not for luck.

incident_description: hi my daughter was playing with her tablet when she heard a poppong sound her battery imediatlly puffed up and expanded and pop the tablet up and is no longer useful doesnt work plz help with this issue i would like a fefund for the product.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage (tablet rendered useless) but no injuries, and while it's possible, it's not likely to happen frequently due to safety measures in modern devices.

incident_description: I bought a phone case from Victoria's Secret for my birthday and I broke out in rashes and hivesfor my birthday
justification: The incident resulted in physical injury (rashes and hives), but it's unlikely to occur again due to the specific product and individual reaction.

incident_description: My husband was in the bathroom reading the news on his Samsung Galaxy S6 Active and the phone back expanded and burst into flames. He dropped the phone on the floor and ran out and away from the billowing smoke. No apparent physical burns on my husband but the vinyl floor is damaged and there is significant electronic smoke odor in the bathroom and closet that will not dissipate and will probably require professional cleaning. My husband is asthmatic and, while the adrenaline kept him from suffering an attack at the moment, I worry the smoke inhalation might exacerbate his condition later on. It also should be noted that the phone was NOT being charged at the time of explosion.
justification: No injuries were reported, but the incident caused significant property damage and potential health risks due to smoke inhalation.

incident_description: I got one of your bombshell ombre snow iPhone 6 cases and I was told by Victoria secret to contact your company. Your case leaked and ruined my iPhone due to water damage it no longer even turns on or anything at all. Unfortunately I did not have insurance on my iPhone 6 so now I am using my super old [REDACTED] phone because I can't afford purchasing another iPhone right now, because of your case ruining my phone on top of that it started leaking while in my purse luckily I did not ruin it too. When my fiance took it off my phone to throw it away it also caused him a skin rash we have been putting cream on it and it has been healing up thankfully. However I am super upset about my iPhone 6!
justification: Skin rash caused by contact with the leaking case, resulting in injury.

incident_description: Have a Motorola cell phone DROID Razar that has a bulge forming on the backside.  It appears to be a batery issue.  Have contacted both the provider Verizon and the manufacturer, Motorola about it.  Neither appeared to be interested in addressing the issue.
justification: Potential for property damage (phone) and possible injury if the bulge bursts.

incident_description:
I purchased a HP Spectre x360-13-40002dx August 2015.  I use this laptop for business travel and presentations.  Although the computer is 2 years old (out of warranty) it only has about 50 hours of computers use.  Today, I started it up for a presentation and it died after about 2 minutes.  I had borrow a computer from my client to continue with my presentation.  When I returned home I tried starting the computer up again.  It started but then died again 2 minutes later.  It would not take a charge, charging lights did not go on.  I then smelled an electrical burning smell.  I removed the cover of the laptop and discovered that a portion of the motherboard had melted and burned in addition to a spot of the cover that burned plastic.

I researched online and found at HP's own site dozens of customers with the same problem as I had.  HP it seems did fix some of the customers laptops for free, when I called to report the issue all they could say is that I was out of the warranty period for the fix to be covered by HP.  I could pay $700 to have it fixed (a new one costs about $1,000).  This was not going to work for me.  I might as well buy a new laptop (which I did.  Not an HP).

I am concerned with the number of times this has happened and the safety of these computers in people's homes.  What happens if it happens at a business or home and noone is around to smell that the computer is burning and lights the business and home on fire?
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident resulted in significant downtime and data loss, and the potential for fire hazard is high.

incident_description:
My Dell laptop, model 15 i5558, overheated and smelled burning. It shuts down in 2 minutes. If I did not take out the battery, one corner of the laptop will burn.
I was using the laptop watching news for 20 minutes. It is still under the one-year warranty.
justification: While no injury occurred, the potential for property damage (burnt laptop) was high, and the incident could have escalated if the battery wasn't removed.

incident_description:
I am reporting a hazardous incident with an Insignia brand television. This tv set was purchased in 2012 and has been used in my living room ever since.

Last week, while in use, the tv made a loud popping sound, and then began smoking. The set was then unplugged from the wall and we discovered that a hole has actually melted in the back of it.

If no one had been in the room at the time, I believe that this could easily have started a fire.

I have also notified Insignia Products about this.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a significant risk of fire, hence severity level 2.

incident_description: My workplace has a 50" Samsung un50j6200afxza TV hanging on the wall in my department. Last night, the TV malfunctioned and part of the TV melted! No one was in the building when it happened, and luckily it didn't start a fire, but it's concerning to think that these TV's can short out so bad, and for no reason, that they start to melt. I looked this up and found many people has the same exact problem with their Samsung TV's.
justification: Although no one was injured, the incident of a TV melting due to malfunction is concerning and could potentially cause harm if someone had been present.

incident_description:
I used this product to all of my interests, reading, banking, hobbies, taxes, any and all household things that could be accomplished on the  computers, i.e. emails, etc.

I am a disabled woman and was using the laptop to pay bills and complete our budget, when I smelled something burning and felt likes bees or a stinging sensation on my left breast.

I lifted the laptop and the pain was pretty significant.  I called my husband back to the bedroom and he took the laptop from me and noticed it looked as if it was melting.  He set it in the sink to not catch anything on fire.

I reached over and felt the stinging area and water gushed out onto my hand and onto the floor.  My husband was walking back into the bedroom and said the entire left side of my left breast was burned.  It was a huge blister that had formed and popped when I touched it very softly.  It was the size of a softball if not a little bigger.  We doctored it up with a cleaner, burn cream and Neosporin. We did that for about two days and it continually got worse

I went to the Doctor and she could not believe it.  I had developed cellulitis (staph infection) she put me on two weeks of an antibiotic and told me if it was no better in a few days I would have to be put in the hospital.  My breast was swollen twice the size and looked horrible.

I called the consumer protection agency after the incident to let them know.  They did not take a report, did not ask for one, she showed no interest at all.  Told me to make sure to get rid of the laptop, I told her that my husband had already taken care of that.  We had three younger children in the house and the last thing was them getting burned as badly to get cellulitis.

I can get the doctor notes if needed it would not be a problem.  This was at the end of 2013 because right after that in February I became very ill with pneumonia and had to have a very critical surgery involving 4 chest tubes.

We have moved from Virginia to North Carolina

OUR NEW ADDRESS IS: [REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in a significant injury (cellulitis) and could have been more severe if not treated promptly.

incident_description: Liquid came out irritated hand & diver, glitter leaked out of case
justification: Liquid and glitter leakage caused no injury, but could have led to slippery conditions.

incident_description:
Caller stated that she experienced similar problems of recall#[REDACTED].  Hazard: The jumpstartÃÂs lithium battery can overheat and cause the units to melt, catch fire and ignite nearby items, posing a fire hazard to consumers.

She stated that her spouse was charging his truck batteries it overheated and caught fire to the unit and the cargo in his truck.   The fire department was called and they contained the fire.  Caller reported that her spouse truck and inventory was completely destroyed, not sure of the estimate of property damages. She stated that they have bought several of these batteries and it was reported to them by the truck drivers that they had incidents with them.

Caller feels that these battery chargers should be recalled.
justification: The incident resulted in significant property damage but no injuries, and multiple reports of similar issues indicate a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: Was using the product to power a laptop in my office, when the box portion sparked and started smoking. Immediately unplugged it as it was clearly unsafe.
justification: The product sparked and started smoking, indicating a malfunction that could have led to a fire or explosion, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: On 6/10/17 my wife and I were having dinner and smelled an electrical odor in our home. After searching our house frantically we saw the tv was smoking. I unplugged the tv immediately and the left side of the tv was melted. This tv is an e-series from vizio that is only 4 months old. I removed the tv from our home in fear that it still may be burning on the inside. I'm still waiting for a response from Vizio and Walmart.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a potential fire hazard, thus severity level 2.

incident_description: Electronic device battery charger was charging on kitchen counter when, according to homeowner, exploded into flames and hurling parts and flaming debris throughout kitchen and surrounding area
justification: No injuries were reported, but the incident caused significant property damage and could have led to injuries if someone had been nearby.

incident_description: I had my Samsung Note 4 on my bed.  When I woke up the next morning the screen was black and I couldn't get it to turn on.  I took my protective case off and noticed there was a burn hole in the plastic backing. The area around the charging port was charred.  If I hadn't had the protective case on, it would have burnt my bed. T mobile sold this phone to me and refuses to replace it with another Note or better phone of equal value. This is my second Note 4.  My first one was replaced by Tmobile because of issues it had. My mother is also on her second Note 4 because her first had issues. I would say the Note 4 is a really bad model. Since Tmobile refused to replace it with a decent phone, I contacted Samsung and had to mail the phone to them.  I'm not waiting to see what they say, and if they are going to replace it.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage (phone) but no physical harm, and the likelihood of occurrence is possible given the history of issues with the Note 4 model.

incident_description:
Caller states that he had a battery charger that exploded and created flames 1 1/2 to 2 feet high burning both of his hands, destroyed the battery including the metal.  
The charger is labeled that it has lithium ion cells.
It is used to jumpstart cars but he states also products in and around the home.
He is creating this report due to the hazard of fire and burning.
The caller treated his own burned hands with burn cream and cool towels.
justification: The incident resulted in severe burns to both hands, indicating a high severity level. The frequent use of the charger for various purposes suggests a high likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description: I purchased a cell phone battery from Amazon from PowerBear.  I received the battery on 5/21/17 at which time I charged it for@ 12 hours.  On 5/22/17, I had real issues except that I had to charge my phone 2 times that day.  I felt that was unusual as it was a new battery.  On 5/23/17, I used my phone briefly in the morning, and as I was preparing to pick my children up from school, I went to grab my phone from my dresser and noticed it was extremely hot, similar to the bottom of a pan on a hot stove.  I noticed that the phone was stuck on the home screen, none of the functions were working.  I took a small piece of wood and pulled the battery out, I was fearful of the battery catching fire.  I placed my original battery back into the phone, upon turning the device, it was stuck on the home screen.  The defective battery caused the internal wires in my phone to get fried ( this is what the AT&T representative).  My concern is that the battery could have possibly burned one of my children.
justification: The battery overheated and could have caused a fire, potentially leading to injury.

incident_description: My college Admissions office purchased ~ 500 portable customized power bank charging units which are typcially used to quick charge a cell phone or other type of tablet as "give-aways" for our open houses.  The units are marked with the college name.  Approximately 40 units were distributed on April 7, 2017 to prospective students.  On Friday April 14th, our admissions office received an E-mail from one of these students indicating that the device had been charged and then ignited.  I have requested this device back from this prospective student and sent her a SASE in which to return it, but have not yet received it back.  I contacted the distributor from whom these units were purchased and she provided the importer information to me.
justification: While no injuries have been reported, the potential for a fire hazard exists as the device ignited after charging.

incident_description: I purchased an Onkyo TX NR717 audio/video receiver new in Nov 2013. Several months ago the unit started having problems powering up, displaying video, etc. Then about 2 months ago I was in my living room, smelled a burning electrical smell, and saw sparks shooting out of the top of the unit's cabinet. Fortunately I was able to quickly unplug the unit before it started a fire. If I was not home I believe the unit could have started a fire which could have damaged or destroyed my home.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard, but no injuries occurred.

incident_description: Both my wife' and my own samsung galaxy 5 mobile phone swelled up and split open 3 weeks apart at 14 months old. neither samsung nor verizon would accept any responsibility and verizon told me to take the wife's home as they had no responsibility. The first failed on July 01 2017 and the second on July 22 2017
justification: Both phones failed within a short period, indicating a possible manufacturing defect.

incident_description: I have a Nexus 5 phone from Google Project Fi.  In charging the phone today so much heat was generated that the Anchor connector melted and literally was welded to the phone.  This is the secord or third time I've seen the phone get very hot while charging.  Had the phone been on a different surface, it could have started a fire.
justification: While no injury occurred, the incident could have resulted in property damage or fire if the phone had been charging on a different surface.

incident_description:
On Sunday the 23rd of April 2017, I charged my Apple iPad 4, a school issued device, along with my school issued Logitech keyboard. Upon inspection of my ipad keyboard I noticed that a corner of my keyboard had melted. The location was near the Bluetooth and battery compartments. The damage to my colleague's keyboard posed a risk of fire, personal injury and a loss to a school device. 

A greater concern would have been should I have taken my iPad device and keyboard with me to complete school work during Spring Vacation.  The potential risk of having this happening on an airplane, the results could have been devastating, should the keyboard have caught fire. At this time, we have not confirmed any Logitech iPad Keyboard recalls.
justification: While no injury occurred, the melted keyboard posed a risk of fire and personal injury, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description: My incident concerns a portable wireless bluetooth speaker manufactured by HMDX that melted and had a small fire that resulted in smoke coming out of a students locker at Northmont Middle School in Clayton, Ohio. We received a general fire alarm when a teacher saw smoke coming from the locker and pulled the fire alarm. School was evacuated prior to FD arrival. The SRO officer was on the premises and he pulled the backpack from the locker and put it out with a fire extinguisher  that was directly across the hall mounted in a fire box. This speaker was in a students locker and no charging cord was in use. The speaker was powered off but the internal battery caused the small fire and black smoke. When fire department arrived the speaker was laying on the floor all smoldering was out due to SRO using extinguisher. There were no injuries due to quick evacuation of the school. Fire department made certain the speaker was completely extinguished and took possession of the speaker with the middle school principle and SRO's permission in order to further investigate and report to CPSC. Pictures were obtained documenting the scene prior to removal.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident involved a fire in a school, posing significant potential risk.

incident_description:
DO NOT USE THIS BATTERY. THIS BATTERY EXPLODED in our home and caught fire to our furniture, floors, and walls as well as minor injuries to us. This battery was purchased from AMAZON and less than one year old. Out house was only saved because we were there to put ourselves in harms way to stop the fire. THIS BATTERY COMPROMISES THE SAFETY of ANYONE WHO HAD PURCHASED IT, if not for our incident then simply for the unknown.

This battery showed no indication of problems for eleven months of standard use until the day it caused multiple explosions. The laptop had not been subject to unusual circumstances and exploded without warning.

AMAZON HAS NOT HELPED with this at all and has been completely unwilling to share the manufacturers information with us so that we can file a report with CONSUMER SERVICES. I have spent 6 hours on the phone with Amazon and countless emails with photographic and video evidence on to be run in circles and ignored. Broken promises from AMAZON of even returning my phone call at all. DO NO BUY THIS BATTERY.

We are extremely concerned by the possibility of an even worse outcome. We adamantly affirm that the only reason we did not lose out entire house to fire was because of the good fortuned of being home and close enough at the time of detonation to be able to actively save our house.
justification: The battery caused explosions, fire, and minor injuries, demonstrating a high likelihood of recurrence given its unexpected failure.

incident_description: The Supco Surge Protector was installed on my HVAC system in 2014 or 2013.  This morning I noticed charring on the side of my home, and a hole in my siding.  The surge protector had caught fire overnight, and thankfully, the fire went out.
justification: Although the fire was contained and no injuries occurred, the incident caused property damage, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
So...bought a new Asus laptop. 6 mos. into use the silver sheathing on the charger end that goes into the computer began to fail. By that I mean that an apparent weak spot began to crack. At that point I contacted Asus and they understood my concern and acted as if they were going to replace it.
After continued contact on my part over 2 weeks time I was told it was my fault and I would have to buy another plug. 
I called them again this week as now it is sparking and I have ceased using my laptop. Asus agreed that this is a safety concern but refused any warranty assistance. 
I know of two other people who have the same issue with their Asus. It's not just me.
It's not about the money, it's their disregard for consumer safety. I'll never deal with them again.
Personally, I believe this is a design flaw because the plug end is a 90 degree angle and was not thoroughly thought through. How about that for alliteration!
I have an old Samsung laptop that has a straight in plug that has never failed and has always felt reliable and safe.
I'm afraid the spark will turn into fire, and not just for me.
Thank you for listening.
justification: Potential fire hazard due to charger design flaw, as evidenced by personal experience and others reporting similar issues.

incident_description:
3/5/2016 
Consumer stated he contacted manufacture and they were unable to assist him because he didn't have a order number. He advised manufacture he received tablet as a gift.

3/5/2016
Consumer stated he had tablet charging with charger for about 30 minutes when he tried to unplug the charger from the 120V receptacle (electrical wall outlet). He stated the cover came off the charger with the wiring exposed. He stated he had to carefully unplug charger from 120V electrical wall outlet, he feels this poses a shock hazard.
justification: The incident involved a potential shock hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
My wife purchased a Samsung Galaxy S7 phone in July, 2016.  After hearing several reports about Samsung hand-held devices catching on fire, we checked to see if her phone was on the recall list.  According to our telephone service provider (Sprint), the Samsung Galaxy S7 was not on any product recall or warning lists.

Last Tuesday (5/16/17), my wife's Samsung Galaxy S7 spontaneously and without warning began to smolder and burn.  At the time of the incident, the phone was resting on top of a granite kitchen countertop.  The phone was not connected to the charger, or any other device.  Additionally, the phone was not near any heat source when it combusted.  My wife stated the she heard a popping noise similar to a soda bottle exploding and then saw smoke emanating from our kitchen.  I was outside and she quickly called to me about the fire.  I witnessed the phone burning within 30 seconds of it catching on fire.  Our house was filling with smoke, which smelt like burning plastic and electronics.  There was also a low blue flame coming out the side of the phone and heat radiating from it. I immediately used a kitchen utensil to push the phone onto a cookie tin and then brought it outside where it continued to smoke for several minutes.

We feel fortunate that the phone combusted on the granite and during daytime, rather than any of the more probable locations that we place it (pocket, purse, bed, couch, driving in our cars, my daughter's hands, etc...) throughout the day and night

Thankfully nobody was injured and the only property damage was the phone itself.

If it would be helpful to investigate this matter, I would be happy to send either photos or the actual phone to any independent consumer safety agency.

Our Samsung Galaxy S7 phone is extremely dangerous and very easily could have ruined the lives of my family.

Thank you for your interest in this matter.
justification: The phone spontaneously combusted, causing property damage and potential injury, but no one was harmed.

incident_description:
USB charger started to melt outside and burn inside.

Noticed phone was not charging in early morning. Checked to see if the charger was plugged in and found it was extremely hot. Immediately unplugged and noticed it actually started to melt on one side. Smelled like burning electronics. 

Took it apart later that day and found scorch marks inside. The PCB was burned brown in one area. Solder melted and dripped on the side opposite the burn marks.
justification: The charger's melting and burning indicate a potential fire hazard, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: I had my laptop sitting on a shelf, not plugged in. I started hearing a popping sound that became louder. Then I noticed where it was coming from. The laptop screen was bulging and cracking! It is almost separated completely, and the battery is visibly swelled up. The laptop was not plugged in at the time not was it recently before the bloating began.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage (laptop) but no injuries, and while similar incidents can occur, they are not common.

incident_description: My Pebble smart watch became extremely hot.  Although removed within seconds of onset it left a red mark on my wrist, which is still somewhat visible approximately 3 hours later.  The watch became extremely hot to the touch, as was witnessed by several co-workers.  It started cooling down after several minutes, but no longer works.
justification: The watch caused a visible burn on the user's wrist, indicating an injury.

incident_description: I purchased a Lenovo laptop computer a few years ago.  I had to stop using over 2 years ago because the power cord (at the jack) melted right where it goes into the laptop, and the heat from the melting power jack damaged the laptop case.  I sent the laptop (my expense) to Lenovo, but their "tech" decided that it was my fault.  How they came to that conclusion, I will never know.  The melted jack could've only been damaged by overheating or if I were to hold a lighter under it!
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no physical injury, and the likelihood of occurrence is possible given the reported issue with the power cord.

incident_description:
(03/03/2017) The consumer was charging his phone. After about a couple of minutes, sparks were coming out from behind the plug where the retractable plug is located. The consumer stated that he has used the product several times prior.

(03/04/2017) The consumer contacted the firm via email but have not received a response.
justification: Sparks indicate a potential fire hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
This caller is reporting that her Galaxy 6 Active phone exploded while on charge sitting in living room while this caller was sleeping.
Her alarm sounded and when she got up to check she saw gray smoke, black soot and fumes that burned her throat badly enough that it is still burning.
The phone and the cover are burned together making it impossible for her to obtain EMEI number. 
Her phone number for this phone is [REDACTED].
This was a very traumatizing incident for this caller after she lost her brother in a house fire as a child.
There are no injuries being reported in this incident
She has not contacted the manufacturer, however, she does intend to contact them.
justification: While no injuries were reported, the incident involved a significant event (phone explosion) with potential hazards (smoke, fumes), making it an 'Incident, No Injury' scenario. The likelihood is 'possible' as such incidents, though rare, can occur.

incident_description: I bought a goalzero 150 yeti from Amazon a couple of years ago, for about $4.00. The battery didn't last very long, then out of juice quickly. I tried it twice, just didn't work, thought I did something wrong so didn't return. I kept it plugged in at home just in case of power outages. I really figured it was just a bad battery, bought another. My husband went to install today, couldn't get the other one out. It had a large bulge in it, the case kept it from getting bigger. It looks like it was a defective battery. Not sure if battery or unit overheats or both.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a defective product with a bulging battery, posing a potential safety hazard.

incident_description:
Philips tv model # 47PFL3603D/27 Serial # YAC1C0814011566
My tv caught fire Saturday morning Apr 8, 2017. As I was watching tv i noticed smoke coming from the TV and the picture began cutting in and out, next thing I knew there was a fire coming up from the top of the tv 2-3 inches high.

I quickly jumped up and unplugged it from the wall and the fire went out. If I was not there to catch this, it easily could have caused a fire in my house or worse even injury to someone if this was not caught quickly. 

I then though it would be prudent to notify Philips to inform them of the issue, so this would not happen to others. I wrote several emails back and forth with Philips Customer service. They asked for additional pictures which I sent and in result they told me the tv failed in a safe manner. I told them I could still turn on the tv and It would still smoke and something internal would turn bright orange and begin to flame. I informed them that I would love to send them the tv for evaluation. They didn't want to see it, basically told me I was over-reacting and that it failed in safe manner. It bothers me when someone is willing to send a faulty product to someone for evaluation and they did not even care to see it.

This needs to be made to the attention of someone as this could have been a very serious situation if the tv was on and I was not around to pull the power. Someone could have been seriously injured or possibly died and my house could have burned down if it caught anything else on fire. Others need to be notified as well, and apparent to this website, my model tv, several others have reported that this tv has started fire on them as well. Please investigate and let me know if you need any additional information from me as well. I could also forward the emails back and forth with them.

Thank you!

It is also would be prudent to warn others of a potential fire hazard with this model tv.
justification: The TV could have caused a house fire or injury if not immediately unplugged.

incident_description:
Upgraded my cell phone in January 2017 and paid over $700.00 to a Samsung S7 galaxy. After few months, my cell phone start overheating. On June 24, 2017 my cell phone got so hot that I could not hold it in my hand. Contacted Samsung CO. and had a long chat with one of their rep. and got a ticket [4143410190]. I was told not to use anymore the phone. To go to my carrier, ATT and get a loaner phone. Went over there they looked at me funny. THEY DO NOT DO LOANER PHONES.That was not right. Called their support team and tried to fix it over the phone. They said no need for a replacement. Then on 07/07/2017 my phone got so hot that I had to place it in the fridge. Called again their support team same day and got another ticket ID 2169324256. Also I was told not to use the phone and call their support team @1-800-726-7864. I did. They promised that they will contact me the very next day,07/08/2017 @ 1pm AT. They did not contacted me. Today I just got a message on my phone that the phone is over heating. At this time I'm afraid to use my phone. It might melt or explode in my hand. All I wanted a replacement and a better phone. Now, I want a refund of all I spent on my phone and accessories. 

Thank you

[REDACTED]
justification: Phone overheating to the point of being unusable and potentially causing injury, despite multiple attempts to resolve the issue with the manufacturer and carrier.

incident_description: (03/20/2017) The consumer stated that her son had thrown the tablet into his trashcan because it did not work. The consumer found it and saw that the battery had expanded. She is afraid that the tablet might explode.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning device with an expanded battery, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
I have a Belkin extension cord with a rotating plug and it could have started a fire. When I went on Amazon to review the product I found some of reports of the same thing, and pictures just like mine with the plug melted in the same way. Belkin replied to my post and asked for me to contact them. I know they are going to ask for me to send them the cord but I read in an article (this has made the news) that the last person who did that Belkin took the cord and wouldn't send it back and said everything was fine. Well things are not fine this could have burned my house down.

I would like CPSC to take the cord and investigate.

To see the review I left with pictures go here: https://www.amazon.com/review/R1PKXBSUKEYRIQ/ref=pe_1098610_137716200_cm_rv_eml_rv0_rv

You can see for that product a number of other 1 star reviews with pictures. Mine is an older model of that product but has the same rotating plug. I think that is the problem.
justification: Multiple reports and visual evidence of the same issue with the product, indicating a high likelihood of the incident occurring again.

incident_description: On 5/2/2017, the Appleton (WI) Fire Department was dispatched for a report of a smoke alarm sounding in a Community Based Residential Facility (CBRF).  Upon arrival, we located a fire burning in a second floor bedroom.  Following extinguishment, fire investigators identified that the cause of the fire was a portable battery charger.
justification: No injuries were reported, but the fire caused property damage, making it an incident with a possible occurrence likelihood due to the presence of portable chargers in residential facilities.

incident_description: Grandson's tablet (Chromo model C13197) began smoking when he turned it on, March 11, 2017.  Filled his bedroom with smoke. I cut the battery wires and placed the unit outside.  We used a fan to ventilate the house.  It was not necessary to call the fire dept.  I sent an email to the company, and they have not responded as of March 18, 2017.  We still have the unit, and will keep it until we hear from you or the company,
justification: No injuries occurred, but the incident involved a significant risk with the tablet smoking and filling the room with smoke.

incident_description:
Normally I will charge my cell phone completely in the evening, and unplug it overnight (so the battery doesn't get overcharged). In the morning while getting ready, I will "top off" the charge so the phone is at 100% when I leave. 

While traveling in March, I had charged my phone fully in the evening, and in the morning when I went to top it off, I noticed that there was significant melting to the power adapter. As this was an obvious fire hazard, I did not attempt to connect and charge the phone in the morning. 

I attempted to contact LG the next morning, and as this has still not been resolved (more than a month later) am I bringing it to the CPSC. 

The phone was less than a month old at the time of incident and there were no signs of damage to the charger when I used it the night before (when the incident occurred). 

I double checked the voltages on the adapter (as I was traveling) before using it, and it does indeed say it can tolerate 110 - 240v.
justification: Potential fire hazard due to melted power adapter, though no injury occurred.

incident_description:
I noticed that the display glass on my Note 3 was de-laminating and there was a gap between the top of the side bezel and the glass.  Upon investigation I deteremined that the battery has swollen.  The nominal thickness of the battery is 5.4mm, and it has swollen about 80% to 9.4mm thick.

I consider this a dangerous condition and have removed my battery.  Samsung refuses to replace it (defective though it may be) because it isn't under warranty.  I bought the phone new 3 or 4 years ago.  It has never been wet, and isn't damaged.
justification: Battery swelling poses a risk of fire or explosion, but no injuries or deaths have been reported in this specific case.

incident_description:
This caller is reporting his 19 year old daughters cell phone purchased from phone store in Johnson City, New York June 17, 2016.
She had no problems with the phone until Thursday, November 17, 2016 when she was using the phone then it began flickering, the phone popping with white smoke coming from it.  She threw the phone at her bed, it fell to the floor then blew up.
IEMI# not identifiable 
The caller said that the phone is burning more on the right side about three inches long, three and one half inches long and the odor from the phone filled his entire home.
He is reporting this incident as a fire and burn injury hazard; if his 19 year old had kept it in her hand or if his 10 year old had been borrowing it as she sometimes did then they could have been very badly harmed.
He contacted the manufacturer and he was assured that the phone will be replaced by them, he is however a bit worried that it must be the same model.
The IMEI# on the phone is burned beyond recognition.
justification: Phone explosion caused burn injury hazard, could have resulted in severe harm if held by the user or her 10-year-old sister.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting that her mother's laptop caused a house fire.  She stated that it was totally consumed in fire, the fire department was able to retrieve the battery from the fire.  She stated that the laptop was charging (not sure how long) but it exploded and the flames started to spread in the home.  the fire department was contacted and they came out.  The fire consumed the home it was a total loss.

The manufacturer was contacted.
justification: The laptop's battery exploding while charging caused the fire, leading to the house being consumed, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
We have been using this phone for 16 days.  Sitting on the couch with the phone in hand we heard a POP.  

NOTE: No pressure or impact occurred, it was not dropped.  My wife and I were both on the couch too when this happened and saw the entire event.

The phone shattered from what looks like a pinpoint from the inside out as you can see from the photos.  From what it looks like It directly on the corresponds to where the digitizer meets the corner.
justification: The phone shattered spontaneously, causing no injury but resulting in a significant incident.

incident_description:
On February 10, 2017, shortly after turning on my Toshiba computer, I observed a flashing orange light with smoke
and burnt plastic smell coming from upper right corner of laptop (above on/off button).! immediately turned off
the computer and the flashing orange light ceased but the burnt plastic smell lingered.
I subsequently used the computer periodically between February 10-23, 2017 without a repeat of the February 10
incident.
On February 23, 20171 received a "Important Product Safety Notification" regarding my computer from Amazon
(from whom I had originally purchased my computer), which stated in pertinent part as follows: "We have learned of
a potential safety issue that may impact product(s) you purchased through the Amazon.com website: Toshiba
Satellite CSS-C5241 15.61nch Laptop (Intel Core iS, 8GB, 1 TB HDD), Black"
When I removed battery to get Serial Number (per instructions from recall notice), the fused plastic (from battery to
computer) broke apart. It was obvious where the fire had melted the plastic on both the battery and the laptop.
After battery reconnected to computer, the computer would not turn on.
The serial number on the battery did not match those on the then existing recall notice.
justification: Potential fire hazard caused injury to the laptop and battery, with a high likelihood given the recall notice and observed damage.

incident_description: On Thursday, 6/22/17 at about 6 pm my wife and I were watching our Samsung HD TV as we usually do but tonight was different.  Some smoke started to come out of the top of the set.  There was obviously a fire inside and the smoke rapidly increased and filled the room but there were no flames visible.  I immediately turned off the TV, pulled all the plugs, and took it outside.   The smoke stopped and the fire appeared to be out so we brought the Samsung inside but did not plug it in.  I called Samsung and the Customer Svs rep said that the dept that handles these issues would call me back in 2 hours or tomorrow.  I also called Sams Club which is where we purchased the TV and told them what happened.  There was no damage to my home.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident involved a fire in the TV, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' case. The likelihood is 'possible' as TV fires, though rare, can happen.

incident_description: I had a portable charger form the manufacturer TYLT model number WA-15TPP5200 in my pocket and it exploded causing 2nd and 3rd degree burns to my upper thigh. Due to the trauma and shock at the time of the incident I did not pick up the smoldering device from the ground and left the area to seek help. Later when family members went to obtain the device it was no longer there. Attempts to seek assistance with the medical expenses (approx $70.000) from the company have been without success as I do not have the product. I do have the receipt from when the product was purchased as well as pictures of the injuries.
justification: The incident resulted in significant injuries (2nd and 3rd degree burns) but no fatalities, and the likelihood of such an event occurring is possible given the product's malfunction.

incident_description: I had used the laptop off an on thru out the morning. I left it on my desk in the dining room when I left my apt to run some errands. When I returned I could smell burnt electric odor an noticed paperwork by the laptop charred upon closer inspection saw where the battery had popped an left the case of laptop an inside components melted or charred.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage (charred paperwork, melted laptop components) but no injuries, and it's possible that this could happen again due to similar circumstances.

incident_description: The charger is overheating but do not deforming the battery plastic cover. The battery will not hold charge and will emit a burning odor if leave the battery on the charger after charger indicator turn green. No injuries.
justification: While no injuries were reported, the incident of the charger overheating and emitting a burning odor poses a potential fire risk, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description: I would like to report a Motorola Motor Z Droid play cell phone that overheated, melted the charge port and burned my son's arm. I am afraid that this could happen again and cause severe damage or harm to someone or something. I have contacted Motorola but they do not seem willing to help resolve the situation. I have pictures that I would be happy to supply. Thanks.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (burned arm) and the likelihood of a similar occurrence is high given the product's defect and lack of manufacturer response.

incident_description:
(12/12/2016)The consumer stated that he had the phone next to his face on the left side.  The phone was not on the charger. The consumer stated that he sleeps with the phone next to his face because he is hard of hearing.

(12/13/2016)The next morning when he woke he discovered that the phone was hot and was stuck to his face. The consumer immediately went to the emergency room at [REDACTED] Hospital. The attendants had to remove the phone from his face. The consumer had second degree burns on the let side of his face

(12/13/2016)The consumer contacted the firm. He was advised to take the phone back to the place of purchase. When he took it back he was advised to contact the manufacturer. 

The consumer contacted the manufacturer and was transferred to the Customer Safety Department. A report was taken by the department [REDACTED]. The consumer was advised to take pictures of his face , pictures of the phone and pictures of his medical bills and upload to the manufacturer's site.

The consumer took the phone back to an Apple store for a replacement but the store refused to do anything with the phone.
justification: Second degree burns on the consumer's face indicate a severe injury (severity level 3), and while the exact cause is not clear, the likelihood of a similar incident occurring again (likelihood 3) is possible given the consumer's habit of sleeping with the phone next to his face.

incident_description:
Folding laundry on 4/23/17 watching tv.  All of a sudden, TV starts having a sizzling/hissing sound.  A minute or 2 later, smoke begins billowing out of the back and begins having a small flame coming out of the back.  I dove for the outlet and unplugged it.  The smoking almost immediately stopped and the flame disappeared.  We purchased the TV new and I have always been concerned about the amount of heat it put off.

Had we not been home (we normally are not home Sunday nights), our house would have burned down and potentially killed our pets.

The TV is a 9-10 year old Samsung Plasma with a 100,000 hour life rating.  This means the TV should have lasted 60-70 years depending on usage, not 9-10.  Now the TV is inoperable.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident could have resulted in a house fire and potential loss of life if not at home.

incident_description: I had the watch for about 10 hours when I went to check time and it exploded on my wrist.  It instantly became scorching hot and I rapidly removed it from my wrist to prevent injury from heat, fire or contents of the battery pack.  At my age (68) the incident startled me but the redness on the top side of my wrist subsided without the need for medical attention and I do not believe physical injury other than the momentary heat occurred.  After two days of trying to work with Apple to no avail, I was left with no other option than to give up and the report the incident for the benefit of other costumers wearing what I have now learned from internet searches is a very dangerous product.
justification: While no lasting injury occurred, the incident caused momentary heat and fear, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
On 4/22/2017, the Appleton (WI) Fire Department was dispatched for a call regarding a cellular phone that had caught on fire.  Upon arrival, the responding unit stated that the consumer had noticed that their LG Model K450 cellular phone, serial #610CYBD115557, was having a problem with the clock display.  The consumer then stated that they were in the process of taking the battery out of the phone when, the phone started on fire.  The cellular phone reportedly was not plugged-in/charging at the time.  The consumer quickly extinguished the fire by placing the phone into a glass of water.  No other fire damage occurred other than to the phone.  The phone was retained by the consumer.

[REDACTED]
Appleton (WI) Fire Department
justification: No injuries occurred, but the incident involved a fire, albeit contained and extinguished quickly.

incident_description: My Xbox controller was placed on the charger.  Afew hours later I could smell a burning odor, removed the controller and felt a burning pain on my hand causing me to drop the controller on the floor.  The battery cover appeared partially melted. I removed it and popped out the battery with a quarter as it was extremely hot.
justification: Injury occurred due to contact with an overheating Xbox controller, which is a possible event.

incident_description: In early March 2017, I purchased two Kensington Expert Wireless Trackball Mice for my office computers.  The night before last, as I was working on my computer, I started smelling something burning. It was the Trackball.  I opened the area where the batteries were, smoke was coming out and it was hot to the touch.  Acid then started coming out of one of the batteries.  I was able to pry out the batteries with a mail opener, and I saw that part of one battery was melted to the device.  The batteries stayed very hot for a very long time.  I think something is very wrong with this product.
justification: Potential fire hazard caused by battery malfunction, no injuries reported.

incident_description: Child was putting Vtech Touch & Teach Word Book into toy bin. His index finger became pinched in the hinge part of it and got stuck. He started screaming, I helped him to get it out. He cried for like 5 minutes. Children toys should not pinch/trap body parts.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (finger pinch) and the likelihood of occurrence is high given the design flaw of the toy.

incident_description: I purchased this Alcatel Idol 4 with googles Phone at the Cricket store located at [REDACTED] on January 2, 2017 . I noticed that the phone gets very hot and freezes. Cricket refused to assist with this issue and advised to to contact the manufacturer. this phone  gets hot enough that it can not be held, and turns your hand and face red. I am concerned about excessive radiation exposure.At work I must keep my phone in my purse and I am concerned about fire. I have contacted the company who finally agreed to look at the phone if I mail it to them. When I went to the Cricket store to change the SIMs, the sales associate told me that she was aware of the heating issues and would not sell this phone herself. ( she was not the associate who sold me the phone)
justification: While no injuries have been reported, the phone's excessive heat poses a potential burn risk, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description: My HP laptop started on fire in the middle of the night. It exploded due to the battery. I woke up and put out the fire. I had to get new carpet, walls and ceiling painted, blinds cleaned, clothing dry cleaned, a new bed, nightstand, mattress/box spring, humidifier, CPAP machine, laptop,  vacuum, sheets, comforter, pillows and several other items. Walls had to be wiped down in several rooms.
justification: While no injuries were reported, the incident caused significant property damage, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description: TV was on and started to dis-color in the lower right hand side where the manual on/off switch is.  It turns out it was overheating and the frame and screen were melting.  It resulted in the screen distorting badly in that corner and prevented a picture from appearing across the entire screen.  Turning it off and back on only resulted in it continuing to burn and getting worse.
justification: The TV overheating and melting, though causing damage, did not result in any injuries.

incident_description: The 2007 Panasonic television made a loud popping noise went black and then caught fire where the plug goes into the back of the television. Fire department said that it was nothing in my home wiring it was the television  2007 Panasonic TH-50PX60U
justification: The television catching fire poses a potential hazard but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
BELKIN BP112230-08, 12 Outlets 4320 Joules Pivot-Plug SURGE PROTECTOR 

One night we see flames and smoke in the kitchen, just as we were getting ready for bed. Only item plugged in was a small chest freezer with max 1500W. We unplugged the surge protector, and put out the fire.

Really concerned if this happened n hour later, the house could have burned down.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the fire could have escalated and caused significant property damage if not discovered promptly.

incident_description: On Monday, April 10, 2017, I received a call from my adult son that my daughter's bedroom was filled with smoke.  I rushed home and he was correct.  It smelled electrical.  We could not find the cause of the smoke and called the fire department.  The fire department determined that my daughter's Jam Box was on her bed and had melted down into the comforter and almost to the mattress.  The speaker was not plugged in or on.  Her bedspread had been tossed over it by accident before she left for school.  The radio had spontaneously began to melt down and cause a fire without being in use.  Thank God my son was home to catch the start of what could have been a very serious fire in our home!
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a significant fire risk due to a defective speaker melting down and potentially igniting the bedding.

incident_description:
The television has been in the same location since it was unpackaged and setup. The television is free standing (not wall mounted) using the factory supplied base included within the original retail box. The television has been atop a multimedia cabinet utilizing 100% of the factory supplied hardware and stand/base. There are no items that contact the television or the base. There have been no instances where the television was impacted, abused, mishandled etc.

My wife was on the opposite side of the living room when the failure occurred. She recalls hearing a series of plastic breaking sounds, which drew her attention to the direction of the television. Immediately after hearing these sounds, she screamed as she witnessed the television fall forward onto our toddlers playpen area. Thank goodness, our toddler son and I were in the other room. The corner in which the television fell is where he likes to stand.

Inspection of the breakage reveals manufacturers defects/casting flaws/insufficient support.  This was an extremely popular item sold on Black Friday and is in numerous households across America.  I contacted the manufacturer, ([REDACTED]) and was routed to their international call center where I asked to speak to someone from their corporate offices - I was told the item is out of warranty and that no assistance could be given as the item is out of warranty. I explained that regardless of warranty status, this is a valid safety concern. I was told I would receive a return call in the future. I have not received a call back at this time.
justification: The television falling onto the toddler's playpen area could have resulted in injury, but fortunately no one was present.

incident_description: On 5/29/17, I had my Samsung Galaxy S6 active phone charging on my bed as I was sleeping. It was not covered by any materials. At around 3am, I wake up to a hissing noise and a harsh, chemical smell. I then see a flash of bright light and start screaming fire. My partner was still awake in the other room and rushed in. He grabbed the phone and threw it on the outside patio. The phone spewed chemicals on my bed, a blanket, and two pillows. It burnt a small hole in the bed and in a pillow. The charger, the charging port, and the outlet were all fine. The combustion started at the top of the phone. Thankfully, no one was injured.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident caused property damage and could have escalated into a more severe situation.

incident_description:
I've had battery problems with this tablet since shortly after my warranty ran out. When I called about getting it fixed, the call center told me I had to give them a credit card with almost $400 clear on it to fix it. That's more than the cost to replace it. So I just plugged it in when I needed it. The tablet was not plugged in at the time of the incident, and had not been plugged in or used for over a month. 

I just happened to be sitting near the tablet when I heard a loud "POP!" like a small firecracker that made my ear ring. I looked around and found the tablet had burst open and the battery looked like a balloon. I placed it outside on concrete just in case it caught fire and that's where it's been ever since.
justification: No injuries reported, but the incident could have caused property damage or fire.

incident_description:
The consumer indicates that his AC power cord is included in recall number 16-089.

The consumer indicates that the battery gets extremely hot while charging. The consumer states that his adapter is chafing at the very end of it where it connects into the brick.

02/11/2017 - The consumer visited a Microsoft store and inquired about the adapter. The representative he spoke to informed the consumer that only the AC power cord was included in a recall. The consumer would like both the AC power cord and adapter to be replaced so he turned down the opportunity to receive only an AC power cord replacement. If the consumer cannot get a replacement adapter, he plans on participating in the recall.

The consumer plans on keeping his adapter for the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.
justification: While the consumer hasn't reported any injuries yet, the adapter getting extremely hot and chafing indicates a potential fire hazard, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description: Hewlett Packard  CQ56-115DX computer was plugged into the charger and the battery exploded causing several fires in the bedroom.  The room filled with toxic smoke which created a life threatening environment.
justification: Battery explosion and toxic smoke indicate potential injuries, making it a 'possible' occurrence.

incident_description:
The phone while charging in normal air conditioned environment caught fire.

The smoke set off smoke detector in kitchen.  Had we not intervened it would have certainly been very bad.

The charging port on the phone destroyed the cable.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident caused significant property damage and could have escalated to a more severe event.

incident_description:
The consumer indicates that her cell phone was charging for approximately thirty minutes when she noticed that it was smoking on top of her sofa. The consume states that although her cell phone is fine, the charger made a small burn in the blanket that was on top of the sofa on which it laid on. The consumer states that the smoke was coming right at the end of the cord, before it actually plugs into the phone.

The consumer indicates that she used her charger on a daily basis for approximately eight hours. The consumer plans on keeping her charger for at least the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident caused property damage (burn mark on the blanket) and could have escalated to a more severe incident.

incident_description:
I have a Samsung Galaxy S7. Not the one that is on the recall list. My phone over heated badly and melted apart. I had to contact Samsung because Verizon said they can't touch it and said it was dangerous for it to do that. 

I contacted Samsung I told them the phone overheated till it was very hot. Informed them Verizon told me it is the same battery issue as the Samsung S7 Edge and Note. They told me they will come pick up my phone. They came Saturday to get it. I received a report today so I called them. They said it was "repaired" and being sent back. I told them you repaired a phone that is having the same issues as the recalled one??? He said once they repair them they are good to go. I told him I don't feel that is safe since the other models are being recalled.  I told him I am not going to use the phone and I will be doing what I need to when I get it. 

The guy who picked up the phone Saturday told me that my S7 Galaxy isn't the only one doing this. He said they are losing money over the first one. Someone told me not to let them get away with fixing a phone that melted apart. Which is what they are trying to do instead of letting people know this is happening.

Today this was the result. I have attached photos to show the damage to my phone. They said backed cover cracked. Back cover was not cracked it melted apart due to the battery issue.
