Ship Company: UPS
Tracking Number: [REDACTED]
Serial number: 355301077384918
Please view additional information below for more details.

Original Problem:
HARDWARE ISSUE - TEMPERATURE ISSUES - PHONE IS WARM WHILE IN USE

Problem found:
TOUCHPAD DAMAGED - ABUSE - BACK COVER CRACKED - ABUSE - REAR COVER - COSMETICS

Solution:
REPLACED LCD - REPLACED COSMETIC - REPLACED COSMETIC - REPLACED COMPONENT
justification: The phone overheating and melting, despite not being on the recall list, indicates a significant safety issue, making future occurrences likely.

incident_description: In early April, I noticed my MacBook Pro case was bulging and expanding. Because I was concerned that something was wrong, I unscrewed the screws off the back of the laptop and noticed the battery in the computer had significantly expanded and looked as if it was going to explode. I immediately removed the swollen battery from the laptop.
justification: Potential for property damage (laptop) but no injury reported.

incident_description: I bought the Energizer 2X Charging System for Xbox One from Amazon.com it was working well, but after 2 weeks the light was 'twitching' while the controllers were in place. Also after 15 minutes or so the controller would get very hot, unfortunately it wouldn't charge all the way because I was afraid it would melt my controller. Since it is my only source for charging I use it occasionally just to get me through a session of gaming.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the charging system malfunctioned, causing the controller to overheat and not charge fully, which could lead to further damage or inconvenience.

incident_description:
(03/13/2017) The consumer stated that her daughter was cooking in the microwave. The consumer heard an explosion and thought it came from the microwave. The consumer discovered that the batteries had exploded. The consumer stated that the batteries were in the middle of her dining table but were not near any heat. The batteries had exploded into pieces and the case flew about 6-8 feet across the room.

(03/13/2017) The consumer contacted the firm and was advised that no one had complained about the batteries. The firm did not get any information from the consumer but offered another set of batteries which the consumer declined.
justification: Batteries exploded, causing property damage but no injuries.

incident_description: I would like to report a defective  VIZIO flat screem TV model VL370M  I have owned  this TV for a while now, recently , at night after turning the set off I have become sick: nauseated/vomiting I became alarmed and finally  noticed that  a toxic fume emanates from the TV after powering it off , this is cause of me felling sick, I contacted VIZIO to no avail
justification: The incident resulted in nausea and vomiting, indicating injury, and the likelihood is almost certain given the consistent symptoms after turning off the TV.

incident_description: Galaxy s8 plus screen shattered and shards are coming off embedding into my fingers
justification: Shards embedding into fingers indicates injury, but not life-threatening.

incident_description:
03/29/2017 9:40pm -The fire chief was advised by the person in the apartment that the smoke was coming from the end of the speaker. When the person picked the unit up, it burst into flames. The renter stated that they poured over the device to put the fire out. 

The fire alarm system activated and alerted the fire department . The fire department came out but the fire was already out. The device was confiscated by the fire department.
justification: No injuries were reported, but the incident resulted in property damage and activation of the fire alarm system.

incident_description: TV purchased 2/2013.  On May 11, 2017 we were watching tv and there a loud pop from the back with sparks and fire.  Unplugged tv and moved it outside and it subsided.
justification: No injuries were reported, but the incident involved fire and sparks, making it an incident with no injury.

incident_description: Cell phone caught on fire while charging on OEM charger and cable. Burnt out the charger port, and phone stopped functioning soon after.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident resulted in property damage (burnt charger port and non-functional phone), hence severity level 2.

incident_description:
I bought an HP laptop in December and the liquid screen of the laptop broke by itself. The liquid condensed and caused a cracked that Hp think I caused. I did not cause it and it is very easy to investigate. I have the laptop returned from hp that did not want to honor the manufactuere warrantee. HP techinican refused to investigate what cause it. The liquid from the screen spilled and caused red spot in my skin. 
Please investigate. I have my pc available for you to take a look at it.
Since this issue happened I have develop a rash. I am going to see my doctor for a check up the 22th. Not sure if this is related to his issue but one thing I know, I did not break my laptop and it cracked by itself causing a liquid spill.
I reported this issue to HP and they ignored me and blamed me. Hp does not want to honor the manufacturer warrantee and now I have to deal with losing a 1000 dollars pc plus the the medical expenses that might cause.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (rash) and potential medical expenses, warranting a severity level of 3.

incident_description:
I purchased the 
PowerSmart 2200mAh lithium ion battery from Amazon on 12/31/2016 for my HP Chromebook as a replacement battery. On 3/30/2017 the battery exploded and caught fire while I was using my computer.  I was able to extinguish the fire by smothering it with a blanket.  I wanted to report this occurrence in case it happened to others.  Thank you, [REDACTED]
justification: The battery explosion and fire caused no injuries, but the event was possible given the product's failure.

incident_description: Over the past couple days, our Samsung Plasma TV has turned itself off and on again at least once a day.  This morning it turned itself off again but this time there was a loud series of popping noises (similar to fire crackers) and sparks coming from the backside of the unit.  There was also a very thick and acrid smell of burnt electronics is the room.  The TV was then basically off with the power indicator blinking.  I then unplugged the unit from my surge protector to prevent any further damage to the unit or my house.
justification: The TV's self-ignition and emission of sparks pose a significant fire risk, making another occurrence likely.

incident_description:
Hp laptop screen broke by itself and cause a rash on me. HP blames me and do not want to pay attention to the problem or even fix my pc.
I have been sick since this spill happen from my stomach and I have develop a rash that does not go away. The liquid of the laptop got in my skin and when i touched my face I got a itchy red rash, nauseas and stomach pain.
I sent the laptop to hp for repair because my laptop is new, I bough it in December. Hp refused to honor the warrantee and now I am have to deal with losing 1000 cost of the laptop and the unconfort of of the rash.
The nauseas and stomach issue is not as bad as before but I still have the read mark in some part of my body. My phisical is scheduled the 22 of this month, so hope by this time the rash is gone or the doctor will prescribe something for me. 
I believe the spill caused the rashed. Please investigate. HP does not want to do anything about it and I know I did not break the pc intentionally, this pc is defective and it is a danger to the public.
justification: Injury occurred due to laptop liquid spilling, causing rash and nausea; likelihood is high as symptoms persist and HP refuses to acknowledge or fix the issue.

incident_description: Coby Flat screen TV caught fire 19"
justification: While the incident resulted in property damage, there were no reported injuries or deaths.

By or before December 2016, we found that the plastic casing on the power adapter / plug had cracked, exposing the inner metal prongs.

On 3/24/17, we received an e-mail from Amazon.com with a link to the following recall:

https://www.cpsc.gov/Recalls/2017/Power-Adapters-Sold-with-LectroFan-Sound-Machines-Recalled-by-ASTI-Recall-Alert

However, when we enter the serial numbers of our two LectroFan sound machines into the Adaptive Sound Technologies, Inc. (ASTI) website, it says the following:  "No Recall Required -- Good news! Your product's serial number is not in the range affected by the recall."
justification: Potential for electric shock due to cracked plastic casing exposing metal prongs, though no injury was reported.

incident_description:
I purchased my Fitbit Charge 2 with the band it comes with from my local Best Buy on April 02. I had no issues with it during the first week. At the beginning of week two, I started to develop a red rectangular rash. I went online to try to resolve my problem and was directed to a page on the Fitbit website about proper product care. After reading, I took the band off, cleaned it thoroughly with an alcohol wipe, stopped wearing it to sleep, made sure not to let moisture build up between the band and my skin, allowed my wrist to have a break from it a few hours a day, and I began to wear it more loosely around my wrist. I have sensitive skin, so I thought that maybe cleaning the band would relieve my skin irritation. After another week, I realized that the rash had become darkened and scaly, so I stopped wearing the tracker altogether. It is now week four and the affected area is not getting better as of yet with the use of moisturizers and creams.

I contacted Fitbit and after verifying my purchase, they are going to give me a full refund. They have also provided me with a prepaid shipping label, in order to return my tracker.

I really wanted to enjoy my Fitbit -- i even got my boyfriend to purchase one so that we could track our health together. In my original message to Fitbit I inquired about whether or not buying a different band would solve my issue, which I did not get a direct response to. After doing more research online, it seems that others are suffering from battery burns, so it is likely that I am as well.

Fitbit has been very responsive and friendly during this whole entire process and I am reporting this to educate others about my personal experience.
justification: The user experienced a skin rash and irritation, which progressed to a darkened and scaly area, indicating an injury. The likelihood is high as multiple users have reported similar issues.

incident_description:
A company called Retro-Bit (http://retro-bit.com/) is marketing and selling a transformer power supply for electronic game systems.  It is called the Retro Versal/RETRO BIT UNIVERSAL 3 in 1 AC ADAPTER FOR NES /SNES /GENESIS 1.  The model/PN is: RB-UNI-1361.  This power supply is specified to output DC 9V/350MA.  They can be found on Amazon at this link: https://www.amazon.com/Universal-Adapter-GENESIS-Nintendo-Entertainment-System/dp/B001S2VT6I 
and elsewhere.

The company advertises this power supply for sale to use with the Nintendo Entertainment System (NES), the Super Nintendo Entertainment System (SNES), and the Sega Genesis Model 1, all classic game systems.  The issue is that the NES and SNES, per their specifications pull 850mA of current.  The Genesis Model 1 pulls 1.2A (1200mA) of current.  When using these Retro-Bit power supplies they get very hot, probably due to the fact the power supplies are not designed to source more than 350mA of current.  An original NES power supply was specified to output 1.8A (1800mA), well above the NES's power requirements.  This Retro-Bit model is incapable of supplying even the bare minimum.  I am aware of no incidents of fire or injury.  But, I believe it is unsafe to use these power supplies in the manner in which they are advertised, due to the heat generated and the risk of fire.
justification: While no incidents have been reported, the power supply's inadequate current output causes it to overheat, posing a fire risk.

We have learned of a potential safety issue that may impact product(s) you purchased through the Amazon.com website:
