Customer Service

Amazon.com

www.amazon.com
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (fire) and had the potential for a more severe outcome (death). The likelihood is high as the defect was known and the laptop was recalled.

incident_description: This morning my wife's HP Laptop model 15-f211wm caught fire while she was working on the sofa.  The unit quietly began smoking profusely from the adapter port.  I had to remove the device from our home to the front walk where it currently remains.
justification: No injuries were reported, but the incident was possible given the sudden and unexpected nature of the laptop catching fire.

incident_description: My Samsung note 7 caught on fire. I put out fire without injury.
justification: Fire incident occurred but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: I picked up my Xbox one elite controller off the charger and it was so hot it burned my hands getting the battery pack out of the controller and it was already melting the controller around it.  We unplugged the unit and boxed it up after it cooled down.
justification: The controller's excessive heat caused burns, indicating an injury (severity level 3), and while not common, it's possible (likelihood 3) given the controller's design and charging process.

incident_description: I purchased the xbox one energizer xbox-one controller charger, and today when I went to play I noticed the percentage light flashing, which it never had done before. I took the front charger off the dock and it felt warm, I then touched where the battery pack goes and burned my index finger. I unplugged it immediately, and removed the battery pack from the charger. About 3 or so hours later I got an email that some of these are being recalled for this same reason, and refunds were being issued.
justification: Burn injury occurred due to overheating charger, and recall email confirms likelihood of similar incidents.

incident_description: My laptop battery overheated and melted parts of the laptop. The laptop was ruined.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no physical harm, and while it's possible, it's not a frequent occurrence.

incident_description: On January 21st 2017 my laptop exploded from my battery. The Battery is melted within my laptop for to get any serial numbers from the battery.  I am currently Overseas where where the incident happen. On February 24th 2017 I received an email saying that the battery I purchased for my Toshiba laptop had a Recall.  I purchased Battery ORDER # [REDACTED] from Amazon August 21st 2015
justification: The incident resulted in property damage (laptop explosion) but no injuries, and the likelihood of occurrence was possible given the recall notice.

incident_description:
(08/30/2016) The consumer stated that her son inserted the battery in the charger and plugged the charger into the wall. After about 10 to 15 minutes, he unplugged the charger from the wall. The battery was in his hand. He heard a crackling sound. At that point he threw the battery up in the air. The battery exploded like fireworks. It was so hot, the battery dropped to the floor and immediately caught the wood floor on fire. There are many burns spots on the floor.

No injuries.

(09/02/2016) The consumer contacted the firm to advised them of the incident. The consumer was advised that she probably used the wrong charger. The consumer was advised to send pictures and answer questions that would be in an email that would be sent to her.

The consumer never received the email.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident resulted in property damage (burn spots on the floor) and could have caused injury if the son had not thrown the battery away.

incident_description:
fire Hazard

Trianium I Phone 6S  charger

Student in an elementary school placed his I Phone 6S in the Trianium Battery Case and then placed both on top of a library book. 
After a few minutes the unit burst into flames.
Student incurred a minor burn to a finger.
justification: Injury occurred due to direct contact with flames, but no life-threatening harm.

incident_description:
Energizer 2X Smart Charger 048-052-NA:

Had product for approximately six months and product operated normally. One day we noticed one of the batteries was staying at approximately 15% charge even after several hours on the charger. I picked up the controller and immediately noticed a "hot electronics" smell. I opened the battery cover and the smell became intense. I burned my fingers attempting to remove the battery from the controller, which was difficult as the battery had begun bulging. I instituted thermal runaway procedures and immersed the battery in a bucket of water and baking soda until it cooled, then disposed of it normally.

Approximately two weeks later, the process repeated with the other battery. I again removed the battery from the controller and immersed it to cool it down, disposing the battery afterward.

There were no serious injuries from the incidents, though had the batteries ruptured or caught fire the damage could've been much worse.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident involved a significant risk of fire and property damage, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' at severity level 2.

incident_description: I had bought the replacement battery  for my Toshiba laptop. A few minutes after I connected the battery  to my laptop, the laptop started smoking . So I turned it over to remove the battery but it burst into flames and the flames started shooting straight up into the air. My husband had to open the door so that I could throw the whole laptop outside before the battery acid and flames got on me or anything else in our home.
justification: The incident resulted in significant property damage and posed a high risk of injury due to the intense flames and battery acid.

incident_description: Wading using the dell Chromebook 11 in lap flat and the product screen starting flashing then the product started to smoke. The screen went black then sparked and smoked more. An open flame appeared for a half second amongst constant sparking for several minutes after the flame. The product no longer works. Contacted dell with no help.
justification: The incident resulted in physical damage to the product, with no reported injuries, hence severity level 3. The likelihood is rated 3 as such incidents, while rare, can occur due to hardware malfunctions.

incident_description:
I purchased an iPhone 7 plus on  11/18/2016 and in the last month I have gone through three charging cables. Apple brand cables at $21 with apple brand charger.  The phone is burning a connection and burnt it so bad it cant make a connection to charge the phone. I've contacted apple and nothing has been done. Can't duplicate problem is what I'm told witch is a lie. They keep trying to get me to buy apple care. I've also contacted sprint with no help there as well. as its only three months old I should not have to send it in for repair but have the phone swapped with a new one.
Apple Rosedale Center tells me to contact my carrier because its on a 24 month installment plan. 
I need help scared my phones going to start on fire.
justification: While no injury has been reported, the incident involves a potential fire hazard due to the phone overheating, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' scenario.

incident_description: On 1/19/15, I purchased Toshiba Satellite C55-B5300 in Amazon.  I then went to Haiti on a medical mission with the laptop 2/1/15.  While I was in Haiti, the laptop caught on fire while it was being charged directly on the wall.  It was my first time using a generator for electricity. I thought the fire was due to the generator, but now I realized it was because of the battery in the laptop.  I want my laptop replaced with proper battery, but Toshiba is refusing asking me for pictures from 2015.  I would have to go to Haiti to look for any pictures, but who took pictures when you are trying to prevent a house from burning down and for everyone to be safe?  This is ridiculous.
justification: No injuries occurred, but the incident caused significant damage to the laptop.

incident_description: I purchased a product from amazon manufacturer Matiricom. The remote started to melt.  I owned this product for one year and one month. The manufacturer would not respond to me after i sent them pictures.  I told them i would be reporting this product as unsafe to government agencies.
justification: Product failure leading to potential fire hazard, but no injuries reported.

incident_description:
I ordered an apple MacBook charger on-line through eBay. The charger was listed as a "new genuine original apple MacBook pro charger 85W Magsafe 2 A1424". However after using the charger for a short time, it became extremely hot and actually scorched my son's comforter on his bed. I returned this charger and stated what had happened. There are several comments on this sellers web site complaining of similar situations. It is my concern that if a child were to use this charger in their bed and fall asleep, it could cause a fire or at the very least burn the child. 
The seller is listed as 24hourchargers on the eBay web site and they also have their own web site 24hourchargers.com. They state that they have a 90 money back guarantee but did not honor this with my purchase. However I did receive a refund through my PayPal account after contacting them today. 
This guarantee provides a false sense of safety when ordering the item. This item is not a genuine apple charger and is not approved by Microsoft for use with their computers. It is misleading and could lead to dangerous results if left plugged into the computer for an extended period of time.
justification: While no injuries were reported, the charger's tendency to overheat and scorch surfaces poses a significant fire risk, especially if used unattended.

incident_description: My product is a Microsoft Surface Table, purchased around June 2015.  The problem with this product is it will get hot after only being on for a short time.  The heat can be so hot you can not touch the back of the tablet.  As software upgrades are pushed out to this device, the device will heat up even quicker.  Sometimes the table will shut off on it own and sometime it will just stay hot and you can hear the fan running.  I reported the issue to Microsoft while the device was under warranty but because their is a small nick on the edge of the table they would not repair the device and refused to address the heat issue.  I would like to use the tablet but I'm afraid it will catch on fire.  In my research of this product and on one of Microsoft's forums, I found several post where other owners of this make and model have reported having the same heating problems.  I sent Microsoft this information to make them aware that on their on user forum site there is an issue with this "lot" of tablets.
justification: While no injuries have been reported, the risk of burns is high due to excessive heat, and the likelihood of occurrence is likely given the numerous user reports and the device's tendency to overheat even after software upgrades.

incident_description:
I have a toshiba laptop and receive an email stating the recall had been expanded to include my laptop perhaps. I went through the information page and put in all my info. The website said my laptop wasn't effected. I strongly disagree with this because my laptop does in fact burn me via the battery pack if I am not careful. It has left an actual burn mark before because it can get so hot. So I believe my battery pack needs to be added to this recall. 

Part #: PSAY1U-01R005
Serial #: 6B317142K

Battery info:

B60301443AYC

G71C000AW210
justification: The user has experienced burns from the laptop's battery, indicating a high likelihood of injury and a severe potential impact.

incident_description: My Samsung TV PN60E8000GF which is 4-5 years old starting shooting off sparks and making loud fire cracking sounds nearly causing a fire. It smelled like burned plastic. The screen went black and is not working.  Our wiring was checked and is fine.  I have called Samsung twice and am waiting for a response.
justification: The TV's failure to function after sparking and emitting a burning plastic smell indicates an incident, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
Charged XBOX controller overnight on the evening of 3/11/2017. The next morning, the controller was hot to the touch, and the battery's casing had melted. After allowing it to cool, I removed the battery and noted some damage inside the controller. Controller is still functional, but impact to its operational life is unknown at this time. 

Received product safety notice from Amazon.com on 3/14.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident resulted in property damage (melted battery casing) and potential functional impact on the controller.

incident_description: This weekend, my husband's Samsung Galaxy S7 phone was sitting on a countertop, not plugged in, when suddenly there was a popping sound, and smoke began spewing out of the phone. My husband grabbed our toddler and ran out of the apartment, and my father used an oven mitt to take the phone onto our balcony. It was extremely hot, and was melting plastic onto the glove. It also melted through the case. We aired the apartment out, but it took hours for the smell to go away, and we had to scrub everything on the countertop (and throw a bunch of stuff away because the smoky chemical smell was so strong). We are so lucky that no one was hurt, and that our daughter didn't breathe too much of the smoke, but it was a scary experience.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident caused significant property damage and potential health risks from smoke inhalation.

incident_description: My Toshiba laptop burned my leg. The computer gets extremely hot sometimes. It is the SATELLITE L75-A7271 brand.
justification: The laptop's tendency to get extremely hot led to a burn injury, making it a possible occurrence.

incident_description:
I was using my laptop while resting in bed & fell asleep. When I awoke, I had a large blister (the scar is 1 1/2" X 3/4") on my right thigh, where the battery edge of the computer was resting. I just thought I was somehow at fault as I had never used my computer this way and was unaware of how hot laptops could get. 

I have always felt the computer ran hot, but until I received the first alert to battery overheating, I submitted my computer and the recall reply was that my computer was not part of the recall.  I purchased a metal frame to hold the laptop and am very careful now with how I use it.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (a large blister), and while it's not likely to happen again due to increased caution, it's possible given the laptop's tendency to overheat.

incident_description:
On several occasions, while using my computer, the laptop has become so hot that it literally left a burn mark on my leg.  I have had to turn it off in the midst of work as the computer started heating up again.  I have to unplug the computer each time I am done using as one morning I noticed that, even when turned off, the computer had heated papers sitting next to the computer and I smelled smoke.

The computer has turned itself off at times when the computer became very hot. It runs slower than it used to.
justification: Repeated incidents of excessive heat leading to potential property damage and discomfort.

incident_description:
I have a Samsung PN59D8000FF Smart TV. The BN59-01134B  (2-in1 Qwerty Remote Control for Samsung SMART TV RMC-QTD) has melted the batteries and leaked acid onto my fingers when I struggled to open it. The batteries are stuck to the battery compartment and the interior of the remote is covered with the acid. It does not work.  This is the second BN59-01134B remote I have had; the first was ruined by the exact same problem of leaking batteries. 

In looking for a replacement on Amazon, I found many reviews that showed the problem I have experienced is common: one reviewer said the remote exploded in her face; another said the batteries were burned leaving a lot of debris and damaged the remote altogether; and yet another said the remote caused batteries to leak inside and that Samsung is aware of this problem.  

The only way this remote can work is to remove the batteries after a few minutes of use.  If one forgets, as we did, the batteries are drained in a few days or melted by the remote.
justification: The incident resulted in chemical burns on fingers and the remote's acid leakage poses a potential health hazard, warranting a severity level of 3. The high number of similar complaints and Samsung's awareness of the issue indicate a likelihood of 4.

incident_description: I own a Toshiba Salellite L875D-S7343 computer that gets so hot on the far right side my laptop has burned my leg. I can only use the laptop with a hard, non-flamable surface underneath. This has been happening almost from the first few months of use.
justification: The incident of the laptop burning the user's leg is an injury (severity level 3) and has been occurring almost from the first few months of use, indicating a high likelihood (4).

incident_description: I fell asleep with the laptop computer on my laptop.  I was wearing short pants.  When I woke the next morning I had several blisters on my right leg.  Fearing that I had some sort of infection such as shingles I went to the local Urgent Care.  I learned there that I had a burn from the laptop computer.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (burn), but it's not likely to happen again due to the unusual circumstances.

incident_description: Severe over heating of HP g7 laptop battery (ct6uep3gbo0l6e7). Have to remove battery to cool down when operating. Hot enough to make thighs red and close to singeing  sheet on my bed.
justification: While no injury occurred, the incident could have led to burns, hence severity level 2.

incident_description: My husband gave me a Charge HR for Chrismas 2016. I wore it fairly regularly during the days and took it off at night. I noticed several hard blister like bumps on my wrist so I switched wrists. I continued cleaning the band with rubbing alcohol but soon I developed the same bumps on my other wrist. I switched again and the rash came up almost immediately so I quit wearing it entirely. It had been over a month now and the rash seems to be getting much worse on my left wrist. Nothing works. Seeking medical advice this week.
justification: The incident resulted in persistent and worsening skin irritation and blisters, classified as an injury.

incident_description:
At 3:30 PM, on Wednesday, February 8th, 2017, I was in my office doing routine paperwork and filing papers. I went to use my paper shredder to eliminate a single sheet of regular paper that had some account numbers.  As I inserted the paper into the intake slot I heard the machine making strange grinding sounds and would only take 1/4 (one-quarter) of the paper.  I removed the paper, turned it around and reinserted it into the machine. As I was looking into the machine there was a sudden burst of flame which came up and burned my face and head.
The lower container of the shredder, holding long, thin strips of paper, also caught fire, and quickly became larger than the shredder mechanism fire.  I picked up the paper shredded container, ran into the next room which is a bathroom, placed it on the drain of the shower stall and turned on the water which put out the fire.
I returned to my office where the shredder mechanism was smoldering on a commercial-grade floor pad, unplugged the unit, and I ran out the door and threw the unit into the snow.
The local fire department, the Worden Volunteer Fire Department, dispatched a unit to ensure that the fire was extinguished and not likely to reoccur.  There was no evidence of any damage to my office area, desk or ancillary items.  There was some smoke which quickly cleared when we opened windows and doors.
For safety's sake, the volunteer fireman suggested I visit the emergency room at the Billings Clinic Hospital, approximately 15-minutes from my house.   I was at the emergency room from approximately 4:30PM, same date, until 10:15 PM, same date. My injuries included first-degree burns on my face and bald head.  I also experienced minor first degree burns to my right arm wrist.  Both of my eye brows and eye lashes were singed. Hair on the side of my head was also singed.  I declined the application of any pain medicine or creams.  It should be noted that my brand-new [REDACTED]-brand eye glasses' lens were damaged beyond repair.
I have taken photographs of the damaged paper shredder which are attached to this report.  I have not discarded or cleaned up the paper shredder or containment basket. I have discarded the burnt paper shreds because of the smell.
justification: Injuries sustained (first-degree burns, singed hair, damaged glasses) warrant a severity level of 3, and the likelihood of such an event occurring again is high given the lack of safety measures and the common use of paper shredders.

incident_description:
I bought my son a iPhone 7 for Christmas. Last Friday this two month old phone blew up on him while he was talking on it. He suffered a burn to the lip from it. 
I of course called Apple and sent pics of the phone. After them sending me on a wild goose chase, I came up empty handed with no replacement phone. They also informed me their safety team said it didn't happen as I described. The burnt port hole at the bottom says otherwise. As does the kids around him and a couple of adults that were on the trip as chaperones. 
The phone will not take charge and is useless. BE CAREFUL APPLE LOVERS. These guys do not stand behind their products or their customers!!
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (burn to the lip) and could potentially happen again given the product's defect.

incident_description: The Kindle fire melted a distinct square below the camera and above the brand name Amazon on the back of the device while it was plugged in and charging.  There was a smell of burnt plastic and the device was VERY hot to the touch.  After removing the device from a protective case it was in, I noticed that the device was melted.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage (melted device) but no injuries, and while it's possible, it's not a common occurrence.

incident_description: My 6 year old granddaughter plugged her iPad into a 10 ft Airssup USB Cord and then plugged an iHome portable charger to charge her iPad.  Shortly after plugging the iHome portable charger the iHome charger started smoking and caught fire,  Fortunately I was right there when she started yelling and I put the fire out.  She was on an air mattress with cover and the cover caught fire.  The USB end of the 10 ft cable smell of burnt material but the iHome portable charger smells very bad. Even now. Did not melt either because I unplugged both but it left a horrible smell in the house and on the iHome charger.  My entire family was home when this happened and came running to find out what was burning just from the horrible smell.  I can't imagine what would have happened if I was not near because my granddaughter did not run she was still holding it on the bed.  She apparently was frightened and did not even try to unplug it but was yelling to me.  Fortunately, no person was burned or hurt, just the bedding on the air mattress that she play on.I was shocked that this happened.  We have use both of these devices before.  Several times.  Don't know what happened different.
justification: Although no one was injured, the incident involved a fire which could have escalated if not promptly extinguished.

incident_description:
Text of Consume's message dated November 19, 2016 (excerpted):

After recent problems with the Samsung Galaxy Note 7 I was wondering whether Samsung should also recalled the Galaxy S5.

I had the misfortune to purchase the S5 only to experience the battery swelling so much that the face of the phone was detached from the base. Fear of the phone causing a fire I retumecl to T Mobile only to be told I definitely should not use the phone. I had to purchase another phone the Galaxy J7 for $520.35 (no rebate, no credit, no apology).

I am sure I am not the only one to have had such an experience with this defective Samsung Product, and fortunate not to have experienced an explosion or fire.

I have enclosed a photo of my phone showing the raised face. I am still in possession of this phone should further Investigation be required.
justification: While no injuries or deaths were reported, the incident involved a significant safety hazard (battery swelling) and financial loss (replacement cost).

incident_description: We have had 2 Ematic 7" tablets (1 blue - 1 pink) I bought for my kids.  The first one to go was the blue one, I took photo's and reported it to the company and they wanted me to pay $50 for my tablet was not insured and the warranty expired. The battery swelled up so much that the casing popped open.  The second time was the pink one 6 months after the blue and it did the same thing except it went to pieces.  I still have that one in the box - and Ematic does not want to deal with their product and the lack of safety due to the battery.  I have all the communication from them from the 1st issue and will be happy to send them and the photos along with the 2nd tablet itself to show that Ematic needs to due something about their product.
justification: Both tablets experienced battery swelling and casing damage, with the second incident resulting in the tablet going to pieces.

incident_description: My TV fell while I was in the bathroom with my daughter  (she is under 2 yrs old) the base part snapped and it tumbled off the stand to the floor.
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the incident could have resulted in harm due to the age of the child present.

incident_description:
My deaf sons Huawei cell phone caught fire and exploded while charging on the evening of Dec. 12, 2016. He
was asleep at the time and his flashing smoke alarm woke him. He lives in a ten-story apartment building and
had he not been at home the results could have been tragic for many residents. I contacted our local newspaper
about this hazardous issue but they did not respond. I also called Consumer Cellular and spoke with a manager.
I was told that there is nothing they can do. I then sent Consumer Cellular a [REDACTED] message and they again
responded that they could do nothing. I then contacted Huawei via Facebook but they have not responded. I feel
that this is a public safety issue and people need to be made aware of the danger of Huawei cell phones. Can
you help?

I wish to add that since I filed this report the AG has contacted Consumer Cellular & they have agreed to refund the price  they charged me for a phone to replace the burnt-up one.

Also, Huawei Company has been very helpful & cooperative & offered to send a replacement Huawei cell phone free of charge.  They requested that I ship the burnt-up phone, charger & cord to them which I have done.
[REDACTED]

The model # is a Huawei Vision.  I do not know the serial number.  Photos are enclosed.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident of a cell phone catching fire and exploding poses a significant risk to property and potential future injuries.

incident_description:
My Coby TFDVD1973 19 inch television set went up in flames this morning.  I was fortunate that I wasn't injured and my house didn't burn down, but I have a lot of smoke damage.  There was no power surge or any electrical system issue, all other electronics in the house are fine.  The Coby TV, which was powered on, just made a lot of noise, started shooting up black smoke, and then lit up in flames.  I just barely prevented the curtains from catching fire.

I know that Coby is out of business, but please warn people to replace these dangerous TV sets!!!
justification: While no injuries or property damage beyond the TV occurred, the incident could have escalated to a higher severity level.

incident_description:
I purchased a Fitbit Charge 2 fitness tracker, which I wore for a week. I received a nasty chemical burn from it without warning or prior irritation. The burn left two "holes" on my wrist aligning with its exposed prongs for charging the battery. I immediately discontinued wearing the band and the burn is still healing two weeks later. I have taken pictures of this and contacted the company directly warning them about this problem. Googling the matter, I see there are long threads on their support web site with similar complaints.

I previously wore a [REDACTED] fitness tracker for well over a year without any irritation, and I am acquainted with proper hygiene guidelines for keeping wearable devices clean. I did not realize this was a burn initially, assuming it was some sort of rash. It did not disappear when I stopped wearing the Fitbit, leading to treatment with antihistamines and topical hydrocortisone. These had no effect, and it is still healing two weeks later.
justification: The incident resulted in a chemical burn with visible holes on the wrist, and the likelihood is high given the numerous similar complaints found online.

incident_description: The rechargeable lion battery of my toshiba laptop started heating abnormaly (burned when I touched) inmediately after this the computer turned of spontaneusly and I couldn't turn it on again during two days.
justification: The battery overheating and causing injury (burn) qualifies as an 'Injury' incident, and its likelihood is 'possible' given the abnormal heating and spontaneous shutdown.

incident_description:
On Tuesday February 21, 2017 at approximately 11:00 am, I was using a 1/4 inch impact driver to install 1.25 inch screws when the tools battery exploded without warning in my hand. The tool is and 18 volt model made by Chicago Electric an sold by Harbor Freight Tools with a serial number of 363831451. The battery that exploded only has a part number of 68860.

The battery and driver was operating normal until this incident when there was a very loud bang very similar to a gunshot. I immediately felt pieces of debris hit my arms chest and face and was left unable to see from what felt like sand hitting my face and eyes. The tool was at most two feet from my face. My ears were also ringing from the sound as it was so loud. I was unsure the extent of my injuries until I was able to clear my eyes enough to see though they were blurry for some time.

It was at this time I found I was bleeding from numerous bleeding cuts on both arms with one cut having a small piece of the battery case stuck in it. My right wrist and forearm had both small cuts and burn on it as this was the hand I was holding tool in. My left arm had cuts on forearm and upper inside arm with some bruising starting. Both arms and face had a black powder which appeared to be from the actual battery insides that burned while on my skin. I needed to rinse eyes continuously to get out what felt like sand and was stinging seriously. My t-shirt had small pieces of debris stuck in the fabric.

The sound was loud enough to be heard from people both downstairs and another outside with closed windows that was there with me. Pieces of debris were scattered throughout the room I was in as well as hallway and room adjacent to hallway. The battery case is blown apart with individual battery cylinders missing and other material burnt and hanging out. The debris was made up of both metal and plastic including a metal cylinder that is split open into sharp edges and bulged out. It appears to be an actual battery casing.

I took pictures of injuries and the aftermath of incident including the tool and battery immediately after, as soon as I was able to. I also gathered pieces of battery debris and have kept them along with the exploded battery itself as evidence of incident.

It has been even more upsetting to find upon a Google search that this has happened before with these exact batteries and has been reported before. The injuries sustained by this failure could easily cause far more serious injury and needs to be dealt with. There is no warning prior to this an does not appear to have been in the other cases either.
justification: The incident resulted in multiple cuts, burns, and potential eye injuries, warranting a severity level of 3. The likelihood is high given the previous reports of similar incidents with the same battery model.

incident_description:
This consumer is reporting that her cell phone batteries were heating up to quite a hot temperature.
Her phone is becoming so hot that she cannot hold it to her ear, in order to hold even a short conversation she has to hold the phone away from her ear.
She purchased the phone around mid 2015 from a Sprint store in Dover, Delaware then around January 19th, 2017 she began noticing that it felt hotter and hotter as time went by.
January 22nd, 2017 she contacted the manufacturer who advised that they would provide her with replacement battery pack.
January 22nd, 2017 She visited her provider's store but she was advised that they would not provide her with a battery pack.
she is reporting this phone as a fire hazard.
justification: While no injuries have been reported, the phone's overheating poses a potential fire hazard, making it an incident with possible occurrence.

incident_description: My lap top was plugged in near my bed.  In the middle of the night I heard a noise, saw flames, and smelled burning.  I looked up and saw a flames burst out of the charger.
justification: The incident involved a fire from an electrical device, which could have caused property damage but no injuries were mentioned.

incident_description:
I had a Samsung Galaxy S7 that has the same issues as the [REDACTED]. The battery was faulty, would not hold a charge and would generate excessive heat. I called Samsung tech support and reported the problem. I was told, by Samsung, to send in the phone with the original box and charger as well as the fast charger I purchased to go with the phone and I would get a refund. I later called to check the status of the refund and was repeatedly told that Samsung "has no refund policy in the warranty." About a week later they sent the phone back with another of the same faulty batteries, in a different box and missing one of the fast charging adapters along with the box for it.

I did some research and discovered that many of the S7s are having the same problems as the Note7s. Samsung lied to me and even stole from me while refusing to correct a single problem that they created.
justification: The incident involved a significant product defect and dishonest customer service, but no physical harm was reported.

incident_description:
On 01/30/2017, I notice a Lenovo Flex3 laptop exhibited a burning smell accompany by periodic electrical sparks I saw from the back of the computer while charging the battery.  I immediately pull the plug out of the computer, but the problem persisted for another 2 hours until the battery was apparently completely discharged.  For fear of fire, I took the computer to work afraid of losing my home to electrical fire (I could no longer trust that computer).

There was no injury, nor property damage, because I took immediately action to prevent the possibility of a fire starting at my house.
justification: Although no injury or property damage occurred, the incident involved a significant risk of fire, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description: I have an HP laptop which caused  a server burn on left thigh,I am a paraplegic so I did not feel it happening the burn is aprox 3 1/2 inches long
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (burn) but did not cause death, and the occurrence was unlikely given the individual's paraplegia.

incident_description: In the fall of 2015, we bought a Vizio 40" flat screen TV Model No. E400i B2. On January 18, 2017, we could not turn the TV on. After examining the TV, we discovered that the plastic backing on the TV had melted and was severely deformed from an interior fire or extreme heat from the inside of the TV. Vizio has rejected our warranty claim saying that the melting was caused by exterior heat such as a fireplace or by the sun. There is no fireplace in the room and I find it hard to believe that the sunshine coming through a window in the middle of the winter would cause the back of the TV to melt. The TV had been in the same spot for over a year and had never experienced any overheating problems from an external source or otherwise. Thank you.
justification: No injuries or deaths reported, but the incident caused significant property damage.

incident_description: Elderly, disabled female  was charging her Samsung SGH-T399 android cell phone and it caught fire. The battery expanded violently and emitted flames  then ignited papers and other items on her kitchen counter. The cell phone battery cover separated from the phone and the battery came dislodged. The two cell phone pieces appeared  undamaged. Charger was a Samsung brand. Fire damage occurred to the wall, countertop and to personal items. The female extinguished the fire with water from the sink. She was not injured.
justification: No injuries were reported despite significant property damage, indicating a possible but not likely severe occurrence.

incident_description: The battery in my HP Pavilion gets excessively hot even with a short amount of usage.  We must turn it off often because of the fear of burning the desk.  The fan will run constantly to try to cool it.  I have checked it with each of the recalls and can't believe that ours was not included. We have not been injured by the heat only because each of us in the home knows to not touch this computer after using more than a few minutes.
justification: Although no injuries have occurred yet, the consistent overheating poses a high likelihood of causing burns if the computer is not turned off promptly.

incident_description: I have a Prime Surge Protector/USB charger that got very hot and melted the plastic cover while charging a cell phone.  I smelled the plastic burning and unplugged the device.  Np flames were seen but the plastic case is melted.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident resulted in property damage (melted plastic cover) and could have potentially caused a fire.

incident_description: The battery pack in question burned out suddenly after only having the machine for 2 months. It cost me $45 to replace it.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage (battery pack) but no injuries, and the likelihood of such an event occurring is possible given the short usage period.

incident_description: Samsung Galaxy S7 battery exploded and caught fire while charging on nightstand.  Produced heavy smoke in home, sent spouse to hospital due to smoke inhalation.
justification: Injury occurred due to smoke inhalation, and the incident was possible but not certain to happen given the charging conditions.

incident_description: While wearing the Bose QuietComfort 30 Bluetooth Wireless head phones this past weekend I felt a sharp pain around my neck. As I began to investigate I saw an arc of electricity emitting from the battery pack around my neck to my skin. The direct location was the power on/off button. I immediately took off the headset and also noted the physical temperature of the battery pack was very hot to the touch.  I was unable to turn the power off the device from that point forward as well. Now, I am able to see a discoloration or scalded appearance to the area near the button and my neck has a first degree burn at that location wear the button and my neck lined up.
justification: Injury occurred due to electrical arc from battery pack, making it a 'possible' occurrence.

incident_description: My Samsung 6-series Smart-HDTV was on and I left the room to take a phone call.  I heard my dog start barking frantically from the other room and also heard a weird popping sound.  I returned to the living room (where the TV was) and saw sparks shooting out of the lower left-hand corner of the TV, where the screen meets the bezel of the frame.  I ran into the kitchen to get a fire extinguisher and by the time I ran back into the living room, the sparks had become an actual flame about 2 inches high and part of the TV was melting.  I used the fire extinguisher to put the fire out and immediately unplugged the TV so it wouldn't start sparking again.  Nothing else in the house was damaged and there were no injuries to me or my pets.  I called Samsung and they've been giving me the run-around ever since.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a fire, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' scenario. The likelihood is 'possible' as it's not common but not rare either.

incident_description: purchased lg v10 from verizon march 2016.  in 4 months, it started to get so hot , it was uncomfortable to touch.  it was replaced by verizon, but yesterday the replacement got hotter than the first v10(it was not being used at the time).  verizon is saying our problem is unique.  they seem to say there is no problem with the phone model--same song as [REDACTED].
justification: While no injuries have been reported, the recurring heat issue with both phones indicates a potential safety hazard.

incident_description:
When the ambient light feature of my TV is turned on I hear an electrical buzzing sound for a few moments then TV powers off. TV will not power on but the power light blinks in a certain pattern. If I unplug TV and wait a while before plugging back in it will operate again until the ambient light feature is turned on again. I have been dealing with this problem for years by nit using the ambient light feature but other people use the TV and often engage the ambient light feature from the remote control which causes the electric surging sound and power outage again. It has been a total hassle and everyone who uses the TV and sees it fail believe Philips products are inferior.

Since the outage has been happening more often, sometimes now without even using the ambient light feature, I searched for info and discovered this model is recalled. However the serial number range which is rather extensive stops one number (or one production week) before my serial number so Philips isn't discussing recall with me. I believe this product is unsafe electrically and should be inspected since it exhibits the exact concern related to the recall. There is no doubt this item should be included in the recall which would extend the recall production inclusion.
justification: Frequent power outages due to a known electrical issue, though no injuries reported.

incident_description:
My son called home about an hour ago to tell me that his  POLANFO 20000M Universal Ultra Compact 20000mah Power Charger, UPC 0701385710064 had just exploded in the student Union Buidling (Norris Hall) at Northwestern University. My son had just gotten seated at a table and felt his backpack getting hot  (he was wearing it at the time).  He reached into the backpack and started taking stuff out and putting it on the dining center table. When he grabbed the charged, he noticed that it was very hot to the touch.  He tossed the charger onto the cafeteria table where it began hissing  and  sending a noxious chemical smoke cloud into the dining center.  The charger burned a hole in the cafeteria table and the smoke led to an evacuation of the student union building.  The device was removed by a hazmat team which had been called to the university.

I purchased the POLANFO 20000M charger on July 27, 2015 from Amazon and the seller ([REDACTED]) was [REDACTED]. The address of Northwestern University is [REDACTED] and for [REDACTED] it is [REDACTED]. My son [REDACTED] can be reached at the following email address if you have any questions for him:
[REDACTED]
justification: Injury likely avoided due to son's quick action, but potential for severe burns or other injuries was high.

incident_description: My Samsung Galaxy S7 Edge phone said it needed to update the operating system and I did it which took over an hour. I was surprised how long it took as I needed to make a call but was not able to on time. I was talking on the phone about two hours and had to plug it in so it did not go dead. I noticed ut was draining pretty fast and that was strange as the display turns off when talking and I had it plugged into a Samsung charger. but I had to end my call as it got too hot and noticed I was sweating just sitting talking and the person I was talking to informed ne my voice was cutting out. After the call my face felt strange and I put the phone in the freezer as it got so hot I could not hold it and it showed low battery but I could not turn it off and thr display was not responding. I went to the bathroom as I was soaking in sweat as the phone was so hot and had been by my head and I realized I had a red rectangle shaped on my face where the phone was and little water blisters. After the phone cooled down in the freezer I was able to recharge it as it had no charge and when I turned it on I could see the image of the keyboard was burnt into the screen. I over the next week noticed it no longer kept a charge for long and if left sitting doing nothing it would get really hot. I looked online and some suggested using an app to control the battery but it was no help. It keeps getting too hot and the temp shows it reaches 300 deg F. The battery drains super fast and the image of the keyboard is permanently burnt into the screen. Sprint where I got it said I have to pay $200 to exchange it saying its not repairable. Samsung the manufacture says I have to send it to them and wait up to 11 days and I had to buy a Tracfone as I already got the sunburn blisters so don't want to have that happen again as I do not feel pain due to medication I take. I can't be without a phone for weeks as I have medical issues and depend on it but my Samsung is neither safe nor reliable. Sprint said I am responsable to pay for my contract even if I have no phone to use on it. Now I'm stuck having to use my Sansung phone and limit how long and cool it in the freezer. Sprint nor Samsung seems concerned and even when I contacted Samsung telling them its so hot it burns my hands they asked I turn it back on to get them some codes off the phone and I explained its in the freezer and the battery is dead and said it burnt my face and I think its unsafe to turn on they asked I try anyways.
justification: The phone's excessive heat caused second-degree burns on the user's face, resulting in injury.

incident_description: My laptop was plugged in and charging.  At 1:30 am,  my husband heard a loud noise, then a flash, then flames coming out from the laptop's battery.  It melted part of the battery case and the side of the laptop.
justification: No injuries were reported, but the incident caused property damage, making it a level 2 severity. The occurrence was possible but not likely or almost certain, hence a likelihood of 3.

incident_description:
I purchased this HP envy laptop 3 years ago.
Since almost the beginning, perhaps 6 months after purchase my daughter began experiencing problems.

For the past two days I have spent hours on the phone trying to get this resolved and trying to send emails and access the website. I am very concerned that my daughter is using a laptop which is dangerous and I cannot even get in contact with someone.  The person I did speak to initially seemed concerned and told me that the recall is being expanded and that the issues we are experiencing sound just like what is happening with the recalled batteries.  A battery should not heat up and stop working so that it has to be removed from the laptop for the laptop to work.  This was not an inexpensive product.

Today I am unable to even get through on the phone.  When I call the HP number for recalls or any number as soon as I press the prompt, the line hangs up.  The website is inaccessible and the email address I was given is invalid.  I have spent too much time on this already and it is not right.  Please help.  Following is the email I have been trying to send to HP  all morning:

START
Hello:


I purchased an HP ENVY TS 15 laptop for my daughter some 3 years ago from BJs.  She uses it in college. Early on she began experiencing problems with the battery.  It would not stay charged long and it would heat up.  Eventually it has reached the point where she can only use the laptop when it is plugged in.  

I saw the recall information and contacted the phone number.  The gentleman I spoke with was very nice and he told me that the first part of the battery number was the same as the recalled batteries but that the battery in our laptop is not part of the recall.  He did say that the issues sound the same as those in the batteries that have been recalled and that he would transfer me to speak to someone else regarding whether my battery should be included in the recall.  He did say HP was expanding the recall to include additional batteries and that I should describe my issues to the person with whom I speak on the phone. I was transferred and spoke with another young man who told me that I should send an email to this address with all my product information so HP can determine if my battery will be part of the recall and I can be issued a replacement battery, because he has limited information and could not tell me that.

Hence this email.  Following is the information I was told to include:

Laptop:  HP ENVY TS 15
Laptop Serial Number:  5CG3253WHG
Battery: 6DGAL01C84M4PR


Please let me know if you can help me with this.  We do need a replacement battery and now I am concerned that my daughter is using a potentially dangerous product.

Thank you.

Sincerely,

[REDACTED]




Thank you for your help.
justification: Potential fire hazard due to overheating battery, though no injuries reported yet.

incident_description:
I purchased an lphone6 new about two years ago. Over the weekend of January 14, 20171 was using my I phone 6
telephone when it got very hot. It had done that in the past but the phone continued to work. Around Sunday
January 15, 2017 I was out to dinner and I was looking at my phone when I noticed that the frame on the left side of
the phone as you view it from the front was bulged out. Closer examination showed the left side was bowed out
enough that I could see some of the inner metal parts of the phone. The phone continued to worked. I looked up
information on this model phone and I saw this was a common problem for this model phone. Yesterday, January
17, 2017 I contacted Apple Inc.; spoke with a senior advisor and described the condition of the phone. He instructed
me to turn the phone off and not use it. He asked me if I had received any injuries and I told him I did not. An
appointment was set up for me to visit the local Apple store and have one of their techs look at it. The senior tech I
talked to said it sounded as if the battery had overheated, swelled up and bent the frame on that side. The tech at
Apple who examined my telephone confirmed the battery had swollen up and damaged the telephone. The tech
said they would replace my phone with one like it for the price of the replacement battery which was$ 79.00 plus
tax.
In my research I found this was a common problem with the lphone6 and 6s. Other companies have had incidents
with the rechargeable batteries used in hover boards etc. and they were forced to issue a recall. I am now
wondering why they have not been investigated and this problem addressed by your agency.
justification: Although the phone was damaged, there were no reported injuries, hence severity level 2.

incident_description:
Dell XPS 9550 Laptop - 

With less than one year of use the high capacity lithium-ion battery has physically swelled a considerable amount.  This laptop is a sealed design similar to many phones where the battery can not be end-user accessed.  The swelling is significant enough to cause the case to deform and touchpad to protrude.  

My concern is with the fire hazard around defective Li-Ion batteries.
justification: The battery swelling poses a potential fire hazard, but no injuries have been reported yet.

incident_description: The back camera glass shattered.  There are numerous reports on line of this happening with the Samsung Galaxy S7 phone.  I sent it to Samsung for repair since the phone had been a protective case and was never dropped.  However Samsung says the glass was not defective and is charging $70.21 to fix the phone.  Because the phone was not dropped or anything pushed into the glass cover it is a flaw in the device.  And with so many people having this issue needs to be investigated. The broken glass could cause injury to the user.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage (shattered back camera glass) but no injury, and the likelihood of occurrence is high given numerous online reports of the same issue with Samsung Galaxy S7 phones.

incident_description: My samsung edge 7 plus gets extremely hot during use, it gets so hot that it can barely be held.  Sometimes when it overheats and gets extremely hot it will.power down instantly interrupting use.  In addition, my phone became so.hot at one.instance that when my daughter went to answer my phone and put it to her ear and face she dropped phone stating that it burned her face although no burn marks her face was physically red where the phone had touch her face and ear.  I believe this is a major concern to be taken.into full consideration.  I believe the heat and possiblity for phone to become so hot that it explodes or cause undue harm and pain is very likely.
justification: The phone's extreme heat caused physical injury (redness) to the user's face, warranting a severity level of 3.

incident_description: HP Pavillion g6 laptop batteries exploded when under charge.  Burned the wall, desk and floor with flaming black plastic and hot batteries.  The hot plastic and fires destroyed the labels showing the model number, serial number, etc., for both the computer and the battery pack.  There was nothing identifiable left of the battery pack.
justification: No injuries were reported, but the incident caused significant property damage, hence severity level 2.

incident_description: I was inserting 3 pieces of paper to shred when the unit exploded and started the paper in the basket on fire.
justification: The incident resulted in no injuries but caused property damage (fire in the basket).

incident_description:
I had use the Fitbit Flex for about 2 years with no incident. I recently upgraded to the Fitbit Charge HR. I have been wearing it since the end of October. I take it off to shower, swim, and to charge, otherwise, I have it on. I noticed a red spot on my wrist by my thumb on or about January 13, 2017. I left my Fitbit off for the day to give my wrist a break.

I have idiopathic hypersomnia, which makes it incredibly difficult to wake up. The silent alarm function on the Fibit has helped tremendously and I rely on it as part of my wake up routine. The redness seemed to go down a bit, so I put it back on before bed so that I could use it for the morning alarm. 

I didn't notice it too much throughout the rest of the week and the weekend. The redness lingered, but was not bright and did not spread. This morning, January 20, 2017, I notice the spot is much more red than before and seems to have gotten a bit bigger. I also have a spot starting on the top of my wrist, about 1.5 inches away. Right now it is splotchy and small, like how the first spot started. 

The first spot feels very dry now and is a bit itchy, which is new to today. It also looks a bit raised. I have called my dermatologist for an appointment since it has worsened and a new spot has developed. 

I keep my Fitbit clean by washing it periodically with soap and water as best as I can. The material the band is made from feels gross when any moisture is trapped between it and my skin, so I always take my Fitbit off after I wash my hands in order to dry the band and my wrist. I don't think this has developed from irritation in that regard.

I do not wear the band very tight. The battery only lasts about 3 days, so I have to take it off for a few hours while it charges.
justification: Skin irritation and potential allergic reaction, with symptoms worsening over time.

incident_description: On December 05, 2016 my hp dv6 laptop battery exploded 2 feet from my face on my nightstand. The laptop then fell on the floor and immediately started the carpeting on fire. While trying to extinguish the fire, I experienced severe 2nd degree and 3rd degree burns on my right hand.
justification: The incident resulted in severe burns, indicating a '3' severity level. The likelihood is '3' as it's possible but not common for laptop batteries to explode.

incident_description:
While charging an IPhone 6 with the original OEM 'wall charger' a thermal event occurred. The wall charger was plugged into small extension cord which was then laying across a pillow. The phone was being used while it was being charged. Apple wall charger became so hot it left a small charring mark on the pillow case. In addition, the plastic case of the wall charger itself partially melted and sustained some dark charring. 
Had the overheating not been noticed it may have caused a fire.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and the likelihood of occurrence is high given the combination of factors involved.

incident_description:
re: Recall Number: 17-071  

Hi - I registered my CQ62 laptop when I purchased it.  

About 2 years ago the battery kept getting so hot I tossed it because I was concerned it would start a fire.

I have a copy of my original registration and I still have the CQ62 laptop, but I don't have the battery.

Now, there's a recall and the Recall Form will not go through without the battery serial number.

Can you tell me how I can submit my information when the company will not let me even contact them without the battery serial number? 

Thank you

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a potentially hazardous battery, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
The Artic Butterfly 724 has a fatal flaw which ensures your cleaner will break and fail. It is hard these days to design a product with 100% failure, but they have. The nonconductive ferrule shaft (it is white in the photos) is apparently made of a soft plastic that easily cracks. The shaft can develop hairline cracks where the brush will not stay securely attached to the DC motor shaft. The brush can then fly off and can lead to personal injury. Every one of these should be recalled until Visible Dust, the manufacturers of the Artic Butterfly, can redesign the brush and attachment point to make sure the the brush cannot fly off. 

The attached photos show a brand new 724 with the brush that arrived today (12/31/16) from Amazon that failed on first use. I was fortunate, the brush only hit me in the leg and did not hit me in the eye. I was not wearing eye protection. Nothing in the instructions suggests that eye protection is required during use.
justification: Brush detachment can cause personal injury, as demonstrated by the incident where it hit the user in the leg.

incident_description:
I purchased a Samsung 8000 55 inch TV on 1/6.  Out of the box the TV came with a bad remote.  I called Samsung support and they said that they would send me a new remote, however it could take up to 20 days.  The TV is useless without the remote.  I went ahead and told them to send me the new remote however they needed the Serial Number on the back of the TV.  The support person said that there was a way to get the Serial Number from one of the menu options, however you needed the remote to get there.  So, I moved the TV to get the Serial Number that you can barely read on the back.  In the process the TV slipped off of the stand because of the poorly designed chicken leg stand.  The TV fell over and cracked the screen.  

I went to a big box store to look at different TVs, and the salesperson told me that he's been seeing a lot of problems with these TVs because of the poorly designed stand.  According to him, these TVs have vibrated off of stands just from regular use.  The chicken legs at both sides is very poorly designed.  These TVs are dangerous when used on a stand.
justification: Injury occurred due to TV falling off poorly designed stand, and salesperson's report indicates this is a common issue.

incident_description: Product was being used to maintain a battery in a snowmobile.  Product' cable from the device the battery melted and could have caused a fire.  Device had been use for two years without an issue.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the melted cable posed a significant fire risk, making it an incident.

incident_description: I had purchased a tablet - RCA Model  RCT6103W46 - from Walmart about a little over a year now and my battery pack has suddenly inflated and the whole back has come off
justification: The incident involved a sudden battery pack inflation and detachment, posing a potential hazard but no immediate injury.

incident_description: We were dispatched to a home to investigate a possible structure fire. Upon our arrival, we found a SUPCO SCM 150 surge protection device was the cause. While we did not witness active flames, the failure of the device produced sufficient heat to melt the casing of the device as well as inflict thermal damage on an approximate 1 square foot of siding around the unit. There was a smoke stain above the device and the contents of the device were described as dripping out. There was no extension to the underlayment board beneath the siding. Approximate damages not including loss of the surge protector were 200 dollars.
justification: While no active flames were present, the device's failure caused thermal damage to the siding and produced smoke, indicating a potential fire hazard.

incident_description:
On January 2,2017 a SHARP USA 70" TV, model #LC-70LE857U, could have burnt down my house.

Approx. a month earlier the screen had gone black and the power light flashed 2 long an 5 fast. I had left the set plugged in thinking that a miracle might happen and it might reset itself. haha wishful thinking

The set was less then 3 years old. It cost $2,600.00 + warranty and taxes. 

January 2nd I was inspecting the TV because when passing by I felt it giving off extreme heat. Looking closer I could smell burning plastic. I immediately unplugged it and contacted SHARP USA.

I insisted that SHARP USA get someone to get this set out of my house. I was about to call the fire dept. to help remove it. I continued to keep a close watch over the set while it seemed to stay hot for hours more.

Sharp refused to send anyone to inspect the set until many calls later finally agreed to do so but not for a week or more.

I had informed every representative I spoke with that I was recording our conversations.

One rep., [REDACTED] insisted I DO NOT turn the set over to the CPSC.

Another rep., on the 4th, [REDACTED], threaten that if I give the set to the CPSC that it will void the warranty because someone other than SHARP USA will have opened the set. Funny thing, she KNEW it was well past the warranty stage.

Finally one week, 7 days later they sent a technician to check the set out.

The tech found the set short circuited which caused it to "OVERHEAT" which caused the plastic burning smell. He said it is very possible the set could have burned up.

So the tech that SHARP USA sent to my house confirmed the set was a fire hazard and endangered my family and children. Still SHARP USA is not concerned of the safety of their customers. They still refused to send someone to take the tv unless I took their deal which would have stopped any investigation by the CPSC.

SHARP USA's only concern was to sweep this under the rug by offering me a "refurbished set", and they would charge me $420.00. I was more concerned about their advising the CPSC.

The last rep. I spoke with was [REDACTED] who stated she was a "display coordinator". I repeatedly asked her if the CPSC was contacted within the 24 hr period they are required to and she had no response. I don't think ANY rep I spoke with knew about the CPSC. That is sad. When I insisted to speak with someone higher she refused. She said she was the highest level I could go. I'm sorry SHARP USA if [REDACTED] is at the top level of your customer relations, your out of your minds.

I want this resolved. I want a full refund. I expect nothing less than that from SHARP USA .

Above all I want the CPSC to come take the television to further investigate. This cannot be an isolated issue. Other families might be in danger.
justification: The TV posed a significant fire risk, nearly causing an incident with no injuries.

incident_description: Our client purchased an amazon fire stick at a local Target store in Tucson AZ. He fell asleep with the remote in his hand and woke up because his hand was burning. He suffered burns to 3 fingers.
justification: The incident resulted in burns to three fingers, classifying it as an injury (severity level 3). The likelihood is considered possible (3) as it's not a common occurrence but could happen due to human error.

incident_description:
I need to report the following item available from Amazon:

Martheroll Video Baby Monitor HD 720P Video Recording with Two-Way Audio and Infrared Night Vision
Link: https://www.amazon.com/dp/B01KE1NPLA?m=AWDIUH8WO32OU&ref_=v_sp_widget_detail_page&th=1

The prong for the charger broke off in the socket the first time we plugged it in. This is an extreme hazard for an item that is supposed to go in close proximity to a baby - this suggests the product was not subjected to the necessary quality assurance for a baby item and represents a fire hazard. 

I have a picture of the item with the broken prong left in the socket. Please contact me at [REDACTED] if you need this picture.
justification: The broken charger prong poses a fire hazard, which could lead to property damage or injury if not addressed.

incident_description:
I have had my MacBook Pro since May 2016 and it was purchased new at a university bookstore tech center.  I have noticed that the square part of the charging cable (85W MagSafe 2 Power Adapter) has begun to get very hot when I charge my computer.
When I picked it up so I could move my computer to another room on Sunday, January 15, 2017, it was so hot it nearly burned my hand and I dropped it to prevent the burn.  
At this point, I'm nervous about charging my computer when I'm not watching it as I'm afraid it will cause a fire.  I'm also nervous about my kids using the computer while it's charging as if they touched the box on the charging cable, one of them is bound to get burned.
justification: The charging cable has already caused a near-burn injury and poses a high risk of burns to children.

incident_description:
(12/26/2016) While removing things to renovate kitchen we saw that this unit apparently shorted out and burned a hole through the outside housing. 

We are fortunate it was not a full blown fire that would have destroyed our house.

12/28/2016 The consumer contacted the manufacturer to advised them of the incident. She was advised to send pictures. No one responded.
justification: Although no fire occurred, the incident could have escalated, hence severity level 2. The likelihood is possible as it happened during renovation.

incident_description:
The battery of my Toshiba L75D-A7283 very easily runs very overheat when I use it.
Kind of afraid to use it as the temperature is really high. Need a replacement of the battery. Thanks
justification: Battery overheating is a recurring issue, posing a potential fire hazard but no immediate injury risk.

incident_description: Battery became extremely hot, and then my laptop stopped working.
justification: The incident resulted in a non-functional laptop but no physical harm, and similar incidents due to overheating are possible but not frequent.

incident_description:
I have a Lenovo All in One PC
At 9.30 on 2nd January 2017. My Wife and Daughter shouted to me that they could smell burning and see smoke coming
from our study. Went I went to the room it was full of smoke. I unplugged all electrical items. I could see smoke coming
from the top of the Lenovo PC
I could smell burning plastic from the top
I called Lenovo technical support as I read on Google that there had been a recall on some product power supplies
I was told that this model was not subject to a recall
And as it was out of warranty they couldn't help
I said that I didn't think that was good enough as there could have been a serious fire
If this had happened during the night there could have been a serious fire and possible injuries
We were just about to go shopping when the incident occurred. If we had left a few minutes earlier it would have been a
different situation
I asked to speak to a supervisor. I was told that there was nothing they could do
I asked the operator to tell the Supervisor that I was prepared to talk to the CPSC
After a few minutes waiting the call was disconnected
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a significant risk of fire and potential injuries, given the smoke and burning plastic smell.

incident_description:
The Belkin surge suppressor, that we have had for years, just caught fire. We heard a buzzing noise first, and when we went into the room, there were flames, about a foot high, coming up from the surge suppressor.  We unplugged the surge suppressor, put out the fire, and then examined the surge suppressor. The fire started on the back of the surge suppressor, there is a large blackened hole, along with electrical fire soot covering the suppressor and the power cords that were plugged in. The fire burned our rug quite severely. Luckily, the damage was limited to the rug.  My [REDACTED], [REDACTED] and lamp, that were plugged in to the surge suppressor, were all working properly afterwards. We do not understand why this happened. Further, we do not understand why the electrical fire didn't trip our breaker. As you can imagine, we were grateful to have been home, as the electrical fire, that started in the surge suppressor, could easily have burned our house down. 
I am sending this information to Belkin as well, as I do not know if this is an isolated incident, or if there is some kind of manufacturing defect in the surge suppressor.
We are totally in shock, and now fearful, as we have 4 other Belkin surge suppressors, of the same type, in our house with electronic equipment plugged in. I am going to replace them with another brand as soon as possible.
Please use this information to warn consumers - I believe Belkin should recall these surge suppressors.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the fire could have been catastrophic, hence severity level 2.

incident_description: (11/18/2016) The consumer stated that the battery was in a catch-all basket. She was on the phone with her sister.  The consumer had dump the contents of the basket out on the floor to sort through them. The contents were on the floor in the sunlight. The consumer heard a pop and a bang. She went over to investigate. She found that the battery had exploded into three pieces. Part of battery hit the consumer door. There was no fire, flash of light or burn mark on the rug.
justification: Battery explosion caused injury (part hit the consumer's door) but no fire or burns.

incident_description:
Etymotic, a manufacturer of in-ear earphones, provides foam eartips that are inserted into the ear as part of the product.

At least one of the types of these eartips that they provide appears to be prone towards falling apart inside of the user's ear. I recently had a 1475 dollar emergency room visit once it fell apart in my ear, and had to be removed by a physician.

The design of this eartip product (a disposable in-ear device that eventually falls apart) appears to be fundamentally fault.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury requiring medical attention, and the likelihood of occurrence is high given the product's design and the user's experience.

incident_description:
Product Information:
Samsung Travel Charger
Model: ETA-U90JWE Input:100-240V-50-60Hz 0.35A  Output:5.0V-2.0A

After about thirty (30) minutes of first using the charger, it started glowing (orange-like) internally and making a buzzing or hissing sound.  Then it sounded like it popped and some smoke came out, along with a strong odor of burnt wire.  These (2) were Christmas presents for my grandchildren and were purchased online at Walmart.   The other charger was immediately retrieved and is not being used.
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the incident involved a product malfunction with visible smoke and a strong odor, indicating potential danger.

incident_description:
I received as a gift from my sister on Christmas Day (so I have had it six days) and used on our kitchen counter to charge our Galaxy S7 phones. It was purchased from Besy Buy. On Jan 1 I smelled something burning and walk over to see the charger smoldering at the usb port. There was no phone on it charging. I learned that the blue light means charging. When I walked up to it, that light was on. There had not been a phone on it for at least thirty minutes. I am guessing it burned itself up continuing to charge with nothing there. Good thing I caught it before it caught my house on fire... We use all Samsung OE products because I know that's important and have two "slow" wireless chargers that have worked perfectly for over a year.  All samsung products I own (phone, chagers, etc...) are all within Samsungs 1y warranty. 

No injuries, I caught it before it caused damage to other persons/items. 

Samsung refused to offer assistance without me providing them the product. I noted that I would only provide the product to the CPSC. I have called and notified Samsung but based on the recent history of items I have declined to send the device to them but instead prefer to send it to your office for testing. Please contact me and I can send you photos for preliminary review. The outlet the device was plugged into is a 20A/125V GFCI in our kitchen, fully compliant with local electrical code, as is the remainder of our home's electrical system. Our home is located in Cobb County, Ga.
justification: No injuries occurred, but the incident could have caused property damage if not caught in time.

incident_description:
My husband treated me to a Fitbit charge HR and after three weeks I notice and fiery red rash appear on the underside of the flash sensor( the hard back , not the strap) I started wiping my Fitbit after my exercise with a wipe then a dry cloth. I charge my Fitbit every 2/3 days. After a few days of cleaning my Fitbit my rash remained
Just as fiery, if not more so I removed it to my other wrist. After 4 days of being on my other wrist the same thing was beginning there so I removed my Fitbit cleaned it , loosened it( but by doing this , my readings changed for he monitor so my strap was too loose. I put a plaster over the areas for a few days and tried that but my skin needed fresh air to heal so I had to remove them. This went on for 5 months until I contacted Fitbit to inform them with photos that my wrist wAs covered in a blistery fiery red rash that was not going away. I started using cortisone cream which helped with the itching and removed the heat from my rash but if I put my Fitbit back on the rash returned. Fitbit instructed me to destroy my Fitbit and they would refund my money within 3-4 weeks. So now I have no Fitbit and as yet no refund. My concern is the damage it's caused to my skin , will continue to happen to others. I'm a member of a fitness group and dozens of people have these very same problems. I'm left with dry patches now though my redness has gone.so it's taken  4/5 weeks of not wearing my Fitbit for it to start to clear. Two trips to the doctors, two tubes of cream and lots of scraping and scratching and discomfort. My thought was that the flashing lights from the back of the watch that act as the hr sensors is causing heat and blistering directly below the sensor.
justification: The incident resulted in a persistent, painful rash and blisters on the user's wrist, with no resolution despite multiple attempts, indicating a significant injury.

incident_description:
Motorola baby monitor MBP36s
Purchased at Target 60 days ago.  The camera was placed on a dresser, flat surface, and away from any obstructions or soft fabrics.  On Christmas Eve, I heard a "crunching of paper" type noise from the monitor so I went to check on my baby in his bedroom. His room smelled like plastic burning.  I picked up the "camera" to check the plug and the camera was too hot to touch.   It had melted the underpart of the Camera and the top of the dresser.
justification: The baby monitor overheated and melted, posing a potential fire hazard and risk of injury, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
We bought our video baby monitor roughly 2 years ago for our first child and started using it with our newborn a few months ago. I noticed it was smelling warm and immediately stopped using it. I had my husband look at it this morning and we noted that the charger/ adapter, started to melt, along with parts inside the adapter. This was in our newborns room! It did not trip a breaker, it did not stop working, nothing. It was not near anything else that was warm, or anything else even plugged in. There is no reason it should have gotten so hot that it began to melt. This is a huge fire hazard and I would hope that you all take this into consideration. 

It was dry, but cold conditions outdoors. We had no electrical issues in our house.
justification: The adapter melting poses a significant fire risk, which could have led to property damage or injury if not noticed.

incident_description:
I have a Lorex security system (Model WL2750) with monitor and two cameras. I went to pick up my monitor and the area where the batter is was so hot it stung my hand. I quickly let go of the monitor and it had already turned my hand bright red. The battery "door" is being pushed out from the back of the monitor because the battery is expanding so much. 

I called the company and they said that they are aware of the battery issue and since I am out of warranty, they will only charge me $200 for a new system. Which is the price of this system on sale. I am very worried that these could potentially start a fire or seriously burn someone. This is the exact same issue they are having with their care n share baby monitor. I'm not sure why these have not been recalled yet.
justification: The battery expansion and heat caused a burn injury, and the potential for fire makes further occurrences likely.

incident_description: Surge protector plugged in behind bed, with only a small portable heater and a short strand of christmas lights connected.  When changing the bedsheets, noticed that rotating plug was melted and wall outlet burned.
