incident_description: I purchased the "Square pefect 24" Folding photo box" from Amazon.com as a Christmas gift for my sister, it  comes with the fabric folding photo box, 41ights (approx 1 0" off the ground with a 3 point stand), and a tripod type stand for your phone. It is advertised in the Amazon product heading as coming with LED lights. In fact only 2 of the lights are LED and the others are halaogen, we found this out only because 1 non LED light lit our carpet on fire! Which could've been very serious if someone hadn't smelled it burning at put it out in time. Besides the fact that the product did not come with the 4 LED lights as told. It also came with no instructions, no warnings, nothing saying that the 2 halogen lights get so hot that they will light things on fire or that they get so hot that you canont even handle them because they will burn you. The lights are on a 3 point stand which is very easy to knock over, a child or pet knock them over and catch something on fire in addition to being serously burnt. I by chance happen to have an infared thermometer and I measured how hot these halogen lights get, after just 2 minutes they got to 171.1 degrees fahrenheit and after 8 minutes were 301 degrees fahrenheit! Keep in mind that you that you are supposed to be able to move these lights around your photo box for best placement and put the lights directly up against the fabric of the photo box as advertised online. Well301 degrees enough for 3rd degree burns and enough to light carpet or any other fabric on fire.! am very very concerned about the saftey of these halogen light products. They sell many versions & sizes of this one it on Amazon and most do not come with any LED lights, these are a burn and fire hazard and should not be sold. And in my opinion they should be recalled.
justification: Halogen lights reached temperatures high enough to cause burns and ignite fires, posing a significant risk.

incident_description:
Design of unit's detachable power supply may cause serious injury or death by electrocution.

No visible signs of misuse was detected.

Visual Land, Model SW-050210.  No clearly identifiable serial number.

incident_description: My several-year-old Uniden LANDLINE phone (PowerMAX5. 8GHz), sitting in its charging cradle had a column of smoke rising from it when I came home and first saw it. The outer plastic case was melted in two places and hot to the touch. I can only assume that had I not come home to detach it, it might have burst into flames and ignited a fire.
justification: The phone showed signs of overheating and could have potentially caught fire if left unattended, posing a risk to the property and occupants.

incident_description:
The printer is a Maker Select 3D Printer v2 13860

While waiting for pre-heat setting on the printer to complete for an ABS print, the printer started smoking and producing a visible flame from inside the control box. I had to quickly remove the power cord from the wall as the flame was growing in intensity and the room was starting to fill with smoke. I proceeded to post a warning in an internet group about the issue and had another member state that the same thing happened to them just before my post. After doing more research I have found that this printer is a rebrand of the [REDACTED] which has had a recall in the past for a fire hazard. It also appears that the newest version of this printer the [REDACTED] also has a recall because of a fire hazard. As more information was posted to the group is appears that [REDACTED] has not programmed the correct settings into the firmware of the printer to keep this issue from happening as well as not having the proper size connectors for wiring inside of the control box. If this is common knowledge, why has [REDACTED] not addressed these safety hazards? I have worked in the electronics industry for 25 years and there is no reason for modern equipment to get to point of a visible fire. Proper settings and use of proper sized components should make a failure a non-event with only localized damage. However when a failure allows a full on fire, it is a major concern and should be addressed by the manufacturer before someone is hurt, killed or their house burns down.
justification: The incident involved a visible flame and smoke, but no injuries were reported, and the issue was addressed promptly by removing the power source.

The MacBook still over heats and has burned several table tops and has caused a black smoke burn. I have received burns to the top of my legs after using the macbook on my lap for schoolwork.

incident_description: On Saturday, 12/31, i was with a group of friends at our recreation center in our community. As i was standing there, my Apple iPhone 6, which was in my right front pocket began to make a loud noise and basically exploded and caught fire. I burned through my pocket and went down my leg. it eventually came out my pants leg but I sustained 1st and 2nd degree burns on my thigh and shin. the phone was not being used or was even touch at the time
justification: Injury occurred due to phone explosion and fire, but not life-threatening.

incident_description: My Apple iPhone 6c was plunged into an Apple charger with an Apple charging cord which came with the original purchase of phone.  I had noticed the phone would become extremely warm if it was in use while plugged in.  This did not seem to be unusual.  My phone was plugged in and lying on my bed.  I got up to let my dog outside. After approximately 5 minutes I returned upstairs to my bedroom. I heard a hissing sound and thought it was the stool running. At the top of the stairs I could see an orange inferno covering my bed. I panicked and started to run and get the hose. Realizing it was unhooked and may have water in it that was frozen. I ran back upstairs for my phone to call the fire department an realized my phone would have been in the center of the inferno.  Black smoke filled the room with the distinct smell of an electrical fire.  To save my home from burning to the ground, I grabbed the side of my down comforter and flipped it over onto the flames. As I did that the fan of air to the flames whooshed out at me and caught the hair on the right side of my head on fire. I backed away to brush the fire in my hair off and noticed that covering the flames on the bed helped. I went into the hall for a breath of less smokey air and realized I must do this again if I were to save my home. This time I was more cautious as I flipped the other side of the comfort or over the flames. My beard melted to my face and all hair on my arms and chest was singed to the skin. Went for more air and saw this accomplished putting out the majority. I have a fire extinguisher down the hall but it all happened in a matter of probably under 30 seconds. Instead of grabbing the extinguisher, I rolled the comforter into a ball putting out the fire to a manageable level. I ran out for air. Knowing there may be smoldering cinders within, and there was upon inspection, a grabbed the black ball of what use to be a comforter and dragged it down the stairs and out the back door. At this point I needed to sit and breath for a moment before going at it more. I found a Cotten shirt with small flames on it and doused it with water using a cup in the bathroom. Almost 24 hours I am still in shock as to what happened. I went to unroll the comforter on the back lawn to see the Apple charger was completely fried. My phone was still plugged in yet is basically unharmed.  I have ruled out every possible reason for this occurance and come to the absolute conclusion that the Apple charger and or cord is 100% to blame. I am thankful I was not overcome by smoke and died and no other furniture or home was set ablaze. To this moment there remains that very distinct smell of an electrical fire.
justification: The incident resulted in severe burns to the individual's hair, beard, and skin, warranting a severity level of 3. The likelihood is rated 4 as the incident occurred while the phone was in use and plugged in, a common scenario.

incident_description:
We purchased an HP Pavilion laptop (Model G6 Serial No. 5CG150093K) approximately five years ago. Tragically, it literally blew up Thursday December 22, 2016. 

The havoc it caused in our kitchen/family room was quite extensive. It was plugged into the outlet. Had just booted up with no apps running. My daughter, [REDACTED], heard a pop (she was sitting about 10 feet away with the PC directly in her vision and a minute later the laptop left the countertop in an upward flight, flipped over 180 degrees in the air then landed on its top and the battery pack was on fire lying on our granite countertop. Pieces of battery, copper, and burning ash with some chemical too spread over a 20 foot square area. The next thing she did was to put out the fire even though she was in shock from the explosion that had just taken place. She successfully did so, and managed to avoid burning herself in the process. 
If she had been in front of the PC she would have been badly burned and if not home our house could certainly have burned down. There was extensive damage in the kitchen which we are still finding two days later. Our hardwood floor has many deep burn marks, the stainless fridge and dishwasher are damaged chemicals, and our floor was covered in copper, ash, acid, etc. Finally, there were burn holes discovered in our handmade cashmere Persian rug. 

We had Seattle KIRO7 TV here that evening for a story which they are still investigating before airing. It appears a battery recall for this model was only for 2013-16 and was voluntary, but we never received an email or letter about this issue (even though I purchased this directly from HP).
justification: The incident resulted in no deaths but caused significant injuries and property damage, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood of occurrence is high given the voluntary recall and the incident happening during use.

incident_description: The 32" RCA television has emitted a mysterious, white crystallized substance continually for several years. RCA claims it is the fire retardant reacting with the environment and claims it is not harmful but does not cite any supporting evidence such as tests or studies.

incident_description: I noticed an irritated area on the side/rear of my neck on the left side. I wasn't sure what it was but it did not cross my mind that it was my Samsung Level U bluetooth headset. I put my bluetooth around my neck and went about my day as I normally do. Later that evening as I was preparing to take off my headset, I noticed that the area was worse and that it seemed to get larger. It resembled a burn and it hurt and itched. My husband asked me what did I burn myself with and I replied that I had not burned myself with anything. Again, it did not cross my mind at the time it was my headset. I took it off, took my shower, put [REDACTED] ointment on the area and went to bed. The next day I did what I normally do, put on my headset and go about my day. That is when I noticed that it got worse every time I put the headset around my neck. I immediately stopped using the headset and went to the doctor. I was diagnosed with a burn on the neck and prescribed a cream for burns. I immediately called Samsung on 10-13-16 and filed a complaint. They emailed me except they kept calling me by another customer's name. I told them who I was and they said I had to call back and re-file the complaint. After doing so, they asked me to send them medical documentation and a receipt. I sent the medical documentation and explained that I no longer had the receipt because I made the purchase several months ago from Sam's Club. About a day later, a lady from Samsung left a message on my voice mail saying that my claim is dismissed because I was not using a Samsung phone. FYI, they advertise the Level U headsets as compatible with android devices, not exclusively Samsung phones. Also, I haven't used the headset since and my neck finally healed only after I stopped using the headset.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury, rated as 'Injury' (3), and the likelihood of occurrence is high (4) as the user regularly wore the headset.

incident_description: I purchased a black Fitbit Charge HR in size small from Kohl's on March 5, 2015. incident_description:
I have a Levana baby monitor which we use during evening hours to keep an eye on our daughter, now 15 months old, when she goes to sleep in her crib. On October 27, my daughter went to sleep and we were monitoring her using Levana monitor while watching a game in the living room. After some time, I could hear crying in the background in very low volume. I thought it was our neighbors as they have kids as well and continued to watch the game. After a while when it didn't stop, it struck me that there is a possibility of the baby monitor screen being frozen and I ran upstairs. 

Unfortunately, it was daughter, all soaked in tears, alone in a dark room, trying to jump out of the crib (luckily she is still not that tall). It broke my heart as she possibly might have been crying for the last half hour or more and look traumatized by the whole experience.

Then, I contacted them on Twitter to which they responded and got my email address and phone number. In the email response, I was given notes about how to maintain the quality of the picture and how to sync etc. There was no response to the problem I faced and the lack of empathy to even learn about the problem really hurt me. 

I really dread about an alternate scenario where I would have not heard my baby crying and she would have been all alone looking for some help for hours before we would have gone to bed. Their monitor didn't have any warning about the signal lost or anything that would have helped us to know the issue with the frozen screen.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident could have resulted in distress and potential harm if the baby had been left unattended longer.

[REDACTED]

The boat was well offshore, about halfway between [REDACTED] and the [REDACTED].

fire at approximately 6:15 - 6:30 pm. The headset was last used the afternoon of Thursday 10/20/16 and plugged

wrong with it. Our building maintenance staff checked and there was nothing wrong with the electrical outlet or

incident_description:
I am a certified marine electrician and I was performing an electrical safety check on a vessel located at the marina at Patrick Air Force Base. When I tested the polarity of a 120 volt outlet on an on-board power strip my tester indicated reverse polarity (hot and neutral wires reversed). I unpluged the power strip and tested the outlet directly and found the outlet was wired correctly. 

I suspected the wiring of the power strip to be incorrect. I opened the sealed strip and found that the unit's white neutral wire is incorrectly soldered to the small terminal on the plug and the black hot wire is soldered to the longer of the terminals. This is completely backwards based on NFPA Electrical Code and is in fact very dangerous, especially aboard a boat.
justification: Potential for electric shock and fire, but no immediate injury reported.

incident_description:
We received information regarding a potentially non-compliant USB Type-C cable and purchased the cable from Amazon.

CeeOne's cable uses the 10k resistor instead of the USB-IF specifcation mandated 56k resistor. If you use it with a 5V 3A capable device (and there are more and more of them on the market every day), it may cause damage to your charger, hub, or PC USB port

This cable fails and it's a dangerous cable. It shows a voltage on CC that looks like 3A advertisement so a capable device will pull too much current from a legacy host.

The USB-IF has tested the cable and provided the failures to Amazon and  CeeOne. Amazon has removed the product due to safety concerns but CeeOne has yet to respond. We are worried CeeOne will continue to sell the faulty cable and cause end comsumer's to fry their phones, etc because the cable draws too much current when plugged into a host.
justification: The cable's non-compliance with USB-IF specifications could lead to damage of devices, potentially causing incidents but unlikely to result in injuries or deaths.

This has been happening since I bought it but as I have checked with other users, I disregarded the heating issue as a normal thing to happen. At that time I was ready to leave the country for two months and he suggested that I bought another compatible battery and sent me to a store that according to him was a reliable store.  He said I could claim a refund after I came back.  I did what he recommended and the battery store sold me a [REDACTED] battery.  With the new battery the phone was not as hot. I was startled and my first reaction was to throw a pillow over the flames.  As I lifted the pillow the battery of the phone was melted (puffed up) over the carpet but was still smoking.  I had a glass of water in my night table and I poured it over the battery.  What an awful experience; waking up to such a scene where the whole room was lighted and heated by flames reaching about 3 feet height and the smelling of burning carpet!  Indeed, an emotionally disturbing experience. I was traumatized, nervous and trembling for a few hours with my heart beating very fast.   

The next day I went to the same Verizon store and told them about my case.  They did not take responsibility.  Then I went to Costco from where I bought the phone and they, too, would not take responsibility.  Well, I left it to that and continued to use the phone as I tried the original battery I have saved and to my surprise, it was still working.  When the battery exploded it separated from the phone in a very weird way.  The cover was still on the night table and the phone was on the floor about 7 inches away from the melted battery.  Yes, I have been using this phone but with a lot of apprehension.  I am so scare that it is going to happen again!  Now that I hear about these other cases with the Galaxy Note 7 and the regulators recalling these phones; asking people to stop using them, I would appreciate if you could assist me and/or guide me on what to do.  
I took pictures and collected samples of the damage to my carpet, pillow, pillow case and phone, which although it is working, the explosion caused a little crack on the glass. I wish someone could help me.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (trauma, nervousness, and rapid heartbeat) and property damage (burnt carpet, pillow, and cracked phone glass).

incident_description: Please investigate the relationship between wearing a Fitbit and wrist pain.  At the end of June, I purchased a Fitbit Alta.  Approximately 1 week after I started wearing it, I began to experience intermittent excruciating pain radiating from my left wrist.  Originally, I thought I had sprained my wrist, but I could not recall any accident I had.  I also thought that maybe I had slept on my arm wrong.  I did wear the Fitbit when I slept to monitor my sleep pattern.  Three weeks later, I lost the Fitbit and did not replace it for approximately 4 weeks.  During these 4 weeks, the wrist pain subsided and eventually stopped.  I bought a new Fitbit Alta.  After wearing it for about 1 week, I began to have the same type of wrist pain that I previously had.  I thought this was strange and began to question whether there was a relationship between wearing my Fitbit and the pain so I stopped wearing the Fitbit.  The pain began to subside and eventually stopped.  Currently I am not wearing it, and have no wrist pain.  I did not speak to anyone about my pain, not even my husband.  Last week my husband began to experience wrist pain.  I was astounded when he described his pain as it was identical to the pain I had experienced.  He wears a Fitbit Charge on his left wrist.  He is also right hand dominant and does not wear the Fitbit when he sleeps.  He has not had any accidents.   I thought this was more than coincidence so I began to research the issue on the internet.  I found many stories of people who had wrist pain and wore a Fitbit.   When I told my husband what I had found, he stopped wearing his Fitbit.  His pain has subsided.  We are both healthy, active individuals with no arthritis, nerve or bone disease.  We had not had a rash or the skin irritation some people complained about.  Something disturbing is occurring as a result of wearing a Fitbit and I feel it warrants an investigation of the Fitbit and its connection to wrist pain.
justification: Both individuals experienced identical wrist pain after wearing a Fitbit, with symptoms subsiding upon removal.

incident_description:
On July 16, 2016 I was working on my Apple MacBook Pro notebook computer at our vacation home, when I noticed, after a break, that the touch pad in the base of the computer was pushed up and out of the space it should occupy. At that same time I noticed an odor of overheated electronics, so I felt along the back of the computer and noticed a hot spot. After taking the back cover off, it was clear that the battery was the cause of the problem, since it was very hot, and it had expanded so much that it pushed the touch pad right up out of the computer.  The immediate problem at that time was a label warning placed by Apple advising the user that they should not remove the battery. I contacted the nearest Apple store that I knew in Christiana, Delaware, but they indicated that they would not touch batteries at that store, even though they did other repairs. 

Since even in a powered down state the battery remained hot, I called Apple support number and advised them of the condition.  That case number is # [REDACTED]. Since I had enough technical proficiency to figure out how to remove the battery, despite special screws that could not be removed with any common tool, I was able to get the battery out and remove it from the building to a safe location, since there was a real concern about the battery igniting or exploding. Apple confirmed that this was the right thing to do, based on the potential harm, despite their warnings and mechanical attempts to the contrary. 

Fortunately I was not injured, nor was there any property damage to the home. However I do not know if any of the electrical connections to the touch pad were compromised, resulting in a potential fire hazard should a broken wire start arcing. As such I have been reluctant to use that computer, and I consider that a property loss.  I did contact Apple and sought reimbursement for  the replacement battery, considering the overall circumstances. They refused to provide that, since their argument is that a battery is a consumable item that has a defined life. While that it true, the defined life most surely is not expected to end in a fire or explosion, and one that may not be avoided by the average users due to Apple's efforts to make removal of the battery difficult or impossible for that average user. 

At this point, at the least, I would hope that you would require Apple to recall all notebook computers using this battery and/or that include the warning label not to remove the battery and to also require Apple to provide for the replacement of the specialty screws with a common Philips or flat head screw that could be removed by consumers. Ideally Apple should also be required to replace all such batteries, or to provide reimbursements where the user has already replaced the item, as you have done with other manufacturers where a fire or explosion hazard is reported. 

Thank you.
justification: Potential fire hazard due to battery expansion and heat, but no immediate injury or property damage.

incident_description:
I have owned my Samsung S6 Edge for just about 3 months. In this time, the phone has overheated frequently, to the point where it has left several burns on my fingers, hands and arms. Some of these burns have left blisters, and at least two have left scars. None were large enough to seek out medical attention, but they have been painful, as I suspect most burns are, and have required ointment and over-the-counter pharmaceutical care.

Contact with Samsung's customer service has been less than stellar. At the same time, the phone has stopped charging (the charging cord no longer fits in the slot provided for it). I was told over the phone that their warranty program was better than the one provided by Verizon. This appears to have been a blatant lie. Regardless, rather than replace the faulty device, the claim to have fixed ONLY the overheating issue. The phone has not been returned to me, no one can confirm or deny whether it is still overheating, and no one will address the issue of the phone not charging. No one has acknowledged the photographs of my blistered burns and scars. I do not know when to expect my phone, and have been told that they fixed it for free this time, but it was a one-time deal (even though it is under warranty for another 9 months, and fixing it should be covered by that warranty).

I remained cooperative with customer service up until I received a random text message that my phone repair was complete. I had not been contacted to discuss the underlying issue with my phone, what my concerns were, what the potential solutions were...anything. I was then told the phone would be returned to me with an additional 90 day warranty. When I asked if this meant the remaining 9 months of my original warranty plus their additional 90 days, I did not receive an answer. I believe this to mean that the repaired phone has a remainder of 90 days warranty, the same as the Verizon warranty I was asked to give up in favor of Samsung's supposedly "better" warranty program (and worse customer service).

In the meantime, I still have scars remaining on my body from the previously obtained burns left from the device they are now sending back to me. Having been given the runaround about the service process on my phone, I have done some research and discovered that overheating is a common issue with this device. I cannot be the only person who has been burnt, blistered, or scarred from the extreme temperatures this phone can reach. And not infrequently. The device gets hot enough to at least redden the skin several times a day, often while not being used. Imagine what could happen if someone had the phone in their pocket and it reached those temperature -- and was able to ignite the fabric of their clothing?
justification: The incident resulted in burns, blisters, and scars, classifying it as an injury (severity level 3). The likelihood is high (4) given the frequency of overheating and the commonality of this issue with the device.

incident_description:
On July 15, 2016, a fire began in our home studio/man cave that was started by a faulty Drop Cam/NEST Security Monitoring Camera.  We have footage recorded, and saved, of the day before the incident, the day of the incident, and when the fire started.  The camera was having issues all day with the night vision and was making loud clicking noises turning on and off.  The only thing plugged into the socket where the fire started was the camera and the air conditioning unit (which was not running and hadn't been on since the evening before for a very short period of time)  we have the video footage proving it was off.  

After the fire, the head fire chief made a report stating that the fire started because of the faulty camera.  He said the cord (which has a box at the bottom of it) was over heating and because it got so hot the cord of the AC ignited and in turn caused the room to go up in flames.  We have footage of the fire starting and smoke coming from underneath the camera, where it was plugged in.  

Our renters insurance sent out a cause and origin inspector, whom explained to me that it is obvious where the fire stared due to the pattern of the smoke prints (at the place the camera was plugged in). He also opened the new socket and wiring, and said that there was nothing wrong inside the building with the electrical.  We have advised NEST of the issue with the camera and the only thing they did was send us a refurbished one and sent out their own investigator.  

Not only are we out over 150K above our policy limits, but I am suffering from PTSD due to the experience.  I was home with my daughter during the fire and I have horrible emotional distress after it.  I cannot work, I cannot sleep, and I am concerned this will happen in someone else's home or god forbid a babies room.  I have turned off all of the cameras in my home and I'm upset that we are being brushed aside.  I have gone to my therapist for help in dealing with the stress and fear after the fire. Every friend I have spoken to about this, that has children, is freaked out and it urging me to speak out to media about this.  Many of them have NEST drop cams in their home and they are concerned, as am I, about the wellbeing of other families.  

My husband has lost his life worth of collections and has lost work having to be home to deal with the aftermath.  I want people to know how dangerous we feel this is and has the potential of being.  We don't want to spend the money out of our pocket on the electrical engineer (which was advised for us to do by the cause and origin investigator) to prove what went wrong with the camera.  We don't want to fight with NEST to recover our damages and go to public form about this, but we believe if they don't help remedy this situation, amicably and go to further measures to avoid this from happening again, then we will.
justification: The incident resulted in significant property damage and psychological trauma, with potential for further harm given the widespread use of the faulty product.

I would like the CPSC to send Blizzard Entertainment a LOA to halt current production, and marketing and correct future production with an increase to the apparent camera distance and to reinstate the configuration variables and console commands that allowed me to enjoy the product I paid for without becoming nauseous, or falling out of my chair due to disorientation.

incident_description: Engine 8, Engine 7, Rescue 7, Ladder 5, Ladder 1, Battalion 2, and Morrisville Pumper 3 were dispatched to a structure fire at 204 Frontgate Drive.  While en route, dispatch advised that the fire was called in by a neighbor who stated that an HVAC unit was on fire.  I proceeded to the rear of the home and found that there was no active fire.  The caller stated that they had extinguished the mulch with a garden hose.  I did find superficial smoke and heat damage to the cement board siding of the home and damage to a HVAC power disconnect box. I assigned Rescue 7 the task of checking for tripped breakers in the home's main panel and also isolation of the circuit for the upstairs air conditioning compressor.  Rescue 7 found that the breaker was tripped for HVAC #2.  They then turned the breaker off.  Engine 8 personnel then opened the cover to the power disconnect box and pulled the fuse.  There was minimal damage inside the box, however some of the wiring did show signs of heat related stress.   There were wires that had been burnt off as they passed through an accessory hole on the side of the box.  Those wires were connected to a surge protector that was mounted to the side of the disconnect.  The entire surge protector had burned or melted away leaving nothing but the connection wires.  We were able to identify the brand and model of the surge protector by looking at the disconnect for HVAC #1.  The homeowner confirmed that there had been a surge protector on each unit.  The homeowner was unfamiliar with the surge protector and stated that it had been installed by a company that performed HVAC service in the past.  I did a cursory internet search for the surge protector and showed the findings to the homeowner.  I advised him to contact his current HVAC company and request that they respond today for repair and further evaluation of both systems.  Furthermore, I advised him that he should discuss the need for the surge protector on HVAC #1.  The homeowner said that he had recently had a whole home surge protection system installed by Duke Progress Energy.
justification: No active fire found, but smoke and heat damage to siding and power disconnect box, with a tripped breaker and melted surge protector.

incident_description: I'd recently moved my Amazon FireStick from behind the television into a more accessible location inside of an entertainment system/cabinet along with other devices.  I have been moving/rearranging items in my home, and thus had been having a lot of contact and interaction with the device, and previously (well over a year) never physically touched it since it was behind my television plugged into an HDMI port. I spent some time testing it in small amounts of time to see if it was still getting hot, and during one of the tests, I left the item plugged in for around ten minutes (which is normal...it is even recommended that this item be plugged in 24/7) and when I observed the item again, it had physically started melting. Thankfully I had been monitoring and testing this item, as the damages caused by this could have been catastrophic to my home, and could have caused severe burns if handled.  I've spent days searching, and cannot find information of anyone else having this happen, but there does seem to be a very well-known issue with this item overheating.

The consumer planned on keeping the unit for at least the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues. However, Belkin says she needs to send it [product] to them, and it has been sent to them on 5/31/16 via mail with tracking.


The consumer provided a letter, received on 6/15/16, stating:

Dear CPSC investigator:

Belkin telephone personnel noted my safety concerns and instructed me to return the outlet via their warranty program. I mailed the claim and surge  protector via tracked  US mail (tracking #[REDACTED]) on 5/3 1/16 to the address they provided. Their warranty description states that they will check the surge protector to ensure it is defective. Hopefully this occurs and Belkin will correct any design defects and/or  recall any other similarly defective devices.

Attached is your report with my corrections and signature. The electrician said the outlet was not at fault. However, I still have it in case either  Belkin or you need it.  I am enclosing pictures as well as the electrician's report.  If you need me to send additional pictures or anything else feel free to contact  me. I consider  myself very fortunate that I was not injured.   I am very grateful for the circuit breaker/GFE and luck that the sparks did not land on any papers or me!

incident_description:
Purchased "Omaker 2 Pack Reversible Micro USB Cable High Speed USB 2.0 A Male to Micro B Sync and Charging Cable Cord with Reversible USB Port" from Amazon. The cable ends have been modified to allow them to supposedly be inserted into the mating female socket in either orientation - similar to how the [REDACTED] cables or USB C cables work. The first time I plugged the cable in to charge an external battery pack ([REDACTED] power bank) from an AC USB charger ([REDACTED] port wall charger), the cable shorted, the battery quickly overheated, and the cable became melted to both the charger and the battery. The charger eventually shut off, but left my living room filled with the smell of smoke and burning plastic. 

If the charger had not turned off as quickly as it did, the battery could have easily exploded, as it contains a Lithium Ion battery pack. 

I feel the modification of an industry standard cable connector type for this function is highly dangerous and inadequate safeguards are built into the product.
justification: The cable's modified design led to a short circuit, causing overheating and smoke, posing a high likelihood of future incidents.

incident_description:
Purchased HP Pavilion from Sam's Club approximately a year ago. 

A few months ago, I began noticing that once the computer became fully charged, the AC power adapter (black box) would suddenly get very hot and a repeating popping/clicking noise could be heard from the black box. It would stop once it was unplugged from the computer. Sometimes, once charged, the computer's fan would come on (high) and the computer would run very hot. These issues, too, would stop when I unplugged from the AC power adapter/AC power cord from the computer. 

The model number for the AC power adapter is 740015-002. The model number for the AC power cord is LS-18M.

The AC power adapter and the connecting AC power cord were always, when used, plugged into a surge protector.

The last time the computer reached 100% charged, all issues happened (popping/cracking noise, hot AC power adapter, hot computer/fan coming on). At that point, the HP laptop's screen went black while the keyboard stayed lit. I immediately unplugged the power cord from the computer and then from the wall. I also forced a power down of the computer. The AC adapter has a slight burn smell.

The computer powered up successfully, after a very long restart cycle. The computer seemed to be fine (although in trying to research the problem, the battery ended up being drained so full testing could not be done). The AC adapter and AC power cord are dead.

Reported the issue to multiple HP representatives. I was told only [REDACTED] has been recalled so I would have to buy new parts if I want to use the computer. It has cost me over $100 to get the two replacement parts.

Was a big fan of HP until now.
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the incident resulted in significant property damage (destruction of AC adapter and power cord), and the likelihood of recurrence is high given the persistent issues.

incident_description: I wore a FitBit Flex fitness tracker for almost a year with no incident whatsoever.  Then in June 2015, I "upgraded" to a FitBit Charge HR fitness tracker for the continuous heart rate monitoring.  After about 4 months of wearing the Charge HR 24/7, I got an electric shock while wearing it - just walking across a friend's driveway.  (Not near water or any other electrical devices).  It sent a shooting, painful electric shock down to my fingers and up to my elbow.  It was painful enough that I doubled over, grabbed my arm and said, "oh my god, what the hell was that?"  I took my Charge off and noticed a red, swollen lump there.  Everyone I talked to said there was no way my fitbit did that to me, and that I must have injured my arm some other way and the fitbit just irritated the injury.  (I hadn't injured my arm, and I hadn't been wearing the charge too tight).  Anyway, I discontinued using the fitbit, I went to Urgent Care - they could see the lump, swelling, and redness.  They took an x-ray - nothing.  They suggested an ultrasound to check the soft tissue, but they couldn't do the ultra sound; I would have to call my regular doctor (who couldn't see me for 2 months).  By the time I went to my regular doctor and she ordered the ultrasound, the lump and swelling was gone because I had stopped wearing the fit bit.  The shock happened in October 2015.  The ultrasound was in December 2015.  It is now April 2016, and two weeks ago I began wearing the fitbit Charge HR again.  I no longer wear it at night, however yesterday I took it off to do some dishes and realized that the lump and swelling are back!  Right under the little green light that monitors the heart rate is where my lump is.  It's about the size of a quarter in diameter and you can definitely see it when comparing it to my other wrist.  Does this sound similar to your experience?  I never wear it too tight, and I've never gotten a surface skin irritation - just the electric shock and reoccurring lump where the Charge HR is worn.
justification: The individual experienced a painful electric shock and subsequent swelling and redness on their arm, indicating an injury.

I went under the dresser to flip the power switch on the Belkin surge protector on and off to see if the surge protector had a tripped breaker, and after switching it back on, there was a loud bang and flash which scared me and also tripped my home's circuit breaker. incident_description:
Caller stated that the tablet overheated turning her 5 year old son's hand red after 10 mins, he dropped it when it became hot.  His hands were not burnt, he did not receive any first aid.  She stated that the child had used it several times since Christmas. Caller stated that she contacted the company and was hung up on 17 times.  She stated that she finally spoke to someone who advised that a manager would contact her.  She did not hear back from anyone and called again before they closed and she spoke to manager that told her that he did not work for Emerson, he worked for Telecon.  He told her that she could return it to Emerson who would send her a refurbished replacement, but could not provide an address.  


Caller stated that the tablet overheat almost burnt her when she tried to retrieve it.  She feels that this tablet is a fire hazard and should be reported.
justification: The tablet overheating and causing discomfort to a child, with potential for more serious injury, is an incident with a high likelihood of recurrence given the product's history and lack of resolution.

incident_description:
We had the mother board of a Dell XPS 9530 laptop replaced by an authorized Dell technician in January 2016. On February 27th, 2016 the laptop was being used (unplugged from AC adapter) when we noticed smoke pouring from the backside of the laptop. We turned the laptop over, and the backside of the case was so hot, it burnt my finger. In addition, we noticed the case itself starting to melt. The laptop shut itself down, but continued to melt. we removed the laptop from the house, and allowed to continue until it cooled in about 30 minutes.

I have reported the issue to Dell, with no response.
justification: Injury occurred due to heat from the laptop, and the likelihood of such an event is possible given the delay in Dell's response and the severity of the issue.

incident_description:
The consumer indicates that, on average, his daughter would use her tablet for approximately four hours daily some days 1-2 hours or even less then 1 hour. After about a week of usage, the consumer and his wife noticed that their daughter's hands and fingers had started scalding and eventually noticed she would peel pieces off of her skin. They noticed that it was due to her using her tablet.  Since the consumers took the tablet away, there is no more irritation to her hand-skin.

01/03/2016 (Approximately) - The consumer took his daughter to her Pediatrician, who informed the consumer that the state of his daughter's hands and fingers was definitely due to repeated chemical burns.  Definition: chemical burns= strong! chemical skin irritation  The Doctor prescribed a cream to be used for the following ten days to help with the healing process. The consumer indicates that he will ask for a referral to a Dermatologist. 

The consumer indicates that his daughter's hands are very wrinkled now and have many small cuts.  Subsequent to January 14, 2016 and up to the date of consumer's signature (February 19) the hands are staying wrinkled and hurting slight cuts. 

The consumer does not know if he will return his tablet as he is considering purchasing a cover for it though he will not give it back to his daughter to use. He will contact the manufacturer and proceed from there.  The device was not used since then (also not touched, the surfaces)

Possible Kindle investigation.  Kindle is left/not touched after the incident.
justification: The incident resulted in chemical burns and skin irritation, warranting a severity level of 3. The likelihood is high as the symptoms persisted and worsened over time, indicating a likely recurrence.

incident_description: APC surge protector caught fire after power outage during storm damaging computer table as well desktop computer, printer/scanner.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and while storms can cause power outages, the likelihood of a surge protector catching fire is possible but not rare or almost certain.

incident_description: On February 27th around 7:30pm I was on vacation in Cancun Mexico and was sitting in the lounge at the Grand Oasis Sens Hotel with my purse on my shoulder and the Soundlogic XL power cell exploded and burst into flames and totally destroyed my Coach purse and gave me 3 small burns on my legs.
justification: The incident resulted in minor burns, hence severity level 3. The likelihood is rated 2 as it's unlikely a power cell would randomly explode in such a manner.

incident_description:
Surge protector was plugged into outlet under my desk.  I bumped my leg up against the power cord, and the power to my computer went off.  I looked under the desk, and the surge protector was no longer plugged in.  Looking more closely, I see the power plug had partially melted and two of the prongs had broken off and were stuck in the outlet.

The melting had apparently occurred earlier, as the plug was not warm.  I did not feel the outlet to see if it was warm.

I see there is a recall on a different model surge protector from the same manufacturer (ref. http://www.cpsc.gov/en/recalls/2010/belkin-international-inc-recalls-surgemaster-surge-protectors-due-to-shock-hazard/).  Though my failed surge protector is a different model, the "plug" looks identical to that of the above mentioned recall -- and it is the plug that failed in both case.

I have uploaded photos from my incident.  You can view them here:  [REDACTED]

Seems to me like any and all products using that sort of plug should have been recalled.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the incident involved a potential shock hazard due to a melted power plug, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
TV in use was a Coby TF-DVD1993.  This was the property of a resident of our nursing home. It was mounted from the ceiling, as are all tv's in hospitals/nursing homes.  Approximately 6:05 am, the tv combusted.  Smoke filled the room, flames started to come from the tv, which then melted the outlet directly above that it plugs into (tripping the breaker).  The residents were evacuated immediately and the fire was neutralized with an extinguisher by our staff, and the Fire Department responded to our alarm to assure it was safe and fully extinguished.  Luckily no injuries were reported.  The staff member that extinguished the flame did request to get a respiratory exam as he had a previous condition and wanted to assure there was no damage from smoke inhalation. 

The entire top of the tv is melted and burned.  The outlet is scorched, but there is no fire damage within the electrical box, or above the drywall, so it is very clear the fire began within the tv set itself.
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the incident involved a fire in a nursing home, which could have caused serious harm if not quickly extinguished.

incident_description: The product is SONY LCD Projection TV Model KDF-42WE655 purchased around 2004. The lamp got burnt out withing two years and was replaced. The bulb again burnt out in Dec 2015. When I tried to remove the burnt lamp I saw that the door where the lamp was cased had some warping and heating signs.
justification: While no injuries were reported, the incident of the lamp burning out twice and causing warping and heating signs on the door is concerning and could potentially lead to more serious issues.

incident_description: My husband was working out wearing his Monster Adistar Wireless headphones when he heard a crackling noise.  He thought maybe they were losing their charge.  So when he got home he started charging them like he always has.  He estimates about an hour later he went into the room where they were charging and smelled something burning.  That's when he looked at the headphones and they had melted and burned at the part that controls the on/off and volume..
justification: The headphones malfunctioned and caught fire, causing property damage but no injuries.

incident_description: On February 14, 2016 Supco SCM150 Type2 SPD surge protection unit installed by Chas Roberts Co. onto subpanel of A/C unit malfunctioned and caught fire.  Supco unit made several loud tapping noises then caught fire and melted.  Fire Department responded & monitored to ensure fire not spreading to internal walls of home.  Side of house (synthetic stucco) damaged by smoke from fire.  FD stated cause was Supco unit.  Electrician responded to evaluate damage, restore power, ensure safety of house, and document.  Chas Roberts HVAC Co. called.  Stated sending someone for ÃÂfire inspectionÃÂ, but instead, regular technician responded.  Technician removed faulty/burned Supco unit and tried to sell and install a different model unit.  Technician stated they were aware of recall of  Supco units by the company 4 months ago, but it was ÃÂunofficialÃÂso Chas Roberts Co. not required to replace units they sold and installed.  Next step is to discuss incident with management level representative from Chas Roberts HVAC Co. to determine their response to my immediate incident, as well as plans for removal of the faulty Supco unit from their other installation locations.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and the likelihood of a similar event occurring is possible given the awareness of the recall but lack of official action.

incident_description: Fitbit surge causing rash
justification: The incident involves an allergic reaction to a wearable device, which is possible but not rare.

incident_description: I bought a Fitbit a year ago and I wore it for a few weeks until I developed an awful, red, itchy, blistery rash underneath it. I tried taking it off and allowing my skin to rest to no avail. I am not able to wear it looser as my wrist is big enough that I must use the largest hole on the band and it is still tight. When I let the rash heal up and then try to wear the Fitbit again I break out in the rash within hours. I have not been able to use my Fitbit at all since the rash began which makes me very unhappy as I was doing quite well with my exercise etc when I could use it.
justification: The incident resulted in a persistent, painful rash that prevented the user from wearing the Fitbit, indicating an injury.

incident_description: iphone 5c electrical ignition - child reported dropping phone a week prior to incident. on the date of the incident, she charged the phone the night before. on the date of the incident child place the iphone in an insulated lunch bag (Embark). the child dropped the bag with the phone inside and the phone immediately ignited and a flash fire occurred. there was damage to the bag and the phone was severely damaged. I conducted the investigation as a fire marshal of the [REDACTED] town fire marshals office.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and the likelihood of this occurring is possible given the combination of a potentially faulty phone and an insulated lunch bag.

incident_description: I have a 32" Samsung flat screen TV that I purchased about 3 years ago. My children were in my room watching cartoons on it but they came out telling me that something smelt really bad and they couldn't be in my room. I go into my bedroom to see smoke and sparks coming out of the back of the TV! There was no picture on the screen but sound still coming out. I unplugged it immediately! I've tried to contact Samsung and have had nothing but trouble from them! It's not like the TV just quit working but the fact that it very easily could have started a fire and who knows what else would have happened if my children wouldn't have told me about it or we were not home!
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a potential fire hazard, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' case.

incident_description: I've been using the fitbit charge HR for several weeks now, and I've started to develop a nasty rash on the inside of my wrist where the metal buckle meets the rubber. It is red and scaling, similar to other reports online.
justification: The incident involves an allergic reaction to the watch, causing a rash but no serious injury.

incident_description: I purchased the iFrogz Golite Traveler from Target retail store in Millbury, MA on December 26th. The item is a 9000mAh charger for cell phones, tablets, etc. I charged the item before using it and used the charger completely (until it ran out of a charge) from Dec 26 - January 4. I then charged it again (with the included cord) and used it maybe once between January 4 and January 14. The charger remained in my work bag with the provided cord in the USB slot (ready to charge my phone). On January 14, 2016, I smelled what I thought was burning plastic on the way to work. I realized it was coming from my bag when I got to my desk, discovered that the iFrogz Golite Traveler charger cord had melted and was melting other items in my bag (I have photos over everything). There was a little bit of smoke coming from the inside of my bag when I opened it. The charging unit was extremely hot. Mind you, nothing was plugged into the charger when this all happened. This scared me because my bag could have caught on fire.
justification: The charger cord melted and caused minor damage to other items in the bag, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
Fire Marshall is filing this second report on a surge arrester.
This is the second fire incident report that this caller has reported for this model surge arrestor.  

He is reporting that the homeowners son was walking around the house when he discovered a scorch mark on his house almost three feet long.

He states that although this is the second report he has actually had five fires involving this same product.

He is asking that this model become investigated and recalled before someone is hurt seriously or potentially loses their lives.

There have been no injures as of this date.

The caller has not contacted the manufacturer.
justification: While no injuries have been reported yet, the repeated incidents involving the same product indicate a high likelihood of future incidents, warranting a severity level of 2 as no injuries have occurred so far.

incident_description:
The power bank was purchased from a vending machine, which was located inside of a restaurant.  It is battery powered and it takes 1 battery, but the consumer is not sure of the size.  The bank can be plugged into an electrical outlet and it will recharge the battery that is inside of it.

The consumer's 14 year old son placed the power bank in an open area of the headboard of his bed.  The power bank was "not" plugged into a wall outlet at the time.  The consumer is not sure how long it was there prior to the incident and nothing was connected to it at the time.

The power bank make a loud popping sound and the consumer's daughters, who were in a different room, heard the noise.  It resembled a firework sound.  The power bank began to emit smoke and sparks flew from it.  Then it caught fire.  The son ran downstairs to get his mother (the consumer).  One of the consumer's daughter grabbed a waste basket from a nearby bathroom and filled it with water.  Then she and the consumer threw the water onto the power back.  There was charring to the headboard of the bed.  The consumer said that approximately 90% of the power bank is burned and discolored.  A spark flew onto the son's arm, but thankfully, he was not injured.

*  The consumer noted that was no information included with the product's package about potential hazards or overcharging the product.

The consumer has been attempting to locate contact information for the manufacturer, but since the product was made in China, it has been difficult.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident resulted in significant property damage and could have potentially caused harm.

incident_description: The Supco SCM150 Surge Arrestor exploded and caught the side of the house on fire damaging the vinyl siding the under layment and the heat pump it was supposed to protect.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and while it's possible for such an event to occur, it's not common.

incident_description: On January 18, 2016 my husband  was in our basement and was preparing to change our car's head light.  He was about to use a flashlight with a lithium ion rechargeable battery that is intended to be worn on one's head.  As my husband was lifting the flashlight to his head he turned on the flashlight and the battery exploded.  The explosion sounded like a bomb.  I was upstairs with my children and thought the noise was one of our basement windows shattering.  I came down to investigate what happened and saw my husband in shock and complaining of ear pain and grabbing his chest.  He had a burn on his chest; the chemicals had gone through his shirt.  Scattered on the basement floor and carpeting were tiny remnants of the battery.  There was a strong odor in the basement.  I contacted the fire department and they removed the pieces of the flashlight and battery.   They took up our carpet and removed it from the basement.  The fire department sent emergency medical staff who advised my husband to go the emergency room.  I brought my husband to the emergency room and he had a chest x ray and his ears examined.  My husband's chest x ray was negative but he was having ringing in his ears.    My husband visited an ear nose and throat physician assistant who ordered a hearing test.  The hearing test results showed considerable hearing loss in my husband's left ear. The physician assistant prescribed oral steroids to my husband and advised him to come back for a follow up appointment in two weeks.  My husband is still having hearing loss in his left ear, ringing in the left ear ,sensitivity to loud noises and generalized headaches.
justification: Injury occurred (hearing loss, ear pain, chest burn) but no death, and likelihood of occurrence is possible given the battery's volatile nature.

incident_description:
The surge protector was installed by her heating and cooling company when her AC unit was installed about 5 years ago. 

The consumer stated that she walked out into her yard and noticed burn mark on a wall adjacent to the electrical box. The height of the burn mark was 12-20 inches. The consumer noticed trail of soot. 

The consumer contacted her electrician immediately. The electrician came out and informed the consumer that the surge protector somehow caught on fire.

The consumer contacted the fire marshall. When the fire marshall came out, he informed the consumer that he has investigated 5-6 identical incidents with this product. He informed the consumer that these surge protectors are not supposed to be used outside. He stated that all of the incidents that he investigated with this product occurred when the product was outside in extreme heat.

The fire marshall informed the consumer that the scorch mark on the side of her house probably occurred because there were flames when the fire occurred.

The electrician disconnected the surge protector.

The consumer stated that there are no warnings on the surge protector that informs the users to not use the product outside.
justification: No injuries or deaths reported, but the incident caused property damage and has occurred multiple times with the same product under similar conditions.

incident_description:
I have/had a APC battery backup 500 ES
Model BE500
Serial # JB0304010587
Today I was sitting at my desk and the lights on my desk started to flicker and I smelled something burning.
Turns out that the plastic on the bottom of the unit just about below where the power switch is on the top started melting.

I sent an email to APC and they say they will reply within I believe it was 24 hours.

Anyway, thought I would let you know as I believe this could have caused a fire had I not been sitting there.

Thanks
[REDACTED]
justification: Potential fire hazard due to melting plastic, but no injury or damage reported.

incident_description: My Fit Bit Flex has given me terrible rashes and burns. I do not wear it while working out, just during daily use in my office job. I do not let lotion, water or soap get under it so I'm not sure why it would be causing this. I took the Fit Bit off for over a week and the burns didn't get any better, they are bad enough to need medication/ointment. This is terribly disappointing and will probably leave red scarred areas for life.
justification: The incident resulted in severe skin burns and rashes requiring medication, classifying it as an injury (severity level 3). The likelihood is high as the user experienced this issue despite taking precautions, indicating a possible design or material flaw (likelihood 4).

incident_description: After wearing the Fitbit Charge for 28 days, I have developed a rash.  After seeing the start of the rash after 14 days, I switched off wrists Now both wrists have a rash.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (rash) but no serious harm, and its occurrence is possible based on the user's experience with the product.

incident_description: Began using FitBit day after Christmas and wore it on my left wrist for a month (removed when showering).  I have developed a sharp pain in my left wrist and it now travels to my thumb.  I never had a pain in my wrist until now.  Went to an orthopedic surgeon this week and he stated that it may be arthritis?  I am 49 healthy female with new pain in left wrist.  I attribute to wearing the fitbit.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (sharp pain and travel to thumb) and the likelihood is high as the pain started soon after using the FitBit and was confirmed by a medical professional.

incident_description: After several weeks of use, I developed a red ras on my wrists where the fit bit was. I moved the Fitbit to the other wrtist. The first went away in some days while a new one appeared on the new wrist.
justification: Skin irritation (rash) occurred but no injury or death.

incident_description: Red rash on wrist that began approximately 3 months after beginning to wear the fitbit.  I took the product off and kept it off for 2 months after a reoccurring rash each time I would put it on.  I put the fitbit back on yesterday afternoon and wore it throughout the rest of the day.  I wore it over night and when I woke up, I noticed that my wrist was red and irritated.  I took the fitbit off this morning and over the next 4 hours the redness on my wrist continued and a rectangle shaped blister formed on the top side of my wrist, in the spot of where my battery was.  The blister has remained on my wrist with a  burning sensation.  I've washed the area with soap and water, but the blister and irritation has continued.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (blister and irritation) and the likelihood of occurrence is high as it happened repeatedly despite taking precautions.

incident_description:
ATT Uverse receiver sparking, arching melting HDMI chord between tv set and receiver.
My Uverse television had not been working properly for a week or so requiring a re-boot each new session.  Friday, Jan. 22nd in the re-boot process, the receiver began to smell like burning electric.  When rebooting, the wall outlet blew out and the HDMI cables began to smolder.  Booting again, the HDMI chord began to arch and spark so I turned off the set and unplugged.  Contacted ATT customer service who spent 45 minutes on the phone before sending out a tech the following morning.  The tech installed a new VIP2250 receiver but could not get to television set to turn on.  He also showed how the HDMI chord between the tv and receiver had melted.  He called his supervisor who acknowledged the situation and informed me that ATT claims office would be in contact to reimburse me for the damaged television and electrical.

The claims office has never called, and repeated calls to the supervisor have been unreturned.
justification: While no injuries were reported, the incident caused significant property damage, including a melted HDMI chord and potentially a damaged television.

incident_description: I purchase Beats Powerbeats Wireless In-Ear Headphones from apple and the material off the ear piece rubber peeled off and the hard metal part inside was exposed and that cause a scratch in the back of my ear it is a really sharp and I believe this is might be a hazard and I have pictures for that effective product I did informed Apple customer service about the incidents.
justification: The exposed metal part of the headphones caused a scratch on the user's ear, resulting in an injury.

incident_description:
Product is an [REDACTED]. It has an enclosed battery pack, powered by 3 AA batteries, powering a small LED light on the desk. 

Child had the device on her lap when it started to heat up and burn her leg. I opened the unit to find the battery compartment melted. The 3 batteries were all new Duracell batteries and only had surface damage from the heat, ruling out a failure on the batteries. 

Found the import tag inside. Contacted that company, and they deny the item was imported by their company. The say it is 100% fraud. 

The item was sold by Kohl's, a national department store. Likely in mass quantities in the Fall of 2015.
justification: Child suffered burns from a product malfunction, indicating a possible design or manufacturing defect.

incident_description: My Vizio TV model(E320VA) caught on fire setti g of the smoke detectors upstairs. By the time I got to the top of the steps the whole upstairs was filled with black smoke. I could see fire in our children's bedroom. I entered the room and the flames were about 2 - 3 feet above the TV. I unplugged the TV and proceeded to put it out. Fire department was called. By the time they arrived the fire was out but the whole house was filled with black smoke. The fire department clear the smoke and checked for hotspots. After doing so they got the TV out of the house and inspected it. After inspection it was determined that the fire started inside, back of the TV around the powe the power supply. Fire Department also inspected the surge protector that the TV was plugged into and was still in good working condition.
justification: Injury occurred due to smoke inhalation, and fire was about to spread to other rooms.

incident_description: Vizio flat screen TV  model # E43-C2 turned itself on and started on fire.
justification: While no injuries were reported, the TV spontaneously combusting is a significant incident, and similar incidents have occurred with other electronics.

incident_description:
Caller stated that while he was charging his cell phone the charging port got extremely hot and started to melt.  The phone was charging for a couple of hours.

(7/2015) The manufacturer was contacted and he was informed that they had not received the phone for inspection.  He stated that he had returned it to his provider but the manufactured advised that they were not in receipt of it.

Caller stated that if he had not been present this could have caused a house fire.

Burned finger when picked up phone.
justification: Injury occurred (burned finger) and the incident had the potential to cause a house fire.

incident_description:
The battery for the cordless drill was in the charger and had begun to smoke and melt without tripping the breaker of the surge protector it was plugged into.  The surge protector is plugged into a 110V outlet.

If not noticed, it would certainly have caught fire thereby setting the garage/house on fire.   There was not a power surge or other electrical incident to precipitate an over-charge condition.
justification: The incident could have led to a house fire if not noticed, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description: On February 5, 2016 about 10:30 pm I was watching tv and noticed a bright light in the lower left corner of my Samsung Smart tv, as I watched it got bigger and then a red spot appeared and it grew bigger also.  I went to the tv and saw that it was actually on fire and immediately unplugged it.  The frame and the screen were actually melted and very hot.  I purchased the Samsung Smart HDTV Model UN50F5500AF in June of 2014.  I believe this is a very serious safety hazard and that if I had not unplugged it, a serious fire would have resulted. I have reported this to Samsung today and am waiting to hear back from them.
justification: The TV catching fire poses a significant risk, though it's not likely to happen frequently.

incident_description: I started wearing the Fitbit charge HR and developed a rash/burn  on my left wrist.
justification: The incident resulted in a rash/burn, but no injury or death, and similar incidents with wearable devices are possible but not common.

incident_description: My Nokia phone charger was plugged into a wall outlet. The phone was not connected. Somehow the charger started a fire in my home. The box section was melted on the side where it had started the fire.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident resulted in property damage, hence severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 3 as it's possible but not common for a charger to start a fire without being connected.

incident_description: This product caused a chemical burn on my wrists so badly it's now peeling. Some say it is a rash but rashes are not Burns. When someone saw they even asked me how I burned my wrist in the weird pattern that matched the wrist band. I contacted the company but have not heard back yet. There are already lawsuits existing over this issue.
justification: The incident resulted in a chemical burn, causing skin peeling and a distinctive pattern matching the product's wristband, indicating a likely recurring issue.

incident_description: I have only had my fitbit charge hr for 6 weeks when I noticed a nasty rash all around my wrist. I cleaned the fitbit as recommended.
justification: The rash around the wrist indicates an incident, but no injury is mentioned, making it a level 2 severity. The occurrence is possible but not certain, hence a likelihood of 3.

incident_description: I received a FitBit Charge HR. After wearing for a few days, I noticed my wrist itching and a red rash around my wrist. I cleaned the band, switched wrists and same thing occurred after a few days.
justification: The incident resulted in a rash and itching, but no serious injury.

incident_description: I received a Fitbit for a birthday present. I was wearing the fitbit to monitor my steps and track my sleep patterns.  I have the Fitbit Flex.  I developed a rash in my wrist and my skin was also burned.  I want to make a record of this in case on have problems in the future, and if this does not clear up properly.
justification: Skin rash and burn indicate injury, though not life-threatening.

incident_description: I have been wearing my Fitbit Flex for only 4 weeks and a rash appeared on my left wrist.
justification: While not life-threatening, the rash is an adverse reaction to the device, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description: Developed a rash while wearing the FitBit Charge HR fitness tracker.  I developed a rash on my right wrist after 3 days of wear.  I followed FitBit's care and wear instructions and kept the band loose, dry, and on my left wrist.  2 days later I have a rash forming on the left wrist and the rash on the right has yet to heal.
justification: The incident resulted in skin irritation but no serious injury, and it's possible for similar incidents to occur given the widespread use of fitness trackers.

incident_description: While watching my Samsung plasma TV a short developed and kicked my breaker off. I have arc fault breaker's in my house not the old type breakers. I had very loud cracking and popping sound  and a small amount of smoke before my breaker tripped.  I contacted Samsung  about this problem I had and the safety concern I also had. Samsung  said that they were going to send an authorized repair man out to find out what the problem was at no cost to me. However the authorized repair company says I will have  to pay for the service call out and I have been going round and round with both parties with nothing getting resolved. I know this TV is out of warranty however  I am concerned about the safety issue. I am concerned if somebody had an older circuit breaker in their house this TV would have caused a fire.  I would like to report what happened to me in my TV so others can be warned also I would like to know if there have been similar problems before mine.
justification: While no injury occurred, the incident involved electrical arcing, smoke, and a safety concern, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' with a high likelihood of occurrence given the widespread use of plasma TVs and arc fault breakers.

incident_description: The product, called Native Union Jump Cable was plugged into a wall outlet in the kitchen. The [REDACTED] was not plugged into it. My dog, who was in the kitchen, saw/ smelled smoke arising from the product 10-15 minutes before I smelled smoke from another room, and started barking.This occurred at approximately 4:00 a.m. After the dog started barking, we were able to grab the product by the cord, disengage it from the wall outlet, and throw it outside on the patio. The lithium battery was melted, as was the product. Smoke was billowing out from under the cabinet. The house had to be aired out by turning on fans and opening doors. The oder was present for several days.
justification: No injuries occurred, but the incident caused significant property damage and required evacuation.

incident_description: I got a Fitbit HR for Christmas. I started wearing it everyday and after about a week I developed a rash on my wrist. incident_description:
I first bought the fitbit charge when my doctors could not provide me with a long term option to monitor my heart trends. In february of 2015 I was diagnosed with Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome. I bought the fitbit on the advice of some of my peers with the same condition and at the recommendation of my cardiologist so I could learn to recognize symptoms. In the beginning I had no problems with it. The reviews for the product was spot on, and in July the Fitbit saved me by  helping my doctors realize that I was in an autonomic crisis. This type of crisis is where things in your body that should operate automatically start to struggle to do so. I was working hard to breathe and laying down while breathing wasn't an option. Sitting up in the ER with heart palpitations confused the doctors until they brought the cardiologist to look at my fitbit read outs for the day. They started me immediately on IV Saline to help get my blood volume up as I didn't have enough to go around to all my organs to function properly. I am thankful for my Fitbit and since then have been a regular wearer. However, about two to three months in I noticed slight bumps on my arm. I thought hmmm must be some atopic dermititis. Washed my fitbit with alcohol and my arm and that seems to keep it at bay. However, around thanksgiving I lost my charger and hadn't been wearing my fitbit, instead relying on an Iphone app that is just as accurate. By this time (thanksgiving) the rash had expanded to the entire site that the fitbit touched. Wasn't painful or anything, maybe occasionally itchy and seemed purely cosmetic. However, the reason I decided to write to you is many fold. One I read online that there are two causes being investigated for this, one is a nickel allergy and the other is a sweat and electrical reaction that can cause a chemical burn. The reason i am leaning towards chemical burn is that the entire time I have been wearing the band I am on 10mg of Zyrtec once a day that takes care of any allergies I have, including skin ones. Also during the weekly cleaning of my fitbit around the sensor and charging port I would have a LOT of dead skin in the nooks and crannies. I get it im human I shed, but with irritated skin I didnt think that would exactly be the case to shed what my body needs to heal. Second reason is that since I have not worn the Fitbit Charge HR for about 6 weeks now, it has taken that amount of time for any and all of the rash and bumps to subside. However, occasionally when I shower now that arm becomes extremely itchy and breaks out, as if its allergic to the water. NO WHERE ELSE does this happen and I use hypoallergenic soap. I would like to know if this is something that others have reported as a long term side effect and sadly I think I may be switching brands instead of getting a replacement charger. Overall it is an extremely helpful medical product and part of me feels I owe my life to it, but if this rash is more than just a rash, A) I have the right to know, and B) I dont want to hurt my body any more than it already has to struggle with. 

Sincerely [REDACTED]
Ehlers Danlos Type 3, Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome, Interstitial Cystitis, A-Typical Migraine, Mutliple Chemical Sensitivies (and other non chemical ones too) Patient
justification: The user developed a severe rash and itching on their arm, likely due to a chemical reaction with the Fitbit, which could lead to further skin damage or infection.

I chose to do a little research into the issue myself before replacing the phone, which is when I discovered the issue has been pretty regular in the iPhone 5.  In some cases individuals were left with burns and other injuries when the phones exploded in their pockets or leaked battery acid on them.  I then took the phone to another Apple store where there, once again, the issue was confirmed to be a swollen battery, and she urged me to replace the phone because of the dangers it posed.

I have to say that i am deeply concerned about this issue because my entire family uses these phones, including my 1 year old son who occasionally watches cartoons on the phone(s).  In my research I had come across several instances where apple had recalled other products because of a swollen battery defect, yet the iPhone 5 was never recalled.  It was obvious that Apple was aware of the issue since it had instructed its employees not to disassemble the phones because it was dangerous.  So why are they not recalling the phones to protect the users?  I am desperately searching for a resolution to this issue because I have several family members who are having similar symptoms with their iPhone 5's, and I would not like to see them get hurt.
justification: The incident involves a known defect (swollen battery) that has caused injuries in the past, posing a high likelihood of harm to users.
