12/07/2015 - The consumer went to pick up the tablet after it had been charging for approximately five or six hours. Immediately after her left and fingers came in contact with the tablet, the consumer burned them because the tablet was extremely hot. The consumer indicates that the cord charging the tablet was not at all hot. The consumer had the tablet charging up against a wall, which she states was extremely hot as well. When the consumer turned on the tablet, she noticed there was a large, black circle larger than a nickel but smaller than a quarter on the tablet's screen.

The consumer proceeded to unplug the tablet and turn it off. The consumer states that the tablet stayed hot approximately eight hours until it finally cooled off. The consumer tried turning the tablet back on and it would not. She tried charging the tablet but it will not charge however, it is getting hot once again. The consumer indicates that it is only the half of the tablet where the black circle was that is extremely hot, stating that the other half is cool. 

The consumer believes this product poses a safety hazard to consumers.
justification: The incident resulted in burns to the consumer's fingers, indicating an injury (severity level 3). The detailed description and repeated issues suggest a high likelihood of occurrence (4).

incident_description: I have a Samsung Galaxy S4.  The model number is SPH-L720.  This phone is approximately two years old.  The battery that came with it was not performing well or keeping a charge so I removed it from the phone and put it in the box that the phone came in.  I was using an extended battery in the phone for the past 5 months.  When I went to retrieve the battery from the box in my desk drawer I found that the battery was expanding and swollen to the point that it could burst at any moment.  It hasn't exploded or caught fire yet but I think that is only because I had stopped using it.
justification: The battery's expansion and swelling pose a high likelihood of explosion or fire, although no incident has occurred yet.

incident_description: On the night of December 25th, 2015, my wife's Nuvision tablet (Model #TM785M3) was in her bedside table and completely powered off.  There was nothing on top of it and it had approximately 2 inches of clearance from the top of the drawer.  We have a thermometer in our room and the temperature was constant between 72 and 74 degrees.  This morning (December 26th, 2015) I opened the drawer to find that it had exploded.  There were glass shards embedded in the protective case, and when we opened the case, it continued to bulge and split apart and there was a very clear chemical smell.  We quickly took pictures of it and then threw it away outside.  I have sent the pictures to Nuvision and reported the problem and am still waiting for a response.
justification: The tablet exploded, causing property damage but no injuries, and the likelihood of such an event is possible given the unusual circumstances.

incident_description:
The consumer states the device is supposed to call Great Call when the person wearing the device falls on the floor but on 5/1/15 (approximately) the consumer's husband fell and the device did not alert anyone. The consumer was in the house and heard her husband fall. When the consumer checked the device she noticed the device did not have battery. The consumer contacted the firm to inform them of the incident and the rep (name unknown) told the consumer that a technician will call her back. The consumer never received a call so she continued to call the firm about the issue and every time she was told that a technician would call her back but she would never get a call back. 

On 6/1/15 (approximately) the consumer called and spoke with a technician (name unknown) who informed her that the device exhausts the battery within 2-4 hours and that when the battery dies it will not detect a fall. The consumer was told she should turn off the fall detection feature when possible. 

The consumer contacted Amazon to return the device but she was told that she could not return it since it was past 30 days of her purchase date. On 9/27/15 the consumer contacted Walmart and informed them about the hazard with the device. The consumer was told she could return the device to Walmart. 

The consumer believes the device is dangerous and could cause someone to lose their life by failing to detect a fall. The consumer is upset that the firm falsely advertised the product.

The consumer has been receiving nasty calls from a bill collector from Great Call.  He wants her to pay another 24.50.  The consumer asked if he had all the notes on the account.  He indicated he did and the consumer said it was very clear that she had over paid.  Has called 3 more times!
justification: The device failed to alert anyone during a fall, leading to a near-miss incident but no injury.

incident_description: I bought a 710T GS3. My phone is getting unbelievable hot so hot can't hold it after 15 minutes of talk time. Just the other day i had it in my pocket it was so hot it was burning my leg. My phone got so hot start somking. Then the system crashed.
justification: Phone overheating to the point of causing burns and smoke, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: While plugging an AC power cord into an energized multiple outlet strip there was a brief flash, sparks, smoke, and a circuit breaker popped. No injuries.
justification: Although there was a flash, sparks, and smoke, no injuries were reported.

incident_description: In August this year I purchased a Fitbit Surge.  I've been using it regularly, especially when working out or running.  Within the last month I've started getting really bad rashes that look a lot like chemical burns.  At first I thought it was a fungus and began a meticulous daily cleaning regimen of the Fitbit Surge.  Despite this cleaning regimen the rashes return within a day of wearing the device again.  These rashes take days to heal effectively making the device unwearable.  I'm concerned about the source of these rashes/burns and hopefully something can be discovered.
justification: The user has experienced persistent, painful rashes, likely caused by the Fitbit Surge, making it unwearable.

incident_description: Purchased a Fitbit HR about 4 weeks ago.  During the first week of wearing it I developed a severe rash on my wrist.  I tried alternating wrist and now I have this severe, blistering rash on both wrists.
justification: Severe rash and blisters indicate injury, and the rapid onset after wearing the Fitbit HR suggests a likely allergic reaction.

incident_description: Samsung S4 phone short-circuited while plugged in to charge overnight, melting/scorching the end of the charging cord and the input connection on the phone.
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the incident resulted in property damage (melting/scorching of the charging cord and phone input connection), warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description: My daughter was using the cloth cord earbuds when she heard a pop. The earbuds had shocked her and it burned her ear
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (burned ear) due to an electrical shock from earbuds, which is a possible occurrence.

incident_description: While watching my coby TV it caught fire.
justification: The incident involved a TV catching fire, which is possible but not rare or certain.

incident_description: An iPhone 3Gs that was used periodically after heavy daily use for 4 years was found to have expanded due to battery failure, splitting the phone open.
justification: The incident involved a physical malfunction (battery failure) but no injuries, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' scenario. The likelihood is 'possible' as battery failures can occur due to age and usage patterns.

incident_description:
I am attaching a copy and paste of 2 emails I sent to [REDACTED] at [REDACTED]. I did not know that there had already been a recall of this item until yesterday but still find it deeply concerning that they do not even have to courtesy to reply.

Upon closer inspection, it appeared as if the Jumpstart had popped/burst, which ignited the carrying case. I do have pictures that I will send later and a report from the fire department it needed. If there is not a safety recall on this product there needs to be a an alert regarding this issue. We were lucky that we had a smoke detector. Follow up email sent on December 15, 2015:

"This is a copy and paste of an email I sent on December 12, 2015:

On Thursday, December 10, at approximately 9:00 p.m., I placed my Jump and Go on the household charger. I was awoken by my smoke detector at around 3:00 a.m. Friday morning. I found the Jump and Go carrying case on fire that was about 6 inches away from the Jumpstart. Upon closer inspection, it appeared as if the Jumpstart had popped/burst, which ignited the carrying case. I do have pictures that I will send later and a report from the fire department it needed. 'I find it very disturbing the lack of concern that Whistler has for a situation, caused by one of their products, that could have been lethal. [REDACTED]

incident_description: While my Lenovo Thinkpad T61 was charging, I noticed the battery was swelling so I removed it and put it where it won't burn anything. The FRU P/N 42T5264 and ASM P/N 42T5265
justification: Potential fire hazard due to battery swelling, but no injury or damage reported.

incident_description: "Good Choice" brand 6-outlet power strip purchased from Family Dollar in Mount Jackson VA on 12/9/15.  The receptacles are faulty.  Plugs fit very loosely and arc when plugged in.  The plug fits so loosely that it falls out unless the receptable is in a prone position.  I reported this to the store while returning the product and was informed that Family Dollar will not report this to the manufacturer but rather that I should.  Do they not accept any responsibility for consumer safety for the products they sell?
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the power strip's faulty receptacles pose a risk of electrical shock or fire, making it an incident with possible occurrence.

incident_description:
Starting in September 2015 I noticed the skin that is under the FitBit Flex I have to start turning red.  I thought nothing of it at first but it persisted and started to hurt and get raw.

I stopped wearing the FitBit for almost 6 weeks.  The rash went away.  I put it back on and the rash appeared within one day.  FitBit stated it likely needed to be cleaned.  I did this.  The rash is still there and it is red, inflamed, itchy, and a little painful 4 days after taking the monitor off.

A dirty band is not the issue.  Something is in the product or something is reacting to the monitor itself which is causing this rash.
justification: The persistent rash, itching, and pain indicate an injury (severity level 3), and the recurrence despite cleaning suggests a high likelihood of occurrence (4).

incident_description: After wearing my Firbit Charge HR I deleveloped a rash and scabbing with peeling
justification: Skin irritation and scabbing indicate an injury, and while not rare, it's unlikely to be caused by a Fitbit under normal use.

incident_description:
After 8 months of being fine my firbit charge HR has started burning my skin. I have always taken the following steps to ensure good hygeine and to avoid irritation
- I keep my charger in the bathroom, so I remove the tracker and place it on charge while I take a shower. During my shower I always pay attention to appropriately clean the area my tracker is worn.
- After my shower I remove the tracker from charge and wipe it down then let it sit on the bench to air while I get dressed
- I then put the tracker back on
- I wear my tracker as per the fitbit recommendations, one fingerspace about my wrist bone as tight as I would wear a regular watch for day-to-day use, I shift it slightly higher and tighter during exercise, and at bed time I loosen it right off so that it can move freely 
- After exercise I follow the shower routine above.

I only burn directly beneath the charging port on the tracker. I have no irritation anywhere else on my skin from the band or heart rate monitor. I am concerned that the battery may be leaking current?

Fitbit responded to my concerns stating that I was to destroy the tracker and send them a photo of this along with my case details, being in another country I would receive a wire transfer refund in 3-5 working weeks. 

To me, this is not acceptable. They're asking me to destroy the tracker and wait over a month for my money back. They would not hear my concerns regardining the type of irritation I was experiencing and just put it down to my poor hygeine however I know I take the appropriate steps to keep myself and my tracker clean. A new burn starts with two perfect dots in exactly the spot the charging port touches.

I have tried covering the charging port with a plaster and while it helps, I still get burnt. 

This needs to be investigated, particularly as fitbit are not interested in my issue or my health or safety.
justification: User experienced skin burns, likely due to a hardware defect in the Fitbit Charge HR, despite proper hygiene and usage.

incident_description: Alcatel onetouch conquest cell phone overheats when running apps such as games and when it is on charge. It gets hot enough to potentially burn someone or start a fire.
justification: The phone overheating to the point of causing burns or a fire is a likely event given the description of it happening frequently while using apps or charging.

incident_description: I purchase a JVC 42 inch flat panel television, model # EM42FTR, serial # TA1DEH04001730. There is a recall notice for the neck cracking.  My TV the neck cracked, TV fell on my son as he was trying to move it.  I called the number for the recall and was informed that it is out of warranty.  I do not understand how a defective product, that they have admitted is defective, can be out of warranty.  The first person I spoke with when I told her I did not understand and could I speak to a manager hung up on me.  The next person, basically told me, nothing he could do and gave me the number to parts for JVC.  So I ordered a new neck which is costing me $34.24 with tax and shipping.  I feel that since they know their product is defective and the recall did not have an expiration date and should not have an expiration date, that they should have shipped me the part at no cost.
justification: The incident resulted in no physical harm, but the likelihood of a similar incident occurring due to the known defect is possible.

incident_description: I was given a Fitbit Charge as a gift for Mother's Day 2015.  I wore it intermittently throughout the summer.  But in September 2015 I started wearing it more.  In October I started wearing it 24/7, mainly to keep track of my sleep.  Then on November 10, I notice the beginning of a rash on my arm, about one to two inches above my left wrist.  It was blistery, red and very itchy.  I applied Cortisone for the next several days but the rash remained.  On November 14 I saw a doctor who told me it was Contact Dermatitis and he gave me steroid cream to apply.  By November 17, the rash was redder, itchier, and not much better.  I had been continuing to wear the Fitbit through all of this.  I finally went online and googled rash.  Immediately, Fitbit rash came up and I realized that the rash was probably from the Fitbit.  I took it off my left wrist at that time.  Still not realizing the extent that  the Fitbit was causing the rash, I wore it the next day for about one hour on my right wrist.  Immediately another rash started-mostly now on my right arm and a little more on my left arm .  This time it was spread out more, still itchy and more scaly.  I then took it off completely.  A few days later, I tried just putting the Fitbit in my pocket.  But again, more of the rash showed up on my arms.  I then stopped wearing it altogether.  I called the company and they have offered to refund me the cost of the Fitbit after I return it to them.  It has been over a week with absolutely no Fitbit wearing and the rash is finally going away.
justification: The individual experienced a severe allergic reaction to the Fitbit, resulting in a persistent and worsening rash, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description: Cable charger caught on fire while being plugged into the car AC outlet.  I noticed a burning smell from inside my car and the charger was sparking.
justification: No injuries reported, but the incident could have caused property damage.

incident_description:
Baby Monitor has rechargeable lion battery that has expanded {blown up/out} twice. Purchased from 
Amazon battery blow out panel as expanded. Returned and second one did the same. DANGEROUS BATTERIES!
justification: Battery explosions pose a high likelihood of causing injury or property damage.

incident_description: Vizio 39" fell off of tv stand while I was sitting on the sofa watching a movie
justification: The TV falling off the stand is an incident but unlikely to cause injury as the individual was sitting on the sofa.

incident_description: I have a fit bit and now have a rash burn in a rectangular design that is right under the band.  I asked some friends that have them also if the same thing has happened to them.  Several of them said yes and one posted this link where I can send a consumer report in on this.  It looks like there was a recall but I never received any information from Fit Bit on that.  It is red and hurts and will probably need to go to the doctor today.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (rash burn) and multiple friends have experienced the same issue, indicating a high likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description: Vizio TV started smelling of hot plastic, within minutes saw smoke, and bright lights, maybe sparks being produced from behind the upper right and left corners of the unit.  Turned off immediately. Model number sv370xvt and serial number LPPFMAK3800933. Please advise.
justification: Smoke and potential sparks indicate a fire hazard, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: I purchased a laptop PC from CyberPower PC for use by my patients.  After 3 months of use, the laptop charging port began sparking, emitted flames, and a large amount of smoke.  The laptop was charging and not powered on.  When I contacted the company, they said they did not manufacture the charging port so it was not likely included in their warranty.  I returned it at my own expense hoping they would honor their warranty on a nearly-new and rarely used computer.  After receiving it, they said it was not under warranty even though it was nearly new, but of greater concern was that they stated that a new port would also not be warrantied and since this was not a part they manufactured, they did not track dangerous performance or fire hazard from that part so they had no way to reassure me that this would not happen again.  Had we not been in the room when it happened, it could have created a deadly situation.  The manufacturer of the computer seemed completely unconcerned and would not create any sort of internal incident report since they did not make the part.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a significant fire hazard, and the manufacturer's lack of responsibility increases the likelihood of a recurrence.

incident_description: RXA 7" tablet broke because battery inside exploded into a fat pillow, breaking case open.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and while possible, it's not likely to occur frequently due to safety measures in place.

incident_description: We had a (Supco SMC150, Type 2 SPD, 120/240V 60Hz Single Phase) installed on the fuse box of our air-conditioning system. During a heavy rain the SMC150 caught fire. The fire department was called, as well as the power company and the HVAC service.
justification: Although there was an incident (fire), no injuries were reported, making it a level 2 severity. The likelihood is rated 3 as heavy rain, a common occurrence, was the trigger.

incident_description: Television broke away from stand and was damaged.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and it's possible that this could happen again due to improper securing of the television.

incident_description: APC BackUPS model BE500U serial number JB0303033833 alarm went off & as I investigated the alarm, I noticed a smell of burned/melted plastic & determined that the top of the unit was very warm to the touch. It had been in use behind my family room home entertainment center for several years. The unit was sitting on carpeted floor behind entertainment unit.  I disconnected the unit & placed it outside the house due to concern that it might catch fire. This occurred around midnight, after everyone in the house was asleep. The following morning, I inspected the unit & noted that the plastic on the outside bottom of the unit near where the power cord enters was visibly melted/deformed. I removed the bottom cover & determined that the melted area was immediately below & in contact with what appear to be 2 rectangular aluminum heat sinks on the main circuit board. Thankful that this did not occur while we were away & burn our house down.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a potential fire hazard, hence severity level 2.

incident_description:
Apple iPhone 3GS 32GB cellular telephone Model No. A1303

Non-removable Battery has expanded within the confines of the case, so much as to displace the front screen and rear cover.  Unit not longer functions and battery appears to have exploded.  I believe this unit contains a lithium battery
justification: The incident resulted in property damage (non-functional phone) but no injuries, and similar incidents involving lithium batteries are possible but not rare.

incident_description:
(10/25/2015) The consumer stated that he had the TV on the stand . He was in another room when he heard the TV fall. The consumer found the TV laying on the floor. The stand was still on the dresser. The plastic that holds the screws in the stand had broken.

(10/26/2015) The consumer contacted the company. He spoke with [REDACTED]. The consumer was advised that the unit was not under warranty.  No report was taken.

incident_description: I was using the Limefuel LP200X USB External Battery Pack when it overheated causing damage to a plastic table. This product which was purcased from Amazon has received hundreds of complains on their website. Many of these complaints have to do with faulty USB ports causing the unit to fail and in some cases overheat and catch fire bursting into flames. When I contacted this company about this device by email the said the product was discontinued. This is after they had sent me a replacement which had the exact same problem. This company claims this device is save but there are over 100 complaints on Amazon reviews saying it is unsafe and many of these show pictures of the product after melting or catching fire. Also this product and a similar one is still being sold on Amazon to this day. I have complained to Amazon to take it off their website to no avail.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and the likelihood of occurrence is high given the numerous complaints and continued sales.

incident_description: I own the Fitbit Flex. I used to wear it all the time and decided to take a break. When I put it back on a week or so later, I started developing a big, red, bumpy and extremely itchy rash around my wrist. I read online that Fitbit had said it may be from sweat, so I decided to clean it with rubbing alcohol. When I put it back on, I was still developing a big rash. It is taking over a week to clear up and I can no longer wear my fitbit. If many people have this same issue, this product should not be sold.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe rash and discomfort, preventing the user from wearing the Fitbit, indicating a significant injury.

incident_description: Fire Commander reported that a paper shredder start to burn at the Salvation Army in Norridge, IL.  He stated that the smoke detectors activated before the fire got away.
justification: Although there was a fire, it was contained before causing any injuries, hence severity level 2.

incident_description: Daughter purchased universal cell phone charger when her original which came with phone failed.  After two months use the phone plug end melted and discolored.  She had plugged it in all night to charge her phone and unplugged when she left for work. When she got to work she realized the phone had not charged.  When she arrived home she found that the phone end had melted and apparently overheated.
justification: The charger overheated and melted, causing property damage but no physical harm.

incident_description: Barnes & Noble nook was plugged in to charge. it was left plugged in for a few days. I picked it up an the nook was very hot. i turned it over and the location of the batter was so hot the plactic was melted
justification: The incident resulted in property damage (melted plastic) but no injuries, and while it's possible, it's not likely to occur frequently due to safety features in modern devices.

incident_description: The FitBit Charger HR was purchased for me as an anniversary around 8/21/15 and I received it on 8/29/15 and began to wear it on 8/31. After a few weeks of wearing the FitBit Charger HR, I began to notice that my left wrist was itching and I had red bumps under the FitBit. I cleaned it off and let it rest for an hour and also  put it on the other wrist. In the morning I would switch it back to the left wrist where it would start to itch. The red bumps looked like a rash and eventually I put some cetaphil was soap on it to stop the irritation.  It did not completely stop, so I asked my doctor at a routine visit what I could use for the itching and she recommended hydrocortisone. My skin was peeling on my left wrist for a few weeks and then it finally healed up
justification: Skin irritation and peeling, requiring medical advice, indicates an injury.

incident_description: I purchase 2 RCA 7" tablets in December 2014, model number RTC6378W2. They seem to work fine for the first 3 months. They began to not hold a charge and shut off on their own frequently. By month 7 one of them would not turn on at all. Now at 11 months after purchase, within the same week, both tablets have blown apart. It seems as though the battery inside has exploded/expanded, separating the front and back sections of the tablet. I am very displeased and concerned with the safety of this product, as these were being used by my children.
justification: The tablets exploding and separating into sections poses a potential injury risk, especially considering they were used by children.

incident_description:
I was utilizing my supplied Samsung charger to charge my Samsung Edge plus cell phone.  I reached to pick up the phone and sustained a first degree burn of my right ring finger due to excessive heat from the charger at the point of connection to the phone while on "fast charge" mode. The charger tip appears to be melting and is now brown in a spot.  The charger has a tag with the following designations: 
SAMSUNG
EP-DG925UWZ
RT1G712AS E
justification: Injury occurred due to excessive heat from the charger, indicating a possible manufacturing defect, making it a 'possible' occurrence.

incident_description:

On 10/8/15 while the consumer was charging the product she noticed flames, sparks and smoke coming from the product. The consumer states the product had been charging for about 2 hours and before the incident occurred the consumer noticed the product was halfway charged (2 of the 4 bars were green). The consumer states the product was on a desk near her laptop and papers. When the consumer's husband grabbed the product it fell on the floor, leaving burn damages to the carpet and floor. The consumer states there are also burn damages on the desk.

The consumer contact the local fire department and filed a report. 

The consumer contacted her home insurance company and she is waiting for an estimate on the damages. The insurance company has asked the consumer to send the product to them for further investigation.

The consumer noticed "Inova Mount Vernon Hospital" was on the product and contacted the hospital to notify them of the incident. The consumer spoke with the director of volunteer services,[REDACTED] . The consumer was informed that the product has been distributed by them as a promotional gift. 
 
The consumer believes the product is dangerous and noticed there were no indication of the product being UL approved.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and the likelihood of occurrence is high given the product's lack of safety certifications and the consumer's report of it charging for an extended period before the incident.

incident_description:
I have a Verizon USB wall charger for IPhone 5s. I don't remember it the charger  was bumped or just snagged in the middle of the night, but when I got up in the morning the main hub was lying on the floor. The prong portion was still in the outlet with 2 open connection tabs. I can send pictures of the charger upon request.

I don't know if it qualifies as a recall but I thought it would be best if reported.
justification: The charger detached from the wall outlet, posing a potential fire hazard but no immediate injury risk.

incident_description:
In the middle of the night we heard a loud buzz, followed by a popping sound.  Almost immediately, we could smell a smoky odor.  I got the lights on and checked behind the nightstand where we heard the sound and found this particular surge protector no longer working and smoking out of the front of the device with discoloration around the front. (see pic)

The surge protector did not have a heavy load plugged into it.  2 incandescent table lamps, an alarm clock, and my wife's heating pad.  There was no inclement weather that night.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a fire hazard due to a malfunctioning surge protector, making it an incident with no injury.

incident_description: As I was assembling the unit, a non-finished piece of plastic had a very sharp and ragged edge and it cut into my thumb. The cut is about 1/2 inch long and DID NOT require stitches, only disinfection.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury, a cut on the thumb, but did not require stitches, making it a level 3 severity. The likelihood of this occurring is possible, given the presence of sharp, unfinished plastic pieces during assembly.

incident_description:
My wife uses a Unitron uDirect 2 bluetooth device to transmit sound from the TV and her telephone to her hearing aids. The uDirect 2 is carried around her neck when she is using it.

Three weeks ago she noticed that the back cover on the device would not close. On inspection, the Lithium Polymer Battery (3.7v, 450mAh, 1.67Wh), Model AE482539P, had expanded and caused the back of the device to break open. The battery was in danger of exploding and could cause serious injury.

We took the device to Johnson Audiology in Chattanooga where she had received the device less than 2 years ago. They sent the device to Unitron but it was returned with a comment that they do not replace batteries but would sell us a new device (approx $300) or rebuild our old device (approx $150). I called Unitron and they told me they don't deal with consumers and don't sell batteries for their device.

Searching the internet for a replacement battery (<$30) I discovered that no direct replacement was available and that many others had had similar problems and at least one other person's battery had exploded. This appears to me to be a serious health and safety issue with this battery and device.
justification: The expanded battery posed a high risk of explosion and serious injury.

incident_description: My surge protector had a melt down. The back surge causes some electrical damage to some appliances, furnace, heated mattress cover, VCR/DVD Player/Recorder and the electrical wiring in my house. I have to have an electrician come to assess the full damages.
justification: While there was significant property damage, no injuries were reported.

incident_description: FitBit model Charge HR leaves half inch by half inch burn on the bottom of my wrist.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor burn, but no injury or death, and similar incidents have been reported with this device model.

incident_description:
(09/17/2015) The consumer stated that the keyboard is outgassing. The consumer stated that her eyes started to sting and she started coughing. She also became light headed.

No medical attention was required.

The consumer placed the keyboard in the window but the product still has an odor. 

(9/22/2015) The consumer contacted Apple Care (800-275-2273) and spoke with [REDACTED]. The consumer advised him of the issue. The consumer purchased an IMac computer with wireless aluminum keyboard in June 2014.  The keyboard began to disconnect from the IMac.  The consumer called Apple Care.  The consumers made some software adjustments.  They same if the keyboard continued to disconnect, the consumer should take it to the Apple Store at 67th and B'way, NYC and exchange it for free.  This the consumer did.  The next keyboard (otherwise identical to the old keyboard which did not smell) stunk. It outgassed so badly, the consumer wrote a complaint to [REDACTED], President of Apple (The reply basically said nothing that was not vague and beside the point.) and called Apple Care again to complain.  The techie who answered said he would call the store and arrange for yet another exchange for a keyboard that didn't smell, and he would like the keyboard that stunk to be forwarded by the store to Apple' tech people.  The consumer took the smelly keyboard to the Apple Store.  After 50 frustrating minutes and five clueless Apple employees later, the manager who had received the phone call from Apple Care showed up with a new keyboard.  It also outgassed.  He tried to clean the keyboard the consumer bought in with alcohol.  It still outgassed.  He said  the consumer must be allergic.  The consumer said she wasn't, and she would like the original keyboard with the disconnect problems back.  He said, "Too late, it's gone."  The consumer took the keyboard home where it has been airing on her windowsill for nearly a month.  The consumer thinks she may be able to use it soon.  The Apple Store manager said the keyboard had been tested by the EPA (in 2007?)} and passed with flying colors.  This the consumer believes since she no problem with any parts associated with her original June 2014 purchase.

The consumer also found 3 or 4 instances of people having intense reactions to this keyboard on the internet.

The parts are manufactured in the US, but assembled in China, a country that has in the past adulterated seemingly harmless products with toxic substances.

The consumer thinks Apple should replace there keyboards with those they were with the IMac in 2014.

Thank you. 
   

The consumer wanted to take the old one back. She advised him that she needed a replacement. She advised him that she would return the product to the store and pick up a new keyboard. When she went to the store to pick up the new keyboard, it had the same smell.

The consumer keep the original keyboard and placed it in the window. She is now using a different keyboard.
justification: Consumer experienced discomfort (stinging eyes, coughing, lightheadedness) due to keyboard outgassing, but no medical attention was required.

incident_description:
Verizon USB wall charger model A36-524A.

Had ipad on charge next to bed at night.  About 30 minutes later my wife and I were awakened to the sound of one of the ipads constantly receiving, losing, and then receiving power from the charger.  Charger was plugged into power strip with three other chargers one of which was the same Verizon model.  All had ipads or iphones connected.  All have been owned for at least a year.  When I touched the charger for the ipad making the noise, it was extremely hot to the point of not being able to hold it.  Covering my hand with a sock, I disconnected the charger from the surge suppressor.  No other charger was hot, and neither was the surge suppressor.
justification: The charger's extreme heat posed a high risk of burns, hence severity level 3. Its consistent malfunction indicates a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: Rash under the band of my Fitbit Charge HR
justification: The incident is an allergic reaction or irritation, not life-threatening, and has a possible chance of reoccurrence.

incident_description: I have the purple Fitbit Charge HR in size medium. The band causes a horrible rash. When I looked online, I found others with the same problem and learned that there was a lawsuit against Fitbit for this. You were supposed to have fixed this issue. It also said there was a recall, but I was never notified. I want to know how to fix this issue. If the issue cannot fixed, I would like to know why it remains on the market. I have had other trackers and have never experienced a rash. I'm also a senior in age and am not prone to rashes or allergies in general. The problem is the rash is causing scarring on my wrists. I no longer wear it to bed (although the sleep tracking was one of the important features for me), and I no longer wear it during the day. I only wear it when I purposely exercise. I even tried putting it over clothing. It is still harming my wrist. Fitbit recommends discontinuing use if a rash arises. Doesn't that defeat the purpose of the band in the first place? This is a serious problem and it is happening to thousands of people. Something needs to be done to fix this or take it off the market. The rash started shortly after purchase and has continued for the past two months. I have stopped wearing the device and I have sent an email to FitBit Customer Service. I have not heard back yet.
justification: The incident involves a physical injury (rash and scarring) caused by the product, affecting a significant number of users.

incident_description: On 10/24/15 I arrived home from a brief shopping trip to find a very strong burning electrical odor in my home.  Working smoke alarms had not activated, and there was no visible smoke, only strong odor.  Upon investigation I found a plug strip had started a small fire which had self-extinguished.  It burned/melted a hole in the carpet where it was placed.  Black smoke had emanated from the first 4 outlets of the strip.  The top back and one side of the strip melted/burned completely away.   The plug strip was plugged into a standard grounded household outlet and was switched to the off position.  It had one appliance (an iron) plugged into the device.  The device is a Tripp-Lite 6-outlet plug strip with phone line receptacles, on/off switch, and indicator light.  The UL label is visible on the device.  It carries a sticker with the number 9918APTIP7542. Other identifying information is not visible, as that portion of the device was melted/burned away.  It was rated for indoor use, which is where it was used.   Fortunately the fire did not spread beyond the device itself and the carpet and pad on which it sat.
justification: No injuries occurred, but the incident could have escalated, making it possible for future occurrences.

incident_description: I purchased and began wearing a FitBit Surge fitness tracker/wristwatch on 4 May 2015.  I wore it on my left wrist as a normal watch day and night except for bathing and charging the device.  In the morning on 14 May I noticed a red sore the size of a quarter under the wrist band keeper.  The red spot was NOT under the metal clasp for the band.  It was about 1" away and definitely under the keeper for the loose end of the band.  I covered the red sore with a large bandage and continued to wear the FitBit Surge that day.  In the morning of 15 May I took the Surge and bandage off.  By that point the injury appeared like a 2nd degree burn after the blister has "popped".  To check my concerns, I wore the FitBit on my right wrist for a short period.  Very quickly I felt a burning sensation on my right wrist so I promptly discontinued wearing the FitBit Surge entirely.  I returned it to the store.  From 15-17 May the injury on my left wrist looked like a large blister as it is peeling.  The underlying skin remained red.  As of 26 October 2015 there is still a red scar approximately the size of a quarter where the original injury occurred.
justification: The incident resulted in a second-degree burn and persistent scarring, classifying it as an injury (severity level 3), and the likelihood of occurrence is high given the user's description and the rapid onset of symptoms when the device was worn on the other wrist.

incident_description: NiCad battery charger-plug began overheating and  melting the casing when charging the proscribed NiCad battery and is an extreme fire danger. When unplugged from the wall, the plugs could be moved up and down like a loose tooth and the transformer portion was extremely hot.  I have two samples of the same model that have overheated.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage (melted casing) and posed a significant fire risk, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: Purchased a FitBit Charge HR on 5/31/2015.  I've worn the device on my left wrist daily.  In October, 2015 I noticed a raised itchy red bump under the device.  The skin on top of the bump came off and the area continues to show a dime size red rash that will not go away.  I've switched the device to the other arm.  If the right arm becomes itchy, I'll have to forget about using this tracking device.
justification: Skin irritation and rash, potentially leading to further injury if not addressed.

incident_description: As my wife, newborn baby, and I were in the living room of our home, we heard a "crack" sound from the kitchen. When I went into the kitchen to investigate, I didn't see anything that had fallen on the floor or anything that seemed like it would have caused this sound. Then we heard a loud "bang" sound, in similar sound and loudness as firecracker or .22 caliber rifle. When I looked around, I saw that a Duracell Ultra M3 9 volt battery that I had removed a few days ago from a smoke detector (due to the smoke detector beeping as an alert that the battery voltage was reduced beyond usable condition) had exploded. The battery was sitting on our wooden kitchen table, not touching anything, and when I touched it, it was not hot or even warm. One of the inner "cells" was a few inches from the battery, and another one was visibly ruptured, still within the metal casing of the battery. This was a very scary incident as we didn't know if more "cells" would erupt, and it was frightening to us as we have a newborn child, and this could have been very dangerous if the baby was nearby when this occurred.
justification: No injuries occurred, but the incident involved an explosive event in the home, posing a potential threat to the newborn.

incident_description:

I would like this complaint forwarded to the appropriate authority at Apple. They need to, at minimum, replace my iPod. The iPod was resting on my iPad, luckily it had a cover and was not damaged, except for the iPad cover which was burnt and needs to be replaced.
justification: No injuries were reported, but the incident involved a significant fire from an iPod, making it an incident with potential for injury.

Lenovo said it is not on their recall list therefore they do not cover it but it is EXTREMELY hot and has not been dropped or damaged in any way.

incident_description:
My wife pressed the power button (rocker switch) on her monitor (plugged in to the same surge protector as the computer), and immediately she heard loud cracks and saw visible smoke.  It took her several minutes to unplug the monitor (hard to reach placement).  She breathed in the smoke which was acrid (my term), in the time it took to unplug the unit.  She described the smoke as "toxic smelling."
She then woke me at 09:00 (we are both retired).  I could still smell the smoke--we open the window.

I immediately called Samsung.  This unit had been repaired before on 2-10-2011 for a power board failure, while still under warranty).  They returned my call today asking if anyone was injured.  I said I didn't know, not knowing what was in the smoke.
I said this appears to be the same problem as before; I stating it appears to be a a power board failure. 
The representative, [REDACTED] from the "Executive Customer Relations Department for Samsung in South Carolina" stated that since my unit was no longer under warranty, I would be charged to fix it.   I stated it was not fixed properly under warranty, or that inexpensive parts had been used in the repair, as again this is power board related.     I requested to speak to his supervisor.
I have a concerned for my wife's exposure to "the toxic smell" emanating from the monitor.
justification: Smoke inhalation is likely, as the victim breathed in acrid smoke for several minutes before unplugging the unit.

incident_description:
I am writing to report a problem with my FitBit Flex Fitness Tracker. I have been wearing this product for just over a month and it has burned my wrist. I take it off daily when I shower and am careful to keep it dry and to wear it loose. 

I am saddened by this as I paid approximately $100.00 for this product. I was enjoying the data and gaining more motivation in obtaining a proper sleep each night as well as striving towards a 10,000 step goal each day.

The burn on my wrist is the same size and area as the open backing space of the Fitbit unit itself. It has been three days and has not yet cleared up. 

I am now afraid to wear the unit as I do not want this burn to get worse.

I cannot seem to locate contact information at Fitbit to address this problem. It looks as if the problem is widespread among other users with the same concerns and it appears that the issue has been minimized and essentially "swept under the rug."

I would like to receive a refund and/or a solution to this problem.
justification: The user has experienced an injury (burn) due to the product, and the issue appears widespread based on user reports.

incident_description: Hi,  I'm contacting you regarding the RCA tablet, Model #RCT6378W2, that I purchased in November 2013.  It was one of the Black Friday deals. incident_description: Eagletec 40W T073 5-Port Intelligent High Speed USB Charger With Brainy Technology is the product being reported. The charger itself was so hot I had to use oven mitts to pick it up off our couch where it was sitting and luckily our couch/house didn't start on fire because we were in the room when it began smoking
justification: The charger overheating and causing a fire is a significant incident, and given the product's design and usage, it's likely to occur again.

incident_description:
My children's IdeaPlay tablet was put away in a dresser drawer in my bedroom for about 3 weeks.  When I got it out, the hard outer shell/case had burst apart due to the battery (silver, foil-packet-thing) inside of the tablet expanding and hardening.  As I mentioned, it was located in a dresser drawer in my bedroom; it was never exposed to water, freezing temperatures, or extreme heat.

Additionally, if the battery had accidentally been punctured it could result in fires and my kids could have been exposed to toxic lithium fumes!
justification: Potential injury to sanitation workers and environmental damage due to improper disposal of the battery.

incident_description: Fitbit Surge wristband causing rash, even when following the care instructions from the website.  Switching wrists cause the same outcome.

incident_description:

incident_description: My infant son got hold of the remote for our Roku 2 and was able to rip the buttons out of it and gagged on them. I was able to clear his mouth. incident_description: I have had my fit for less than a month and can no longer wear it.  I developed a rash/blister on my rash that makes it impossible for me to continue to wear it. I have had the fitbit on the other wrist for a couple of weeks and the rash has no gotten better whatsoever

The red spots appeared where the beams were emitted from the Charge. I didn't wear it for a week giving my skin a chance to heal.  that has developed just under the area were the sensors are. Is this normal? I've stopped wearing my Fitbit in hopes that it will heal but will the sores come back when I start wearing it again? I purchased a Fitbit Charge HR on February 9, 2015 and immediately began using it that day.  One morning out of the blue near the end of May 2015, I woke up with huge blotches and skin peeling on my left wrist.  I contacted Fitbit customer service and the agent basically blamed me for the product irritating me and then tried to charge me for a new band to ship to my home. I currently have photos in my cell phone of the stages of my injuries.  Unfortunately, I had just got a new job and did not have insurance so I did not seek medical care.  Also, my injuries seemed to just slightly worsen with each passing day in appearance and the skin would itch and the blotches on my wrist would look darker and got scaly.
About a little over a month later, my injuries subsided.  I still have not received a call from Fitbit concerning my injuries but did receive a "how did we do" email from Fitbit a couple of days after my initial call.
justification: Skin irritation, peeling, and itching caused by the Fitbit band, with numerous user reports confirming similar issues.

incident_description:
I purchased an Alienware MX18 R2 laptop gaming computer from Dell on 5/14/14. It came with a 1 year warranty. 

This laptop was serviced twice under warranty to replace the NVidia GTX 680M mobile graphics processor. 

On the first occasion, the unit got so hot that it cracked a 1.5" thick solid wood table top clear through, and to a length of 15". This was documented. The representative came out and replaced the main left side GPU. (It is important to note that due to an undiagnosed error, both cards were not simultaneously running as intended for several months, or I do not doubt both cards would have been overheating.) The GPU was reaching temperatures of >90C and the computer was shutting down to prevent hardware failure.

On the second occasion, the Alienware representative technician replaced both of the graphics cards due to them continuing to overheat. This was documented. The left side card was again running >90C and the computer shutting down to prevent hardware failure. When the technician left, the GPU was running >70C. I was told at this time that the cards "ran hot" but that "it should work fine now."

The last repair took place in April of 2015. In mid September of 2015, I experienced catastrophic failure of the left side NVidia GTX 680m resulting in a brief electrical fire. As this is a laptop I cannot imagine what would have been the result if it had indeed been in my lap.

If you search the net, there are multiple forums where this has been reported to be happening, the most closely matched was another Alienware Mx18 R2 computer owner who experienced the issue in mid 2014. That story is posted on Reddit; his laptop also caught fire.

I have contacted Alienware via several avenues and corporate complaints, to no avail. The same with Dell. I have also contacted Nvidia without reply to date. Alienware refuses to acknowledge that this is a known issue, and after receiving photos of my laptop responded with, and I quote "The case was escalated to our safety department. The lack of damage to the outside surface of the laptop is not consistent with the hardware catching on fire as you described. " They similarly denied the other person on Reddit's claim that his was the result of "wear and tear". They will take no responsibility.

I do not know if the fault is strictly with the GTX 680m graphics processor, or if the issue is a lack of necessary ventilation design in the MX18 R2 chassis. As we own a second MX18 R2 that contained a different graphics card, which has had no failures of any kind, I am inclined to believe it is the GTX 680m card itself, and there is a long record of reports of that card overheating to be found online. I do believe that this is a dangerous piece of equipment and should be recalled for consumer safety. 

For further information, my laptop - the unit in question - has been treated in a manner consistent with the purpose it was sold for - personal gaming. It is kept in a smoke free environment of 68F with controlled humidity, away from pets, and always used on an elevated hard non-enclosed surface for optimal cooling while in use.
justification: The laptop's overheating led to a catastrophic failure and electrical fire, posing a significant risk of injury.

incident_description:
My husband's HTC One Remix spontaneously shattered while nobody was touching it while eating at a restaurant around April 18th, 2015. He noticed the screen cracking because it was audible. Small shards of glass began shooting off the phone and the cracking continued for around 5 minutes. Both my husband and I ended up with glass slivers because of this. There were 4 people who saw this happen, including my husband and myself.
I notified HTC and sent the screen to be repaired. After 2.5 months I finally got the phone back.
Then, the phone shattered again on September 5th after being dropped. Again, the phone continued to crack for several minutes and shards began to shoot upward.
I called the HTC corporate office to report the safety concern and express my irritation that the phone didn't seem to have the shatter proof "gorilla glass". The company didn't seem to be concerned about selling an unsafe product, only that they couldn't replace my phone with a different model or repair it under warranty. I repeated multiple times that we had been injured by the shattered glass and that it was unsafe to have in a household with children. I also emailed them photos of the most recent break, but due to file size, was unable to send the video I took of the first phone shattering.
justification: Injuries occurred due to spontaneous shattering of the phone, with glass shards shooting off, and the incident repeated under similar circumstances.

incident_description:
We were using the Infant Optics DXR-5 baby monitor. The monitor was accidentally dropped approximately 2 feet onto a hardwood floor. When it was picked up the battery exploded. It started spewing smoke and gas before igniting in flames. The battery burned holes in our floor before we were able to safely get it out of the house. It also burned a hole through the trash can we used to get it outside. The floor and walls were covered in black soot and the entire upstairs of our house smelled like toxic fumes. Luckily the nursery door was closed so the baby wasn't exposed. I sincerely believe under different circumstances this could've caused a serious fire or injury. 

We contacted Infant Optics about the event. They asked us to return the monitor so they could study the problem but reported they haven't seen any other incidents like this. They sent us a new monitor, the DXR-8 as recompense. I shared concern that this could happen again and they assured me the device is manufactured using a different material and method and it wasn't a safety hazard.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident resulted in property damage and could have potentially caused a fire or injury under different circumstances.

incident_description: My family purchased the FitBit HR last June as a Fathers Day gift and after several days I noticed a rash on my wrist and didn't pay much mind to it. After another couple of days the rash turned into boils causing me to take the fitbit off. I assumed maybe something came into contact with skin under the band that caused the rash or I was wearing it too tight. The boils ended being infected and I chose to see my doctor. He informed me to put over the counter [antibiotic] and not to wear it until it cleared up. After 3 weeks it had left a small scar from the rash but I was willing to give it another chance and avoid wearing it too tight and consistently cleaning the armband in between exercises. justification: The incident resulted in infected boils and a scar, indicating injury, and the recurrence after re-use suggests a high likelihood of reoccurrence.

incident_description:
I have an uninterruptible power supply (UPS) which I recently placed back in service after being stored for a year (though I do not believe that contributes to this issue). I discovered that all the 120v power receptacles on this device have virtually no tension in the contacts for the hot and neutral conductors. In my opinion a device of sufficient current consumption plugged into this UPS could very easily cause the receptacle to overheat and potentially catch fire. An arcing condition caused by these deficient contacts would not trip the device's built-in circuit breaker, and could potentially damage the connected equipment.

Note that I do not know when the contacts begin to fail because the grounding contacts in the receptacles seem fine. The hazardous condition is masked when a plug with a ground pin is used: it gives the appearance of being secure in the receptacle.

THE CONDITION OF THIS PRODUCT IS EXTREMELY UNSAFE. THE UNSAFE CONDITION IS ALSO NOT OBVIOUS TO USERS. SUCH PRODUCTS WITH THIS CONDITION SHOULD BE REMOVED FROM SERVICE AS SOON AS POSSIBLE.
justification: The severe lack of tension in the 120v power receptacles poses a high risk of overheating and potential fire, which could lead to injury.

By April the discomfort had become too much and I found myself removing the band to relieve the burning irritation.  Upon removing and then inspecting the band I found that the metal surround the heartrate sensor had become discolored (almost corrosive) and had multiple pimples throughout the metal that were not there originally.  I contacted Microsoft support and they stated that they had no experience with this issue, so I had sent them photographs of the product.  I was surprised they had "no knowledge" of this, since there is a forum with pictures similar to my product found here, http://forums.windowscentral.com/microsoft-band/339559-microsoft-band-after-3-months-everyday-use.html .  I was sent another Microsoft band to replace this first flawed model, which arrived shortly after I sent the original in on approximately April 23, 2015.  By May 15, 2015 my replacement band had begun to pimple (pockmark, bubble, whatever you want to call it) on the same heartrate sensor metal.  This occurred within approximately 2 1/2 weeks of use.  On May 16, 2015 a service case was opened, I was told to "return the product because it is only going to get worse," so I did as directed and returned the Microsoft Band for the second time.  Shortly after returning that band I received my replacement (band #3).  I wore this band sporadically for approximately 2 weeks before the first pimple appeared and sensitivity and irritation began to occur on my wrist.  I contacted customer support, they requested photographs, which I sent on June 17.  I was again told that this is very uncommon, but that they will send me a replacement band and extend my warranty an additional ninety days and also offer me a streaming music service for 3 months to xbox music (whoop-dee-do).  So, I will be returning this third flawed band, all for the same heartrate monitor, pimpleling/irritation problem, and will move onto my fourth band as they are not offering me any alternative.  I hope that you will look into this $200 product and find that more than just myself are experiencing this issue and the product will be recalled.
justification: While no injuries were reported, the repeated incidents of product malfunction and customer dissatisfaction indicate a high likelihood of similar occurrences.

incident_description:
June 22, 2015 
Subject: Possible Problem with [REDACTED] Model No. [REDACTED] Fire Alarms and 9v Batteries 
This home was built in 2008 and First Alert Fire hard wired alarms on all three floors. Recently we purchased a 4-pack of 9v [REDACTED] batteries to have on hand and the first one used was installed about a week ago on the first floor. The alarm seemed reset properly after a test press of the test button but started intermittent alarming from then on. [REDACTED] online suggestions were tried to no avail after loss of sleep, thinking the problem was fixed. 
The new 9v battery tested good with my voltmeter. I took the alarm apart and noticed positive leaf spring was not vertical and not protruding as far as the negative. In trying to find out how the pin got bent, I also noticed the [REDACTED] negative battery spring posts was also different when compared to an Eveready Energizer I had on hand. The [REDACTED] has a square post. Having roughly measuring the 9v negative and positive post the dimensions of the [REDACTED] versus Energizer, they are about the same. 
What I learned in placing either battery in the [REDACTED] alarm was the positive and negative leaf springs are bent near the end and goes inside the battery post holes leaving the only lower one edge to touch the posts. The lower edge allows for less tension resulting in a poor contact. The bend of the leaf spring needs to be made at a lower point and possibly lengthened to make contact at both ends of the battery posts. 
My view is this is a defective product and a recall may be in order. Please notify me of your findings as I am interested in knowing what needs to be done to replace all of my alarms. 

Sincerely, 
[REDACTED] 
Phone: [REDACTED] 
Email: [REDACTED] 

Sent to: http://www.cpsc.gov/ 
Consumer Safety Product Commission 

[REDACTED]
justification: While no injuries were reported, the incident caused significant disruption and potential safety risk due to intermittent fire alarm malfunctions.

I found what appears to be an open recall on this product. We also checked my brothers pocket jump starter that was purchased at the same time and it was swelled also.

FITBIT SURGE
I PURCHASED A FITBIT SURGE SEVERAL MONTHS AGO FOR $249
WITHIN A week my wrist started to break out in a rash which led to layer of skin peeling. I switched wrists and it did the same thing

Once I remove the fit bit the rash so he healed after a few weeks and never returned.   I wear the fit bit 24/7 and the only time I took it off was when I took a shower.

incident_description: I purchased a Fitbit Surge in January 2015.  After I wore the Fitbit Surge for just 24 hours I developed what appeared to be a burn on the outer side of my wrist about the size of a quarter.  I removed the Fitbit and to allow the area to heal. Every time I wear the Fitbit the area develops. I changed wrists and it happened also.  I did what the manufacturer advised to no avail.  I continue to wear my Fitbit Surge, but I cover the area with a bandaid to prevent the skin problem.

incident_description: I am the owner of a Fitbit Charge.  I received this as a Christmas gift and wear it daily.  I have experienced rashes and blisters along my wrist on a number of occasions.  This only happens when I am wearing the device, and directly underneath it.  These rashes are usually about as large as a half dollar coin, very red, blistered and sometimes itchy.  They usually go away over a couple days and peels as it heals.  I am very concerned about why this is happening.  I won't be wearing this device anymore!  Fitbit needs to investigate this issue and correct it to ensure safe use for consumers.

incident_description: I wore my Fitbt tracker daily to log exercise, sleep and count steps. After about a month or so I got a rash on my left arm where I was wearing the band. It burned and itched and made me very uncomfortable. After a few days I removed the band and have stopped using it altogether. The rash remained for over two weeks.

incident_description: Rash/irritation on my left wrist after 5 days of use. It took 3 months for the rash to clear up completely after I discontinued skin contact.
justification: The incident resulted in a rash but no injury, and its occurrence was possible given the duration of use.

incident_description: I continuously get a red rash while wearing the Fitbit Charge product.
justification: The incident involves a non-life-threatening rash, and while it's possible, it's not certain that the Fitbit product is the cause.

incident_description: Rash from wearing fitbit, bumps, redness, pain on wrist

incident_description:
Received an upgrade from the Fitbit [REDACTED],which I use everyday for 14 months,with no reaction.
I use the Fitbit Charge HR and have received 2 cigar shaped burns on my left wrist. I only remove it for charging and while I shower. After the last burn I waited for a minimum week and the burn blistered and peeled off like a bad sunburn. It faded and after a week continued to use it and within a week the red marks were back and I decided to start to look if others were suffering like I was. I found an article on my local ABC affilate and they suggested that I should report this.

incident_description: I bought a Fitbit flex November 2014 and started wearing it on my left wrist. After about 2 weeks I notice a red raise bump the size of a nickel, with redness tissue surrounding the area. It continued to get bigger and more irritated. I stop wearing it and some of the redness went down. But after a couple of week I went to the dermatologist to have it looked at because it was still irritating. He gave me a steroid cream that I had to use for 2 weeks. It has gone down but the skin was still red and I have a small scar on my wrist. I have never showered or swam with it. I saw a piece done on the news that other people were having the same problem so this is why I am reporting it.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (skin irritation and scarring) and there are reports of similar incidents, indicating a high likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description: I received a Fitbit Surge as a gift. I have been wearing it continuously since I received except when I shower. I love having one to monitor my steps, heart rate, etc. However, I developed a rash a few days ago. I am still wearing the watch but have covered the rash with band aides. The rash has gotten worse. I love my watch but I also don't want a rash.

incident_description:
I was an avid user of the Fitbit [REDACTED] until it was recalled.  I then waited for the Fitbit Charge to come out and purchased it very shortly upon release to the public.  I had been using the Fitbit Charge for a couple months and then back in March started to feel a "zing" from the wristband.  The "zing" became more prominent and started to bother me more even after I took the Fitbit Charge off.  There was a slight raised red bump on the back of my wrist, but it was the "zings" that really hurt.  It seemed like I was getting a shock or burn every time it zinged.  The zing/burning sensation lasted a couple days and then it finally went away. I contacted FitBit support and they wrote me back and said that all their rash issues were taken care of and that I should read the "how to take care of my FitBit" and make sure I kept it clean and to try it out again.

I decided at that point that FitBit was not going to stand behind their product and just discontinued use of the product.  It's like that Pavlov Conditioning.  If I get burned and it hurts once, why would I try it again?!!

I just saw an article from 7 on Your Side in the SF Bay Area and realized that I wasn't alone in the burning sensation.
justification: User experienced painful 'zings' and burns from the Fitbit Charge, lasting for days.

incident_description:
On 5/1/15, a 10 month old baby was in his crib for a nap.  A video baby camera which was fastened to the wall was turned on.  The electrical cord for the camera was outside of the crib.  The mother held the monitor while she went in her yard with her 5 year old child. The monitor began to beep and indicated "Lost Signal."  This was the same beep sound that it makes when the battery is low or when the mother walks to the basement or mailbox. The monitor made this beeping noise for about 20 minutes.

Since the mother also had a SIDS monitor which indicated that her infant was still breathing, she was not alarmed by the video monitorÃÂs beeping sound.  When she walked into the nursery she was surprised to see that the video monitor cord was wrapped around her childÃÂs arm, chest, and neck.  The infant was taking very shallow breaths and had broken blood vessels on his face.

Immediately the mother un-wrapped the cord and the infant caught his breath.  The mother observed that her son had pulled the electrical cord out of the camera  and through the rails on the crib.

The baby was very lethargic.  He was examined in an emergency room at which time an x-ray showed that his lungs were clear.  He was diagnosed with facial petechiae from a near death experience.
justification: Injury occurred due to the baby pulling the electrical cord through the crib rails, wrapping it around his neck and chest, causing shallow breathing and facial petechiae.

incident_description: Wearing a Fitbit Surge fitness tracker, I have developed several instances of a rash where the tracker is worn on my wrist. I have followed their wearing instructions carefully to avoid this but the rash still appears.
justification: The incident resulted in a rash, but no serious injury, and its occurrence is possible given the user's careful adherence to wearing instructions.

incident_description:
This caller is reporting her Lithium Charger manufactured by manufacturer in Bentonville, Ark and purchased from retailer in Wetumpka, AL 36092 on November 28th, 2014.
Around April 15th, 2015 the caller and her husband had their charger plugged into an outlet but not charging any item.
This charger is recalled with release# 15-123.
They went out for maybe four or five hours and when they returned they first heard their smoke alarm sounding.  They entered the home to heavy gray/black smoke and black soot on the walls of kitchen.
Their Ipad had melted, picture frame had burned with glass breaking and the charger was still in flames.
The caller's husband was able to blow the charger flames out and begin opening windows and doors.
The caller states that she had to re-wash all dishes, flatware etc., she washed the walls and trim and is now in the process of re-painting the kitchen due to this incident.
There are no injuries being reported
The caller has not contacted the manufacturer but does intend to contact them.
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the incident caused significant property damage, including melting of an iPad and burning of a picture frame.

I removed it from the port and it almost blistered my fingers.  The reader now is terrible at transferring information but the card is also damaged and slower than before..

This is a dangerous product and i'm sure it would have damaged the card if let plugged in.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury, and the device's malfunction posed a risk of further damage to the card and potentially other components.

justification: The incident involves a skin rash, which is an injury but not life-threatening, and while it's possible, it's not certain that the Fitbit is the cause.

incident_description: The battery on my daughter's MacBook Pro laptap (which I bought December 2010) malfunctioned so badly that it expanded to the point where the case was forced open more than 2"inches and the trackpad destroyed.I brought into an Apple store who diagnosed this yesterday,May 21,2015.They took the battery out immediately and I was told it was put in some type of vault as a safety precaution.My wife is completely disabled, with global aphasia and wheelchair bound.If this had started a fire in our home when I was out,it would have ended in tragedy..At the Apple store i was qouted a price of $218.00 to replace the battery and trackpad which I really had a problem with.The 'expanding' battery was not caused by misuse or accidental damage but a manufacturing defect.Which then caused a perfectly fine trackpad to be ruined.If this was an issue of a 4 year old battery not holding a charge thats one thing but this was clearly a defective battery,causing a dangerous situation that could have resulted in the loss of property or even life.This is definitely a serious safety issue.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that the battery was put into the charger. The charger was plugged in and placed on a shelf in the laundry room.

The charger had been plugged in for about two hours when the consumer woke up to smoke detector in the middle of the night. The consumer stated that the laundry room was engulfed in fire and smoke. The consumer stated that he cut the circuit breaker off and threw water over the fire. The consumer and his wife moved everything that was on fire to the outside.

The consumer and his wife suffered some burns on their hands in trying to move things outside.

The consumer stated that the battery charger caught on fire. The consumer stated that other things were damaged/destroyed in the fire (cabinets, paneling, curtains, washer, dryer, clothing, iron, other 7.2V batteries, porter cable, porter cable charger with battery, extension cables, etc.). Most of the ceiling fell down and the paint was damaged. The washer and dryer turned black from the smoke.

They ventilated the area and made sure the fire had not spread to the other areas in the house. 

The consumer stated that he started the cleaning process the next day. The consumer stated that the burnt odor is still present in his home.

The consumer stated that he contacted the firm regarding this issue in April 2015 (on 04/03 or 04/06) . On the first call the consumer was informed that they would send out a replacement charger and two batteries. They were also going to replace two other 7.2V batteries. 

About two weeks ago, the consumer received a letter from the firm's attorney with a return slip to send the destroyed batteries and charger for inspection. The consumer stated that he was not asked to hold onto the product when he first contacted the firm in early April 2015. If he was informed to hold onto the product, he would not have thrown it away. The consumer notified the attorney that he no longer has the product. The consumer is waiting on a response from the firm.

The consumer stated that if the fire in the laundry room was not caught early on, the whole house could have engulfed in fire.

Could not determine whether the charger is included in recall #01-010/#01-057.

Injury information:  Slight burns on hands & arms, smoke inhalation, constant persisting cough.
justification: Injuries were sustained while attempting to extinguish the fire.

incident_description: I have a traumatic brain injury wth epilepsy from my service in Iraq. Now, I use vaporized medicine to control my seizures. I purchased a MicroG vaporizer battery from Grenco Science for a MicroG vape pen system. After using it for a couple months, an incident occurred. I pushed the button to use it, and then I released the button. But when I released the button, the light stayed on and the battery kept heating the tank. It got so hot the tank turned orange. I thought it must've been a fluke. I told Grenco Science and they sent me another one. After using the new battery for a couple months, the same thing happened except this time it burned my leg and my pants. I reported it to Grenco Science again. They offered to send me another one. I am very concerned about the danger of this product and Grenco's lack of concern for public safety. I have nothing to gain from this report (I'm already getting my money back) other than to prevent serious injury to another consumer. A more frail or less reactive person could seriously hurt themselves or start a fire with this defective product.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury, and the likelihood of recurrence is high given the repeated occurrences and the company's inadequate response.

incident_description: I would like to report a problem with my new Fitbit Charge HR fitness watch that my husband had given me for an anniversary present in April 2015.  After wearing this product for a number of days, my wrist broke out in an itchy rash.  Apparently they use nickel in their clasp and I am unfortunately allergic to nickel.  I really enjoy this product but not do not enjoy having an rash.  I wish they would create a fix for this product.  I can't believe they use nickel for a sports band.
justification: Allergic reaction to nickel in the watch clasp caused a rash, but no other injuries reported.

The next night I picked up my Kindle and saw that the side was split open from a swelling battery.  The device still works but I am afraid to recharge it because the battery is so swollen.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the incident involved a potentially hazardous battery swelling, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
This mother's day started with a boom. Literally.   Around 3 a.m. [REDACTED] and I woke up to a strange noise to discover our Summer Infant baby monitor had exploded and was on fire on our floor and a stack of papers on the desk (where it had been sitting) was also on fire.  THANK GOD we heard it. I mean, it took us about 5 seconds to wrap our head around what was happening and act...fast.  I ran to bathroom and got a towel wet and thru it on the fire. And just like that it was over.  Could've been a different scenario.  It fell right by our long curtain that covers our window/door, had that caught fire, im not sure WE would've been able to put it out. Smoke alarm went off as we were putting it out, so we definitely would have been alarmed had we NOT heard the little explosion.  There was a recall on these monitors. I have 3 emails from babys r us dating back to 2011. Apparently I read them (I have no recollection) I must've checked ours and determined ours wasn't one of the affected.  I also have an email from them in 2014 that was unopened,  guess I missed that one. So parents, check your monitors to make sure they are safe. Check your smoke alarms. Read all recalls. Our house will be getting a complete safety check. 

Meanwhile our kids slept peacefully in their beds never knowing the danger that had just occurred.  You truly never know when life is going to give you a jolt of reality.  Accidents happen to everyone.  Im beyond thankful that this story has a happy ending. Holding my precious babies a little closer today.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a fire, posing a significant risk.

incident_description: While wearing the fitbit flex activity tracker I sustained a rash to my right wrist.
