incident_description:
I wanted to tip you off to an issue I've been experiencing with my Fitbit Force. I pre-ordered a Force and received the device on November 13, and started using it immediately. I loved the device and sang its praises to friends, family, and colleagues. I loved having all of that data about my healthy (and not-so-healthy) habits.

In the last week of December, things started looking not-so-great. My girlfriend had noticed a red blotch under the device where the battery and charging port sits. After some researching, it turns out several other people have the same exact issue. The pictures looked like the same wound I have. Red, dry, scaly skin, eventually some blistering, and then peeling skin. And their wounds were also in the exact same location -- right under the battery and charging port. Of course, with the internet being the internet, users suspected it may have had something to do with making contact with the charging port, a leaky battery, or something else entirely. While researching, I took the device off of my left wrist and put it upside down on my right wrist. Sure enough, two days later, a red blotch started to appear on that wrist too in the device's range of travel under the battery and charging port.

I did end up seeking medical care for this as the wound just got worse and worse, even after a week of not wearing the device at all. The nurse practitioner that had seen me at the clinic stated it was contact dermatitis due to the device and the wound on my left wrist had also become infected and will probably scar.

I opened a case with Fitbit on December 30 requesting a return. While I had heard nothing but good things about Fitbit customer service from my colleagues, I've found it to be abysmal at best. Responses would range anywhere from one day to four days -- usually closer to the latter. They did offer to refund my money upon receiving the product, but they're not acknowledging that the Force has a design flaw while they tout the device at CES all week like nothing is wrong. I really wanted to buy into the Fitbit ecosystem and I loved the device -- before the injury -- and considering I have medical expenses resulting from treatment, and the fact that healing is slow-going and may scar me, Fitbit has done nothing to show me that they care for their customers' loyalty and I can no longer recommend any of their products due to their response (or lack thereof).

There is a rather lengthy thread on the Fitbit website about this issue where people are posting pictures and their experiences. It seems that in the past week or two activity is really picking up with more and more people having the same issue. Perhaps these were all folks that received the device as Christmas gifts or using them as part of their new year's resolutions. It's really such a shame. The thread is here, I'm not sure if you have to be a member to view it, but membership is free. 16 pages with 239 posts so far: https://community.fitbit.com/t5/Force/Fitbit-burned-arm/td-p/3661/highlight/true

I've also attached some pictures of my injuries. They are date-stamped so you'll be able to tell the progression.
justification: Multiple users have reported skin irritation and infection due to the Fitbit Force, with some cases requiring medical attention.

incident_description: As with many other people, I had a reaction to wearing the band as it was designed. While the company is refunding my money, I feel that they are downplaying how many people have had a reaction. We are all out time from work, doctor visit co-pays and prescription costs. They really should recall the device before more people go thru this ordeal.
justification: Many people have had a reaction, leading to time off work and medical expenses.

incident_description:
Purchased Fitbit Force unit in December, 2013.  One week after wearing, noticed red patch on my wrist where charging port comes in contact with skin.  Immediately stopped wearing product and did some research.  Found numerous complaints about skin reactions to product at that time.  They continue today.
Burn continued to grow for several days.  Wound up having to go to doctor and get steroid creme.  Two weeks later, still experiencing burning sensation on arm.  I am convinced that this is some kind of chemical burn.  I have never had any metal sensitivities or reactions to metal.  I have worn a stainless-steel watch almost 24/7 on the same arm for 20 years with no reaction.
This product needs to be recalled immediately.  There is a long thread on the company board with numerous complaints about this product.  Meanwhile, fitbit continues to blame the consumers for this situation.  And, they are completely inconsistent in how they are handling customer complaints.
justification: Skin reaction leading to medical intervention and persistent symptoms.

They are saying this is an allergic reaction to nickel but it appears to be coming in the spot on where you charge the device. incident_description:
The product is called the FitBit Force and it is meant to be worn 24/7 as a fitness tracker, sleep tracker and pedometer. It is worn on the wrist (mine on my left wrist) loosely, but I would take mine off to shower and do dishes. The tracker is claimed to be water resistant. It is a polymer type bracelet with a front display as well as an open charging port opposite the display on the back which directly rests on the skin near the lateral aspect of the wrist. 

Now to tell you about my reaction and why I am concerned for the safety of others;  My reaction began 9 days ago on 1/15/14 and I began wearing the force on 12/25/13.  My reaction began as a very small itchy red hive, that began to ooze clear fluid.  This bump began on the lateral side of my left wrist underneath where the charging port comes into contact with my skin.  The next morning when I woke up, the redness had increased in size to about the size of a nickel and there was a weeping area oozing clear fluid in the center.  I covered the area with some sterile gauze as I am a physician and cannot have it open in the hospital.  At this point I switched the force to my right wrist.  I notified my husband of my wound and he said it may be my force as he had just heard on the news that there were cases of allergic reactions. The next day (1/17) I noticed a red bump underneath the charging port on my right wrist.  I decided to continue to wear the band above my long sleeve shirt the remainder of the day.  During this time the rash on my left wrist became larger and was now spreading outward around my wrist and was becoming swollen with bubbling of the skin and blister like lesions.  I decided on 1/18 when I woke up and the rash had encompassed my entire left wrist to take it off of my right wrist, and at this point my right wrist lesion has also grown slightly in size.  At this point I took an antihistamine and began using hydrocortisone 1% OTC ointment as directed, 3-4 times daily.  Over the next few days, my rash grew in size, became much more swollen, began to hurt and feel tight like a bad sunburn, along with more bubbling and blistering lesions showing up.  It was difficult to sleep at night and to wear any long sleeve clothing.  When I went to a family physician on 1/20/14 to receive a steroid injection to kick start the anti-inflammatory process, the doctor was appalled at the site of my wrist and without any explanation he asked me how I had burned myself so badly and told me this appeared to be a chemical burn.  He then prescribed me a course of prophylactic antibiotics as well as [REDACTED] burn cream to apply daily.  I have also been using hydrocortisone cream as well between [REDACTED] applications.  My rash/burn has become slightly less inflamed and has stop spreading after these treatments, however, the original area of skin where the rash began on my left wrist is bubbled, thick, discolored, is insensate to touch and I am afraid these are signs that this area will be scarred.  The rash is gross, embarrassing, and in all honesty not welcome at the hospital where I spend most of my waking hours.  For someone training to be a general surgeon, I need to be scrubbing into the operating room frequently, and this rash does not allow me to do this.  Surgical scrubbing over this would be extremely painful and an open wound such as this is actually considered non-sterile and I would not be allowed into the OR.  Luckily, I am currently on a non-surgical month of my job, however, as of Feb 1st I will be expected to scrub into OR cases, and I am very nervous this will not be anywhere near to presentable for the OR in a weeks time.  I will attach pictures of the progression of my reaction below.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe skin reaction and potential scarring, affecting the individual's ability to work, with a high likelihood of similar reactions in other users given the widespread use of the product.

incident_description:
I purchased a FitBit Force in November of 2013.  I wore it continuously and developed a rash on my wrist on 1/13/14.  I moved the FitBit to the other arm and realized yesterday that the small bumps have now started forming there.  I have had this "rash" for a week and half now and it got worse and isn't appearing to get better.  I then found out many other FitBit Force owners are experiencing similar rashes.  FitBit is claiming it is an allergy to Nickel, but I have no allergies and no skin sensitivity issues.  Plus, if it was a nickel allergy, it should have produced the rash reaction within 12-48 hours... not 2 months later.  I'm hoping FitBit is doing the proper testing to see what the issue really is and not just picking the easiest "excuse."  

The next issue is that they are offering a refund or product replacement.  Great.  Until it was shown on their website message boards that they are offering different refund policies to different customers.  For instance- if you bought the Force at a retail store, you could take it back to that store to get a refund and FitBit will STILL send you a replacement item. https://community.fitbit.com/t5/Force/Fitbit-burned-arm/m-p/102981#M10588

incident_description: After using my Fitbit Force for about 2 weeks, a small red patch began to appear under the face of where the device sat on my wrist. It looked like a bug bite so I covered it with anti-itch cream and put a band-aid over it and moved my device further toward my hand. Within 2 days another red spot appeared and the original wound was becoming much larger and beginning to blister. I immediately removed the device and contacted the manufacturer who at the time down played the incident and speculated that I may have an allergy to something in their product. They offered to replace the device or refund me. I declined both tentatively until my growing injury healed entirely. Several days later the injury grew to the size of about 2.5" x 4" along my wrist. Fearing infection, I scheduled an emergency appointment with my Dermatologist. He diagnosed it as a severe case of contact dermatitis; warning that the device must have something very irritable in it. He prescribed Clobetasol Propionate Ointment to help heal the injury and recommended a product with Zinc in it to prevent scarring after the injury finally healed, but cautioned that it could take up to 8 weeks. During this whole process I joined a community discussion on Fitbit's forum only to discover that there are at least than two dozen people who have come forward (so far) with the same issue. The conversation thread is now 80 pages long with irate and injured people from this product. In reading back through other threads, the first incident appears to have surfaced back in November. I feel it was very negligent of Fitbit to keep this product on the market, especially through the holidays where an exponential number of additional people could be exposed. They risked injury in favor of profits and they provided no warnings on their product packaging to give consumers a heads up. It took until January 21st for the CEO to make a formal statement on their website (which you have to go digging to find) and three months later they are STILL speculating on what the cause is. I don't know how my injury will heal, hopefully without a scar. But Fitbit needs to assume responsibility for their negligence, stop selling this product and stop treating consumers like it is OUR fault that this happened to us. Please let me know what additional info I can provide. I have stage progression photos of my injury and can get you anything else you need to pursue this.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe case of contact dermatitis, causing significant injury and potential scarring, affecting multiple users.

incident_description:
Product: Fitbit Force (fitness device) online purchase price $129.95.  This ÃÂdefectiveÃÂ product should be recalled, consumers should receive complete refund for product and reimbursement for their medical expenses.

I purchased a Fitbit Force fitness wristband device online from the manufacturerÃÂs website (www.fitbit.com).   I received the item on December 6, 2013 and began wearing it on my left arm. On January 3, 2014 the rash on my left wrist was so severe I scheduled a doctorÃÂs visit and was diagnosed with a fungal rash and prescribed medication. However on January 5, 2014, I developed a very similar blistering, red rash on my right wrist. I was now certain the fitness device was the cause of my two rashes.

I contacted the manufacturer, Fitbit through their website.  I requested exchange of product for another model. Fitbit did agree to accept a return of my original product and replace it with another model.  They stated: ÃÂWe are sorry that you are experiencing skin irritation and for our delayed response. We want to follow up with some comments about Fitbit devices and provide some options to assist you, such as replacement of your device or refund of your purchase.

Our Force and Flex wristbands are made of a flexible, durable elastomer material similar to that used in many sports watches. They do not contain latex. The clasps and casing are made of surgical-grade stainless steel and contain traces of nickel. As with any type of jewelry, some people may experience allergies. Numerous factors can cause an allergy, such as a nickel sensitivity, reactions to bacteria that can accumulate in watch wristbands or other wearable devices, a reaction between the wristband and your soap or perspiration, or an allergy to the material of the wristband. 

While we cannot diagnose whether you are experiencing an allergic reaction, allergies may be unpredictable and cause intense responses. Allergies may result from any combination of things, including irritation over time, a reaction between a watchband and your soap or perspiration, or an allergy to the material of the watchband. Certain people may have allergies to the nickel in stainless steel or from certain type of bacteria that can accumulate in watch wristbands or other wearable devices.
In our ongoing interest in learning more about our customer experience, if you would like to help us better understand and assess your issue, you can help us by responding to following questions/items.

3. Have you had similar skin allergies or sensitivities from other bands?

4. Have you tried cleaning your Fitbit device with warm soapy water, if you think you may be subject to microbial allergies?
5. Please describe the weather conditions when the irritation occurred, including the approximate temperature and humidity.

All this stated, it looks like you purchased your Force on the Fitbit.com store. If you are interested in a full refund or a partial refund for the cost difference for a One, please let us know and we arrange this for you.ÃÂ

It should be noted I have never had an allergy to nickel, nor do I believe my burn was caused by an allergy.   I have documented pictures of my injury from use of this fitness device.  Both of my wrists are still burned and are still not completely healed.

The system operated properly & the Ethernet cable was removed as only tne WiFi functton was to be used.
On 15 November at approximately 11 AM I was using the Gateway WiFi connection with my [REDACTED] when 
the [REDACTED] reported the WiFi link was suddenly lost. I looked over at the Gateway, which was 
located on my desk about three feet from me and noticed all the panel indicator lights were off. I 
stood up to walk over to the Gateway when I heard a snapping and crackling sound and a large cloud 
of acrid white smoke emanated from it. There was a strong oder of burning electronics. I picked up 
the Gateway and saw, through a ventilation grill, small flames and/or sparks inside the plastic 
case. The case top was quite hot to the touch. I immediately disconnected the power unit from
the wall outlet, removed the phone connection, and took the Gateway outside the house. The smoke 
dissipated and the Gateway cooled off. The Gateway had been powered continuously for only about 39 hours when 
it failed. I am very concerned that this AT&T provided product could have started a fire, 
especially since it was near papers on my desk. A major conflagration could have resulted. I'm 
lucky I was home when the incident occurred.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and the likelihood of occurrence is high given the continuous use and the short time before failure.

On 15 November 2013 my 2 cell AA flashlight exploded shooting the lens and reflector out shattering the lens. Luckily no one was injured just shocked by the loud bang and flying debree. 
I believe the problem is that LEDs require far less voltage to operate than traditional light bulbs and this discharges batteries beyond the threshold of tipical ÃÂbad batteryÃÂ placing them into a unstable condition where now gasses are produced compared to older light bulbs that get to dim identifying time to replace batteries. Most flashlights are sealed to prevent moisture from entering and under these conditions the gasses have nowhere to go and Bang it explodes. 
I feel that LED flashlight need a sensor installed to prevent discharging batteries beyond there safety limits and a pressure relief valve installed to prevent dangerous gasses from building up inside the case. Or have Battery manufactures ensure that discharging batteries do not produce gasses! 
The exploding of my flashlight had serious potential to injure someone, and since many of these sealed flashlights state suitable in hazardous environments a detonation like the one I had can cause an explosion of the hazardous material as well

incident_description:
I bought the Sony Vaio VPCF115FM from Best Buy in July of 2009. The very first day I had the Vaio, I experienced overheating problems. After doing some research, ÃÂthese notebook computers may overheat due to a potential malfunction of the internal temperature management system, resulting in deformation of the product's keyboard or external casing, and a potential burn hazard to consumers.ÃÂ The information about the recall is found on the Sony website at: 
http://esupport.sony.com/US/perl/news-item.pl?template_id=1&news_id=401.

According to the recall page:
"If you have one of the VPCF11 or VPCCW2 series models, Sony recommends that you download and install a firmware update specifically designed to prevent the potential overheating symptom."

After downloading the firmware update and install, the only thing that I noticed that was different was that the fans would run at full speed all the time. Whether I was browsing the web or watching a movie, the noisy fan would be running at 100%. This update did not fix my problem. I was still getting temperature readings above 100 degrees Celsius (the temperature at which water boils). This laptop gets so hot, that it will cause a burn if set on your lap. This is not only a safety hazard but a fire hazard. Whenever my Vaio reaches processor temperatures of over 100 degrees Celsius, it shuts off due to overheating. 

I currently own a business repairing computers, networking businesses, building custom PC's, and doing web design. I have a bachelors degree in computer science and minored in information systems. Basically, I have a well rounded knowledge of computers and how they work. I also know that processor temperatures over 100 degrees Celsius at under 50% RAM usage is completely unacceptable. 

A while back I attempted to have Sony service my laptop without success. After talking with many different people in customer service, I was told that there was nothing I could do and that my call could not be escalated any higher. Since no one was helping, I did some research and got a hold of the emails to the CEO's and other important sony chairmen. I sent them the following email and I believe the only reason they decided to help me was because I send a mass email out to people high up in the Sony department. Below are excerpts from an email I sent them last year:



"I first called about this issue in August of 2011, and was shipped a prepaid box to send my unit out for repair. As I mentioned earlier, I am a computer science student and at the time I was starting school and did not have time to ship my unit for repair. I called at the beginning of January 2012 and requested a new box be sent so I could ship my computer for repair. After sending my unit out for repair, I got an email from the facility in Lerado, TX. The email is as follows:

ÃÂDear Valued Sony Customer
 
We have completed the repair estimate for your unit based on the
information  you provided us. The estimated charges for your repair is
labor charge $ 99.99  and parts charge $ 100.00  plus applicable
sales tax. Please contact us at your earliest convenience by phone or
email to approve or refuse this estimate. Our contact information is
listed below. To help us expedite your repair please have your credit
card number ready when you call. For your security we do not suggest
including your credit card number in an email response.
Thank you for choosing Sony and feel free to contact us if you have any
questions regarding your service request.
Customer Information
Notification: [REDACTED]
Model       : VPCF115FM/B
Serial      : 27514932-3004946
Event ID    : [REDACTED]

I called and spoke to [REDACTED] at the Lerado, TX repair facility today, February 13, 2012. I asked her why I was being charged $200 for repair on my unit. She informed me that the $200 was to repair the audio out jack on the laptop, and that the technician found NO overheating problem. After talking with [REDACTED] for a few minutes, I asked her how there could be NO overheating issue, yet the computer is recalled for that very reason and that the computer got hot enough to cause burns when touched. She did not have an answer, other than ÃÂwe stand by our technicianÃÂs results and that there is NO overheating issueÃÂ, which there clearly is.

 I asked [REDACTED] to be escalated and she gave me the phone number for Vaio hardware support. I called at 10:00AM and spoke with [REDACTED]. I explained my situation to [REDACTED] and he escalated my issue to customer relations. I spoke with [REDACTED] in customer relations at 10:30AM. After talking with her about my issue, she called the Lerado, TX facility while I was on hold. When she came back on the phone, she told me that the technician found NO overheating problems with the unit. I again asked, ÃÂhow can there be no overheating issue with the unit, yet it is too hot to touch?ÃÂ She had no answer. She asked me what I wanted replaced to fix the issue, and I told her a new system board. I asked her to escalate me to the next level and she attempted to transfer me to the national customer relations department. [REDACTED] came back and said that they were busy and would call me back.

I am writing to you to not only address my issue but to address the poor, unsatisfactory support and customer relations department. I feel as though I am being charged $200 to repair an audio jack, when I sent my computer to be repaired for an overheating problem in the first place. I am telling you, the computer is NOT safe and poses a burn hazard as well as a fire hazard. If my issue was addressed with care, I would not be writing to you for a solution. What I am most upset about is that this is a recognized issue with the unit, it is recalled, and that no one seems to want to fix my issue. Instead, it is being claimed that there is no problem with it overheating, but that they will fix my audio jack for $200.

Upon inspection of the "fixed" vaio, I noticed that they did manage to fix my audio jack (which I told them I didn't want replaced). I'm not completely sure as to whether or not they replaced the whole motherboard, but regardless I still had major overheating problems.

Here it is, 9/8/2013 and I stumbled upon the saferproducts.gov website and decided to make an incident. My vaio still overheats and some of the hardware is starting to go bad, since heat causes computer components to wear and break faster than properly cooled components. At this point, the only thing Sony could ever do to keep me as a customer would be a full refund for $1299.99 + tax or the amount credited towards a new Sony laptop. Tonight, I picked up my 3GS to turn it on and the screen had popped loose from the case on one end.  The phone did not turn on. Research gave me info that Apple designed the batteries to expand or explode in order to keep them from leaking. Apple should research their problem and change in the future in order to protect the consumer.  If this had exploded on me while using as a phone and injured me, Apple would find themselves in a legal lawsuit.

incident_description:
My wife and I live in Kansas City, MO. And were leaving to go on vacation on the 27th of July.  On July 26th 2013 my wife set her phone alarm and plugged it in to charge placing it on her nightstand.  We were getting up early to drive to Marion NC. the next day. 
Around 1:00a.m. we heard a hissing sound and then a loud POP.  My wife yelled FIRE.  I jumped out of bed to a smoke filled room saw that her phone was on fire.  
The phone is a SAMSUNG GALAXY SII MODEL NO. SPH-D710.  I grabbed it and threw it in the master bedroom bathroom sink and turned on the water.  The smell in the bedroom was bad enough to take your breath away.  We aired out the bedroom put the phone in a baggy.  There was minimal damage to the end table and carpet.
If she hadnÃÂt set her alarm on the phone she would have plugged it in the living room to charge.  We feel that if she had done that the house would have been on fire, and we wouldnÃÂt have known it.
When we got to Marion, NC. We tried looking up on the WEB to see if there had been any other phones reported catching on fire.  We found 2 cases one in a mans pocket in Australia that was contributed to the fact it was in his pocket and couldnÃÂt get proper ventilation, and one in a girls backpack that was for the same reason.  My wives phone was laying on her nightstand when it caught fire so we felt it had plenty of ventilation.  
We went to a Sprint store in BOONE, NC. And was told that it was not the phones fault that we needed to file an insurance claim that it was our fault for charging it.  The manager there took a picture and sent it to his superiors, and they agreed with him.
We went back to our Daughters house and filed an insurance claim with ASURION on line.  We had to pay $100.00 deductible to get my wife a new phone.  We had it sent to my sons house in Chapel Hill, Tn. Since we were headed there next.  When we filled out the claim we were told to return the old phone in 10days or we would be charged $500.00.  
We received the phone when we got to my sons home and we went to a Sprint store to have it activated in Spring Hill, TN.  The lady helping us couldnÃÂt believe the phone that caught on fire and she removed the battery saying that we shouldnÃÂt ship it back with the battery in it.
justification: No injuries occurred, but the incident could have escalated to a more severe level if the phone was charging in the living room.

incident_description:
MacBookPro battery is bulging out of its metal casing: In early 2008 I purchased a MacBookPro from Apple, Inc. Since then the battery that came with the aforementioned MacBookPro has been replaced once (by Apple) due to it reaching the "end of its life cycle" and presenting extreme bulging out of its metal encasing and consequently the slot in which it's located.
Last week the same issue started to develop with the replacement battery, serial number W0115094Z9DA, about a year since I began using it. I believe there's an intrinsic manufacturing defect on these batteries rendering them unusable after they've reached a percentage of their "life cycle". 
Most importantly however, these batteries seem unsafe to consumers using them under normal operation specifications. As described above, the initial battery that came with the laptop battery bulged so much that I feared for my safety. 
Regarding the early stages of bulging presented by the current battery, I was reassured by Apple's Employee ([REDACTED] at Portland's Pioneer Square Apple Store) that battery serial number W0115094Z9DA remains safe to continue operations for "several more months or years". He reassured me specifically that there is no risk of the battery exploding or leaking its contents.
My uninformed guess is that these batteries aren't safe for use and therefore I hereby submit this unsafe product report to further evaluate the safety of this battery.
justification: Battery bulging is recurring, posing potential safety risks as seen in the past.

incident_description:
Purchased a 100' package of 14gauge speaker wire as shown http://www.3kings.com/p-2389-xxx-brx14100-14-ga-100-bag-high-quality-economy-speaker-cable-14-gauge.aspx

When stripping the insulation off at the end of the cable to install it, I discovered it was approximately 19 gauge wire (which is non-standard size). Product was made in China.

The http://www.3kings.com/ web site sells several size packages/spools of this product and it is further distributed for them by Amazon.com.

At the http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B009XULXBS/ref=s9_psimh_gw_p23_d0_i1?pf_rd_m=ATVPDKIKX0DER&pf_rd_s=center-2&pf_rd_r=13M1PV6DREF1VM4KXSX7&pf_rd_t=101&pf_rd_p=1389517282&pf_rd_i=507846 site, several people who have also purchased this product have had the same experience as indicated by their feedback left under the product review area.

UPDATE FROM CONSUMER:
Undersized wiring labeled as much heavier gauge wiring can be used in applications where the thickness of the wiring is critical to avoid overheating. The approximately 19 gauge wire reported in the attached report, labeled as 14 gauge wire could be used in application passing as much as  15 amperes, which would melt the conductors. Since speaker wire is essentially the same as two-conductor lamp cord, it can be used interchangeably by home owners to repair electrical appliances causing them to overheat and cause fires, electrical shorts and shocks.
justification: Multiple consumers have reported the same issue of undersized wire, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence.

justification: The incident resulted in property damage (burnt power cord) but no injuries, and the likelihood of occurrence is high given the numerous reports of similar incidents.

incident_description: My iPhone 3GS screen suddenly popped out. I investigated the problem online and it seems that there were several similar reports relating to the iPhone 3GS. The problem is caused by a rapid/almost ?sudden expansion of the battery which reportedly may explode causing potential fire or bodily injury.
justification: While no injury occurred in this instance, the potential for bodily harm due to the battery expansion makes this a level 2 incident.

incident_description: Right after dinner Tuesday night, June 18, I smelled "electronic" smoke.  I saw that my Hewlett Packard monitor was smoking.  When I picked it up, flames and sparks started coming out of the back of the monitor.  The monitor at that time has been in "sleep" mode in conjunction with my HP desktop computer.  The monitor is Model w2408h.  Serial number 3CQ8210JFS.  I unplugged the power cord and the inputs going into the monitor.  I will hold the monitor for a while in case you or Hewlett Packard need to inspect it.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident involved a significant fire hazard from the smoking monitor.

incident_description: Battery pack bulged
justification: Battery pack bulging could lead to an incident but unlikely to cause injury.

incident_description:
The fire investigator wanted to inform us that someone in his office responded to a fire that happened caused by surge protector. The investigator stated that the home owner went home and found that there was a fire inside of the unit. He stated that they found that there was fire damage to the interior of the surge protector. 

The fire investigator stated that he was not aware of all the details, but it seemed that none of the 6 receptacles were damaged. He stated that the front of the surge protector looked undamaged and the fire was confined to the interior of the item and there were sharing to the outside paint of the bottom of protector. 

The investigator stated that no one was injured. He stated that he also researched and found no recalls on this product. 

The investigator stated that he believed that this product should be investigated since it poses a fire hazard.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the fire caused by the surge protector poses a significant risk, making it an incident with a possible likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: Kindle Fire color tablet computer, purchased in April 2012 from Best Buy. Case apparently overheated and expanded.Electronics and software appear to work without a problem. The case expanded and broke open on the right side. I found several reports of this happening on Amazon.com tech support forum. This unit was not being charged when the case expanded.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage (broken case) but no injuries, and there are reports of similar occurrences, indicating a possible likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: Back in February I upgraded to an iPhone 5. I since then left my old iPhone 3gs in my living room at room temperature since then. A few days a go I decided to use it for music, charged it up and today I noticed the battery had swollen up, and is popping the front glass off.
justification: While no injury occurred, the incident involved a hazardous situation (swollen battery) that could have led to property damage or injury if not noticed.

incident_description: I own a portable Sony 9-inch DVD player (model number NP-FX110) which, to my surprise, stopped functioning suddenly. It wasn't dropped, spilled on or put in the sun. It was safe in it's case in my climate controlled locker at work. Strange. Upon inspection I noticed what others have reported to saferproducts.gov. The battery pack is swollen!
justification: Although no injury occurred, the incident involved a product malfunction due to battery swelling, which is possible but not rare.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that his son woke up, went into the computer room because he heard a noise and found that the surge protector was arcing. The consumer stated that his son immediately unplugged the surge protector and the arcing stopped. 

The consumer stated that there were black burn marks on the floor and on the actual surge protector. 
The consumer stated that no one was injured.
The consumer stated that he did not contact the manufacturer.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the arcing surge protector posed a potential fire hazard, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
Battery for MacBookPro laptop computer self-destructed while in place in the computer, which was operating on AC power at the time, and resting on a fan platform powered via a USB port from the  computer.  The battery swelled or expanded to the point that its cover plate was bent and side seams ruptured.  Internal structures of the battery were visible through gaps of several millimeters.

The damage was apparently incurred over 5 to 10 minutes, based on my observation that the computer was stable on the fan platform when I booted it up but rocked on the platform when I pressed the "power off" button in response to the crash message.  It felt as if something was entrapped underneath it, and indeed there was: the deformed battery, bulging from its normal docking position on the underside of the laptop.

This laptop is 5 1/2 years old, and the battery is the original one.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and while it's possible, it's not likely to happen frequently due to the age of the laptop and battery.

incident_description: After inserting memory card product became very hot started smoking. I burned my thumb while trying to remove the memory card.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (burned thumb), and the likelihood of occurrence is high given the product overheating and smoking.

incident_description:
Within the last 6 to 12 months I purchased a package of
Ray-0-Vac, D batteries, expiration 12-2017,lot RG6F.
They came in a plastic package which contained about 8
batteries. They were probably purchased from Ocean
State Job Lot or Wal-Mart, but I cannot be sure. I
placed them in various flashlights in our home and
cars. One of those flashlights was placed upright on an
end table near my bed. Recently I noticed a ring on
that table under the upright flashlight. I opened the
flashlight and observed that one of the batteries was
leaking a fluid. That fluid caused severe damage to the
finish on the table. I then we to observe the
remainder of the batteries remaining in the container.
Another one was leaking and some of the fluid spotted
my jeans.
In May, I call the company and reported the above
details. They asked me to return the batteries for
replacement but I choose instead to report it to this
Agency.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident caused significant property damage and potential harm (jeans staining).

incident_description: Device was left in the charging cradle for a week while it was not being used. When device was being placed back into use the battery cover was no longer fitting correctly. Removed battery cover and found battery inoperative and excessively bulging to the point where the cover no longer will fit correctly.
justification: Potential for property damage (device) but no injury reported.

incident_description: The cord heated up and melted.  The cord was plugged into a UPS and sitting loosely on its own on metal wire shelving.  It was not covered.  The device was not powered on.
justification: The cord melting could have caused a fire, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: My Kindle Fire from Amazon was 14 months old when the battery began swelling and bulging. It is very strange and when I called Amazon they just said they had never heard of the problem. Also too bad it is out of warranty. Buy a new one they advised. I researched on line and alot of people having the same problem and I believe they need to recall this product! An exploding battery can cause injuries!
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the potential for injury due to battery swelling is high, as evidenced by numerous online reports of the same issue.

incident_description:
My husband and I were watching TV today June 2, 2013. We have a 32 inch Vizio. Model # E321VL.

This TV was purchased October 10, 2011.

The TV produced a burning smell and the screen went black. Smoke came from the back of the TV. My husband immediately unplugged the TV.

I am concerned as I have read other postings about this make of TV and read that some of them have caught on fire. I have two more TV's (Vizio's) of various sizes.

I am afraid that the other TV's might catch on fire during the night and burn my house.

Thanks
[REDACTED]
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident involved a potential fire hazard, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' scenario. The likelihood is 'possible' as similar incidents have been reported for the same make.

incident_description: I have a first generation KINDLE FIRE that's 17 months old and used only occasionally (purchased Dec 2011 when it just came out).  I charged the device last week using the charger that came with it, and noticed the edge of the tablet split open.  At first I thought it was just a problem with the adhesive, but after 2 later battery charges i observed the following:  the center of the tablet now has a bulge (almost double the thickness of the tablet), the area of the bulge is very hot while the device is charging, and the casing of the kindle eventually gave and split open on the right side.  I checked amazon.com and other websites to see how I can get the kindle serviced.  I read that the same problem has happened to other kindle owners, as early as May 2012, and that it is a problem involving a defective battery that could leak/explode with continued use.  I called Amazon's customer support and was told that because my device is out of warranty (they offer a 1-year warranty), they can only offer to sell me refurbished kindles.  I was told that they do not have a repair service system in place.  What was very shocking is that customer support sounded as though they have not heard of this problem being reported before, when i fact a lot of people have complained about already.  I am very upset that the device was not recalled immediately, and amazon refuses to replace the device now that it is out of warranty - a convenient excuse for them.  The first generation kindle fire must be recalled as even children use and play with this device.
justification: The incident involved a potential fire hazard due to a defective battery, which could have caused injury if not addressed.

incident_description: I was charging my 3 year old iphone 3Gs when I noticed it swelling. Within about 15 minutes the screen nearly popped off on its own, I couldn't get it out of my house quick enough. once outside the screen came off and the motherboard popped up on one side on its own due to the pressure from the expanding battery.
justification: The incident involved a swelling battery leading to the screen popping off, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: The headset unit (GN Netcom) caught fire!  It burned fast and long until put out by a fire extinguisher, causing damage to the desk on which the headset was sitting.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and while it's possible for electronic devices to catch fire, it's not a common occurrence.

incident_description:
We purchased two General Electric plug-in multi-outlets two weeks ago from Target.  My son plugged his cellphone charger into one of them and the additional GE outlet spit a flame, burning and electrocuting him.  He has a burn on his index finger and one on his thumb.  There is smoke residue on the GE product itself.  My son said the GE outlet shot out a flame and a spark, electrocuting and burning him.

His room smelled of burning flesh and hair.  His finger and thumb are charred with cuts on them.  

The outlet had no other devices plugged in and the circuit breaker light was still on.  Again, this was a brand new electrical item and the phone charger plugs into the wall outlet without incident.

We photographed his injuries and still have the electrical product.

Who can I complain to?  I have not contacted Target or General Electric but this product is unsafe, there is something wrong.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries (burns and cuts) to the victim, hence severity level 3.

incident_description:
The consumer says the bouncing icons and high contrast as well as its flashing lights on her IPAD can start an epileptic seizure.  She is able to turn it down to dim the brightness and wear sunglasses but then she could not see the screen.  She contacted the manufacturer who told her that there is nothing that they can do.  

She says after using the product is makes her nauseated, shaky and gives her a headache.  Also she suspects that there is something that can be done about it but the manufacturer is very difficult to talk to.  

The consumer says her main concern  is that the flashing lights and high contrast and the bouncing icons all combine to cause serious health concerns for persons who are epileptic.  She says it should be properly labeled.
justification: The incident description mentions potential severe health impacts, including epileptic seizures, nausea, and headaches, which could lead to injuries.

incident_description:
The consumer says that the TV was installed properly.  He put it up for the Superbowl.  He called the company the next day telling them that a toxic odor is emitting from the unit.  The manufacturer told him that the odor would go away.  He says that the smell has not gone away.

The consumer says it smells like plastic is burning.  He says he has seen numerous complaints online from other consumers.  The consumer says that his face has gotten burned due to the radiation.
justification: Consumer reports facial burns due to radiation from the TV, indicating a severe injury.

incident_description:
(04/13/2013) The consumer stated that she was in her mother's kitchen making lunch. Her mother was in the den and had just left from the den when she heard a crash. She went into the den and saw that the stand had snapped in half. 


(04/13/2013) The consumer called the manufacturer but they were not open. She called them back on 4/15/2013) and spoke with a representative. She was told that they would send a replacement part because the television is still under warranty. 


The consumer stated that she qoogled the name of the televison and found the other compliants.
justification: No injuries reported, but the incident of the TV stand snapping is possible to occur again based on consumer complaints found online.

incident_description: My daughter was using and charging her computer on May 04, 2013 when she smelled what would appear to be burning wires.  Upon investigation, she discovered that the smell was coming from her computer. The wires in the charger were smoking.  When she removed the charger from the computer, a plastic piece of the charger had melted into the computer and damaged it to the point that it could not be recharged.  We returned the computer to Samsung and are waiting on them to repair it.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and the likelihood of such an event occurring due to a faulty charger is possible.

incident_description:
The consumer says that she had the charger attached to [hook and loop fastener] on an upper shelf, with the cord snaked down to the back of her desktop.  All of a sudden it stopped working.  The cord was no damaged in the area of the desk shelf.  

She thought it was a flashlight issue.  She swapped out the rechargeable battery but it still did not work.  She then realized that the wiring from the flashlight is melted and exposed.  The transformer looks distorted.  It does have a UL stamp on it.  No beading seen on the cord wiring.  Transformer was plugged into a power strip.  UL listed.  Made in China  

The caller checked with an electrical inspector who could not determine how this happened.  

Incident location: business office
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a potentially hazardous electrical issue, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' case.

incident_description:
The caller stated that his laptop battery exploded, there were flames erupting from the unit.  The desk where the laptop was located caught fire and burnt the paint on the wall nearby, this dissipated in a few minutes.  He immediately removed the unit to discard it outside in doing so he received 2nd degree burns to his left thumb. The fire extinguisher was used to contain the fire on the laptop. The fire dept was contacted and he received treatment for his injury on the scene.

There is no estimate of property damages at this time.  The manufacturer was not contacted as yet.

The caller feels that this laptop is a fire hazard and should be investigated.
justification: Injury occurred due to direct contact with the exploding laptop battery, and the fire could have been more severe if not contained.

incident_description:
Dell XPS 15z laptop computers have a bezel trim ring that is chromed plastic.  The chrome flakes off (regularly reported on Dell's support website) and leaves a very sharp surface.  The metalic flakes are sharp enough to slice open skin.

Dell has had numerous reports of this issue.
justification: The sharp metal flakes from the bezel trim ring can cause skin injuries, as reported by numerous users.

incident_description: While I was using my Kindle Fire it began to make popping noises. I shut it off quickly and then it popped once more and sizzled. The casing expanded and the face of the device peeled up on one corner. I did not have the device plugged in while this was happening, it was just running off of the battery. When I called Amazon about this, they said that it was out of warranty and there was nothing they could do about it. I saved the device in case anyone wanted to look at the damage and determine what occurred. If this had been charging, or I had not turned it off quickly, I am afraid that it may have caused a fire.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the device's casing expanding and face peeling up indicates a significant malfunction, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
I noticed my devices plugged into the Belkin Relocatable Power Taps, model number BV108200-06R-BLK, listed number: E152555 was not providing any power.

I also heard an electrical arc sound and took a look around for the source of the problem.  The problem came from the 360 degree wall outlet plug where the plastic housing surrounding cracked, and the separation was the reason why there was no power.

I was fortunate enough to unplug it without getting shocked and had to temporarily relocate a better surge protector to run the equipment.
justification: Potential for injury due to electrical arc, but no reported injuries.

incident_description:
Numerous years ago I bought a Dell 5100 CN color laser printer which I still use.  Recently [REDACTED] done some software updates and the printer reported a PCL error when I tried to print a page.  As I had to go out to the doctors today I ignored it and though I would look at it later when I got back, and print the documents I was working on, on top of the printer.

A few minutes ago, which is about 12 hours later, I smelt something like smoke / burn and picked my documents up off the printer and they were very hot.  The printer was also very very hot on the case, and even hotter inside to the point that it was to hot to touch.

I do not know what caused the issues, but something is causing the printer to want to print, but fail before the printer finishes that job.  I strongly believe that if I were not here, or noticed the slight smell as I am allergic / have sensitivity to what seems like everything, then the printer would have continued to heat up until the printer set on fire, which I am pretty sure would have then continued on to set my house on fire.

Note that I have used this printer for 8 years without any issues. IF I use the printer with [REDACTED] it works fine, the problem only occurs when using [REDACTED] with the PCL Error.   After about 20 minutes of waiting after the issue above, I tried printing from [REDACTED] which it did perfectly fine, but once again when I tried with [REDACTED] the same PCL error came up, so I shut the printer physically off this time. 

Also, this printer even though old is still very common as it is fast, generally reliable and inexpensive to use.

I ask that you report of do something as this issue could potentially cause mass damage or cost innocent pople their life's.
justification: The printer overheating and potentially causing a fire poses a significant risk of injury.

incident_description: Battery case on my Sony DVD player has cracked open due to swelling of the Li-Ion battery. The unit was not on charge and had not been used for several weeks. The unit was without problem after its last charge and use. No injuries occurred due to this swelling, but has rendered the unit unusable. I am concerned of what could have happened if this had occurred when the unit was charging.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the incident could have resulted in property damage or injury if it had happened during charging.

incident_description:
Heard loud pop while in other room. Ran to living room where Samsung LCD TV was emitting thick smoke with an electrical burning smell.  Quickly unplugged TV and set outside. 

No injuries, but could have caused major fire damage if incident occurred when no one was home.
justification: The incident involved a TV emitting smoke and a burning smell, posing a high risk of fire, but no injuries occurred.

incident_description: Fellowes P-8S Paper Shredder flash exploded. Was just taken out of the box and used for 1st time. Have 1st and 2nd degree burns on left hand. Singed hair and eyelashes. Small damage to left eye. Treated at ER. Will need skin graft on left hand.
justification: Injury occurred due to unexpected flash explosion during first-time use, indicating a possible manufacturing defect.

incident_description: One World Technologies Inc and CPSC issued a recall for Ryobi 1+ charge centers. It limited the recall to model P108 number 130429028. The recall should be expanded based on my experience with model P113 number 140501013. Description follows:  My Ryobi battery charger began smoldering as I awaited a battery to recharge so I could finish weedwhacking my property. At first I smelled what resembled ammonia or urine as in when my dog had had an accident and lifted his leg to mark territory. Then I realized the odor that was by then burning my throat and causing a headache was more like that of a corroded battery compartment in a small unit like a flashlight. I approached my sitting room window seat where the charger was plugged in. The unit was smoking copiously and the odor very intense. I knew it was smoldering to catch fire but was more afraid it would explode. I am a 65-plus female homeowner living alone and cannot afford to be incapacitated. So despite my fear of explosion I opened a nearby window, unplugged the unit and gingerly tossed the hot object out the window onto the grass below. Several hours later, still fearing it might burst, I approached for a closer look. It was cooled off but I was unable to release the battery. It had fused to its compatible Ryobi charging unit. My local mechanic pried it apart and verified that the battery and charger were compatible based on the information printed on each. Home Depot would not hear of any compensation or replacement without a receipt which I did not have. They made no mention of problems or warnings regarding their Ryobi specialized product. I searched the internet to reveal the recall information. I will be writing to both Home Depot Corporate and to the listed distributor, One World Technologies of this Chinese-manufactured product to document my incident and to notify them of this e-mail to you, the CPSC. My photographic documentation is entitled THE RYOBI FIRE STARTER. I would attach a copy of the graphic representation here but there seems to be no mechanism for doing so. The melted and disfigured components are quite obvious.
justification: Potential for severe injury due to explosion or fire, as evidenced by the incident where the charger smoldered, smoked, and fused with the battery.

incident_description:
[REDACTED]I have a cell phone that was purchased for me my daughter, [REDACTED]. She bought the phone in
November of 2011 at the Metro PCS store at 2113 Harwood Road in Bedford, Texas 76021. l rarely used it
but the one time I did it blasted my ear with a loud, shrill noise. It really hurt my head and my ear as well
as deafening me for a while. After the first day the pain stopped and the ringing in my ear wasn't as bad; but
it has affected my hearing and there is still an annoying roar in my ear. When I went for a hearing test f was
told that I did have hearing loss in my left ear. The tester also said there wasn't much they could do to stop
the roar. For the last few months I have tried repeatedly to contact Metro PCS. Mr. [REDACTED] from their
insurance company called me and wanted some information on the phone which I faxed him. I received a
letter stating my phone was bought from Millenium Wireless,Inc. dba Wireless Shop an independent dealer
and is now owned by Metro PCS. My daughter said it was Metro PCS at the time she bought the phone.
The phone has Metro PCS stamped it. Her phones have always been Metro PCS. No one will give me any
information as to the date the store supposedly changed its name. Mr. [REDACTED] and Metro PCS refuse to
answer my letters, texts and phone calls. My ear was damaged by their phone, the hearing loss affects my
job which is mostly answering the phone. I feel they should be held responsible. If the store was not Metro
PCS at the time of purchase why can't they give me information on the store they say it was? Why won't
anybody tell me when the name of the store changed and why does the phone have Metro PCS stamped on
the front?
