incident_description: Rechargable battery pack for Wii remote malfunctioned. The inside portion of the battery pack (the battery cell) has expanded significantly. The assumption is that the cell contained inside has exploded. The product is made by Gigaware and is model number BK053450 and says "Custom Mfd. in China for RadioShack Corp" on the pack. The pack is UL listed MH28232
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the expansion and potential explosion of the battery cell poses a risk of property damage and future injury if not addressed.

incident_description:
COMPUTER MONITOR SPONTEOUSLY COMBUSTED!

PRODUCT INFORMATION:
LCD 24 inch flat screen computer monitor Emprex LM2601 Model SW26B Product ID 6702501894 Manufactured in May of 2008 Serial number B2612B82200261 by Innolux display corporation.  

DISTRIBUTOR:  Frys' Electronics in Tempe Arizona.  Sold in December 2008.

PRODUCT USE: Installed in a home office.  Plugged in with manufacturer supplied cables.  The monitor was well ventilated and not touching any surface except for contact between the stand and the desk.

INCIDENT:  On Saturday September 8, at approximately 1:00 p.m. Phoenix, Arizona time, the monitor began to emit smoke from the upper right ventilation area.  I reached behind the unit to pull the power cord from the back in order to stop the smoking and to prevent more damage.  The power cord connected to the back of the unit.  You have to reach over it in order to disconnect the cord.  As I detached the cord, the smoke became worse, and I saw a small spark or flame.  The flame did not grow because I was able to pull the plug.  However, in the process of pulling the plug, I inhaled fumes.  This caused me to feel dizzy, nauseated, and to vomit.  I had a terrible headache for about 6 hours.  

INHERENTLY DANGEROUS:  This product should be recalled.  If I had not been sitting in front of it, it would have caught the blinds behind the monitor on fire.  It could have burned my house down.  It also poisoned me with the smoke from the ventilation slots.

ATTEMPTS TO REDRESS:  Frys' electronics has disclaimed any liability.  
I have been unable to find contact information for Emprex / Innolux Display Corporation.  I have found web sites for Emprex and Innolux, a Taiwanese Corporation, but the contact pull downs do not launch.

I have the monitor.  I have not opened the case so I can prove that I did not alter it from its manufactured status.
justification: The monitor's spontaneous combustion caused injury (dizziness, nausea, headache) and posed a significant fire risk.

incident_description:
Manufacturer Printer with manufacturer cartridges that have melted inside the unit to the point that there is no plastic remaining.

He had smelled burning earlier but did not know where it was coming from.

The printer was plugged in with surge protector intact to access fax.

Caller was going to print from this printer on August 1st, 2012 and when printer would not print he looked inside and saw that plastic had melted away. 

There was not even a pool where it would have melted and reformed.

Printer was printing perfectly July 31, 2012.

Consumer contacted manufacturer the night of August 1st, 2012 and filed a report.
justification: No injuries reported, but the incident caused significant damage to the printer.

incident_description:
Sony rear projection TV model number kf-60we610 was recalled and i never found out until last weekend. Recall expired a few months ago.

This television repeatly had the projection bulb blow out, twice smoke came from the unit as a result. 

Call Sony, they asked me to have it checked out at my expense and to unplug the TV right away. Which I have done.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the repeated bulb blowouts and smoke incidents pose a potential fire hazard, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
I went to unplug my Duracell AC charger from the wall.  Instead of coming out of the wall socket, the case separated into two halves, and the bare connections to the power prongs were exposed (remember the prongs were still plugged into the wall).  My hand was right next to the live wires!  I didnÃÂt get shocked, but I could have if I had been careless and let my hand move a little bit closer.

I carefully removed the case half from the wall socket.  Apparently when the case was assembled, the two screws were too big for the holes in the plastic posts, and the posts split.  When I went to unplug it, I did not exert excessive force on the case, I just pulled on it, expecting the whole case to come out of the socket like it should have.  Instead, the split plastic posts broke, and the two haves of the case separated.  A picture of it can be seen on my blog.  http://rustybolt.info/wordpress/?p=3668
justification: Although no injury occurred, the incident involved direct exposure to live electrical wires, posing a significant risk.

incident_description: On August 8 2012 our fire department was called to a residence for a report of a fire in the bedroom. This fire was the result of a LCDI protector that had melted off the wall outlet and started the curtains on fire. This incident occurred about 30 seconds after the power company restored power to the house that had been out for about 6-8 hours following a lightning storm. Alone this may seem insignificant, however just two months earlier a very similar device caused alarm when it also filled a shop with smoke and tripped the circuit breaker powering the device. I have both of these devices if you would like to see them.
justification: While no injuries were reported, the incident caused a fire in the bedroom, resulting in property damage.

incident_description:
I own a product labeled Super Switch, manufactured by King Sound Enterprise Co., LTD for Blackstone International, LTD.

The product consists of 3 outlet adapters and a remote control unit which enables the on off switching of the electric at an outlet via remote control.

I have had the unit for about a year but it has only been in use for approximately 6 months.
This past weekend i was in my garage where the unit was controlling a light fixture through an outlet, the light started flickering when i inspected the plug the Super Switch unit was glowing orange with an internal fire.

I quickly yanked the unit out of the outlet and burned my hand on melted plastic.

I do not intend to be overly dramatic but had i not been in the room while this happened i believe there is a very high risk that there could have been a catastrophic outcome.

I have found absolutely no way to contact either King sound or Blackstone in regards to reporting the safety issue or pursuing reimbursement.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (burnt hand) and could have led to a catastrophic outcome (fire spreading) if not discovered promptly.

incident_description:
I fell asleep with the television remote in my hand. When I woke up, I was lying on the remote and had a burn on my stomach where the remote was touching my skin.

I have pictures of burn dated 06/23/12. I was not able to upload them to this report. I am not a medical professional. The burn was quite deep and probably would have been classified as a 3rd degree burn.
justification: The incident resulted in a deep burn, likely a 3rd degree, indicating significant injury.

incident_description:
I have (had) an Apple 8Gb iPhone 3Gs which I had been keeping in the event my new primary phone, another Apple product, decided to quit. I have occasionally been using it as an iPod touch since it was no longer connected to my cellular account.  
Today, the front glass separated from the housing, and a pop was heard as this happened.  Upon examination, the battery pack had expanded, and while not completely bursting (yet), the battery had quadrupled in size, pushing the glass out.
The ex-phone now sits in a bag, which is in another bag, which is in a box in my garage.  I fear that the battery will eventually explode, and don't want it in my living area when this happens.
justification: While no immediate danger is present, the battery expansion poses a risk of explosion in the future, hence the high likelihood.

incident_description: My two year old laptop battery exploded and burst into flames destroying my lap top and a coffee table.  I had entered this information on an early date and believed I would be adding to the details of that report.
justification: While battery explosions are rare, the likelihood of it happening to a two-year-old laptop is unlikely due to typical battery degradation over time.

incident_description:
Motorola Droid 2 Global Cell Phone

18Aug2012, Columbus OH

The cell phone in my front pocket suddenly overheated and started smoking.  I quickly removed the phone from my pocket and dropped it on the carpet.  I burnt my fingers trying to remove the battery.  I kicked the phone to the kitchen floor to keep it from burning the carpet.  The phone continued to smoke and melt until the battery was fully removed.

The cell phone was purchased directly from Verizon and was not modified in any way.  The phone contained the original factory supplied battery and was only charged using the factory supplied recharging cord.  The phone did not have a cover on it.
justification: Injury occurred (burnt fingers) and the phone's behavior was unexpected and dangerous.

incident_description: In January of this year I purchased a 46-inch Apex brand television. I have been very pleased with the television for the most part due to the relatively low price, however the adage still stands that if it seems too good to be true, it usually is. Last night in August of the same year of purchase I came home to a site that was initially very confusing. My television that seemed so great for the last 6 months was lying on the floor with a broken screen and stand. What had happened to my television was that the plastic stand that was built into the bottom of the tv had snapped causing the television to careen forward flipping over itself and knocking the screen directly into the front corners of the furniture I had set the television on. Upon closer inspection the inside of the stand contains a very cheaply made cylindrical post where all the screws are supposed to gain hold. This post was not only broken in half, but it was broken into no less than 10 pieces. This broken stand post is what caused the tv to fall. I want to stress that the the stand that broke was not a piece of furniture I set the television on, but the included plastic stand itself. I was mostly relieved that there were no children in front of the tv at the time it fell because the 50+ pound television would have caused serious injuries to any child it fell on. Although the price of these television sets may be enticing, I insist that nobody with young children should ever purchase an Apex tv. My girlfriend and I are currently trying to work with the Apex customer service for a refund of our money because the 1-year warranty has not yet run out, however they are trying to pull every stop in order make it seem as though what happened was our fault and not covered by the warranty. I saw on this website that at least one other person has reported the same problem. If I ever do get my refund I will most definitely spend a few extra bucks and get a [REDACTED] for safety reasons. If I don't get a refund unfortunately my budgeted expenses currently will not allow me to replace it for a long time.
justification: The television falling due to a defective stand poses a high likelihood of serious injuries, especially to children.

incident_description: The motor cooling intake is located inside the paper bin and when shredding a piece was pulled in and began smoking. I pictures of the receipt and paper available. Even if the grid was smaller, I am concerned the paper dust would be a problem too and reduce the life of the machine.
justification: Potential fire hazard due to paper dust, but no injuries reported.

incident_description:
We own a Royal MC14MX paper shredder, which does a great job shredding paper BUT doesn't seem to have a safety off if fingers get close to the opening where the paper is put in.
On Saturday the 18th of August my 12 year old son got his 4 fingers pulled into the opening on the machine. He quickly turned off the machine and I unplugged it, my husband had to use giant (they type used on semi's) screwdrivers to pry open the slot to get his hand out.
Luckily there only appears to be bruising & cuts.
I thought all paper shredders had an automatic safety off feature.  We wouldn't be using this shredder anymore.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries (bruising and cuts) to the child's fingers, and the likelihood of such an event occurring is high given the lack of safety features on the shredder.

incident_description: This laptop was purchased in 2009 and began overheating then. The laptop caused a blanket to be burned that was sitting under it while on the couch downloading songs from [REDACTED]. The laptop was turned off, brought in for service, determined to be fully functional, and was given back to me. Later, it caused red burning on the legs. This laptop was then sold for parts after the issue was failed to be fixed. It has now been acknowledged that this laptop could have been repaired for free -- but it is better to file a report now than later on this laptop
justification: The laptop caused property damage (burnt blanket and legs) but no injuries, and the likelihood of such an event occurring again is possible given the history of overheating.

incident_description:
I purchased a Philips 47" LCD HD TV in August 2009 from Wal-Mart (Model # 47PFL3603D/27.  During the last 6 months the TV's picture would black out.  When this occured, I could feel the heat coming from the unit, so I would turn the TV off for 5-10 minutes, let it cool, and then turn it back on. This problem would happen several times per week and I began to worry about it catching on fire and harming my house. Eventually, this problem got much worse, when the unit began smoking profusely this july.  You could see sparks from behind the tv on the top right.  I turned the TV off and have removed the unit from our family room.  I have since contacted Philips and they act like this problem doesn't exist at all.  A quick google search and even checking reviews on amazon show this problem is huge, and many consumers are dealing with it.  

As a concerned consumer, and parent, I feel obligated to share this potential fire risk with your organization with the hope that others will be alerted and avoid potential injury or death. 

Should you need any additional information, please contact me via [REDACTED].
I will keep contacting Philips, and leaving posts on other forums until i get a proper response.
justification: The TV's overheating and sparking pose a significant fire risk, which could lead to injury.

incident_description:
I recently purchased a cell phone brand new(sealed). It is an LG MS840 . Within the first week, I had notice very intense overheating with the phone. I tried to take all steps to make sure it was not something I had downloaded on my phone that was causing this. After trying and checking all programs and applications, the problem still continued. The phone overheats mostly when charging, and also randomly when it is in my pocket. 
 The heat of the phone gets so extreme at times, that I cant even hold it for more than a few seconds. I had tried to contact LG and they offered no help. I discovered via Google search that many other users like me have been experiencing the same issue. 
  I believe this product has a defect within the battery sector. It is only a matter of time before someone gets hurt.
justification: While no injuries have been reported yet, the extreme overheating poses a high likelihood of causing burns or damage to surrounding objects.

incident_description:
The battery in my laptop computer exploded in flame 
I suffered a 3rd degree burn on my leg which required medical treatment. 
The computer was damaged beyond repair 
After I dropped the computer on the floor and went to tend to my burn it burned the hardwood floor 
The computer was a Compaq presario, V3500, however the battery was a generic replacement made in China and purchased on the internet
justification: The incident resulted in a 3rd degree burn, requiring medical treatment, hence severity level 3. The use of a generic, potentially substandard battery makes the occurrence possible but not likely or certain.

incident_description: The lamp to my Sony Bravia KF50WE610 rear projection LCD tv burned out.  There had previously been a smell of burning plastic.  In replacing the bulb, I noticed that the housing and surrounding area of the tv had melted.  It appears as if it had been burned by extreme heat.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the incident involved a significant fire hazard due to melting of the TV's housing, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description: The side of my computer heats up badly enough that I burned my my hand today.  My understanding and research on the internet shows that the DV7T has KNOWN overheating issues, and HP has refused to resolve this.
justification: Burn injury occurred due to known overheating issue of the computer, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: The intec rechargeable battery pack for one of our Nintendo Wii remotes browned on the outside.  My 12-year old son told me he found it that way, it was not on the charging base when he found it, and that it smelled like metal.  No one was using it when the device apparently overheated.  Nobody was hurt and nothing was damaged other than the remote, which we are not going to use again.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident involved a potential fire hazard (overheating battery) and could have resulted in property damage or injury if not discovered in time.

incident_description: The phone I have is the HTC Amaze sent to me by T-Mobile. This phone gets so hot you would think it was going to over heat! So much that if it were by anything flammable it would definitely catch on fire. I have explained this to T-mobile, but their unwilling to assist and providing a different phone. They have sent 6 replacements of the same phone with the same outcome and I think at this point until someone is hurt it will never be rectified.

incident_description: On July 7th she went on a 7 mile run.  When almost done the IPOD burned her and gave her 2nd degree burn.  She went to her Dr. who prescribed a cream ([REDACTED]).  She was burned on her upper arm where the IPOD holder was sitting.

incident_description:

Risk of serious injury or death.

incident_description:
I purchased an AT&T  cordless telephone answering system on 2/27/2009 at BJs Wholesale CLub in Voorhees, NJ for $129.99
Over time we noticed that the handsets get very hot - sometimes too hot to handle. We were afraid of fire.
I contacted AT&T and was told the handsets should be warm but not hot and that the mondel is discontinued and we should buy a new system. 

It seems to me this product should be on the recall list

incident_description:
Slingbox Solo (model# unknown) which enables user to view television stations by internet.. Power supply connector burns up on the motherboard.

Unit has been used for four months with no problems until June 30th, 2012 when the caller smelled smoke, checked inside the motherboard, viewed burned components in motherboard.

justification: Potential fire hazard due to power supply connector burn, though no actual fire or injury occurred.

incident_description: DirectTV H25-500 Receiver, SN D32BC1HL311340 overheats  due use posing a safety and fire hazard. DirectTV was notified  by phone on July 21, 2012 . Specifically, Consumer requested a replacement product. DirecTV subsequently denied consumer request.

incident_description: I have a Macbook air from Apple. The battery inside the laptop is swelling and it's about to explode. incident_description:
I am the service manager for a electronics repair shop in Fresno CA
I have installed 6 sets of AV-30 and AV-20 speaker sets manufactured by M-Audio.  Each one of the sets has failed and been returned to my shop.  I got replacements from M-Audio, and the replacements have all failed as well.  I opened up the speakers and discovered an overheating condition caused by faulty filter capaciters in the power supply.  The Caps and power transformer are so hot after running for  hour that the insulation has cracked off, and the plug socket for the transformer has melted.  I have attempted to communicate this to the product support department of the manufacture.  They only will replace the units, and not offer any dialog regarding a voluntary recall of the product.

I think this is a serious safety issue, and an imediate recall must be ordered ASAP, before a fire or injury occurs.
justification: Overheating speakers pose a fire risk, and the likelihood of this happening again is high given the repeated failures.

incident_description: My Apex 40 inch LCD caught fire in the back of the television.
justification: The incident involved a fire in an electronic device, causing property damage but no reported injuries.

incident_description: I own an HP mini notebook.  The battery started to bulge and would not stay connected to the computer.  I checked online for the cause at their website and seen they had recalled numerous batteries due to explosion or fire hazards.  I am concerned that mine was not listed, the year it was manufactured is the same year of the recalls

incident_description: I have an iPhone 3gS that I use for development and as a music player. When I came home today the case had come apart (screen was mostly popped out) due to the battery being extremely bloated. It looks like it will pop at any moment. There doesn't appear to be any damage to the motherboard but it is bowed a bit and the screws appear to have been popped from their holes. It stays indoors (air conditioned) and it does not stay on a charger all the time. This is definitely a defective battery and if it explodes it could cause serious harm.
justification: Battery bloating and potential explosion pose a high likelihood of injury.

incident_description: On July 3, 2012 while siting in my dining room my wife and I heard a loud crashing noise in the living room .Please be advised that there are no walls between these rooms so we could see into the living room. What we saw completely surprised us our 46" Apex flat screen TV had fallen over. This TV Apex model LD4688 had been in the same place since we purchased it over 18 months ago. On inspection I found the base which came with the TV had failed. I called the company and was told to send them pictures of the TV and stand with a copy of the recept which I did. My reply was 'why would I want to buy a new stand from you when the old one just failed. The response they gave me I found very disturbing I was told "they had a problem with the other stand but were now making the new ones out of a different material'. We were lucky no one was near the TV when it fell so no one was injured but had our grand children been here it could have been a different story.I'm sure Target sold thousands of these TVs and the manufacturer knowing of this defect should have at least notified the current owners of the problem before serious injury or even death occurs. As for us will just count our blessing but I just can not belive that Target and Apex could be aware of this problem and choose to ignore it
justification: Although no one was injured this time, the potential for injury, especially to children, is high given the defect and the widespread distribution of the TVs.

incident_description:
I have an HD cable box provided by Comcast and branded as Xfinity. It is a Motorola RNG200N HD Tuner box. The box was installed by Comcast and sat on a tempered glass TV stand from Target. 

Last night the cable box overheated causing a small explosion of the glass, sending a millon glass fragments  throughout my apartment.
justification: The cable box explosion resulted in widespread glass fragments, posing a high likelihood of injury.

incident_description: Electrical power surge caused plug in surge protector to catch on fire.
justification: While the surge protector catching fire is an incident, there's no mention of any injuries.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that he was using the shredder and the paper was jammed, when he went fix the shredder he noticed that the blades were exposed. 

The consumer stated that his paper shredder does not have a protective shield to guard against exposure to the cutting blades. The consumer stated that it poses the same hazard stated on release# 01-034. The consumer stated that he could easily cut his fingers due to the fact that the blades are exposed.

The consumer stated that manufacturer informed him that this product was not on a recall.
The consumer believes that this product should be investigated.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the exposed blades pose a high risk of injury, making it an incident.

incident_description: I bought a 42" Philips television just under 2 years ago.  We use cable and it appeared that something was wrong with our service.  Our cable provider sent out a technician to investigate.  He went behind the television, touched the input piece and was blown back.  It made a loud bang and blew him back.  He received a bad shock which hurt his arm.  Large amounts of electricity were being emitted from the input piece.  He tested the input with a voltmeter and it read off the chart.  He said that TVs have a safety mechanism in them that keeps this from happening.  Not only did the main board fail, but so did the safety mechanism.  This is a serious safety issue.  I called Philips, but they had no comment.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury to the technician, and the likelihood of such an event occurring is high given the failure of both the main board and the safety mechanism.

incident_description:
Intense electrical short within Belkin surge protector's rotating male plug caused the plastic housing to melt and seperated the blade from internal connectors (metal blade is now at an awkward angle).

The following is what I reported to Belkin,USA, Customer Support:

Re: Relocatable Power Tap
Surge Protective Device (Type 3)
15A - 125v

I was reassured that despite the battery in my device having the same over-heating issue that it was unaffected by the recall. The recall was later expanded to include more batteries but mine still did not fall under it.

My concern is that despite the battery for my device not being included in the recall of HP batteries to date, something may still be seriously wrong with it. The entire unit including the laptop itself, the removable battery, and adapter all over-heat from time to time. More often than not, I'm forced to use a laptop cooling fan or place it on top of a cool surface to avoid over-heating. Sometimes, it gets so hot that my laptop will shut down completely. 

I am worried about being injured or having my computer damaged if something were to explode or otherwise seriously malfunction because of this issue. In the meantime, I also have an HP Pavilion dv2000 which uses the same type of battery. I use the battery from that device or take out the battery and run my computer off the adapter to minimize the risk. However, that battery is getting old and dies quickly and the adapter over-heats as well.

I'm putting the incident date was May 2010 because that is when I called HP about the problem. It has been an intermittent issue for a few years now. The injury I am reporting is minor at most. If it starts to over-heat and is placed on my lap, it does begin to burn them. This "burn" is similar to the feeling a person gets when touching something very hot and pulling their hand away quickly. It is uncomfortable for a short time but leaves no lasting injury.

incident_description:
I am writing this description of the product defect with the Promethean Board device so that you can better understand what needs to be done to make this product safe for everyone to use. I don't think that the original report that I called in and submitted online was accurate or detailed enough for your organization to take the proper action needed to resolve this issue properly. 

The Promethean Board is an integrated LCD Projector and hard bodied screen that is used to make presentations in a school. Teachers regularly teach lessons on this interactive board and students use it as well. It is used on a daily basis for most of the day and is a very popular teaching aide that has replaced white boards and dry erase markers almost entirely. 
The problem we are experiencing is that the mounting system employed by the board is not robust enough for its purpose. The board uses only a hanger style mount to secure it to a bolted wall mount system. In other words the entire hard display board, an 82 inch screen not too different in size and weight to a large flat panel LCD TV, is held only by a very loose mount that can easily be toppled over by any accidental movement to the board. The board itself is not securely bolted to the wall mount as it should be. 

To better illustrate this point we had two teachers who tried to adjust the board's position on the wall last year. The board fell on top of the teachers as they jostled the board off its hanger mounting system. Although these two people were not hurt in this case they could have been. If this had been small children this similar incident could have become a tragic accident with serious injuries or even death as a consequence. 
I sincerely feel that a simple retrofit kit could be designed and installed that would make this board much safer with a solid bolted mounting system. I don't think that the company that makes this product would have any technical issue at all with designing such a safer mount. How they could ever think that a, loose mount holding a large heavy screen in a classroom would be safe around teachers and small children is beyond common sense. In California where earthquakes are a common occurrence such a weak mounting system has no place at all within a school.  

My only goal in making this report is to see that this engineering oversight is remedied. I want to make sure that this firm and their US distributor Logical Choice make all of the upgrades, including parts and labor, available at no cost to all of their clients and customers. The safety of all of our children has no price. What would you pay in order to help keep your children or the children of your neighbor safe?
justification: The loose mount poses a high risk of injury, as demonstrated by previous incidents involving teachers, and could potentially cause serious harm or death if small children were involved.

It was so scary and alarming as it is never safe if products like this just explodes inside our homes! right?
justification: Although no one was injured, the sudden explosion of the TV base caused a loud crash and could have resulted in injuries if someone had been nearby.

incident_description:
The glass base on my 50 inch Samsung plasma tv exploded and glass flew everywhere.  Glass fragments flew up to 15 feet in all directions.  Large chunks and little slivers. Thankfully no one was in the room at the time.  Now the tv is unstable with what is left for a base which consists of a much smaller metal plate.

This does not appear to be an isolated incident.  After this happened I started checking the internet.  This has happened to other people as well.
justification: No injuries occurred as no one was in the room, but the incident caused significant property damage.

incident_description: A fire occurred on a bed with a sleeping bag on top of foam mattress. A Kindle Touch was on the bed and had been there about 24 hours. It is not known if the device was in the sleeping bag or on top, but possibly on top. It was probably on. The fire was discovered early, so was confined to bed and small amount of furniture. Heavy rolling fire on bed was obsereved on discovery. Owner used garden hose before FD arrived. The device was not plugged in. Electricity was not a factor. No other source of ignition was present. The device was retrieved. Another possible device was also retrieved and a charge wire for a cell phone, which was not plugged in.
justification: No injuries were reported, but the fire could have spread further if not discovered early.

incident_description: Sony portable dvd battery pack split open.
justification: The battery pack splitting open could cause property damage but is unlikely to cause injury.

incident_description: We plugged the battery into the charger and left it to charge overnight. We woke up early in the morning to a strong chemical smell in the house and found the battery extremely overheated (boiling-we could hear it) and it looked as if it were ready to burst.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a significant risk due to the battery overheating and emitting a strong chemical smell, indicating a potential fire hazard.

incident_description: The fan on my Lenovo ThinkPad T520 manufactured 09-16-2011 in China stopped working and the laptop overheated. It was burning hot to the touch.
justification: The incident resulted in no injuries, but the laptop overheating poses a potential fire risk, making it possible to occur again.

incident_description: I went to turn on my tv and it started clicking trying to turn itself on and it wouldn't work.  So I took the front panel off and I noticed the heat lamp was warped and toasted.  Parts of the tv were also warped an burned. So ther is damage to the tv now.
justification: Damage to the TV occurred, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
Sony battery pack Model No. NP-FX110 split open while attached to portable dvd player while in use. Upon inspection, one of two 3.7V cells has expanded to approximately 5-7 times the volume of the other (unaffected) cell. Feels squishy to the touch, as if filled with a gas under pressure. 

The unit was not subjected to trauma or temperature extreme, and was in normal use playing a dvd at the time it expanded. It is suspected that, had the malfunction not been detected, the cell could have burst and spread its contents outside the casing.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the potential for harm was high as the battery pack could have burst and spread its contents, causing property damage or injury.

incident_description: I have a potentially defective SONY LCD PROJECTION TV model KDF-50WE655.  SERIAL NUMBER is 9232259.  It has recently displayed potential problems and shut itself down.  I have emailed my concerns to sonylistens@am.sony.com.  I am aware of the pending class action lawsuit against Sony.  I am HIGHLY CONCERNED that the heating and melting issues may cause product and or other property damage.   I am also HIGHLY CONCERNED that SONY has not issued a recall of this product.  I found out about the current status of the product when I searched the internet to have the unit serviced.  I am not willing nor should I have to pay for the cost of repair and or service the unit.  This product could have caused serious harm to my property and or family members.   WE WERE COMPLETELY UNAWARE!
justification: While no immediate harm has been reported, the potential for property damage due to heating and melting issues is high, making it an incident with possible occurrence.

incident_description: My TV  in the bedroom was turned on earlier today and while i was in the kitchen all of a sudden  the fire alarm went on . I came to the bedroom and first noticed a poisoness smell but  first I thought that its coming from my neighbors   thru the AC vent  and called conciege and notified him about this problem then few minutes later i've  noticed clouds of smoke pouring down  fom the corner  on the room . Since my TV is standed on top of high cabinet right  next to the AC vent  , first i though that smoke is coming from my neighbor ( because AC was on and blowing the smoke away from the TV ) , also my TV was  ON and working  normal while  the smoke was coming out ) .  Building maintenance people came right away and couldn't notice that smoke is coming from my TV either so they called fire fiighters to examine the entire building ) . At that time i turned the TV off and smoke still was coming out for  several minutes after that . When fire fighters came , they checked every  cable in my apartment , asked me about the TV and said that this poison smoke smell like some kind of cable or electronics burn and its a common thing in their experience  that these kind of burns cause the fire in the house . I was lucky to turn off the TV almost right away or it could blow up and get my entire apartment on fire .  I tried to turn the TV back on in about 1 hour after they left and picture and sound came on OK for about 10 seconds but the entire screen turned black but i still could hear the sound . I've tried to turn if OFF and back ON again  with same results, then i just unpluged  the TV and turned it around to examine . I  smelled it and found out that burned part is located in the upper middle back side on the TV . I'm very concerned about the statement that fire fighters told me that this kind of burn could cause a fire in the house . I already searched your web-site for consumers reports about same TV model and already found  dated in march 2011 . This guy reported the exact same smoke problem as mine . I also checked other web-sites and found quite a few similar burn and smoke problems on same  model  ,reported by consumers so it is clear to me that this is a common problem with this model ( Samsung HPS4253 ) and manufacturer should take some action  such as recall or offer free  or discounted repair on that model or at least free parts replacement . I've owned  many different brands of flat screen TVs  for years ( including the ones at my business location ) but i've never had any , even minor problems with any of them  , except this one . Very upset and disappointed at Samsung ;(  I paid total of US$2633  including very high % on my consumer  18 months loan and sure expected it to last little longer then 5 years (  not even mentioning that lived with my boyfriend for 2 years  so the TV really was only used  for 3years out of 5 ). For me , It is a pretty  expensive purchase  for  just  3 years use as a second TV ( the main one  from the living room ( also Samsung )  is still working , thank goodness ;) ... P.S.  While  checking for serial # on my broken TV , I just found out that it was made in Mexico .  All other flat screen  LCD's and plasma TV's I've owned in the past was manufactured in Asia  and  worked  GREAT  without any problems for years . I'LL NEVER BUY MEXICAN TV AGAIN !!!!
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved smoke and a potential fire hazard, hence severity level 2.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she noticed that the battery in the I-Phone had overheated after she had left it charging for approximately 8 hours.  This caused an expansion to the battery and cracked the casing, the rear part of the phone became warped.  There was no injury.

The consumer contacted the manufacturer and was advised that the phone was out of warranty and that there would be cost involved in servicing the phone.

The consumer is concerned that this cell phone is a fire hazard which could have caused an explosion and should be reported.
justification: While no injury occurred, the incident resulted in property damage (cracked casing, warped phone) and posed a potential fire hazard.

incident_description:
Sharp 27 inch conventional tube Tv caught on fire. Smoke alams woke us up a 1:00 am.
The Tv was used in the kids play room almost everyday. Tv was off. When we got to the basement there was a foot of smoke covering ceiling. I look the the left and he tv is there with 6 inch flames coming out of where the power switch is. We quickly responded and put out the fire.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident could have been severe due to the fire and smoke, hence a severity level of 2. The likelihood is rated 3 as such incidents, though possible, don't happen daily.

incident_description:
Optical bulb Sony XL 2100 blew. . .examined unit and found plastic door used as 
optical block was melted and burnt.
justification: The incident resulted in damage to equipment but no injuries, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' scenario. The likelihood is 'possible' as such incidents can occur due to equipment failure.

incident_description:
I came across the website https://sites.google.com/site/sonylcdrptvproblems/lamp-overheating-issue
and after my television died i tried to replace the lamp only to find out that the door was starting to melt. the television model is KDF60XBR950 from sony. I contact them with my safety concern and asked that they replace it with a diferent model since it is still under warranty 
http://esupport.sony.com/US/perl/news-item.pl?&news_id=261&mdl=KF60WE610

they offered to repair it but i do not feel safe with this product since they have already tried to fix this problem but the plastic on the tv started melting again. 

I took pictures and i have the repair documentation if you need it,
justification: The incident involved a potential fire hazard due to overheating, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: Purchased an item from Harbor Freight which contained. Three AAA Envo-Max batteries which has oozed a clear liquid from them
justification: The incident involved a product defect (oozing batteries) but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
The consumer states that while driving her vehicle she received a call on her mobile phone. She answered the call talking on her left ear. While on the call for 10 minutes she noticed her face began to burn. 

When the consumer arrived home she looked into the mirror and noticed her cheek (on the left side) was bright red and sore to the touch.

The consumer drove herself to Vaughn Regional Hospital in Selma Al. where she was treated in the Emergency Room. The consumer was treated for First Degree Burns to the left cheek and prescribed medication, then released.

The consumer states that she had charged the phone earlier in the day for only 15 minutes. When the incident occurred the phone did not overheat and was not hot to the touch.

The consumer went to the emergency room on 3/30/2012 and was advised to follow up with her  Primary Care Physician. The consumer has a follow up appointment on 4/3/2012.

The consumer  contacted the retailer and was advised that they would replace the phone with the same model. The consumer states that she declined and was advised to use the mobile device on speaker when talking. 

The consumer states that she has contacted an attorney for the matter (no information on the attorney was provided). She has not and will not contact the firm because her attorney advised her not to.

The consumer currently still uses the phone on speaker phone only.
justification: The consumer suffered first-degree burns, indicating an injury (severity level 3), and while the exact cause is unclear, the event is possible to occur again (likelihood 3) given the consumer's continued use of the phone.

incident_description:
I purchased a microSD memory card, and a SD memory card adapter, from Amazon.com. The brand for both was Amazon Basics. On May 2, I used the adapter for the first time. I inserted a microSD card into the adapter, and placed the adapter into my [REDACTED] computer. Within a few seconds I smelled burning plastic. I removed the adapter. In so doing I sustained a second-degree burn to the tip of my thumb, and a burn to the tip of my forefinger. The heat was so intense that at first I thought I had received an electric shock. The adapter had melted around the memory card. The melting was most intense where the metal contacts of the memory card touched the internal metal contacts of the memory card adapter.

I [REDACTED] "melting sd card adapter" on the internet, and found several other reports of melting SD card adapters, not limited to Amazon Basics brand.
justification: The incident resulted in burns to the user's fingers, and the widespread reports of similar incidents indicate a high likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description: Vizio TV started smoking and burning.  No flames visible.
justification: While no flames were visible, the TV smoking and burning indicates a potential fire hazard, making it an incident with possible reoccurrence.

incident_description: Using a [REDACTED] while reading a book when I heard popping and sizzling sound coming from back of my neck.  Instantly removed [REDACTED] and went to a workshop area to remove battery cover.  Discovered that the Duracell AA battery had overheated and blown the negative cap off the end of the battery.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the incident involved a hazardous situation with a battery overheating, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description: I came home from work one evening to find my Samsung 46" TV base had exploded all over my apartment. There were shards of glass all over my apartment as far as eight feet. I was so baffled by how this could have happened I decided to do some research online only to find that this is a common (or more common than expected) occurrence. The only consistent thing I have seen in YouTube vidoes and other photos is the common exposure to sunlight. The TV was off and has no damage. The core of the base is still intact and thankfully there was no one around when this happened. If someone were within the range of the debris there could have potentially been serious injury from what I can tell. This is very hazardous and I think it is Samsung's responsibility to follow up on this sooner than later before someone really does get hurt.
justification: Although no one was injured, the incident could have caused serious injury if someone had been within the range of the debris.

incident_description: Plugged quartz heater into Prime6-outlet power tap, started to smell plastic burning.Traced the odor to the power tap outlet unplugged heater, removed power tap found that it had started to melt.The wall plug had also started to burn.Called the company but received no response.
justification: No injuries reported, but significant property damage (melted power tap, burned wall plug) indicates a level 2 severity.

incident_description: My daughter pulled out the plug on an electronic unit from the wall, a portable speaker system for he ipod. The plug broke apart, the components spilled out and she tried to put it back together and was shocked. I heard the shock from downstairs. She cried and her hand was numb for a while.
justification: Injury occurred due to electrical shock after the speaker's plug broke and components were exposed.

incident_description: MSI computer motherboard started making a crackling sound and caught fire. There was a strong scent of electrical burn.  Unplugged it quickly and this stopped the fire.  Opened up the case and components inside are burned.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and while it's possible for such an event to occur again, it's not likely.

incident_description:
The consumer used the USB card in a desk top computer for an hour when he noticed that it became extremely hot. The consumer immediately removed it from the computer and while doing so it was hot to the touch. No injuries were reported. 

The consumer examined the USB card and noticed that it was melted on the underside along with the controller chip on the board. 

Approximately five minutes after removing the USB card the consumer attempted to use a different brand USB card. While doing so the computer froze up and would not read the card. 

The consumer reports that he has used the USB card since he purchased it and has never experienced a hazard or any concern with it. 

The consumer has not contacted the firm but states that he will eventually.  The consumer has returned the USB card to the retailer.

The consumer reports that he is glad that he was nearby when the incident occurred because there could have been a  potential fire.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the USB card overheating and melting, along with the subsequent computer freeze, indicates a potential for serious damage or injury.

incident_description:
When I first open the box and put everything together, I place a CD in it to test it.  It would not recognize the CD.  I tried to take it out and it would not open.  I unplugged it and plugged it back in.  The screen went haywire, showing mixes symbols.  I tried unpluggging and plugging it back int, same thing happend.  It still would not open and $15.00 CD was stuck inside.  I tried the radio and cassette player nothing.  I left the room to call a friend to see if he knew how to open it without damaging it to get my CD out. When I came back, I smelled electrical burning.  I rushed to unplug it, it was hot.  I let cool, and plugged it back in, it went haywire again for a few min then it worked and started playing the cd.  I tested everything again and it worked. Next day came home went in to the bedroom where I keep it and it was on.  Turned it off.  That night while sleeping it turned on by itself.  Next day came home, smelled the electrical burning smell and it was on again.  I removed my CD, unplugged and put it back in the box.  Because this was a close out sale, I couldn't take it back.  So I contacted the company  in December 2011for the warranty hoping they would replace it.  No reply to my online submission.  Tried again February 2012, [REDACTED] replied and said they could do nothing.  Ia asked how about the warranty, no reply.  I filed a BBB complaint, the company never replied to BBB.  The unit is cheaply made, worse than anything I've ever seen and could cause a fire.

This unit starts playing when it wants
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning device that could potentially cause a fire, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: Mophie case overheated and melted while charging
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and while overheating can occur, it's not a common occurrence with properly functioning devices.

incident_description: I have a padded tray for my laptop. the light went out and I went to replace the battery,s. I noticed they were warm to the touch. replaced them and the light worked. the next day it was out again checked the batter,s again and they were so hot you could not touch them. It does not matter if the switch is on or off they get hot. the battery,s are jumping spark at the connections. It takes 3 aa battery,s. Even at four and a half volts they are extremely hot. I am worried they will start a fire either on or off in use or not.
justification: Batteries overheating and sparking pose a high risk of fire, though no injuries reported yet.

incident_description: My xbox 360 malfunctioned and I nearly burned myself after trying to get my disk. I tried to bring this up to them and they said there was nothing they could do and that I should not use it. The have failed to see how dangerous this product is. I spent hours online with them then spent more time on the phone with them. No help to fix this unsafe product that was sold to me.
justification: While no injury occurred, the incident could have resulted in burns, making it an incident with potential injury.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she purchased a laptop almost a year ago and she had no problems with it. The computer battery started heating up around the second year, and she decided to purchase a cooling fan for the computer. The consumer decided to stop using battery, because after using it one day it over heated and would not recharge.

The consumer started using the A/C adapter to plug her computer up to use her laptop. The computer was working, but after 30 to 45 minutes the A/C adapter heated up. The computer did not heat up; the A/C adapter heats up turning her computer off. The consumer stated that computer is usable after letting the A/C adapter cool down which takes approximately 30 minutes. 

The consumer burnt her fingers on the left hand when she touched the A/C adapter. She treated the burnt with Preparation [REDACTED] cream. The computer was sitting on a couch which became very hot.

The consumer believes that this is a fire hazard. She stated that the A/C adapter become so hot that she is afraid that it will cause a fire. She feels that this product should be investigated.
justification: Consumer suffered burns due to overheating A/C adapter, indicating a high likelihood of similar incidents.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that on Saturday March 3, 2012 his TV in his restaurant was smoking. The consumer owns a restaurant and has five of these identical TVÃÂs mounted on the walls in the establishment. The consumer came into work on the morning in question and the TV was on for roughly an hour. The consumer saw that the TV began smoking from the back panel. 

Initially, the TV  screen was flickering and then suddenly went black. The consumer ran over and unplugged the TV and soon after the smoking stopped. The consumer went to the retailer that same morning and explained he had an incident happen with an identical TV two days prior. The consumer was told that the retailer could not help him. 

The consumer mentioned that no one was harmed or injured and did not have to call the fire department. The consumer also stated that he has not called his property insurance company. The consumer stated that there is no property damage in the restaurant. Upon inspection of the TV it appears that there was a power failure that caused the incident. 

The consumer said that the TV smoking did not trigger his sprinklers. The consumer found that his TV is similar to the 26 inch models that were cited in release 09-183. His model is a 37 inch model. The consumer believes that the TV is the house brand of the retailer.
justification: No injuries or deaths occurred, but the incident caused property damage (smoking TV).

incident_description: I was watching TV when the glass base on my Samsung TV exploded into a million pieces.  Luckily I was sitting about twelve feet away.  The glass flew about 10 feet in various directions.  If a child had been sitting on the floor near the TV they would have gotten a face full of glass.  It is also supposed to be safety glass but much of it was in small shards.  I have called Samsung and they have told me there have been no recalls.  I am still waiting for an answer on how they will resolve this.  I note there are several incidences of this happening per the internet.  It is a very forcefull explosion and extremely dangerous to anyone that is near it when it happens.  Pictures are attached.  Samsung has said they don't need to see them (at least not yet).
justification: Although no one was injured this time, the forceful explosion of the TV's glass base and the presence of small shards pose a high likelihood of injury in future occurrences.

incident_description: I bought a new Sony Vaio laptop about 6 weeks ago. I sat down today to browse the internet and noticed four of the keys on the keypad have melt marks on them. This poses a potential fire, and or burn hazzard. The laptop never felt warm during use, never felt it was overheating, and when the lid is closed it would apparently go into hibernation. Not sure what is causing the keyboard to melt but it is scarey. No harm was done to me or my home, but the potential exists.
justification: Melt marks on keyboard pose potential fire hazard, but no injury or damage reported.

incident_description: My parents ELEMENT 32" LCD TV was turned off and caught fire.
justification: The TV catching fire is an incident but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
My children received Discovery Toy cameras for Christmas. They all worked well for about two months. Then one of the cameras needed it's battery changed. I went to change it and closed the cover and I could smell it getting really hot. I touched around on it and noticed the battery compartment was really hot. I took the cover off immediately and let it sit. When my husband got home later that night he tried again and it did the exact same thing. Gets really hot on the battery compartment and smells awful. 

Just a week or two ago, we needed to change the batteries in one of the remaining two cameras that still worked. This camera did exactly the same thing as the first. It got really hot and started smelling. I am assuming that these batteries would get hot enough to explode and because it is a camera, a kid is going to have this right up against their face.
justification: Potential for severe burns or facial injury due to battery overheating, given that the camera is designed to be held close to the face.

incident_description:
Purchased a floor lamp at our local Lowe's store that has 2 bulbs, one being a 3-way bulb shinning upwards and another task-reading light.  The fixture came with a 'Zing Ear' current limiter, to prevent over-loading the wiring within the lamp.  The limit is rated for 180 watts.  We have the fixture set up with a 100W max 3-way bulb and a 40W bulb for the task light.

While sitting at the kitchen table (about 15 feet from where the floor lamp is located), I heard a strange noise that lasted for about 5 seconds.  I didn't notice anything wrong when taking a look around the area..  About 10 minutes later, I heard the same noise again, only it was louder this time..  I finally tracked down that it was coming from this Zing Ear current limiter..  What surprised me was the lamp this unit was hooked up to was NOT turned on as it was during the day time hours.  I unplugged the unit and noticed the plastic box of this limiter itself had started to melt.  I have since cut the cord so the lamp can not be used until it can be re-wired properly.  

I just took the 4 screws off the cover of the limiter and find the circuit board is toasted.  Had this happened while we were not at home or at night time, I can see where there is a real serious risk of this unit causing a fire. 

The Zing Ear is model WLD-01 "ZH" and marked with Patent # ZL2006201318934.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the melted limiter posed a high likelihood of causing a fire if undetected.

incident_description:
After connecting the usb cord into the cell phone within 20 minutes  the consumer noticed flames coming from the [USB cable]. The flames were coming from the portion of the [USB cable] that connects to the cell phone.

The consumer was charging the cell phone by using the usb [cord] to his computer. The phone was laying on a glass desk while it was charging He unplugged it immediately and the flames extinguished on their own.

The firm was contacted around 3/2009 and they advised the consumer to mail the [USB cable] back into then so that it could be inspected. 

He returned the cord to the firm and he was advised that he could get a new phone by paying the difference. The consumer has received the new phone and no longer uses the phone that he experienced the failure with. 

There were scorch marks on the end of the phone  where the [USB cable] connects. The [USB cable] was sold with the phone
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident of the USB cable catching fire poses a potential risk to consumers, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' at severity level 2.

incident_description:
In December, 2009 I purchased a Vizio VO400E LCD HDTV from the Costco in Lihue, Hawaii. In March 2010 I was "camping" in the living room with my sons when in the middle of the night, with the T.V. off, I was woken by a loud popping sound. I looked up and could see bright white sparks shooting out of the back of the television and the room filled with the smell of an electrical fire. I got up and unplugged the surge protector that the television was plugged into as quickly as possible fearing that the cord would shock me. 
I was still a few days within the 90 day return period provided by Costco and returned/exchanged it for the same model on 3/6/10.
This morning, 4/15/12, at around 4am my wife was sleeping on the couch with one of my daughters that was sick and had been coughing so much that my wife wanted her to sleep in a more up upright position. Again the television was off when she was woken by the same popping, flashing, and smell that I was two years before.
It's scary to think what may have happened if on both occasions one of us were not in the room to quickly unplug it.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident of the TV sparking and emitting an electrical smell poses a significant risk of injury or property damage if left unattended.

incident_description: B & N Nook Color , AC battery charger and charger cable. Charging cable from charger to the tablet  becomes frayed and loose, exposing the wires at the connection point.   Charger gets very hot to the touch.   B&N refuses to replace after one year, even though a well know problem and product defect that is dangerous.
justification: The exposed wires pose a fire hazard, but no injuries have been reported yet.

incident_description: My Apple iPhone 4s purchased new in December 2011 all of the sudden quit holding a charge. I took it to an apple store on 4.15.12 where they hooked it up to diagnostic software and told me the battery was fine adn they just needed to change some software settings.  As of 4.16.12 the phone was still no holding a charge.  I took it to a non apple service store to get the battery changed and upon doing so they discovered the existing lithium battery had ruptured. This is a very dangerous fire hazard.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (ruptured battery) and could have caused a fire hazard.

incident_description: The consumer stated that his 6 outlet surge protector was a potential fire hazard as last night it flared up. The consumer noticed a flash coming from the indicator light. The consumer unplugged the surge protector from the outlet and the flashing stopped. The consumer stated that he had 3 of the six outlets occupied. The consumer stated that he was not harmed or injured by the product and did not call the fire department. The consumer did not sustain any property damage. The consumer cannot recall the place where he purchased the product. The consumer called the firm this morning and they documented the incident for him.
justification: While no injury or damage occurred, the surge protector's indicator light flaring up indicates a potential malfunction, warranting a 'Incident, No Injury' severity level.

incident_description:
The consumer wanted to express his concerns about his 9.2 volt battery drill as the consumer was working on a job and his battery was very hot. The consumer was operating the drill for a short time after he was inserting 6 screws (one minute elapsed time) before the consumer noticed that the battery began to make a gargling noise. 

The consumer took the battery out of the tool and allowed the battery to cool down. The consumer found that the product smoked for nearly 3 minutes. The consumer was not harmed or injured by the product and did not cause any property damage. The consumer placed another battery in the drill and  the battery seems to be working fine with the drill. 

The consumer did not call the fire department about the issue. The consumer reported that there was no further property damage. The consumer called the retailer  and the firm today; both seemed as  if they were not concerned and referred him to a service center, while the firm explained that there was nothing more that can be done for him. The consumer has not had any problems with the battery prior.
justification: The drill overheated and smoked, but no injury or property damage occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she had plugged in the rechargeable batteries and then removed them from the charger, after they were fully charged.  The batteries were charging for approximately 8 hours, however, she noticed that the batteries seemed to be corroded and the plastic that was covering it had melted.  She stated that the batteries were extremely hot as well.

The consumer had not contacted the manufacturer as yet.

The consumer feels as if this rechargeable battery pack is a safety hazard and should be reported.
justification: Battery overheating and corrosion indicates a potential safety hazard, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
After putting batteries into transmitter for My Zone, the transmitter starting smoking.
It continued to smoke for about five minutes until we removed batteries.
justification: Transmitter smoking indicates a malfunction, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: My HP Pavillion DV4-1275mx laptop computer started smoking and a bright red glow emerged from the area of the left display hinge.  It appeared to be on fire in that area.  The power was quickly disconnected and the battery pulled and the glow and smoke subsided.  The cause has been traced to an abrasion of the screen flex cable by the screen hinge pivot pin, causing an electrical short and incipient burning of the cable insulation and a small portion of the plastic housing around the hinge structure.  The machine is less than 3 years old.  I was riding in the back of a car at the time and had the driver pull off the road until I was sure the smoke and fire hazard was stopped.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a fire hazard, hence severity level 2.

incident_description:

incident_description:
This incident happened on Monday April 2 2012.  Some background: my mother is semi-invalid and almost completely homebound.  She has congestive heart failure and foot trouble.  as a result, she has a hard time getting around. I am her daughter and I live with her.

Mom has a home security service provided by ADT.  She has a personal emergency button that she wears around her neck when she is home alone.  If she falls or has some similar problem, she should be able to push this button and emergency help is notified and should come to help her.

In the afternoon, my mother went out into our back yard and sat on a lawn chair.  One of the back legs of the chair sank into soft ground.  She kept herself from falling backward by catching hold of the backyard grill.

She pushed the ADT personal alert button.  It did not work.  She sat in the back yard for at least a half hour, holding herself up against the grill and calling and waving for help.  Finally a neighbor, who was out for a walk, heard her, came into the yard and helped her get out of the chair.

Mom called ADT about the unresponsive personal alert button.  They made sympathetic sounds, but told her this was essentially her fault, that she was supposed to call them on a regular basis to make sure the device is working.

The button is sealed, so we can't change a battery in it.  There is no light or other indicator on it to tell users that it is failing or has stopped working.

When a device fails in manufacturing, production just shuts down.  When this kind of device fails in the field, a person, like my mother, may die of a heart attack.  This was the first time she really needed to use it, and when she did, it was defective and ADT's system failed.  She could have died as a result.  She's had that particular device for, I would estimate, 5 years.  They have since sent her a new one after this happened. It is significant that they required my mother to send the defective one back to them before they would give her a new one.  Obviously the company does not want defective equipment in the field where their incompetence can be investigated with it.

my point is, ADT should not place the onus on the customer to keep calling ADT to make sure their device is working.  Because it is a life-saving device, they should learn what the operative life span of these things are, then send customers new ones proactively when these things approach the end of their operative life, instead of requiring customers to do their due diligence for them and continually call ADT "to see if the device is still working". 

There could be hundreds of these non-responsive devices currently in use by ADT's clients, who are fragile and unwell.  What percentage of these devices are in use but are not working?  That is why I am calling you to report this.  By the way, I used to do product failure investigations for CPSC in the Chicago area back in the 1980's.  I was a "commissioned officer", as they called it.  This incident really bugs me, and I think the training I got from your organization sort of kicked in when this happened to my mother.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the incident could have resulted in serious harm or death due to the device's failure.

Lamp Overheating Issue 
Compiled by [REDACTED]
Last updated 3/21/2011

Between 2002 and 2007, Sony Electronics Inc. manufactured numerous large-screen high-definition rear-projection TV models based on liquid crystal microdisplay technology. These TVs contain a high-intensity mercury vapor arc lamp to produce the image. All of the 2003 models and some of the 2004 models contain a design defect that makes them susceptible to being warped, melted, cracked, scorched, and/or burnt by an overheated projection lamp, which can cause the TVs to fail to power up. In addition, it can cause heat damage outside of the TV, so it could pose a risk of injury and/or property damage. This includes all TVs that contain the designations "WE" or "XBR950" in their model names (see the full list of models in the table below, as well as sample pictures). Note that, as of the date of the last update of this web page, the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission has not compelled a recall, although multiple reports have been filed.

Photo of KF-50WE610 lamp access door by [REDACTED] posted on an Agoraquest forum:



The projection lamp is a user-replaceable part that is located in the lower-front area of the TV. Beneath the main viewing screen, there is a removable plastic trim panel. Behind the trim panel, there is a removable plastic door (the "lamp access door") used to access the lamp for replacement. Warping of this door is often the first evidence of the overheating issue. However, heat damage to the door is usually not evident unless the aforementioned trim piece is removed (e.g., during a lamp replacement). In addition, even if damage to the door is minor or not detectable, other parts adjacent to the lamp on the inside of the TV could be warped, melted, cracked, scorched, and/or burned.

Therefore, I encourage everyone with WE or XBR950 TVs to check their lamp access door and other areas surrounding the lamp for any signs of heat-related damage. To do this, go through the "Replacing the Lamp" procedure contained in the Operating Instructions that came with your TV, including removing the lamp. Follow Sony's procedure carefully so as not to damage your TV. If you no longer have your Operating Instructions, they can be accessed at the links in the table below.

If you find evidence of heat damage, I encourage you to take pictures and send them to me. More importantly, if you feel that the problem could be a safety issue (potential injury or property damage), I encourage you to file a Consumer Product Incident Report with the Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC). Currently, Sony does not actively inform all customers of the problem, but the CPSC could compel them to issue a recall with mandatory notification, if they find the issue to be a safety issue. Incident reports from customers are essential to this process, and there is evidence that the CPSC has started to take actions.

Sony has issued four warranty extensions for this issue, which they have restricted to arguably obscure notices on their support web site. The fourth notice, which was released in March of 2011, extended the coverage through 3/31/2012. Sony refers to the defect as "warping of the lamp access door," and they claim that damage to other components is rare, and that "...this issue has been evaluated extensively and...there are no product safety concerns." However, pictures I have seen do not seem to be consistent with these claims. Damage to components other than the lamp access door seem common, which is not surprising since the lamp and reflector actually face away from the door. In addition, some pictures show relatively extensive damage to the interior of the TV, including burnt wires, which raises safety concerns, as well as damage to a TV stand directly under the lamp area.

Sony's warranty extension states: "Sony will repair the lamp access door and any other components damaged as a result at no charge for any of the covered televisions." When the issue was first identified, a repair kit was apparently provided by Sony to repair technicians, which reportedly included a replacement lamp access door, three replacement fans (presumably for enhanced cooling), and a revised thermal switch (presumably to shut down the TV at a lower overheat temperature).

Unfortunately, in apparent contradiction to their own warranty, federal warranty law, and other laws requiring availability of replacement parts (see details below), beginning around October of 2009 or earlier, Sony began telling at least some customers that they would not or could not repair their TVs, and that they should pay Sony for a discounted replacement TV instead. Interestingly, the alert on the Sony Canada web site only refers to getting a discount off another Sony TV.

In some cases, Sony claimed that they were out of the repair kits. In other cases, Sony claimed that the heat damage was too severe to repair. In many cases, customers have both an optical block problem and the melting issue, which is not surprising since heat is a contributing factor to optical block failure. Adding insult to injury, in some of these latter cases, Sony apparently justified their position that the TV was not repairable by citing the optical block problem, as opposed to physical heat damage to parts.

Regardless of any of the above claims, I believe US laws require that, if Sony is unwilling or unable to repair your TV free of charge, they must replace it with another reasonably equivalent TV free of charge (e.g., equivalent size and features, although it could be a refurbished model). See the legal information below for reference.

For methods for dealing with Sony, please refer back to the Options for repair, replacement, and/or legal action section on the main page.

On April 15, 2010, a class action lawsuit was filed in US District Court, Southern District of California for the lamp overheating issue that affects the 2003-2004 3LCD models WE and XBR950.

incident_description: One of our employees received a mild shock from portable equipment powered from a Coleman Cable POLAR/SOLAR "Quadnector" extension cord. These UL listed extension cords terminate in a 4-receptacle power block. Investigation discovered that the shock came from normal leakage current from the equipment and that one of the extension cord's receptacles had lost continuity to the ground pin on the portable equipment's plug. Other "Quadnector" cords on site were tested, and 13 of 14 cords tested had the same lack of continuity on one or more receptacles. While some of the cords had been in service for some time, at least one was new and still in its original packaging. Concurrently, the Pacific Northwest National Laboratory (PNNL)  found the same issue on a "Quadnector" cord at their site and submitted that cord to CCI. CCI sent an email to us saying that they had duplicated the lack of continuity condition with the cord submitted by PNNL and offered to replace our similar cords. Our site instructed employees to turn in all "Quadnector" cords. During the collection, a few discontinued cords from Coleman Cable Systems and Electrical Conductors, Inc. (ECI) were turned in during the collection.  These cords are similar to the "Quadnector" cords but have solid yellow receptacle blocks. Tests on these cords showed that they also had a loss of continuity on the grounding conductor. Tests done by us at our site on other CCI extension cords having only one or three receptacles did not find a lack of grounding continuity.
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the incident involved a mild shock, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' (Severity Level 2). The widespread issue with the extension cords and the confirmation by the manufacturer indicate a high likelihood of occurrence (Likelihood 4).
