incident_description:
This letter is being sent to you about an incident concerning a BELKIN backup battery Mod.
#BU3DCOOl-12V, SN #BDC-11B42598D2.
In November, we were having problems with our TV signal. AT&T customer service was called
and a technician was sent out. The problem with our TV was fixed. Shortly thereafter, we
started having problems with our telephone. Again, I called customer service and was told we
needed an updated modem. The modem arrived along with a new backup battery referenced
above, which we really didn't need since the original backup battery was working fine. I then
installed both the new modem and the new battery.
On December 19, my wife had several messages on her cell phone from AT&T. The message
stated that several e-mails had been sent to us and that the referenced battery needed to be
replaced. We both checked our e-mails and our spam folders and we could not find any e-mails
from AT&T. A toll-free number[REDACTED] was also given to call. My wife called on
Tuesday, December 20th. The toll free number, as it turned out, was to the BELKIN company.
The representative asked for the serial number of the battery (80C-II84259802) and she was
told that was indeed a defective battery. My wife asked what the defect was and was told that
the battery would not provide back-up power in case of a power outage. She was told that a
new battery would be sent and should arrive in 3-5 days. The battery arrived late Thursday
evening, December 22nd. I did not install the battery on Thursday since we were led to believe
that the only problem with the battery was that it might not provide the backup needed in case
of a power outage.
On December 23rd, we were awakened by our dog barking at 4 a.m. We immediately could
smell the odor of burning wires. After a search of the house, we determined the smell was
coming from our office and, specifically, the battery. It was no coincidence that the same week
we were advised of a defect in the battery that we had this incident. My wife called tech
support for Belkin and all she was told was the battery we were sent was among a bad batch of
batteries. She kept questioning the agent at Belkin asking if the real problem with the battery
was a safety/fire hazard and not the original reason we were given and the lady said: "how can
I say this to you" and then immediately asked if there was anything else she could do for her.
Needless to say, we are very disappointed in the way this matter was handled by both the
BELKIN company and AT&T. If we had been told from the beginning that the battery was a
potential fire hazard, I would have immediately disconnected it and waited for the replacement
battery to arrive. Fortunately for us, we were home at the time, but, if we had not been home
we definitely would have had a fire with dire consequences for us. At this time, our perception
is that we were misled about the reason we were given regarding the defect in the battery and,
we are seriously considering other options for cable service. Enclosed you will find five photos
of the internal parts of the battery case.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (burns from smoke inhalation) and could have caused death if not at home.

incident_description:
I used a Wagman Tech Car FM Transmitter (Item # 2516) (this is a type of MP3 player) with a [REDACTED] USB memory
stick to play MP3 music through my car radio while driving at night. The memory stick contains an LED indicator
light which flashes when the memory module is accessed by a computer (or MP3 player in this case.) The LED was
very bright compared to the interior of my car at night, and was flashing at the rate of about 5 Hz (5 times per
second.) After about 5 minutes, I suddenly felt like I was waking up from being unconscious. The image of the road
I saw was skewed, even though my head was straight. I suffered from vertigo and mild nausea for the rest of the
night. It took me a minute to realize that I was suffering from Flicker Vertigo (http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki!
Flicker_vertigo), and I immediately turned the MP3 player off. I did not suffer further problems. I have been tested
for Epilepsy, and am certain that I DO NOT suffer from it. I have never suffered from these symptoms prior to this.

Had I not been aware of the phenomenon, it is likely I would have continued listening to the music, being distracted
by the flashing LED, suffered additional episodes, and been involved in an automobile accident.

As an electrical engineer, it is my opinion that this issue is not unique to this model or brand of transmitter or
memory device, but could potentially affect drivers using ANY type of MP3 player with ANY brand of memory stick
any time between sunset and sunrise.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (vertigo and nausea) and could have led to a severe accident if not addressed.

incident_description:
In the morning of 1/1/2012 my wife smelled smoke, and we traced the source to a desktop computer. I found that there was a fire (flames) inside the computer. After disconnecting the computer, I removed the hot computer, blew out the flames, and moved the smoking computer outside in order to remove the source of the smoke and let the PC cool down. I then opened windows and turned on several fans to remove smoke from the area.

I inspected the computer and took pictures during the inspection and disassembly. The source of the fire was an LG HD DVD drive, Model: GGC-H20L, SN: 803ZBHC002073, Date: March 2008 03 31. The rear of the drive was heavily charred. The flames that were observed during removal were being fueled by the burning plastic of the power and SATA connectors at the rear of the drive. The flames also melted and set fire to the plastic filter screen that was part of the InWin chassis.NOTE: The filter screen and the PC were not dusty since the PC had been located in the side cabinet of an oak "Mission sytle" office desk. The pictures that I took show the chassis before disassembly and the subsequent disassembly. I also have saved the defective DVD drive in a plastic "zip lock" bag.

The PC had been located on a shelf of the side cabinet of an oak desk. There were about 6 inches of clearance on the sides, about three inches of cleaance above the PC, and at least 10 inches of clearance at the rear. The front door of the cabinet had been open, and there was no significant dust in the cabinet or the PC. Ventilation was not obstructed, and there were no other sources of heat.

Although there was not much fuel within the PC that had not been already consumed by the flames, there was probably a reasonable chance that the fire would have spread to the desk, the office, and the house. Thus there could the house could have burned down, and there could have been a loss of life.

The DVD drive had not been used during the prevoius 24 hours prior to this incident, and had actually been used very infrequiently. A file had been burned to a DVD disk a few days before the fire without any problems.

I expect that the fire in this LG DVD drive was caused by failed components. While looking at a review of a small PC chassis earlier this week I noted a comment by the reviewer who noted that the capacitors that had been used on the chaassis power supply had been implicated in some electronic fires, so my current concern is that the LG DVD drive also was made using similar capacitors, which also failed and caused the fire.

Besides the concern that the LG GGC-H20L drive was defective due to poor components such as a dangerous type of capacitor, I am now concerned about whether other LG DVD drives also contain the same types of defective comonents. If evidence shows that this type of component has a chance of causing fires when they fail, I feel that they should be recalled and replaced with DVD drives that use more reliable components.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the fire could have spread to the desk, office, and house, potentially leading to significant property damage and risking lives.

incident_description: December 24th 2011, while getting ready for a Christmas Eve party I was in my bathroom downstairs while my girlfriend was upstairs finishing getting ready in my room.  The multi-outlet surge protector was plugged into an outlet in my bedroom upstairs.  The wall outlet (top) had a controller (remote on/off switch) receiver plugged in with two Christmas lights in series.  While the bottom outlet had the surge protector plugged in with three items plugged in at the time; a plasma TV, the cable box, and my girlfriendÃÂs hair straightener.  Typically only the TV and cable box are plugged into the surge protector, the top outlet usually will have one light plugged into the controller receiver.  While I was downstairs getting ready I heard my girlfriend call my name, I started heading up the stairs when I heard her call my name again except with more urgency so I ran.  By the time I reached the top of the stairs smoke was filling the room and I saw my girlfriend standing over the surge protector while it was on fire.  Fire was coming from the open outlets and had actually melted through the bottom.  I picked the item up, shaking it and blowing it out, then unplugged the item from the wall.  There was still power in the room, the circuit was not broken.  My girlfriend said she had the hair straightener plugged in with no issues, when she turned it on the surge protector started crackling and making buzzing sounds as well as sparks being seen inside the unit, spurring her first cry for help.  After she tried to unplug the hair straightener the unit caught fire causing her to scream for my help, I then ran up the stairs and put the fire out.  The room was filled with black smoke and burn marks were on the wood floor.  The surge protector appears fine on top but actually has a hole melted through the bottom.  Once I cleaned up the black marks on the floor all that was left were two dime size burn holes in the wooden floor.  The hair straightener appears to work although the plug was a little blackened by the fire.  The tv and cable box seem to work fine, after I replaced the outlet in the wall and hooked up a new surge protector I plugged both back in and they turned on without issue.  The only major damage was the burn marks in the floor, no injuries happened in the incident.

incident_description:
I purchased a Sony Rear Projection Television in 2003, a Sony KDF60XBR950. It was their top of the line TV that I was assured I would never have to replace, only purchase a new lamp in the future when the lamp "wore out."  About 3-4 years in I needed to replace a lamp in the unit, and one was replaced for me under my extended warranty that I purchased. When I replaced the lamp I noticed that the plastic door assembly seemed to be somewhat warped. But the salespeople at the location where I purchased the TV told me that it wasn't an issue, only a lamp and "not to worry."  After my television was outside of the warranty period I began noticing that the lamp access door was warping further to the point where it would no longer stay in place, and the television would intermittently turn off and then back on. When I called the place where I purchased my television I was told that it was outside of the warranty period and that they couldn't service the television and the closest television repair center for Sony was in Billings, MT - over 200 miles from my home. 

I was told again to replace the lamp in my TV, which I did, and paid for retail out of my own pocket. At this point there was severe warping of the lamp access door but I was assured that Sony had been in contact with the specialty retailer and that there were no "problems" to worry about andthat it was simply from "letting the tv run too long during the summer" and not to worry. Roughly a year later another lamp burst inexplicably after watching sports on the tv for a few hours.

At this point in time I began to be concerned as I went to replace the lamp again (I'd purchased a couple of lamps as backups as it was cheaper to buy a lamp than another $6,000 television) and the door assembly was completely warped and would no longer fit on the front of the television and wouldn't allow the TV to turn on any longer even after replacing the lamp. I examined the insides of the lamp assembly unit and there was significant warping and scorching from what looked to be excessive heat inside the unit. I checked online with Sony and there was no incidents reported on their website that were readily available for my particular unit. It wasn't until I browsed around the Internet that I discovered I wasn't alone and there were thousands of others who had the same problem with their televisions. One of the links from a forum about warped lamp doors on Sony TV's said that Sony was going to extend a warranty out to cover this problem. I followed the link to Sony's website and it spelled out that there were no known safety issues but that they would "repair" the television for free - see link (http://esupport.sony.com/US/perl/news-item.pl?&news_id=261&mdl=KF60WE610)

Upon contacting Sony I was first told by a customer service agent that I would need to call someone and have the TV repaired myself, to which I responded that their website was contradicting their own statements. After several more phone calls a local TV repair center was contacted and they came to look at my television.

When the TV tech arrived he told me that he'd need to take apart the television to look for damage to the unit. Upon completing his inspection he told me that there was extensive heat damage to the unit, inside the television itself things were warped, there were wires that had overheated, melted and were burnt and the surrounding areas also showed heat damage issues. When I asked how such a thing could happen without so much as a safety email from Sony he said "they know that these things are dangerous, but they simply won't admit to it because they will owe consumers millions in settlements." 

My television like many consumers is located in the middle of the house and next to my child's bedroom. The repair tech stated on the phone and in person that "there have been incidents where these televisions and this problem have caused fires." Yet I was never contacted to be warned that my TV could have overheated, and burnt down my house. I was told the only reason my entire television unit hadn't burnt down or overheated completely and melted was that I kept it in a well ventilated area on a stand

At best this is simple oversight, at worst it's criminal negligence on the part of Sony for not reporting clear safety hazards in their television units. Something should be done so that other customers whom haven't experienced any outward signs of damage to their television aren't caught by surprise when their televisions fail and possibly cause irreversible damage.
justification: Potential for severe injury or property damage due to fire, as evidenced by the TV technician's report of heat damage and the risk of fire.

incident_description:
I bought two Apple MacBook Pro 17-inch laptops (Macintosh) for personal and office use.

Both of these computers came with the standard OEM factory parts, including the Apple-branded rechargeable lithium ion battery, as it should.

What should NOT happen is the following: In the 2 years of owning them, I have always exercised safe and very gentle operating and maintenance of the computers (I BABY THEM; I know how sensitive and delicate electronics can be, plus I never want to get even a scratch on the nice aluminum body).

I followed all the guidelines in the printed and electronic documentation included with the computers (including the user guide/manual). I always have and always do.

HOWEVER I noticed one day that the trackpad (built in touch pad) was difficult to operate and sometimes clicking was especially difficult. Soon I felt the computer was rocking back and forth. So I looked underneath and saw that the rechargeable battery had expanded/swollen out of its "normal" size. I knew something was wrong so I took it in to the "genius" bar at the Apple Store in Santa Monica, California (Third Street Promenade), where they brushed this incident off as "normal" and "the battery does that when it is consumed and no longer works. Time to buy a new battery." I replied that the battery still holds a solld 3 to 4 hour charge, and that System Profiler reports the battery status as "Normal" as far as charge-holding and discharging capacity. It was working fine for what it was made for, but not working fine as far as my computer's keyboard and trackpad operation. They suggested I spend $142 on a new battery (129 + 10.25% Tax). Or buy a bulk packaged battery from the genius bar for "only" $100. I denied their sales pitch and said that this was a manufacturing defect, and that I was worried it might further expand and burst. "Isn't this a health and safety issue? can't this cause a fire, and therefore possible damage and even death?" They didn't know what to say. I repeated that I would like a replacement free of charge for this manufacturing defect. They said no. So I left and continued to use the computer. The battery held a charge just fine. Well the next morning I came to my Office and the battery had indeed burst open, spewing some kind of chemical/gook all over my desk. It smelled like burning metal. I took it back to the genius bar, and they again said this was normal and that Apple is not responsible for it. Because my computer was "out of warranty" they felt they had no need to replace the now exploded Apple battery. 

A couple months later, I removed the Apple battery from my other 17-inch MacBook Pro, as I was leaving town for a couple weeks and feared a repeat of it blowing up in my house, possibly burning down the building. I placed in on my office desk and  when I came back from my trip, amazingly, the removed battery had somehow swollen up to the point of bursting the metal battery casing apart. No goo/liquid escaped this time, but the product was clearly unusable. I can see the cells inside bloated up. This is clearly not normal. This is a manufacturing defect that Apple is trying to cover up. If you google the phrase "Apple MacBook Pro Battery exchange" or even "Apple Macintosh PowerBook battery recall fires", you will see a lot of this happening in the past, and you'll see that up until 2008 or 2009, Apple admitted fault in their OEM laptop/notebook batteries, and said there is a risk of fire. They offered to replace such batteries for certain models/years, free of charge, no questions ask, regardless of Warranty status. This program for MacBook Pros (same model year as mine) is now closed. you can see the page still on Apple.com if you search the above. But they knew about the issues and HAD a recall, but ONLY for 15-inch MacBook Pros (as opposed to my 17-inch MB Pro), and they decided that they weren't responsible for any of them explooding, burning, catching fires, possibly destroying homes and possibly claiming human lives. Why? They fessed up before!

I called AppleCare (Customer Relations) and they interviewed me with a barrage of questions, it felt like a court deposition. They said they'd get back to me on what their "engineers find." I said okay, but never heard back from them. I called and left several kind but persistant messages. No callback, no reply, no replacement battery. No apology for possibly burning my house down while i slept. 

APPLE, YOU NEED TO DO THE RIGHT THING LEGALLY, MORALLY, and BEYOND. 

REPLACE ALL SWOLLEN BATTERIES FOR FREE WITHOUT HASSLE. 

DON'T LET THESE "normal" BATTERIES EXPLODE ON ANYONE ELSE.

Apple should issue a RECALL and offer one of their EXTENSION REPAIR PROGRAMS on their site apple.com and/or issue a full refund to owners who have already been FORCED to buy a new battery from Apple at almost $150 after tax per battery.

I thank you, APPLE COMPUTERS INC., for correcting this mistake in all fairness, and in accordance with U.S. Consumer Protection Laws.

incident_description:
I purchased a replacement cord connector for an extension cord.  The connector is a 3 bladed female cord connector (Two 2 flat blades and one U shaped ground blade, NEMA 5-15R configuration) marked for 15 amps and 125 volts AC.

DEFECT: The flat neutral blade is connected internally to the U shaped ground blade (inside the molded housing), creating a pathway for electric current to energize any metal component of an appliance connected through this cord connector. 

When plugged into a 120-volt circuit which has a Ground Fault Circuit Interrupter, this causes the GFCI to trip.  This happened to me when I installed the cord connector in accordance with the instructions provided.  Therefore, I checked the polarity of the hot and neutral terminals and discovered that the neutral terminal of the cord connector is connected to the U shaped ground blade inside the molded housing of the cord connector

This causes the connector to trip any Ground Fault Circuit Interrupter, if present in the circuit the cord is plugged into.  Unfortunately, if the defective connector is used in an ordinary 120-volt circuit without a GFCI device, 120 volts can flow through the grounding wire and into any appliance which has a 3 prong plug that is plugged into this defective connector.  

Since this incorrect configuration will not trip an ordinary circuit breaker, the user is unaware of the ground fault.  Any metal component of an appliance connected through this defective cord connecter would have a full 120 volts available to flow through the unaware user if the user became grounded by touching a water faucet, for example This is a serious shock hazard which could result in death.
justification: The defect allows 120 volts to flow through the grounding wire, posing a serious shock hazard that could result in death.

incident_description:

On 9/15/2011, my daughter and a group of friends were walking home from school, she had the cell phone in her pants pocket and the Nokia phone began to get really hot at which time my daughter reached in her pocket and pulled out the phone.  Once she got the phone in her hand she noticed smoke coming from the battery compartment and the phone shocked her, the heat was so hot that she dropped it then the back of the phone flew off the phone, the battery flew out and the phone was on fire. My daughter was so scared and after the fire went out she went to pick the phone up which also burned her hand.
 
On 9/16/2011, I placed a phone call to the pre-paid customer care and told them about my issue and the representative indicated that there was nothing they could do and when I asked to speak with a supervisor they transferred me to technical support.  The technical support representative told me that he was very sorry but that he could not do anything but make a note on the account. I told him to make a note and let me speak to a supervisor at this time the representative told me that their supervisor would not be able to help me so I would have to take the phone back to the store that I purchased it from. I then told the tech support representative to make a note in the account that I will be coming to the T-Mobile store the next morning, 9/17/2011.

She pulled up my account and stated that the note said for her to call when I arrived at the store.  [REDACTED] place the call to pre-paid customer service and was transferred back and forth from customer care to technical support, from technical support to customer care and again to technical support then back to customer care.  At this time, I asked to speak with customer care myself and the representative [REDACTED] informed me that I should contact Nokia and that my phone did not have a warranty, that I could recieve a replacement phone but she could not tell me if they would be able to do anything further for me.  At this time, I informed her that this product is defective and not subject to warranty restriction and that I would not like a replacement but would like my money back for the defective phone and for the month I have paid. She told me that this is not an option.. At this time, shel then asked to speak with [REDACTED]  again and then transferred her to someone else to find out if my account could be credited or something.  I left the store and after 1 hour of being transferred [redacted] was still on hold, when I left.  I have to applaud her because she did try to help me as much as she could.  I then placed a call to T-mobile customer care from my cell phone and was told that there was no corporate number address or supervisor who would be able to help me and that I would have to call pre-paid customer service .
 
I called pre-paid customer service again and reached [REDACTED]  and then asked to speak with yet another supervisor. she offer me a replacement phone but like I told her, "why would I want to replace the phone with a similar phone that traumatized my child?" then she told me that if I wanted the replacement she would see if I could get it before the 2-3 week delivery time that it normally takes, I told her, "No Thanks" and transfer me to her supervisor. I then asked supervisor for the corporate phone number and he told me that there was not one and I would have to write the P.O. Box.

I am very concerned that this could happen to another child or adult who has the same phone but may not be so lucky when and if it catches on fire as my daughter's phone did.  My daughter doesn't even want another cellphone from T-Mobile.  The pre-paid department has been extremely shady in my eyes and is ruining the reputation of T-Mobile with their underhanded ways of transfer after transfer, rude demeanor and ridiculous hold times. I made a payment one time via telephone and was transferred 3 times and then told my public record information would have to be pulled to confirm my payment, that was another day, ridiculous nevertheless.   I feel as though, if T-mobile is going to contract out its superior service it should make sure the contractor shares the same views of customer service and quality. justification: While no injuries were reported, the incident involved a potentially hazardous electrical failure in a consumer device, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' (Level 2) with a high likelihood of occurrence given the number of similar reports.

incident_description:
On September 14, 2011, I turned on my television and the DirecTV box, the television came on, but, the DirecTV box did not. Followed instructions given by DirecTV to check the box, it still did not work. They are sending a new box.

On September 15, 2011, in the morning was walking into the bedroom when I noticed smoke and the room smelled like an "electrican burn" was in progress. Noticed smoke comming from within the DirecTV box. unpluged and took it outside. Smoke was very powerful and toxic. Aired the room with fan and open windows.

Have box. Holding it for your inspection. Will not return it to DirecTV unless told to do so.

PLEASE ADVISE WHAT YOU RECOMMEND...

Thank you.

[REDACTED]
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a fire hazard, making it an incident with potential for injury.

incident_description: I purchased a GPX CD Boombox model BC111W on 3-29-11 as a gift for my daughterÃÂs birthday. We starting using the boombox in her bedroom on a dresser in late April. One week later I discovered that the product was overheating. The four black rubber feet on the bottom of the boombox had partially melted leaving four black marks on the dresser. There were also brown scorch marks on the dresser top where the boombox was placed. I contacted the manufacturer on 9-8-11 and was given a response on 9-14-11 that this was a normal occurrence and there was nothing that they would do to fix the damage to the dresser. The damage is so severe that I will need to have the dresser top refinished. The dresser was new. It was purchased in January 2011. I am concerned that this product is a fire hazard.
justification: The product's overheating caused damage to the dresser, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: Duracell silver oxide battery 303/357 exploded. I put two of them into an electronic tire pressure gauge. When it didn't work, I took them out and replaced them the other way. It still didn't work. I suspected the gauge was bad anyway. I left the battery's in for a few days. Tonight, I took them out and put them in the original package, then taped the package closed with two inch clear packing tape. I set the package of batteries on my garage counter, and after about 5 minutes, I heard a loud POP and then a tinkle across my garage. I looked over at the battery package and had seen that one of the batteries had exploded and threw shrapnel across the garage. What was curious was that this occurred after the batteries had been in the device for days, and that then in the package for a number of minutes after removal. Pictures are enclosed.
justification: The battery explosion caused property damage but no injuries, and while similar incidents are possible, the specific circumstances (battery type, duration in device, packaging) make it less likely.

incident_description: Sony Bravia 40 LCD TV, purchased December 2007, today started smoking with an acrid smell and turned itself off.  I am sure that if I tried to turn it back on, a fire might have ensued.  This is a very dangereous situation and indicates some problem with quality control.
justification: The TV starting to smoke and emitting an acrid smell indicates a high likelihood of fire if turned back on, posing a significant risk.

incident_description:
Investigator stated that the laptop was placed on the bed plugged in but not powered on.  The smoke detector alerted the occupants and they went to the bedroom and noticed that there was small flames emitting from the location of the laptop, they used the fire extinquisher to put the fire out which left a charred spot of where the laptop was located.

Respondent stated that the power cord and the exterior sides was damaged, melted. After incident, laptop still operated on battery power. Due to the occupants quick response, the fire was contained.  The fire department was called and a fire report filed.
justification: Although the laptop caused a small fire, no injuries were reported due to the occupants' quick response.

incident_description: I was using  my Acer aspire one, after about 30 min of use it shut off, I tried to restart the computer and it would come on then shut right down again. With no luck restarting I reached up to close the computer and I burned my thumb on the upper left where it says acer on the border of the monitor. After I pulled my thumb away I could see where the plastic had melted. I tried to call Acer, but they said because it was out of warranty they could not do anything. I found on the acer website where they had some recalls [REDACTED], but my computer was not part of the recall. They were not willing to let me explain my issue.
justification: Burn injury occurred due to computer overheating and melting, which is possible but not common.

incident_description: My laptop gets extremely hot. When it is placed on a wooden table the table gets so hot that it is warm to touch on the bottom of the table. If you place the laptop on your lap after a short time it will start burning your legs (they will become reddened and hurt). It is very hot to touch. This is a huge hazard. My father-in-law also owns the same model laptop and has the same issues with it being very hot all of the time.
justification: Laptop overheating causes burns on user's legs, posing a high risk of injury.

incident_description:
Our office has purchased several Digital Concepts Converter Drives (USB), Model CR45TD-R, for conververting XD disk drives.  If the USB converter is not removed from the computer immediately after use it begins to overheat and the plastic shell beigns to melt.  This has happened at several different work stations in our office.

This morning the USB was left in for approximately thirty minutes and it begin to overheat.  It was not noticed until office personnel noted a burnt oder.

This product was initially purchased from Radio Shack.  I beleive more recent purchases were made through Amazon.
justification: The USB converter overheating and melting is an incident, but no injuries have been reported.

incident_description:
(8/9/11) At 5:00am, The TV/DVD player was plugged into an electrical outlet at the time of the incident, but it was in the "off" position.  The consumer's 11 year old son was awakened by smoke and flames coming from the back of the TV.  The son yelled that there was a fire in his room and he ran out of the room.

The consumer's husband extinguished the fire and they also called the fire department.  The husband used a blanket to put out the fire and then he sprayed it with a fire extinguisher.  The flames were approximately 2' tall.  The incident lasted about 5 minutes.  The entire back of the product is charred, but the front screen is still intact.

There was soot and smoke damage to the room.  Two adjacent rooms were affected by soot damage.  The carpet in the son's room had to be replaced and the room had to be repainted.  


The consumer contacted her insurance company [REDACTED] and the estimates are still being worked out.  The consumer said that so far it is in the ball park of $10,000.

(8/10/11)  The consumer called the mfr. and she was given a reference number [REDACTED].  The consumer provided details about the incident and she was told that someone in their corporate office would call them back.

There were no injuries.
justification: Although there was a fire, no injuries occurred, but the incident could have been more severe.

incident_description:
I have a Sony Vaio VGN-SZ750N laptop computer.  This device discharges a constant, direct current, shock through the user when the touchpad and/or chassis.  This discharge is enough to feel highly uncomfortable to a grown adult.

This device was returned at the request of Sony who in turn did not fix the issue after holding the device for three weeks longer than agreed upon.  The device was under the direction of the San Diego office for this time and to address the issue I was provided a new AC/DC power adapter.  This does not correct the problem.  I filed a complaint with the BBB and was only offered a refund if I could provide a receipt.  The device was purchased from the Sony Store the summer of 2008 and I, as well as Sony, am unable to locate an original receipt.
justification: The incident involves discomfort but no injury, and the likelihood of occurrence is possible given the history of the device.

incident_description: Lacerated finger on sharp edge corner of battery cover when sliding open.
justification: Injury occurred due to sharp edge, but not life-threatening.

incident_description: The Battery gets so HOT you can't handle the laptop, in fear of burning yourself. It smelled like it was going to start on fire. It no longer functions.
justification: The incident involved a hot battery with potential fire risk, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
Swimp3 player made by Finis allows you to listen to music while swimming 
The swimp3 player needs to plug in to your usb drive every few hours of use in order to recharge it or to add or delete music.
When I plugged it in yesterday, I started to smell burning rubber about a half hour later.  I touched the plastic connector and it burned my finger.  It was very hot and the heat had melted the plastic insulation, exposing the raw wiring.  I'm not aware of anything wrong with my usb port or computer that would cause this.

I imagine it would be quite dangerous if it was then worn in the pool, as intended, and turned on with the wiring exposed.
justification: Exposed wiring from overheating poses a high risk of electrical shock in a wet environment like a pool.

incident_description:
Caller had been watching television all day that he had purchased online (Shop NBC) in 2006.

He walked out of the room for approximately twenty minutes then returned to room thinking he would continue watching television but when he walked into the room he saw a white smoke coming out of the product.

He walked over to it and saw that the wires inside of the television were burning/glowing & that the insulation on the wiring he believed was already burned/fried.

He immediately pulled the plug out of the wall.

He contacted the online purchasing station 08/16/2011, was asked, "What do you want us to do about it", he replied that he was merely informing them and he then was told that the manufacturer was out of business.
Caller did not obtain name.

Shop online identifying #'s  Item# = V35788, Invoice# [REDACTED] dated 07/21/2006, Order# [REDACTED]
justification: Although no injury occurred, the incident involved a potential fire hazard due to faulty wiring in the television.

incident_description:
My husband and I really enjoyed this monitor for the first few months that we had it. We even bought a second camera to put elsewhere in the house so that we could monitor his playtime.

However, on 09/01/11 at 2:00am, I woke to the sound of static coming from the monitor. My husband reached over and tried to turn the video feed on (the screen had gone black), but it wouldn't come on. Just a black screen and static on the audio. He turned it off and back on, same result. Then he turned the device over and we could see a bright glow coming from the little vents on the back of the device, and could quickly smell the odor of burning electronics as the back inside of the device caught fire. We immediately jumped out of bed, unplugged the device from the wall and carried it outside by the antenna.  

The device was plugged directly into a wall outlet, not into any crazy chain of surge protectors or anything else, and had never been wet, played with, handled by our child, pet, was not close to any moisture or heat, etc. or anything else out of the ordinary. It was simply sitting on our nightstand like every other night for the past 4+ months. 

This device is apparently poorly manufactured and had we not woken up when it started to catch on fire, who knows what would have happened.
justification: The incident resulted in no injuries but caused property damage, and its occurrence was possible given the device's poor manufacturing.

incident_description:
While asleep in our bed we heard a loud pop noise, like that of someone who clapped their hands.  This awoke us only to see a foot long blue flame start to rush from our apple ipod nano.  It also sounded like a stream of high pressure air.  I threw the Ipod off our desk onto the ground and then unplugged the charger from the wall.  The flame disappeared as I was tending to the other materials on the desk that had caught fire from the Ipod.  I contacted apple and told them what had happened.  They had an entire list of questions already prepared for such an instance.  Such as what was damaged, what kind of smoke/soot was involved, what color was the soot/smoke/flame.  

From my understanding and research online, it sounds like perhaps it was the lithium battery inside the Ipod that ruptured and sparked into a torch like flame.  The Ipod was never altered in anyway, nor was it excessively mishandled.  It was being charged at the time, and was in a surge protector.  There were no other electrical problems with any other equipment plugged into the same surge protector.  The Ipod simply popped and produced a large flame which caught some other items on fire.  If we had not been home or in the same room as the Ipod, it could have been disastrous and possibly fatal.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a significant fire risk, with a blue flame rushing from the iPod and igniting other materials.

incident_description: We have had tv service from Direct TV for about 6 months--the DVR was installed then by a Direct TV technician.  Yesterday evening, I came home to discover that the DVR had "combusted":  the power cord melted from the DVR and detached, there was soot going up the wall behind the DVR about 10 inches and the table that the DVR was sitting on was burnt and had a brownish liquid on it.  There was also a small puddle of the same brown liquid on top of the DVR.    I unplugged the DVR and called Direct TV.  They are sending someone out to replace the DVR, but I'm concerned about a design/manufacture/product defect of a component part that may cause this to happen again or to other consumers.   It appears to be consistent with a defective capacitor that failed.    I took photos of the DVR and scorch damage.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident caused significant property damage, indicating a potential safety hazard.

incident_description:
I purchased new a Tenergy Multifiunctional Charger for Li-ion batteries. On it's third use, it POPed and ignited into flames. [REDACTED]  The unit was sitting on a tiled surface, fortunately, and we were able to extinguish the flames before the structure of our house caught fire.

UPDATE:  After further investigation, and speaking with an expert at a local battery store, and examining the battery, I now believe that the battery burst and ignited the fire.  The battery is SP Lithium CR123A 3V Made in China and evidently NOT meant for recharging.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and the likelihood of occurrence is possible given the incompatible battery used for recharging.

incident_description: Woke up in the middle of the night from the smell of smoke and saw smoke coming from monitor charger cord.   The smoke was specifically coming from the end plugged into the wall. The product was returned to Babies R Us and replaced at no charge.
justification: Smoke from a charger cord is a potential fire hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: The DVD player was plugged into the wall during the night and caught on fire. Luckily my son woke and saw it and we were able to put it out with minimal damage.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and while it's possible for a DVD player to catch fire, it's not a common occurrence.

incident_description: My daughter was using the Disney branded Phineas and Ferb Walkie Talkies for the first time. I noticed they do not work well as [REDACTED]. She brought them to me and said she didn't want to play with them anymore. When she handed it to me, I noticed one of the units was very hot (not warm) to the touch. I opened the unit and pulled out the four batteries that we had put in before our daughter started to play with them. They evidenced melting.
justification: The incident involved a product malfunction (hot batteries) but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
Friday, August 19, 2011, fire reported to 911 at 10:06 hours by the fire alarm monitoring company.
The structure was a two story apartment building, located at [REDACTED]. The fire originated in one of the apartments on the second floor of [REDACTED]. The fire room sustained moderate fire damage. The remainder of the second floor of B-Wing sustained minor smoke damage. Two of the sprinkler heads in the fire room activated and extinguished the fire. The loss value of the structure was approximately $400,000. The loss value of the contents was approximately $280,000. 
The cause of the fire was classified as accidental. It resulted when an unspecified failure in a paper shredder caused sufficient heat to ignite the paper inside. The single occupant was in the apartment at the time of the fire. He was transported for a minor burn on his finger. Another occupant was transported because of chest pains.
justification: Injury occurred due to a minor burn, with another occupant transported for chest pains.

incident_description: While tablet computer was plugged into wall charger it started smoking and became very hot to the touch
justification: The incident resulted in property damage (smoking tablet) but no injuries, and similar incidents are possible but not frequent.

incident_description: On August 9. 2011, [REDACTED] had his samsung droid cellphone in his pocket.  Instantaneously his cellpone got hot and burned his leg.  It was such a serious burn that he had to drop his pants and roll.  He sustained burn injury to his leg and was taken to emergency room and treated.  He is still receiving treatment consisting of topical ointment and pain medication.  He has been out of work since the incident.  He contacted U S Cellular who directed him to Samsung.  Samsung personnel requested the phone but [REDACTED] has retained it for inspection.  Please advise.
justification: The incident resulted in a serious burn injury requiring medical treatment, hence severity level 3. The likelihood is rated as 'possible' (3) as it's not a common occurrence but not entirely unlikely given the use of electronic devices.

incident_description: I bought a secure digital card reader made by Targus, item # TGR-MSD500 on 8/13/11.  I used it on 8/14/11 and left it plugged into my computer.  This morning, 8/15/11, I smelled a melting plastic smell and traced it to the card reader.  The card reader was very hot to the touch, and it had partially melted.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage (melted card reader) but no injuries, and while it's possible, it's not likely to happen immediately after first use.

incident_description: I bought a brand new Targus High Speed SD/SDHC/MMC Micr SD/ T-F Card Reader/Writer model#2665 from Target in Clearwater, FL, two weeks ago. I was using it on my laptop when I noticed it got really hot.  I tried to pull it out of the usb drive and the whole plastic back of the reader was melted and burning hot. I had only used the reader in the usb for approximately 20 mins. My husband  pulled the reader out of the computer and the card out of the reader.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage (melted reader) but no injuries, and while it's possible, it's not likely to happen immediately after purchase.

incident_description:
All 3 (three) of my Apple iPhone dock connector to USB cables have become unreasonably dangerous after typical use in a period less than 1 (one) year. I experienced mild electrical shock after coming into contact with exposed and frayed wires at the dock connector end of the cable (NOT the USB end). It is apparent that the plastic coating on wire becomes loose and tears, exposing the wire. Furthermore, this occurs at the hand's contact point to the cable, making electrical shock especially likely. 

Electrical tape proved to be an effective but temporary remedy to this problem.
justification: Exposed wires caused mild electrical shock, posing a high likelihood of more severe injuries if not addressed.

incident_description:
The laptop battery in an unattended laptop emitted a large volume of smoke and then ignited. The laptop was not on, and the laptop power adapter was connected. The laptop was quickly moved out of doors and placed in the driveway.
The laptop was sitting on the kitchen table, and I believe that the flames from the battery might have ignited materials on the table (resulting in a larger fire) had nobody been in the kitchen.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident could have escalated to a larger fire, posing a potential risk to life and property.

incident_description:
Almost started a fire. Had I just gone off to the airport after buying this, there would have been a fire. TARGUS laser presentation remotes with spare battery compartments ARE A FIRE HAZARD!!!

As another report shows on this site these spare battery compartments are a fire hazard and I am just lucky I tried it before packing for the plane.
justification: The incident could have resulted in a fire, but no actual fire occurred, hence severity level 2. The likelihood is high as the issue is known and another report confirms it.

incident_description:
The television set was powered in the on position for an hour. Smoke was pouring from the back of the set . The set was setting on a stand no power was lost. He unplugged the unit from the wall outlet and placed it outside. There was a plastic burning odor in the home.

He contacted the firm and they did not offer any assitance since it was no warranty on the unit. He will not make any repairs to the unit but may agree to replace it.

He has placed the unit back in the home but it is currently in the unplugg position.
justification: Smoke and burning odor indicate an incident, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: Bought a new Toshiba L675D-S7049 in February 2011. The power cord has always been hot. Recently, I inadvertantly leaned too near it, and it left a large blister, through the fabric of my jeans on my hip. Blister is approximately 2x3 inches and was instantaneous.
justification: The incident resulted in a significant burn injury, and while it's not likely to happen frequently, it's possible given the consistently hot power cord.

incident_description: I noted a strong smell of hot or burning plastic coming from the unit as well as an audible beeping sound.  The red power light indicator flashed with the emission of the sound.  The top of the unit was hot to the touch and upon turning the unit over I saw warped, sagging plastic that was extreemly hot.  I immediately unplugged the unit.
justification: Potential fire hazard indicated by burning smell, heat, and warped plastic, but no reported injuries.

incident_description: This incident happened in the morning. The phone had been charging overnight, as I do every night, and I went to go unplug the charger from the phone when I realized the phone was incredibly hot. It was so hot that I could not even try to hold it or I would be burned. The phone eventually restarted itself, as I believe it overheated. A few days later, this incident happened again as I was entering the car. Luckily, I had my phone in my car's cup holder. Again, the phone was incredibly hot to the touch. If the phone would have been in my pocket or on my person, I would have been burned.
justification: Phone overheating incidents occurred twice in a short period, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: Son was using Kodak Class 2 Battery Charger (Model K625) that came with his Kodak Z981 digital camera (purchased 12/2010).  He noticed a burning smell, checked the charger and noticed that it had started to melt on the front of the unit, between the "front" and "back" display (between the two red lights).  He immediately unplugged the charger and removed the batteries.  We are very fortunate that he was in the same room when this happened so he could unplug the charger, as it could very easily have started a fire in our home if it had gone unnoticed.
justification: The incident resulted in no injuries but could have caused a fire if not noticed, hence severity level 2. The likelihood is possible as it occurred once and the charger was used for a significant period.

incident_description:
My ASUS EEpc 1000HE netbook PC (SN 94OAAQ231418) normally goes into standby mode when I close the lid.  Yesterday it started shutting off completely instead (as if a power switch had been turned off), when I closed the lid.  Today it started smoking from the hinge area when I slowly closed the lid.  I quickly removed the battery to prevent a fire.

I contacted ASUS technical support and they said it was out of warranty.  They did not seem concerned about the fact that it was smoking.
justification: The netbook smoking and requiring battery removal indicates an incident with potential for injury, and the repeated issue suggests a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
Its 4 AM and three firemen are standing in my bedroom because a faulty power strip has failed in the middle of the night burning a hole in the carpet. Were it not for the acrid smell of burnt wiring the house would have been in flames. Now I keep my power strips on a cookie sheet. I'm done baking for today.
 
It appears that the fire started in the surge protection circuirty beside the rocker switch in the middle. The smell was so pungent it woke us out of a deep sleep.

Forensic disassembly of the powerstrip in the presence of the fire chief showed that the light in the power strip was the source of the fire.

We have images of the unit, and the unit itself.

The unit says "ElectriPak" Catalog Number 7100FA
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident could have escalated to a severe fire, hence severity level 2.

incident_description:
In 2009 we purchased a Phillips Flat Screen T.V. from our local Wal-Mart we paid over $100.00 for it.  It functioned fine for about a year.  Just after the warranty ran out in 2011, August we began experiancing problems.  The set would turn off just after turning on, when it did come on a shreek sound would be heard and often it would show half a picture.  I was working in the kitchen one morning when I could something electronic burning.  When I turned the set was smoking.  The set had been turned off at the time.  I immediatly un-plugged the set and removed it from the room.  

     I notified Phillip's and was quickly told that the warranty had expired and they wiuld replace or have it fixed at my own expense.  Replaced incadentally with a refurbished set.  I explained that there were grave safety issues with there product.  They told me no one has ever complained and there products were first rate.  More B.S. they hand out!  I went on the net and found a complaint site pertaining to Phillips, including complaints about simular T.V.'s to mine.  

    I contacted the Georgia Atty. Generals Office and they sent me back a letter that the company no longer was in that state.  I contacted the Atty. Generals Office here in Penna.  I sent the complaint to the Consumer' branch and was told it was out of there jurisdiction yet the products are being sold in Penna. to Penna. Citizens.

    Something has to be done with this company, according to the complaint forum injuries and property damage has already have occured.  Now the light bulbs they produce are being recalled for safety issues.  How many more items will it take to take action against Phillips.  I was told several other electronic items under various names are manufactured by Phillips as well.
justification: Although no injuries were reported in this specific case, the incident involved a potential fire hazard, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' (Level 2) with a high likelihood (4) of occurrence given the similar complaints and product recall.

incident_description:
The TV sparked and smokes when turn on by my kids. The green power light comes on and off then
something rattles in the back of the tv and it goes dead. After a while it does it again and again..
justification: The incident resulted in a malfunctioning TV but no injuries, and the likelihood of it happening again is possible given the repeated occurrences.

incident_description: I am writing this in order to prevent anyone else getting hurt. I bought my SONY VPCF115FM MAY 2010 from Best Buy. I noticed immediately how the fan ran all of the time and felt hot.. I bought a Logitec desk with a fan hoping this would fix the problem. It didn't. I received an email 7-8-10 and 8-13-10 from Sony instructing me to update the BIOS firmware. It did not help the problem. Over time, the computer became worse, now it gets so hot that it shuts down. When you touch the computer, it is hot. I wrote a complaint to Sony. They emailed me a long distance number that I called and waited on hold for fifteen minutes. After hanging up, I tried to call the next day with the same holding time. I attempted the call the following day, after holding ten minutes, finally, someone answered the line. After a long discussion with the Customer Service Rep., he reluctantly agreed to send me a box to ship it to Sony to repair. This was over three weeks ago, I don't have a box! All I receive is emails instructing me to call the long distance number. This makes the third Sony Lemon that I bought! Only this time, this product is a FIRE HAZARD! Sony has the worst Customer Service. In the mean time, I can't use my lap top for more than thirty minutes without it becoming too hot to touch or crashing. After researching on the internet, I noticed many people have this same issue and they also complain that the Customer Service has been worthless. Today was the final straw, I actually burnt my hand resulting with a blister. This model is dangerous!
justification: User suffered a burn injury due to laptop overheating, indicating a high likelihood of similar incidents occurring.

incident_description:
I purchased a Targus laser presentation remote, installed the battery as directed and placed the spare battery in the spare battery slot.  As I was using the remote, I smelled something burning or melting.  I removed the battery cover and discovered that the spare battery was overheating to the point where it was almost too hot to touch.  Had it been left in, it would have destroyed the batteries and the remote.

As I looked in the slot where the spare goes, there is a metal contact at the bottom where I put the Negative end of the battery but no contact on the positive end.  This issue needs to be addressed as it is a considerable safety hazard. 

Thank you
justification: Potential for property damage and injury due to lack of positive contact for spare battery, making overheating likely.

incident_description:
I have a Dell Inspiron 1545 that I purchased in October 2009 which included a one year warranty. Last year before the warranty expired the power adapter to the laptop stop charging the battery. It would promt a message say "plugged in, not charging".

Today that happened once again but this time what make it much more alarming is both the charger and the laptop are extrememly hot. I am afraid that the laptop could catch on fire.
justification: Both the charger and laptop are extremely hot, posing a risk of burns and potentially a fire.

incident_description:
I have a MacBook laptop, which I purchased in early 2009. The laptop last year started to bulge a bit at its battery cover. Since it is a metal case, I thought that I had bent the bottom of the laptop when picking it up. However, two weeks ago, I noticed the bulge had grown quite a lot and my trackpad (mouse) would not click. So, I removed the MacBook Rechargeable Battery (model number A1280) and found that it had swollen substantially. When I replaced the cover without the battery, the laptop was working perfectly.

The laptop and battery are out of warranty because of age. However, the battery still holds a charge of a number of hours, and it has only reached around 270 cycles, which is less than the 300 cycle life. The swelling seems to be a manufacturing defect, as the battery still works. 

So, I took the battery and laptop to an Apple Store (in SoHo, Manhattan, New York). The specialist looked at it and said the battery had outlived its useful life and I would have to pay a hundred dollars to replace it. When I protested that the battery was within its cycle life and still held a charge, the lady told me that rechargeable batteries swell, indicating their life is over. I protested again, she insisted I buy a new battery so I can use the laptop without being plugged into a wall. I again refused, and she gave me the battery back. Of course, I am not using a potentially dangerous, swollen battery.

My battery's information: Serial Number 6N841U7413CB; Model Number A1280

I researched the problem, and have found numerous other complaints about the battery swelling, with different results. Mine is simply swollen. Some swell until they break open, exposing the individual cells. Others overheat.

http://store.apple.com/us/reviews/MA458LL/A

http://www.cultofmac.com/apple-service-rep-swollen-macbook-battery-ÃÂnormalÃÂ/77201
justification: Potential fire hazard due to swollen battery, though no immediate injury reported.

incident_description: Ordered and received Cyberpower CP1500AVRLCD Uninterruptable Power Supply (UPS) from Amazon.  However, after a few days, began releasing ozone (?) smell and personnel began complaining of headaches. Preparing to return to Amazon.
justification: Potential chemical exposure from UPS, causing headaches, but no injuries reported.

incident_description:
My second NTA2340 battery has just started showing signs of not holding a charge and is slightly swollen. I have already had one Harmony One replaced because the battery swelled so much that it would not come out. incident_description:
Electronic networking device has electrical potential of over 40 volts present on exposed metal case parts during normal operation:

I purchased a Hawking Technologies model HOWABN1 Hi-Gain Outdoor Wireless-N Multifunction Access Point at Fry's Electronics in Anaheim, CA on 7/10/2011. After initial installation, I found that its power supply shut down when I connected an external antenna (which was grounded for lightning protection) to the unit. Further testing revealed that the device had a potential of just over 40 volts DC on it's exposed metal case when installed according to manufacturer's instructions, and the power supply shutdown symptom was caused when the external antenna shorted the unit's case to ground. I returned the item to Fry's for a refund the following day. I reported the unsafe condition to the Fry's employee who handled my return. 

On 7/12/2011, I purchased the same model of device from Micro Center in Tustin, CA. This time, I initially wired up the unit on my test bench prior to installation, and found that this unit also had a potential of just over 40 volts DC on its exposed metal case. I connected the case to earth ground through a 100 ohm half-watt resistor to verify that the case was not simply floating to a DC potential when measured with my high-impedance meter, and the resistor immediately became very hot, thus indicating that the case was electrified by a low-impedance source capable of providing a substantial current.

I plan to return this device to Micro Center tomorrow for a refund. I will report the unsafe ground fault condition to them, and I will also attempt to contact the manufacturer to report this unsafe condition. Since I encountered this same unsafe ground fault condition on two devices purchased from different dealers, I am concerned that this may be a systematic design or manufacturing fault affecting this product, so I am reporting this to CPSC for further investigation in case a product recall is justified. 

I am an electrical engineer and licensed amateur radio operator with experience in electrical testing and safe installation of outdoor antenna systems. Please feel free to contact me about this incident.
justification: Potential for severe injury due to exposed metal case with over 40 volts, likely to occur given two defective units from different dealers.

incident_description:
I purchased my Sony Vaio in February of 2010.  It has always overheated, but about 6 months ago I started searching for a solution.  I found the safety warning and BIOS update here:  http://esupport.sony.com/US/perl/news-item.pl?news_id=401&mdl=VPCF115FM. Although I installed the BIOS update, nothing changed.

My laptop continues to overheat.  The back of the laptop gets so hot that it's not safe to touch.  It frequently shuts itself down due to overheating.  It is used only on a hard surface with an extra cooling riser for maximum air flow (http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B001K7I608/ref=wms_ohs_product_img_T2).  The level of heats threatens to melt the plastic of the case and damage the internal components.  It would definitely burn skin.  The temperature of the internal components is 90C according to SpeedFan (a program that gives access to the computer's temperature readings).

My CPU (quad core i7) generally hovers around 5% and I never use more than 50% of my 6GBs of RAM.  This is a heavy duty laptop that should not be overheating with its current level of usage.  This is clearly an unsafe product.  

Sony has informed me that because I'm 4 months out of warranty, there is nothing they will do to rectify the issue with my laptop.  Technically, every laptop sold with this issue (and there are hundreds of thousands of them) is out of warranty -- they were manufactured between January and April of 2010.  I just want a safe laptop that I don't have to warn my children not to touch.  If I move this laptop off a hard surface with extra cooling, it is definitely hot enough to damage property and burn skin.  This product needs to be recalled -- it's not a BIOS issue, it's a hardware issue.
justification: The laptop overheats to dangerous levels, threatening skin burns and component damage, despite low CPU usage and adequate cooling.

incident_description:
One month ago I purchased a Targus Remote Presenter, which is the little gadget that let's you run a PowerPoint presentation and has a red laser pointer. The product comes with 2 AAA batteries and has 2 battery compartments. One is marked to show which way to install the battery. The other is labeled as the spare battery but there are no markings to indicate which way to install the spare. It should not make a difference as there is no metal contact point in the spare compartment. 

I needed to test the product with our computer equipment so I installed the first battery by following the + and - markings. I installed the spare battery facing the same way. I then turned the presenter on. Within 2 minutes the bottom half of the product became hot in my hand. I continued trying to get the product to work with our computer and it got hotter and hotter to the point where it was uncomfortable in my hand. At that point, I shut the product off and removed the battery cover. The batteries were melting and there were signs of battery acid seeping out of the seam. I returned the defective product to Staples and was issued a refund. 

Because I still need a presenter, I purchased another Targus Remote Presenter yesterday. It was the same exact model as the one purchased last month. The exact same thing happened again. When I removed the battery cover, the label around the "spare" battery was already separating from the battery. In other words, it was melting due to the heat. I again returned the defective product to Staples and a refund was issued. 

There is something seriously wrong in the wiring of this product. No surprise it was made in China.
I went to the Targus website but was unable to find any where that I could alert them of this problem.
justification: The incident occurred twice with the same product, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence.
