incident_description: My 16 year old son had cell in his pocket and it caught fire.
justification: Cell phone catching fire is possible but not common, and no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
Was using a Targus multi-card reader with its 24" USB  cable extension to start a download pics from SD card to a computer USB plug.  After only about 2 minutes I smelled sometime hot while I was troubleshooting why my drive was not pulling up on the computer to start the downloading.  The hot smell was my USB extension cable that very hot to the touch that I had to pull it to unplug it from the computer to prevent a fire.  Luckily I only plug in the cable when I need to use it.  I thought maybe the USB plug on my computer was bad so I tried another USB cable and the Targus reader itself but neither got hot, so to test the cable again I plugged it in and quickly unplugged it as it was getting hot quickly.  The cable has no visible damage to the covering or the ends.

This cable is maybe about 6 months old, I think I bought it around Xmas time at Radio Shack or Walmart.  If I remember correctly it came as a package with the Targus multi-card reader.

The only writing on the plastic card reader is Micro SD/T-F on the back.

The front has High Speed SD/SDHC/MMC  
                     Micro SD/T-F  
                      Card Reader/Writer
justification: The incident resulted in no injury, but the potential for fire was high due to the overheating USB cable.

incident_description: Consumer wanted to report that his battery in his HP laptop gets very hot to the touch and burned his lap. He stated that the laptop on was on his lap and on for a few hours. The laptop did not emit smoke or have a burning odor. At the time he burned himself, the consumer was using the laptop with the A/C adapter plugged in. The consumer stated that the battery is normally very hot to the touch  when the adapter is plugged. He feels that specifically the battery is a burn hazard as the ones mentioned in release 09-221. The consumer report no problems with the computer and the computer has never been serviced. When the consumer burned himself the laptop was on his lap and the computer itself seems to get very hot not the A/C adapter. The computer shows no sign of damage the consumer didn't experience any electric shock. He contacted the manufacturer and the retailer today. He cannot recall the names of the people he spoke to but stated they offered to do nothing for him. The consumer stated the product is still usable. The consumer felt it was imperative to report this product.
justification: Consumer experienced a burn injury due to the laptop's battery overheating, despite the A/C adapter being plugged in.

incident_description: We have two laptops. One is a presario that we have had for over 7 years and have NEVER had any problems with.  The other, the one I would like to make you aware of, we purchased not even two years ago. The battery gets so hot, that if you set the laptop on your legs, you get burned if you don't remove it right away.  It's the equivalent of touching your finger on a pot that has boiling water in it.
justification: The laptop's battery overheating to a burn-inducing temperature is an incident, but no injuries have been reported.

incident_description:
The glass base of our Samsung 63' Plasma TV EXPLODED sending hundreds of pieces of glass flying in all directions. 

The explosion occurred  at approximately 8:00pm.  The TV was not on and had not been used since approximately 10:00 pm the prior evening.  

The debris covered a distance of more than 20' side to side and 8'-10' forward and back.

Thankfully we were not in the line of the explosion as we were just heading into the room to watch evening TV when the explosion occurred.  It took us a minute to realize what actually happened.  

My wife did sustain a cut finger when she picked up a piece of the debris before realizing it was all Glass chunks, pieces and shards. We collected most of the pieces and have saved them. 

We did an internet search afterward and found similar incidents involving other Samsung TV products including video of the aftermath that was posted on U-Tube by someone.
justification: Injury occurred due to glass debris, though likelihood of occurrence is possible based on similar incidents found online.

incident_description:
The battery of my laptop burned me and it keeps heating up to a point that we have to close it, so i did but one day i just did not open and will give me only a black screen, i called HP company and the answered was , if i want help i need to pay 40$ to get someone to help me on the phone because my guaranteed was finished, so no help at all from them whats so ever... it costed me 2000$ that laptop and i use it for work, i hurd about the recall but apparently my battery do not have the right number to be changed, but now its more then the battery, its the whole laptop, i am just not happy with the way they treat us after , even online you will get no service if you dont have that stupid guaranty, is there something i can do?? thank you will be waiting for your reply


[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury, but no serious harm or death, and the likelihood of such an incident occurring again is possible given the recurring heating issues.

incident_description:
There have been numerous complaints on the Internet regarding the La Crosse Model BC-900 being a fire hazard. Recently my unit got so hot that the batteries blistered and one could not be removed from the charger because it is melted to the plastic of the charger. 

Prior to this incident, I e-mailed La Crosse telling them that I was burned while removing the batteries from the charger. They requested all kinds of information but did not offer a repair or replacement. 

There is a risk of fire and/or injury using this product and it should be recalled.
justification: The melted battery and blistering unit indicate a high likelihood of injury due to the product's fire hazard.

incident_description: I have a Sony KDF-50WE655 TV that has evidence of lamp overheating.  The lamp housing shows burn marks and has deformed the plastic.  I guess I am fortunate that the lamp appears to have died before the TV could catch on fire.
justification: While no injury or fire occurred, the incident involved a potential fire hazard due to lamp overheating, hence a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
Phillips 42" ambilight plasma TV
Pop and shot a fireball out of the top of the televsion
Then TV was dead
justification: The TV malfunctioned and shot out a fireball, causing property damage but no injuries.

incident_description:
I have an iHome iH8 iPod docking station made by iHome Audio in Rahway, NJ. The unit is about a year and a half old. The power adapter has been plugged in without incident since we moved several months ago and has not been moved or touched since then. Today, I went to move the docking station. As I went to unplug the adapter, I noticed that the plastic had split apart and the wires and components inside were exposed. I cut the power to the outlet and removed the adapter from the outlet. When I tried to put it back together, it wouldn't go back down since the parts inside had swollen from the heat.

I have never had a power adapter do this before, and it doesn't seem like it would be safe.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the exposed wires pose a potential fire hazard, making it an incident.

incident_description:
The consumer says about two weeks ago he heard this loud noise.  He checked the detector and he saw that the bottom of the battery blew out.  He called the electrician the next morning.  The electrician told him the battery is the problem and that he had never seen anything like that in his 30 years.  The consumer says there was another loud noise a couple of weeks later.  He found a cylinder on the floor 25 to 30 feet away.   The electrician showed him how that cylinder came out of the battery.  The defective battery was sitting on the kitchen counter.  The electrician checked the wiring in his entire house and determined there was nothing wrong.  Electrician was with [REDACTED].  This is a very serious and dangerous problem. The cylinder that exploded out of the defective battery and travelled some 25-30 feet would certainly injure someone.  After first incident, consumer was in the process of reporting this incident to Duracell. Luckily they did not request to have the battery returned.  It may have very likely exploded in the mail.

As of the date this report was submitted, consumer had no response from Duracell- only a coupon for the next purchase.
justification: The battery explosion could have caused serious injury, as evidenced by the cylinder traveling 25-30 feet.

incident_description: The Li-ion battery supplied with my Logitech Harmony One remote stopped maintaining a charge after 15 months of use.  I wanted to make sure the battery was seated correctly within the remote, but I found the battery stuck (wedged) in the remote.  I was finally able to remove the battery (with the help of some pliers) and I found the battery was swollen and the seams of the battery were beginning to split.  I'm not sure how long the battery has been in this condition, but the battery stopped maintaining a charge approximately 2 week ago.  I looked on Logitech's website and in their FAQs it says this is normal.  I have many electronic devices, most of which use Li-ion batteries and have never experienced a battery swelling like this before.  I'm mostly concerned with the fact that if I had not removed the battery, it may have ruptured and caused injury.
justification: Battery swelling and potential rupture pose a high likelihood of injury.

incident_description: After purchasing earphones for use with an Mp3 player (Coby CVE22), I noticed a very small warning printed with the instructions indicating that the plastic cables contain lead and the user should wash their hands after handling them.  Earphone cords do not just touch hands, they touch the neck and face for extended periods of time-- the use of lead in this product is irresponsible and completely unacceptable, and the warning that is printed on the package is far too small to actually attract the attention of the user.   It is now common for young children to listen to music or work on computers using this kind of earphones, and they would be exposed very dangerously.  Coby Electronics Corporation are knowingly exposing their customers to close contact with a dangerous, well-known toxin.
justification: Lead exposure from earphone cables can cause serious health issues, especially for children with prolonged use.

incident_description: I have a HP laptop computer which the battery gets very HOT. It leaves red marks by my knee area even through sweat pants or jeans.   It wasn't listed in the recall.  The number on the battery is CT 6291904V8V3X14.  It should be on the recall.
justification: The battery's excessive heat and potential burns pose a risk of injury, making it likely to occur again.

incident_description:
ME:[REDACTED], Board Certified Physician, AND
Chief Medical Information Officer (CMIO)

PRODUCT: Laptop Computer VPC F11 model (specifically VPC F1109x). Refurbished. bought directly from Sony.com on 12/12/2011. (I was unaware of recall on product 6/2010 due to overheating). Moved into brand new house at same time, and 15 amp circuit breakers( with arc fault protection) kept shutting off.

EVENT: Tripped 15 amp circuits approx 40-50 times, and i presumed I had a faulty house.  After consulting two licensed electricians today 5/11/2011, it was deemed the house, and the four "faulty" circuit breakers were fine.  and the root cause was the laptop. Professional Electricians opinion: short in the AC adapter and/or hardware.  

Sony was contacted by email and phone. They were unwilling to address the issue citing "warranty" issues.  

***As an MD, I am keenly aware public safety is not limited by 'warranty' statements. And the warnings on Sony and your web site suggest this is a PRODUCT DESIGN FLAW, not just one  bum computer.
*** I have strong  concerns that others with more dated electrical systems will not shut down, and the  computer may be a root cause of a house fire.

REQUEST: DUE DILIGENCE by SONY and CPSC to collect data and monitor if this is a valid concern, and prevent injury before it occurs.
justification: While no injuries have been reported, the frequent tripping of circuit breakers due to the laptop's faulty AC adapter poses a significant risk of house fires, potentially leading to injuries.

incident_description:
On April 29, 20011 my son was playing with one of his Phineas and Ferb Walkie Talkies. After playing with the toy he must have left it on and placed it on our leather sofa. Approximately 4 hours later we returned home and my husband went to move the walkie talkie so that he could sit on the sofa, when he did this he noticed a gooey melted substance on one side of the walkie talkie. He then called me over to look at what had happened and we both noticed a 4-inch melted and burned area to our leather sofa. The melt/burn caused the sofa to rip and actually show the stuffing on the inside of the sofa. The shape and size of the burn was the exact shape, width, and length of the walkie talkie. The walkie talkie itself felt warm to the touch and had little to no battery power left. We immediately cleaned the substance off of the walkie talkie and then took both walkie talkies away from our son.

We then reached out to Toys R Us, where we purchased the walkie talkies, as well as Digital Blue, the company that produces the walkie takies. Toys R Us has followed up and informed us that the case is being reviewed and will be taken very seriously due to the burn that was a result of the product. Digital Blue has not been accommodating or helpful in trying to rectify the situation and will only communicate about this matter through E-mail, no phone number or contact person has been given after numerous attempts acquire one. Digital Blue has also requested several times that we send them the walkie talkies back so that a "new and tested set" can be sent back to us. The company does not take this matter seriously nor are they concerned about the safety and well being of their consumers!
justification: The incident resulted in property damage (sofa burn) but no injuries, and it could have happened again if not for the parents' intervention.

incident_description: I installed a new nicad battery in a Tivoli Pal radio and after charging for about a half hour, the battery exploded, blowing the back cover off the radio. The battery was installed with the proper polarity and the correct charger was used.
justification: The battery explosion caused property damage but no injuries, and while it's possible, it's not likely to happen with proper charging.

incident_description: DeWalt battery charger melted the charger and battery
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and similar incidents have occurred in the past.

incident_description: New Duracell NiMH batteries corroded and labels melted off when charged for the first time.  The Energizer battery charger has been used previously with Energizer and Radio Shack NiMH batteries with no issues.
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the incident caused property damage (corroded batteries, melted labels) and could have led to further issues if not noticed.

incident_description: Charging cord for Kindle (Amazon reader) disintegrates.  Outside plastic cover falls off of the cord.  This is a serious safety hazard.  If I hadn't noticed the damage before I plugged it in, I could have been electrocuted.  I contacted Amazon, and they issued a credit so I could by a new one, but this item should be recalled.  Several reviews on the Amazon site address the same problem, yet they haven't issued a recall.
justification: The incident could have resulted in serious injury due to the potential for electrocution, and the likelihood is high given the number of similar reports.

incident_description:
I purchased a Sony Vaio laptop, model VPCF11JFX/B, in January 2010, and have applied the remedy of firmware update, as provided by Sony, to prevent the laptop from overheating. Unfortunately, the laptop continues to overheat and has now damaged the video display. 

On April 13 of this year, I contacted Sony Technical Support and was told they would extend my warranty in order to replace the faulty cooling processor, at their expense, and was given the option of either receiving a mailing box to send computer directly to factory for repair, or I could take it to the nearest Sony Style store for repair. I was given a reference #, E50071684. I confirmed this information via a second call to Sony - this time to the In Warranty department.

On April 28, I delivered my laptop to the Sony Style store at the Menlo Park Mall (Edison NJ 08837) and a day later (April 29) was told by the service technician [redacted],  my laptop was NOT under warranty. 

On May 2, I phoned Sony Technical Support in hopes of receiving confirmation of my recall extended warranty only to be told the original tech support person had made an error and would be retrained in Sony policy, as a result. I then spoke with a customer relations rep and expressed my disappointment with their inconsistent customer service.

Today, May 3, I retrieved my laptop from the Backstage department at the Menlo Park Mall Sony Style store and was told out-of-warranty repairs such as mine would cost approximately $400-600, as the motherboard would require replacement.

As indicated on your site, 233,000 of the faulty units are included in this recall, so I am certain my problem  - the failure of the firmware update to remedy the faulty hardware part of which Sony was aware - is not unique. To that end, I wish to be included in whatever legal action - a class action suit (?) - may be taken against Sony in order to have the faulty part AND the subsequent damaged part(s) replaced at their expense in a timely manner.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage (laptop's video display) but no physical injury, and the likelihood of similar occurrences is high given the widespread recall.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that while using the laptop for approximately 1 hour he heard a weird sound emitting from the CD/DVD portal and the smelled an odor of electric fire and the unit started emitting sparks and then a blue flame dispersed from the hinges of the laptop towards the screen which caused the lap to be inoperable. Consumer stated that he immediately unplugged it to prevent further damages.

4/12/11  He contacted the manufacturer and was advised that there was nothing that could be done since his laptop was no longer under warranty.

Consumer feels that this product is a fire hazard and should be investigated.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and the consumer's description suggests a high likelihood of similar incidents occurring due to the product's design.

incident_description: My television started on fire. After watching it for a minute and realizing the orange glow was the refection of the cabinet grid on the wall I disconnected it while it was burning, set it on the floor, looked through the back to see actuall fire beginning to melt the outer case. I poured water on it to put it out. It would have burned my house down no doubt.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a fire that could have spread and caused significant damage, making it a serious incident.

incident_description: 911 call in reference to a electrical fire. Call came into dispatch in reference to an overloaded outlet. Upon fire dept arrival and my arrival, we were ushered into a rear office area where there was a strong hot electrical smell. Upon walking around the desk I had a visual of a Surge protector that had burned internally and had started to melt the bottom side of it out. Surge bar was still plugged in and the outlet was energized, verified by tester. Thermal imager showed that the surge bar was the area and point of origin. Computer hard drive and monitor were the only items plugged in and their respective cords were negative for thermal loading via thermal camera.
justification: No injuries were reported, but the incident involved an electrical fire, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' case.

incident_description:
His 38 year old daughter placed the lap top on top of her lap. The lap top was powered in the off position and the adapter was plugged into the lap top and the wall out let (amount of time is unknown) on and it began to smoke immediately. She then placed the lap top on her bed in which was covered with four blankets and one sheet. 

The lap top was so hot that it burned through all the layers of covers on the bed straight to the mattress. She then picked the lap top up and threw it to the floor and it melted the fibers from the carpet.

The victim picked up the lap top and placed took it outside while the smoke continuously began to pour from it. He received minor burns to his right hand. He flipped it over and noticed that the battery was red hot. He took the lap top back inside and used a screw driver to remove the back piece and placed the battery inside a metal small pale. The battery engulfed in flames immediately. He then applied a pitcher of water to put the flames out. As he noticed the battery immersed in the water it still continued to smoke then the fire went out. 

The victim and his daughter both experienced a minor smoke inhalation.

The laptop was purchased used froma n online auction site.
justification: Injuries occurred due to direct contact with the overheating laptop and subsequent battery explosion.

incident_description: My HP Pavilion over heats to a point of being dangerous. There is no way it can be placed on your lap while using it. When I remove the battery and just use the ac cord, it does not get nearly as hot. The product sn matches the recall, but the battery serial number does not. It is now out of warrenty and HP will not discuss it unless I pay for additional support, even though I complained once before and they said that I should monitor the recall and see if my battery gets added.
justification: Overheating could potentially cause burns, but no injuries were mentioned.

incident_description: My television has burn marks on the inside and the door to the lamp of the television is warped. It appears very unsafe and looks like a fire hazard.
justification: Burn marks and warped door indicate a potential fire hazard, making another incident likely.

incident_description: I have a sony vaio laptop (VPCCW17FX) which burnt out abruptly yesterday.  Machine is 15 months old.  Unfortunately I did not purchase warranty.  When I contacted Sony they indicated that while the issue is the same as encountered by VPCC11X and VPCC2X models and they were recalled or provided a solution to address, the situation I have I am on my own despite any safety concerns.  I tried to contact the safety department but the call was cut short abruptly without any resolution.  Sony informed a non refundable charge or $139 to determine if the issue was valid since I do not have warranty.  While I admit warranty is important I am surprised that Sony can be callous about products that can result in bodily injury.  Please advise if you have any suggestions on the same.
justification: While no injury has been reported, the potential for bodily harm due to an electrical device malfunction is significant.

incident_description:
I purchased a 12V, 7amp lead-acid alarm battery from Radio Shack in Aiea, Hawaii.  At the register, I inspected that battery and commented to the sales clerk that the battery looked used.  He brought me another battery and assured me that the batteries were new.

I installed the battery in my alarm system.  The battery was exactly to the alarm system's specifications.

Within an hour I noticed a strong rotten egg smell emanating from the alarm system. In investigating, I discovered that the battery had become so hot, I could not touch it with my bare hands.  I disconnected the battery, used pot holders to remove it, and took it outside.

When the battery cooled, I returned it to the store.   I marked the battery's box with a blue indelible pen.  I explained to the clerk the dangerous situation that had occurred.  She issued me a full refund and on the return receipt the product is described as a "defective item".

Less than a week later, on April 19, 2011 I returned to the same Radio Shack store.  The exact same battery that I had marked with the blue indelible ink was back on the shelf for sale.  I notified the store manager and told him that I thought this was an extremely dangerous situation.  He promised to remove the battery from sale.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident could have resulted in burns or fire, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that he received this cell phone as a replacement to the first phone he had , however the brightness of the phone illuminates every now and then and he is concerned that this is an overheating of the batteries which could cause an explosion.

Consumer feels that there is a safety hazard and it should be reported.
justification: While the consumer's concern is valid, there's no immediate indication of injury or death, hence severity level 2. The likelihood is possible as the consumer has experienced the issue, but it's not certain.

incident_description:
I have a Toshiba Laptop and about 4 weeks ago my laptop shut off after only 1 and 1/2 hours of use and was warmer than normal.  Then about a few days ago it shut off after a 30 minute use and was extremley hot, i left a red mark on my hand after I touched it.

I called Toshiba and they said they is nothing they can do.
justification: The laptop overheating to the point of causing injury (red mark on hand) indicates a severe incident.

incident_description:
A power strip that I bought recently (Stanley #31610;Model EM0901M, made by Hang Zhou Kaite Electrical Appliances Co., Ltd., with the numbers 3121738 in the lower left of the back label, shorted, twice, when I was attempting to re-fit plugs to the strip.  The first time it happened, I thought perhaps the plug was faulty, checked the plug which seemed OK, tried it again in another socket, and it worked fine.  Because this strip is behind a group a small appliances in our kitchen, it needs dusting.  Once again. on attempting to re-insert a plug into the strip, it arced. and also caused my gfci into which the strip was plugged, to react.  I removed the strip from the kitchen but could not re-set the GFCI (it had apparently worked, but no longer could be re-set).  I then removed all the screws from the rear of the power strip, unplugged of course, and looked inside.  What I saw was the black channel that forms the bottom of the device, followed by a white, translucent plastic sheet, cut to fit the interior of the device, and a small circuit board in the area of the switch, at one end of the top portion, and three copper wires running the length of that section. The wires were soldered at various point into what appears to be copper projections, forked to receive the wire at their tips, on the back sides of each plug housing; eight in all.

There are two areas on the otherwise white plastic sheet that show blackening, and careful examination of the plastic shows points at which it has been penetrated, presumably by the aforesaid copper tabs through which the wires run.  Further examination reveals that attempting to insert a plug into two of the receptacles on the strip forces one of the tabs to move away from the insertion force.

I have photographs that show the pieces.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the power strip's repeated short-circuiting and failure to reset the GFCI indicates a significant safety hazard.

incident_description:
Two years ago, I purchased a Phillips LCD television model #47PFL3603D/27. Several months ago, it began to black out and would work for a while when I restarted the TV. Soon after, I would hear popping sounds, and then I saw smoke coming out the TV and smelled a strong fire-like odor. 

I then went on the internet to see if others had experienced this problem any found many complaints.

I contacted Phillips and was told that because my TV was out of warranty that they would do nothing; that any repairs would be at my expense. 

This TV is an obvious fire hazard they should either repair or replace it.
justification: The TV's smoking and popping sounds indicate a potential fire hazard, though no injuries or deaths have been reported.

incident_description: A fire occurred in a lithuim polymer battery used for an airsoft gun, thebattery was left unattended while charging.
justification: The fire in the lithium polymer battery, though causing damage, did not result in any injuries as it occurred in an unattended airsoft gun.

incident_description:
I purchased a Philips 47" LCD HD TV in October 2008 from Wal-Mart (Model # 47PFL3603D/27 and Serial # YA1C0821003459) and began having problems in late 2010. The TV's picture would black out, however, the audio continued without a problem. When this occured, I could feel the heat coming from the unit, so I would turn the TV off for 5-10 minutes, let it cool, and then turn it back on. This problem would happen several times per week and I began to worry about it catching on fire and harming my family. Eventually, this problem got much worse, when the unit began smoking profusely on February 14, 2011. I turned the TV off and tried to remove the unit from our family room to limit the smoke and odor, but it was too hot grab with my bare hands. Needless to say, I had to use my silicone oven mits to physically remove the unit to let it cool down and finish smoking on my back porch. I have since stored this faulty unit in my garage after learning that the Philips warranty expired after 1 year and the cost to diagnose and repair the unit is prohibitive. 

As a concerned consumer, husband and father, I feel obligated to share this potential fire risk with your organization with the hope that others will be alerted and avoid potential injury or death.

Should you need any additional information, please contact me via email at [REDACTED] or by my cell phone at [REDACTED].
justification: The TV's overheating and smoking, along with the consumer's fear of it catching fire, indicates a high likelihood of injury.

incident_description: We use the Summer Infant video monitor.  We would sit the camera on the top of the crib corner, and at 9 months the baby was able to reach it and pull it down along with the long cord.  We would watch her playing with the camera, and when we came into her room noticed that the cord was tightly wrapped around her neck, but there was not injury.
justification: The baby was able to reach and pull down the monitor, which could have led to an injury if not noticed in time.

incident_description: Westinghouse HDTV Model: SK-26H730S.  In use about 2 years.  Although my area is not subject to power surges, this unit has always been plugged into a quality surge protector.  Within a month after buying it, the TV began to make a constant mild high pitch noise when turned "off."  I contacted Westinghouse and was told it was "normal."  The TV is in my bedroom, used on sleep timer for 15-30 minutes each night as I am falling asleep.  About a year ago I began finding the TV "on" when I would go into the bedroom.  I thought perhaps the remote had gotten bumped.  It became more frequent, and began coming "on" during the night.  The TV began coming back "on" immediately after I would manually turn it "off."  Now, sometimes, it will enter a cycle of continuously "on-off" and has a funny odor.  Possible Fire Hazard.
justification: The TV's spontaneous on/off cycling and emission of a funny odor indicate a potential fire hazard, despite the use of a surge protector.

incident_description: The computer battery in the docking station of my Dell X300 laptop caught fire this morming. It
justification: While no injuries were reported, the incident of a laptop battery catching fire poses a significant risk to property and potential injury in the future.

sweat where the iPhone had touched. The wet area felt hot, numb and was red. I had to
finish the conversation holding the iPhone several inches from my face. I do not know
what caused the superheating. My initial guesses were defective batteries,
electromagnetic waves (from phone antenna, blue tooth, GPS and WiFi which were all on
at the same time), chemical reaction from chemicals on the phone and my face, and
tampering by the iGenius from when he put my iPhone in his possibly contaminated case
and pocket.

I immediately took the iPhone to the store where the rep said it was probably the battery
and offered me another iPhone. I believe he was aware of the problem. I told him that my
face still felt numb and warm and that I did not want to risk it again. I also stated the
terms were unacceptable due to the terms that stated at AppleÃÂs discretion, I could wait up
to two years to get a replacement if I lost or damaged the iPhone, and the iPhone was
uninsurable. The iPhone was checked for damage, no damage was found and a refund
was given.

The following day, Monday, June 29, my face still felt warm and numb. Other people
initially pointed out to me that the right side of my face was swollen. A Mac enthusiast
told me there is a lot of information on-line about this problem. I researched the matter
on-line, found that this was not a unique situation, and realized Apple must be aware of
the problem. I called the Apple store manager, [REDACTED] , and told him I
believed the iPhone had injured my face. I do not recall his exact words, but believe he
refereed to my injury as an ÃÂunpleasant experienceÃÂ. I said to him not ÃÂunpleasant
experienceÃÂ, ÃÂyour !@#$& iPhone burned my faceÃÂ and if I ever heard a product burned
someone, I would pull it off the shelf and have it checked. However, he stated he had no
authority to do that and only the corporate office could make such a decision. I also
called AT&T and talked to [REDACTED] , who said to go get medical aid.
On Tuesday, June 30, the next morning, I went to my family doctor and uncle ([REDACTED]  
who checked my face and ear. He said I needed to have a Neurologist
and/or Ear Nose and Throat (ENT) specialist look at it. He tried getting an appointment
for me with one of his associates but could not get a timely appointment. He said I should
go to the emergency room now, request to be seen by a Neurologist or ENT, and referred
me to UCLA or Saint Johns in Santa Monica.

That same day, I went to Saint JohnÃÂs emergency room, told them a doctor sent me there
and asked to see an ENT or Neurologist. Initially, a physicianÃÂs assistant evaluated me
and said this could be Bells Paulsy or Shingles. I asked her if she had read my file from
admitting. She said she had not because people in admitting have poor handwriting. I said
I was there because I believed my iPhone had overheated and had injured the right side of
my face and ear. I have never had Bells Paulsy or Shingles and the symptoms were local
to where the iPhone had been in contact. She said that iPhones do not get hot enough to
cause this kind of problem. I was kept waiting for 2 more hours. I asked to leave at that
point. A doctor who overheard my request said, I have been overlooking the physicianÃÂs
assistant that has been treating you and will put in your file that you are leaving without
our consent. I protested and said but I have been sent here by a doctor to be checked by
an ENT or a Neurologist. She looked surprised when I said a doctor had sent me with the
request to see specialists, and then said we do not have any available right now, but we
have to make sure that you have not had a stroke or a brain tumor. I was then given a
CAT scan of my brain, told ÃÂgood newsÃÂ, you do not have a brain tumor or stroke and
sent home with several referrals to ENTÃÂs and Neurologists, given a prescription for antiinflammatory
medication and told if my condition worsens come back. I found I had
trouble with my bearings on the way out and continued to have trouble with direction for
two more months after the incident.

I was very upset that evening and made an on-line complaint to the California Attorney
General. A week later, [REDACTED], from the California Department of Justice
responded, saying the US Consumer Product Safety Commission in Washington is in a
much better position to render assistance in this matter.

On Wendsday, July 1, I called the Neurologists and ENTs the emergency room had
referred me to, but could not get an appointment for one or two months with any of them.
The symptoms had gotten worst.

On Thursday, July 2, the right side of my face had swollen more. The swelling had
increased to the area around and including where the iPhone had been in contact with my
face and throat. I called my family doctor again and he said go back to the emergency
room and tell them that ÃÂmy doctor said to ask you to do it right.ÃÂ I went back with my
request. The head nurse reviewed my case. This time an ENT doctor checked the
swelling and ordered x-rays to make sure the swelling was not obstructing my airway.
The doctor said, we could try a few things now, but potential complications are too high
and recommended waiting it out. The head nurse came to me afterwards and said call
back the doctors they had referred me to and tell them that the emergency room physician
had requested you be seen as soon as possible. I was again sent home with a prescription
anti-inflammatory. I called the doctors again and the earliest appointment I could get was
with a Neurologist, Doctor , [REDACTED],  on July 9th. I also got an appointment
with an ENT, Doctor , [REDACTED], on July 17, 2009.
Doctor , [REDACTED],  examined me on Thursday July 9th, and ordered an MRI. The MRI was
done on Sunday, July 12. On July 16, the neurologist called, advised that internally
everything looked okay, and scheduled a follow up.

On July 17, 2009, about 20 days after the incident, the ENT did an evaluation and
scheduled a hearing test and noted that I still had swelling on the right side of my face.
He said we could inject steroids or wait it out. I asked him, if it was possible that my
symptoms were unrelated to the iPhone incident and he said it was unlikely to be caused
by anything else. I chose to wait it out and get healthy as possible. A subsequent test and
evaluation by the ENT, six months later, showed there was no significant hearing change
from the first test, but said it may take a while for the feeling in my face to get back to
normal. He said a year is a relatively short time for this type of injury.
While waiting for my face to heal, I experienced several issues and complications that
required attention related to this matter. , [REDACTED], , DO (Doctor of Osteopathic
Medicine) started treating me on Sept 9, 2009. Various methods were tried including
getting off old meds that I was on for years. At this date, although my secondary
symptoms have gotten better, the primary problem, unusual sensation in my face,
remains.

I shared my ÃÂiPhone experienceÃÂ with several people. Most Mac lovers were very
disappointed with Apple, some did not believe me, and some attacked my honesty,
intelligence, education, financial stability, and character. For the record, I am a computer
systems developer. I have been self-employed for over twenty years. I am the CEO of
[REDACTED]. I have subcontracted as a systems
developer for Lockheed, Microsoft Consulting Services, and AT&T in the past, and have
personally influenced the decisions of the CEO of Microsoft. At this time I have a perfect
credit score of 990 as reported by three credit reporting agencies. I have a an AA degree
in Chemical Engineering with a pre-med emphasis, a BS in computer Science and an
MBA, and taught computer technology as a college instructor at the age of 24. I
developed and marketed medical imaging systems that communicated diagnosis and
treatment information with digital images over 14 years ago. I have had a Series 7 license
in the past for investment banking purposes. Part of my business now revolves around
integrating the Mac and PC environments using thin clients, virtual machines, and cloud
computing technology. I also develop hybrid telephone call routing and recording
systems that route calls to voice over IP, landlines, cell phones, PCÃÂs (Linux & Windows)
and Mac computers. I actively try not to offend Mac users.

Another Mac enthusiast who was very upset about what I had said about the Mac iPhone
tried to discredit me by pointing several people to this article on the Apple support web
site http://support.apple.com/kb/HT2101. This article has had several revisions. The last
revision is dated April 15, 2010. The first time I saw it, there was a photograph showing a
full iPhone screen with ÃÂTempertureÃÂ at the top in large letters. Below that, an
exclamation point in a yellow triangle. Below that, a message saying, ÃÂiPhone needs to
cool down before you can use itÃÂ. And at the bottom of the screen a barely readable
message ÃÂSlide for EmergencyÃÂ. Now it is showing a cropped image of the iPhone screen
with the triangle and the words ÃÂiPhone needs to cool down before you can use itÃÂ, the
ÃÂSlide for EmergencyÃÂ is not showing at this time. The article states ÃÂOperate iPhone 3G,
iPhone 3GS, and iPad in a place where the temperature is between 0ÃÂº and 35ÃÂº C (32ÃÂº to
95ÃÂº F)ÃÂ. There are many days in California and Minnesota that exceed the iPhoneÃÂs
limitations. The original publish date of the article has been removed. It also states ÃÂStore
the device in a place where the temperature is between -20ÃÂº and 45ÃÂº C (-4ÃÂº to 113ÃÂº F).
DonÃÂt leave the device in your car, because temperatures in parked cars can exceed this
range.ÃÂ There are many geographic areas in the world that exceed these limitations.
The excuse that the heat shutoff was programmed in the iPhone just in case you left the
iPhone in a hot car makes no sense. A person would have to burn his hand first picking
up the iPhone, not put the iPhone to his ear, and read the screen before he gets this
message. This message would have to pop up while the iPhone is in use or already in the
possession of a person for it to serve any meaningful purpose. The fact that the
messages above have been programmed in the iPhone shows that Apple was aware
of the heating issue with the iPhones before Apple sold them.
The heat shutoff message did not come up when I was on the iPhone with the operator.
The documentation stated that it is still possible to make emergency calls when this
message shows by following a sequence to unlock the iPhone. The documentation does
not state whether you can talk to the operator when this message is activated, or if it is
activated while already on the iPhone.

Even if the iPhone is functioning the way it was designed, the iPhone is supposed to stop
functioning in extreme temperatures. That means if someone has to call from a fire,
extreme sunlight, or blizzard or any emergency environment, were extreme temperature
is likely, the iPhone will not function normally. In a hot fire where there is likely to be
smoke, an individual will not be able to use the iPhone as they normally would. If there is
no smoke, they may be able to figure out what the surprise message states, to unlock the
iPhone and make an emergency call. One could ask, ÃÂwhy did they not program the
iPhone to simply play an audio message that states ÃÂThis iPhone is too hot to useÃÂ, instead
of disabling the iPhone, requiring the user to read the screen, and go through a sequence
of events to unlock the iPhone in an emergency?ÃÂ

I believe this feature, the way it was programmed, caused me to suffer significant injury
and likely to cause additional injuries and death to Apple iPhone users. I believe AppleÃÂs
product is defective; a telephone appliance should never behave like a microwave
oven, or even a heating pad for that matter, with or without warning. A phone
should never disable or alter functionality to make or receive an emergency call due
to a controllable problem on the phone. I have already mentioned one method above to
remedy this situation, loud audio warning and no disabling of calling functionality.
justification: The incident resulted in injury to the user's face, and the likelihood of occurrence is high given the widespread use of iPhones and the known heating issue.

incident_description:
A CASIO MOD. KL-750 SUFFERED A MELTING OF THE PRINTHEAD SHIELD AND BURN MARKS ON THE POWER SUPPLY. THIS UNIT IS NOT USED EVERYDAY, BUT IS KEPT PLUGGED IN.

THIS ITEM IS APPROX. 2 YEARS OLD.
justification: The incident resulted in damage to the printer but no injuries, and it's possible that this could happen again given the unit is kept plugged in.

incident_description: The consumer says the projector bulb caught fire after a few minutes of being installed and turned on.  The consumer says he contacted the manufacturer and they reached a settlement.  The consumer says he unplugged the unit and the fire went out.  The consumer says he has a video of the fire and pictures of damage to the bulb.  After the bulbs were returned Apex lamps balked on the agreement.
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the incident of the projector bulb catching fire poses a potential risk to users.

incident_description: I have a Sony laptop model VGN-S270 that has been burning me for quite awhile now without me realizing it or paying much attention to it as it was not bothering me before. I'm aware of Sony's known issues with their computers burning people but I didn't find my particular model in the list of know pcs to cause this. My laptop generates so much radiated heat that Now that I'm more concious about it I realize that it's been burning me all this time. All this radiated heat can't be good for me and now i don't want to use it anymore.
justification: The laptop's excessive heat has caused burns, indicating an injury (severity level 3), and the user's awareness of Sony's similar issues makes it likely to occur again (likelihood 4).

incident_description: Earlier this week I returned home after major surgery.  Most of my time is now spent in a fully extended reclining chair.  To occupy my time I use a netbook computer to surf the internet, send & receive email and read books downloaded from Google. Most of the time I rest the netbook flat on my stomach.  Yesterday morning, my wife noticed a large blister near my surgical dressing.  We returned to our surgeon's office and the nurse said that the blister was most likely a burn.  She asked how that might be possible.  I remembered that the bottom of my netbook was often warm and sometimes hot.  When we returned home, we reconstructed the conditions I have described and are now convinced that the combination of placing the laptop flat on my stomachand thereby impeding the circulation of cooling air resulted in the internal temperature of the netbook rising so much that I was burned.  Hence I report that this particular model of netbook (sometimes called small laptop) should have additional cooling capacity, should not be used while resting on a lap or, at least, significant warnings of the possibility of burns should be prominently displayed somewhere on the device.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (burn), and given the direct cause-and-effect relationship between the netbook's heat and the burn, it's likely to occur again under similar conditions.

incident_description:

incident_description:

I am unable to contact HP regarding this, as my computer is out of warranty and they do not provide the ability for consumers to e-mail regarding safety concerns.  They also charge for telephone calls.
justification: Potential fire hazard due to bulging battery, but no immediate injury reported.

I have also found on there website  on securing the tv a mention of missing screw holes  but they still won't help   hopefully you can help with this problem
justification: Potential tip-over hazard due to missing screw holes, posing a possible injury risk to young children in the household.

incident_description: We had the mintek portable dvd player.  We had just gotten home from vacation.  The next day we plugged in the dvd player to charge it.  We were out of the house and when we came home our house was on fire.  Since we live in a rural area our home was a total loss.  We had a fire investigator come out and it was in fact that dvd player that started our house fire.  We did not know that the dvd player battery was recalled.  Thankfully no one was home and everyone is safe.
justification: The fire was caused by a recalled battery in a portable DVD player, which was unlikely to be known by the homeowners.

incident_description:
The following incidents involving the Line 6 DT50 guitar amplifier have been reported on the Line 6 support forums.  I have this amplifier in my home and I am concerned about a possible fire hazard.

OMG - this is too strange. I just received my DT50 112 today, went home on lunch to check it out and no more than 5 minutes later I lose all the low end in my tone, then no guitar sound, then a loud hum followed by a fairly loud fizzling sound, like lighting the fuse of a firework. So much smoke started coming out of the unit that I brought it outside afraid my house was going to burn down. Several minutes passed by before the smoke stopped. This is unfortunate, because I was planning to transition from high end boutique amps to my HD500 with DT50 and JTV59, which is on order. I hope these are rare occurrences. I gig weekly and need something reliable. I've never had this kind of experience with Line6 gear, but suffice it to say I'm a bit rattled. I bought this one from Same Day Music due to a special invitation only sale. Now they're out of 112s so I agreed to upgrade to a 212 for the replacement. I'll keep my fingers crossed that lightning won't strike twice (or three times if you count getstrat's experience).

I had 2 DT-50 112's and I connected them together with the V-link.  When I did this, one unit started making really bad incredibly loud noise.  Then it started smoking (a lot of smoke in a very short time). I have returned the smoking unit as defective and have ordered a replacement. 

I was playing my DT50 1x12 with the band Tonight , everything was fine for 1&1/2 hour and then the sound started to fade out ! And when i checked the amp , it was SMOKING and then everything went down ! No Light on the panel or any sound anymore !!! HELP !!! Is there something i could check out  ? Tubes ? Fuse ?
justification: Multiple reports of smoke and malfunction within a short period, indicating a possible design or manufacturing issue.

incident_description:

The cover guard is still warped and the lower cover guard is cracked.  We would like these items replaced and/ or repaired.

thank you,

[redacted]

incident_description: The television was being used in a normal way, watching television, when it began emitting a strong "burning electronic" smell.  The smell resulted in a severe headache.  The television picture blinked out and smoke was emitted from the television resulting in the need to unplug it.  It has not been plugged in since this incident.  The electronics were burning inside the television and it could have caught on fire if it had not been unplugged.  The television was plugged into a surge protector and was being used properly.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the incident involved a significant risk of fire, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' (Level 2). The likelihood is 'Possible' (Level 3) as it happened under normal usage conditions.

incident_description:
Small AC/battery powered speakers for iPod devices. Power cord does not insert properly into the speaker device, so this appears to be a potential electrical safety hazard.

I did not include pictures, but if you want them, I can do so.

incident_description:
HP Computer causes painful thumb strain due to a defective/unrepairable right and left click bar that is way too hard for a normal person to push effectively.

On January 25, 2011 my husband purchased a HP G62t customizable notebook PC online directly through HP.  The computer itself works quite well.  However, the left and right click bar on the notebook is so hard to press that I quickly strained my right thumb and was forced to switch over to a mouse.  I have been in contact with HP five times seeking a resolution to this problem, on the phone for nearly 5 hours with at least 10 people!  I was directed by HP to send in the computer to be ÃÂlooked atÃÂ only to be told by the technician that there is no way to correct this known problem.  I would suggest this could be viewed as a consumer product safety issue.

incident_description: 18 months ago I purchased a Hewlett Packard Notebook with the model number dv7-1448dx.  Twice I have had to ask for an optical drive on this unit because it stopped working.  I am now reporting a possible unsafe product due to the following issues.  This laptop is no longer working due to an extreme overheating problem that is occurring with the unit. After 15 minutes of using the notebook it gets so extremely hot that it shuts down and will not restart until it completely cools down.  This notebook I feel is a fire hazard waiting to happen.  I have not been able to contact HP due to the fact that it is out of warranty.  Any help that you can give me regarding this issue will be helpful.

incident_description: Sony Rear-Projection Television Model #KDF50WE620 rear-projection lamp so hot it melted frame and door protecting heat from escaping the lamp housing causing toxic smoke to leech in home causing health issues including heaches and television to nearly catch fire.

incident_description: The lamp in my Sony KF-50WE610 LCD projection television became so hot that it melted the plastic housing around it, as well as the enclosure door.  It is unclear what other damage this caused inside the television, but this would appear to be a significant fire hazard.  This happened under normal use, and seems to be a recognized issue with this particular television model.
justification: The incident caused significant damage to the television and posed a fire hazard, indicating a high likelihood of occurrence given the recognized issue with the model.

incident_description:
A surge protector in a power strip produced by Belkin (http://www.belkin.com/) was defective and caught our house on fire on October 27, 2010. The fire did approximately $70,000 worth of damage to our home. The house had to be completely stripped down to the frame and rebuilt. The process of rebuilding our home took almost six months. 

At the time of the fire, there was a power surge which triggered the surge protector in the power strip. My father was at home sick at the time. When he walked into the kitchen and discovered that there was no power, he went out into the garage and started flipping breakers in order to restore power. Almost immediately after that, electrical sounds such as sizzling and crackling flew through the ceiling and into the wall behind the living room couch. Moments later, the Belkin power strip exploded throwing flames and catching the couch on fire. If my father had been asleep on the couch, who knows what may have happened. 

Belkin [REDACTED] reimbursed [REDACTED] my father's deductible. We plan to sue for pain and suffering.
justification: The incident resulted in significant property damage and posed a high risk of injury or death, as evidenced by the power strip explosion and the potential for the homeowner to be asleep on the couch.

incident_description: Consumer wanted to report that her HP laptop became verry warm to the touch and died. She had been using it for an hour. She bought it in November of 2009. At the time it was being used with the adapter and this would beceome hot with or without the adapter. She had taken it in to the technician and was told that the processor or the south bridge may be the issue. It was serviced by Cam's Computer sale and repair. She was using it on top of a table with a book underneath it as she always does. So far just the computer overheats. She has also noticed that the battery is not on a recall. There is no discoloration or charring. She had experienced no signs of shock. She called HP today and spoke with [REDACTED]  in Tech support. The computer is usable and wont stay on because it overheats. She has not sent it to the manufacturer for service as she is past warranty. The computer did not burn the table or the book. She felt it was imperative to report this issue to the CPSC.
justification: While no injuries were reported, the incident of the laptop overheating and dying is concerning and could potentially lead to property damage or injury if not addressed.

incident_description:
Using an ATT 3-handset cordless phone set SL82318 model for routine household use for over a year.

One of our handsets melted in the base this week. The other 2 handsets started "shorting" out and heating up over the last couple of weeks.

Based on web research we figured this was a battery problem rather than a phone problem although we do have one mishapen handset that could have started a fire!

We tried the ATT customer support line on base of phone after seeing online that maybe it is just the batteries' fault that one of our phones MELTED and the other 2 keep dying. We have asked ATT to send us an email to advise what our fire hazard risk is and what fix is recommended. In meantime, we took the remaining 2 batteries out of the handsets.

While we did find a recall notice for other models' batteries due to these types of problems these are not replacement batteries. They are the original batteries we got with the set.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a fire hazard with handsets melting and heating up, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description: Targus power adapter for my dell laptop computer. On several occasions I noticed a spark and some smoke come out of the back of my laptop at the plug. When the adapter quit working, I bought a second one and the same thing happened. On the worst event the sound card and the card reader both quit working. Later my computer would no longer turn on at all. Even after I purchased a dell power cord. I believe the targus power cords are directly related to my laptop's complete failure to operate.
justification: Multiple incidents of sparking and smoking, leading to hardware failure and laptop becoming inoperable.

incident_description:

thank you
[REDACTED]
Ft. myers,Florida
justification: While no injury occurred, the incident could have resulted in significant property damage or even a house fire if the user had been away longer.

incident_description: I was scanning a document with my HP OfficeJet 6310 on 3/19/11, and heard a pop.  I looked over at the scanner and the display was off as if I turned the printer off.  All of a sudden smoke started to pour out of the unit, filling the room with smoke.  I called HP and told them, and all they said was this never happened before, and since it is out of warranty, I could purchase a new printer at a $10 discount.
justification: While no injuries were reported, the incident of smoke emission from the printer indicates a potential fire hazard, making it an incident with no injury but possible severe consequences.

incident_description:
I was charging a dewalt battery # DW9091 usung a dewalt charger # DW9107 DATE CODE 9729.

the battery and charger got hot enough that it melted the battery to the charger.  The battery also was very hot and deformed (bulged out).

incident_description:
The Kindle reader by Amazon.com uses a thin power cord for recharging and transferring information.  My cord suddenly flaked off the coating at each end as I going to recharge it, exposing bare wire. I researched it at amazon.com, and came across a "kindle accessory" forum that has the topic " Kindle2 power cord fell apart" with 178 participants and 241 posts (as of 3/15/2011).  I registered my complaint, and eventually was offered the opportunity to buy another.  I complained that this is a product defect that is a safety hazard, and demanded to know what they intended to do about this.  Amazon has not responded. Most posts talk about working around the problem such as taping the cord.  A solution that is likely to lead to injury.  The forum can be accessed at:

incident_description:

The computer gets to 100C and then shuts down. It's not neccesary to do heavy work on the machine for this, with just being on is enough.

I don't expect to get my machine repaired, but at leat you should do something so companies don't continue selling faulty products and then wash their hands as if nothing ever happened.

Regards,

incident_description:
DeWalt "Guaranteed Tough" 12 ga 25 foot extension cord purchased at Costco about 2 years ago.
Clear molded connectors on each end.  Was using the extension cord to power a 1500 W load from a space heater.  On the male end (that goes into the plug on the wall) the crimp between the wire in the cord and the spade lug that goes into the plug, overheated, charring the plastic in the plug and heating the cord and outlet so that it was too hot to touch.  I stopped using the cord, cut off the plug and replaced it with an aftermarket plug from the hardware store.  This cord is a potential fire hazard due to faulty construction.
The markings that still exist on the cord are "DeWalt Guaranteed Tough" and
<UL> SJTW 12AWGX3C 60C VW-1 E215210 100281-001
justification: Potential fire hazard due to faulty construction, overheating, and charring, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: A mother placed her 1-year-old child in a supine position in a crib, with a fleece blanket over her legs, and gave her a book to look at before falling asleep on 08/292023. At approximately 1615 on 08/29/2023, the mother went to get the children up from their nap. She came into the bedroom, turned toward the decedent's crib, and found the decedent seated in the corner of the crib with her legs out in front of her, partially suspended, with the cord from a wall-mounted Motorola COMFORT75BU baby monitor looped around her neck and her head positioned with her chin against her chest. A mild to moderate ligature furrow was noted around the neck.
justification: The child's death was caused by strangulation with a monitor cord, making it a severe incident with a possible likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description:
14 year-old boy was racing in a motorcross ATV event wearing a helmet mounted Contour camera on a Kinetic racing helmet.  During the race he collides with other races and crashes.  Video from the camera appears to show him flipping over the handlebars and striking the left side of his head on the ground.   The camera is also mounted to the left side of the helmet.  The video appears to show the camera breaking off the helmet and spinning into the grass after the impact with the ground.   He is unresponsive when first responders arrive.  Resuscitation is not successful and he is pronounced dead.

I performed the autopsy.  There was a focal depressed skull fracture of the left side of the skull that was the most significant injury on the body.  The appearance of the depression suggests that the head struck an object that was protruding off the ground, such as a large rock or the cylinder of the camera.  A large rock seems unlikely given that this is a motorcross racing track.  The left side of the helmet is fractured.   The camera is cylindrical shaped and was mounted to the left side of the helmet via a plastic mount.   Based on the video, the point of impact appeared to be at the camera mount site.   I know that these cameras are designed to break off the helmet with relatively minor impact as a safety mechanism.  However, in this case, the camera may have broken off only partially, or in such a way that the front of the camera turned inward toward the head, and became trapped between the head and the ground, such that when the head struck the ground, it also struck the protruding camera, resulting in the fatal depressed skull fracture.
justification: Death resulted from a severe head injury caused by the boy's head striking the ground and a partially detached camera mount.

incident_description: Inside the living room of the decedent's home was a large wooden entertainment center cabinet with a large hole in the middle for a television. On the carpeted floor in front of the entertainment center was a large, approximately 40" Sony Trinitron box television. The television was estimated to weigh approximately 100lbs plus. The televisions measurements were L39"xH30"xD25". The television was damaged on the top and the side with cracks and missing parts. A piece of the missing part, which fit into the side of the television had small droplets of blood on it. There was dried blood noted on the top front part of the television. There was what appeared to be multiple finger prints noted on the top of the television. A blood stain was noted on the carpet next to the T.V. Blood droplets were noted inside the hallway towards the kitchen/dining area. Measurements for the opening for the television from the back wall to the front shelf edge was 22".  The decedent was a 2 year old that appeared to have suffered head trauma when a large 40" boxed television fell on top of her. The decedent was playing in front of the T.V with a 4 year old when apparently the 4 year old bumped the T.V causing it to fall off the shelf. Measurements of the shelf and space from the back wall to the front edge of the T.V stand appeared to be smaller than the T.V's depth.
justification: A 2-year-old child died from head trauma after a heavy television fell on her.

incident_description: The decedent is a 2 1/2-year-old female who was attempting to get a movie from the top drawer of a two drawer nightstand upon which a 32-inch large box television (147-pounds) was located.  The mother, who was cleaning up the kitchen after dinner, heard a loud noise and saw the child lying on her back on the living room floor with the television resting on top of her head.  The mother and a friend who was over for dinner moved the set off the child and called 911.  Emerency responders transported the child to the hospital where she could not be revived.
justification: The child's death was directly caused by the heavy television falling on her head, making this a severe incident with a possible likelihood of occurrence.
